$parserComment: The three ceilings the parser puts on a nested construct, all of them CONFIG-DRIVEN from this block and all three of them fail-loud COUNTERS -- a nest past any of them emits a positioned diagnostic that NAMES ITSELF and recovers; none of them ever crashes, and none of them is allowed to surface as a syntax error against a token the author wrote correctly. The loader reads each key into the matching `ParserConfig` field via `parserConfigFor` (src/analysis/compilation_unit/compilation_unit.cpp); each C++ field default is only the fallback when its key is absent, and toy/tsql/the assembly dialects omit the whole block. || (1) `maxExpressionDepth` = 1024 -- the Pratt walker's expression-NESTING cap, threshold of the positioned `P_ExpressionTooDeep` backstop. RAISED 256 -> 1024 by plan-24 Stage 7, which flattened the parser's operator/ternary/prefix/infix descent and all of cst_to_hir/hir_to_mir/semantic/const-eval onto explicit work-stacks (O(1) host-stack per level), leaving ONE residual recursion: the paren/postfix-body arm (deferred Stage 5b), one host frame per nested '('. The cap must trip BEFORE that arm overflows on the WORST supported build, so it must sit BELOW the tightest crash ceiling. || ** THE HEADROOM CLAIM THAT USED TO STAND HERE WAS MEASURED ON THE WRONG THREAD, AND IT IS CORRECTED RATHER THAN DELETED SO THE ERROR STAYS VISIBLE.** It read: MEASURED native-Windows paren-crash ceilings on the 64 MiB worker -- MSVC Debug ~3000-3200, MSVC Release ~16000-16500, MinGW Release ~20000-24000 -- '1024 leaves ~3x headroom below the tightest'. Every one of those numbers is a LARGE-WORKER number. `src/program/program.cpp` builds every CU inside `substrate::callOnLargeStack(64 MiB)`, but a library embedder, the LSP and every unit test parse on an ORDINARY ~1 MiB thread, and that is the stack the safety argument has to be made against. +RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 on the ORDINARY thread (Windows, MinGW gcc 13.2.0, Debug), through `tests/hir/test_frontend_deep_nesting_probe` with `DSS_HS_PROBE_KIND=paren DSS_HS_PROBE_STOP=parse` and the cap lifted out of the way: a 1260-deep paren nest parses, 1300 dies of stack overflow. So the real margin under 1024 is about **1.23x, not 3x** -- thin enough that a build with fatter frames than MinGW Debug would CRASH before the cap fired, which is the fail-loud contract broken. The VALUE is left at 1024 here deliberately (it is pinned by tests/analysis/syntactic/test_parser_c_smoke and is not this row's to move); what changed is that the number in this comment is now the one that was actually measured. || (2) `maxSpeculationDepth` = 320 -- how deep the parser may nest SPECULATIVE probes while disambiguating alternatives, threshold of the positioned `P_MaxSpeculationDepth` backstop. **WAS A HARDCODED 8, AND 8 WAS A CONFORMANCE DEFECT.** c's `operand` alt speculates once per nested cast (`(int)` can start `castExpr` or `compoundLiteralExpr`, so the LL(k) prune cannot pick one), so `(int)` x8 compiled and x9 was REFUSED -- with `error[P_NoAlternativeMatched]: expected 'Identifier', ... -- got 'int'`, i.e. the compiler blaming the author's own correct `int` (D-PARSE-NINE-NESTED-CASTS-ARE-REFUSED-BY-THE-SPECULATION-CAP-WITH-A-FABRICATED-SYNTAX-ERROR). +MEASURED reference matrix for `int main(void){int x=0; return (int)...x;}`, each reference probed SEPARATELY: gcc 13.3.0 (WSL) compiles 65536 rc 0; mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 compiles 32768 and dies at 65536 with NO message; clang 18.1.3 compiles 1349 and SIGSEGVs (rc 139) from 1350; MSVC 19.51.36252 compiles 2985 and from 2986 refuses LOUDLY with `fatal error C1026: parser stack overflow, program too complex` -- naming its own limit and no token of the user's, which is exactly the shape DSS now adopts. All four accept 8, 9, 16, 64, 256, 512 and 1024. || WHY 320 AND NOT 1349 (the tightest reference ceiling). Speculation is still HOST RECURSION -- one `trySpeculativeBranch` + `stepOnce` frame per level, ~1.63 KiB measured -- so the cap is a real stack guard, not a taste. +MEASURED 2026-09-03 on the ORDINARY ~1 MiB thread (Windows, MinGW gcc 13.2.0, Debug) through `tests/analysis/syntactic/test_parser_speculation_ceilings`'s `DSS_NC_PROBE_CASTS` probe with all three ceilings lifted: **640 nested casts parse, 641 dies of stack overflow.** 320 is that floor / 2 -- a 2.0x margin, which is what covers a build whose frames are twice MinGW Debug's. It is 40x the old 8 and 5.1x the ISO C23 5.2.4.1 floor of 63 nesting levels of parenthesised expressions (a FLOOR, not a target), and it is ~18x the deepest nesting the sqlite amalgamation actually contains (18). ** THE RESIDUAL GAP IS RECORDED, NOT GLOSSED: at 321 casts DSS refuses where all four references compile.** That gap is the un-converted host recursion, not a policy choice -- the operator's standing ruling is that input-proportional recursion becomes an explicit HEAP work stack with the limit surviving as a counter that still fails loud, and the speculation drive is the site that has not been converted. Until it is, 320 is the largest value that keeps the promise that the ceiling, and never a stack overflow, is what a too-deep program meets. Raising this number without converting that recursion trades a loud refusal for a crash. ** THE C++ FALLBACK IS 64, DELIBERATELY UNEQUAL TO THIS 320: if they matched, deleting this key (or the `parserConfigFor` line that reads it) would change nothing observable and 'config-driven' would be a claim no red-on-disable arm could refute. `examples/c/deep_nested_casts` carries a 65-cast chain for exactly that reason. || (3) `speculationBudgetFactor` = 64 -- how many tokens ONE speculative probe may consume, as a multiple of the alt's own declared `lookahead`; threshold of the positioned `P_SpeculationBudgetExhausted` backstop. **WAS A HARDCODED 16 WITH NO DIAGNOSTIC AT ALL** -- the probe simply failed, the alt fell through to its non-speculative fallback replay, and the replay produced the same fabricated `got 'int'`. +MEASURED with the two depth ceilings lifted: `(int)` x341 compiled rc 0 and x342 was refused, because `operand`'s `lookahead: 64` times 16 is a 1024-token budget and 341 casts is 1023 tokens. || RAISED 16 -> 64 (a 4096-token budget for `operand`) ON A SECOND MEASUREMENT, not on the cast chain -- for a cast chain the DEPTH ceiling is now the tighter of the two, so the factor would have been unobservable there and the raise unjustified. The axis that reaches it is a construct long in TOKENS and shallow in NESTING, which is the shape a real corpus actually has (the sqlite amalgamation nests only 18 deep but carries a single 1765-element initializer in fts5.c). +MEASURED on `(int)(x+1+1+...)`, one speculative probe holding the whole chain: at factor 16, 505 terms parse and 510 are REFUSED; at factor 64, 2040 parse and 2050 are refused. So the old value silently capped a legal C expression at ~509 terms -- a ceiling nobody chose, arrived at by multiplying a DISAMBIGUATION distance by an arbitrary constant. ** THE PREMISE THAT FIRST JUSTIFIED THE RAISE WAS AN INFERENCE AND WAS REPLACED BY THAT MEASUREMENT: the sqlite initializer figure says the shape EXISTS in real code, it does not say the budget is what refuses it. The 505/510 pair does. || ** ALL THREE ARE READ AT ONE CHOKEPOINT AND NONE OF THEM HIDES BEHIND ANOTHER. There used to be a FOURTH, invisible: `BuilderConfig::maxSpeculationDepth` = 64, hardcoded, which would have become the binding ceiling at 65 casts the moment the parser's 8 was lifted. `Parser::parse` now DERIVES it from `maxSpeculationDepth` -- the parser's speculation probe is the only checkpoint construction site in the engine, so the two are the same number and one key drives both.**
$languageReferencesComment:
★★★ FC17.9(i) / plan 29 P1+P2 (operator decision 2026-08-12, *'we don't have this mechanism, and is the only one acceptable, so asm language is reused'*): THIS FILE CONTAINS NO INLINE-ASM GRAMMAR RULE. It contains a REFERENCE to the language that owns them. `src/dss-config/sources/asm.lang.json` declares `asmStmt` and its eleven companion rules ONCE; this block says which of C's own rules and token kinds fill the holes that grammar declares, and `statement`'s alt reaches the result through `asmStmt` like any other statement.
★★ WHAT MAKES THIS A MECHANISM AND NOT A FILE SPLIT: `asm.lang.json` never spells `Colon`, `ColonColonOp`, `AsmKeyword` or `expression`. Those are THIS language's vocabulary, and the twelve rules would be a C feature in a different file if they named them. It spells ROLES — `sectionSeparator`, `sectionSeparatorFused`, `asmKeyword`, `operandExpr` — and the table below is where C says what its roles are. A SECOND host with a different lexical surface binds the same roles to ITS kinds and inherits all twelve rules, the semantic refusal and the HIR-lowering row with ZERO new grammar. That is the deliverable; the asm grammar is its first consumer.
★ EVERY HOLE IS BOUND OR THE LOAD FAILS. The loader checks BOTH directions: an unbound hole is a load error (never a silently non-matching rule), a binding naming a hole `asm.lang.json` does not declare is a load error (never a silently ignored line), a binding naming a rule or token kind THIS file does not declare is a load error, and — the one that would otherwise be invisible — an `entry` no shape here references is a load error, because a reference that merges cleanly and is never reached looks identical to a working one until someone writes an `__asm__`.
★ WHAT C INHERITS FOR FREE, and the reason ownership sits over there: `semantics.inlineAsm` (the precise extended-asm refusal) and the `asmStmt` → `InlineAsm` lowering row both live in `asm.lang.json` and are merged in from it. The refusal 'extended asm is not yet supported' is a property of the ASM language's implementation maturity, not of C. ⚠ The loader REFUSES a collision in either direction rather than picking a winner, so this file cannot silently weaken a refusal it did not write.
★ TOKEN BINDINGS, TWO NOTES ON THE NON-OBVIOUS ONES. `sectionSeparatorFused` → `ColonColonOp` is not a curiosity: `::` is ONE token here by maximal munch (C23 attribute namespaces need the spelling), ✔MEASURED on the real DSS binary, so the fused section boundary is a distinct KIND and must be bound separately from `sectionSeparator` — see asm.lang.json's `asmStmt` $comment. `symbolName` → `Identifier` serves BOTH the symbolic operand name (`[out] "=r"(x)`) and the `asm goto` target labels, which in C are the same lexical class. The three qualifiers bind to the SAME `VolatileKeyword`/`InlineKeyword`/`GotoKeyword` kinds C already has, which is why `__asm__ __volatile__ (…)` — the form real headers write — parses with no new spelling: `__volatile__` aliases onto `VolatileKeyword` (see $gnuDunderSpellingsAreUnconditionalComment).
★ `operandExpr` → `expression`, NOT `assignmentExpr`, and that is MEASURED: `__asm__ ("" : : "r"(a, b))` is accepted by gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 — the comma operator is legal inside an operand's parens, and `assignmentExpr` exists precisely to stop before it. `templateText` → `stringLiteralExpr` (not a bare StringLiteral token) so adjacent concatenation and the L/u/U/u8 prefixes decode through the SAME decodeAdjacentStringBodies chokepoint every other string payload here uses.
$preprocessComment: FC13: opts c into the config-SELECTED C preprocessor pass (src/analysis/preprocess/). `enabled:true` runs the pass between tokenize and parse: it builds ONE synthesized buffer by recursively splicing quote-#include"h" headers' text, tokenizes once, then runs the object-like macro pass (#define/#undef, expansion + rescan + blue-paint self-ref guard, directive removal). The TOKEN-name fields (directiveIntroToken/quoteIncludeToken/angleIncludeToken) are validated against the interned token kinds; the directive-keyword strings (define/undef/include) are matched by lexeme TEXT against the token after `#` (define/undef are NOT grammar keywords -- they lex as Identifier). Angle #include <h> is LEFT in place for the existing post-parse FF11 import resolver (so angleIncludeToken lets the PP RECOGNISE and pass it through). toy/tsql-subset declare NO preprocess block -> their pass is a strict identity (token stream in == out).

preprocess.$elifdefComment: C23 (D-PP-ELIFDEF-ELIFNDEF; C 6.10.1): the `#elifdef`/`#elifndef` directive WORDS. `#elifdef X` == `#elif defined(X)`, `#elifndef X` == `#elif !defined(X)` (C 6.10.1p5) -- routed through the SAME #elif conditional-group state machine, but evaluating the operand with the DIRECT #ifdef-style definedness lookup (the operand is a bare macro name, NOT run through the #if expression evaluator). Matched by lexeme TEXT (they lex as plain Identifier, like elif/else/endif). OPTIONAL: a config that omits them (or strips them) makes the directive fall through to the unsupported-directive fail-loud -- never a silent branch skip.
preprocess.$vaOptNameComment: FC18a (D-PP-VA-OPT, C23 6.10.5.1): the va-opt-replacement introducer. `__VA_OPT__( content )` in a VARIADIC macro's replacement list yields `content` when the variable arguments' SUBSTITUTION is non-empty, and a placemarker otherwise. Matched by TEXT like `variadicArgsName` (it lexes as an ordinary identifier, so there is no token kind to resolve). NOT a spelling of `variadicCommaElision`: ✔MEASURED on clang-18/clang-19/gcc-13, with `#define EMP` the GNU idiom `g(f , ## __VA_ARGS__)` keeps the comma for `GNU(1, EMP)` (the argument is PRESENT) while `g(f __VA_OPT__(,) __VA_ARGS__)` drops it (the argument's SUBSTITUTION is empty) -- two predicates, two keys.
preprocess.$variadicCommaElisionComment: FC15 paste residuals (D-PP-VARIADIC-GNU-COMMA-ELISION): opt into the GNU `,##__VA_ARGS__` extension. `sep ## __VA_ARGS__` with an EMPTY variadic part drops the preceding separator (`LOG("x")` -> `f("x")`); non-empty keeps it. Without this flag, standard C placemarker behavior leaves the separator. The separator/__VA_ARGS__ are matched by the config KIND/name above, never hardcoded.
preprocess.$predefinedMacrosComment: FC15b (C 6.10.8): the predefined macros. Each entry names the macro IDENTIFIER + a materialization `kind`; the engine keys EVERY behavior off `kind`, never the name. `line`/`file` are OFFSET-derived (resolved through the line-map against the INVOCATION offset -> the invocation line / the presumed file name); `date`/`time` are computed once at preprocess construction (`"Mmm dd yyyy"` / `"hh:mm:ss"`); `constant` carries a static `value` spelling verbatim. `#define`/`#undef` of any of these is a constraint violation (C 6.10.8.1) -> fail loud. __STDC_VERSION__ = 202311L (C23). VLA support LANDED (D-CSUBSET-VLA C1b, 2026-07-13): `int a[n]` now RUNS (dynamic-stack `sub sp,<size>` + a conditional frame pointer, agnostic x86_64/arm64 x ELF/PE/Mach-O), so __STDC_NO_VLA__ is REMOVED from this table -- a VLA-SUPPORTING implementation must NOT define it (C11 6.10.8.3 / C23 6.10.9.3; the mirror of the fail-loud-era decision that defined it). __STDC_NO_THREADS__ (FC17.9(a) D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-TRAMPOLINES): REMOVED ENTIRELY. C11 6.10.8.3 / C23 6.10.9.3 make the macro the conforming announcement that <threads.h> is NOT provided; <threads.h> is now COMPLETE on ALL legs — thrd_create/call_once/thrd_join land on elf (libc.so.6 FFI), pe64 (kernel32 synth: CreateThread/InitOnceExecuteOnce/WaitForSingleObject) AND macho (libSystem pthread synth: pthread_create DIRECT-PASS / pthread_once DIRECT / pthread_join + truncate; the macho trampolines closed the last carve-out) — so a conforming impl must NOT define the macro on ANY target, and the row is deleted (was momentarily macho-only after Cycle 2 while macho lacked thrd_create). c95 (Windows-host sub-arc): the OPTIONAL `availableObjectFormats` per-entry filter (mirrors the shipped-lib descriptor field; EMPTY = every format, a non-empty set of object-format NAMES restricts the macro to those formats — validated against objectFormatKindFromName at load, an unknown name fails loud) lets the Windows-selection macros be predefined for the `pe` target ONLY: `_WIN32`/`_WIN64` (value 1) make sqlite's amalgamation select os_win.c (SQLITE_OS_WIN); `__stdcall`/`__cdecl`/`__fastcall`/`WINAPI` ERASE to nothing (empty value) since PE64 has a single MS-x64 calling convention and imports are un-decorated (a `__stdcall`-qualified declarator then parses on pe, stays an ordinary identifier off-pe). None leak onto elf/macho. The 7 core C 6.10.8 macros carry NO availableObjectFormats filter (available everywhere); the formerly-CONDITIONAL __STDC_NO_THREADS__ (C11 6.10.8.3 / C23 6.10.9.3) is now DELETED — threads.h is complete on all legs (see above). ★★★ `_MSC_VER` IS DELETED — THE pe64 IDENTITY IS GNU-ON-WINDOWS, NOT MSVC (D-LANG-PE64-DEFINES-BOTH-MSC-VER-AND-GNUC). Until now the pe rows also carried `_MSC_VER=1943` while `__GNUC__`/`__GNUC_MINOR__`/`__GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__`/`__clang__` sit UN-GATED above, so a pe64 TU saw `_MSC_VER` AND `__GNUC__` AND `_WIN32` at once. ✔MEASURED (`clang-19 -dM -E -x c /dev/null --target=<triple>`, Ubuntu clang 19.1.1): `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` defines `_MSC_VER`/`_MSC_FULL_VER`/`_MSC_EXTENSIONS`/`_WIN32`/`_WIN64`/`__clang__` and NOT `__GNUC__` — clang SUPPRESSES `__GNUC__` in MS-compatibility mode on purpose; `x86_64-w64-mingw32` defines `__GNUC__`/`_WIN32`/`_WIN64`/`__clang__`/`__MINGW32__`/`__MINGW64__` and NOT `_MSC_VER`. NO reference compiler produces the union, so presenting it was a BIDIRECTIONAL conformance defect ([[feedback_reference_compilers_are_the_spec_2026_08_10]]): PRESENTING what none of gcc/clang/MSVC presents is as much a defect as missing what they all support. ★ WHY GNU IS THE HONEST HALF, argued from what this compiler IS rather than from what is least disruptive: (a) DSS implements GNU EXTENDED INLINE ASM (`__asm__ __volatile__` with operand constraints and clobbers) and MSVC x64 implements NO inline asm AT ALL, so `_MSC_VER` was the one identity that contradicts the feature set actually shipped; (b) `__GNUC__`/`__GNUC_MINOR__`/`__GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__`/`__clang__` are the language's UN-GATED base identity on EVERY format, and the GCC_VERSION encoding `__DSSCP__` documents above exists precisely to keep them truthful — dropping `__GNUC__` on pe alone would carve a hole in the language's own base identity and re-open the sys/cdefs.h `extern __inline` linkage trap `__clang__` was added to close; (c) the pe rows `__declspec`/`_declspec`/`__stdcall`/`__cdecl`/`__fastcall` are MACROS here, which is the MinGW shape (✔MEASURED: clang's mingw target defines `__declspec(a)` as `__attribute__((a))` and `__cdecl` as `__attribute__((__cdecl__))`) and NOT the MSVC shape, where every one of them is a KEYWORD the compiler never spells as a macro. `_MSC_VER` was the ONE foreign row in an otherwise GNU-on-Windows table. ★★ WHAT THE FALSE CLAIM COST, MEASURED: sqlite's `src/hwtime.h` opens `#if defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_WIN32)` -> `#include <profileapi.h>` and only LATER offers the `__GNUC__` rdtsc / `mrs cntvct_el0` arms, so pe64 ALONE took the FIRST arm and died `error[F001A]: profileapi.h` while the other four legs compiled — the claim routed DSS into the one header world (`<intrin.h>`, `<profileapi.h>`, the Windows SDK) that `_MSC_VER` promises and that DSS does not have. ⛔ The fix is NOT a `profileapi.h` descriptor: that treats the symptom and leaves the impossible identity in place to mis-route the NEXT header the same way. `_WIN32`/`_WIN64` STAY — they are the honest half (they name the OS, not the toolchain) and they are what selects os_win.c. ★★★ `__MINGW32__`/`__MINGW64__`/`__MSVCRT__` ARE NOW **ADDED**, IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT MADE THEM BACKABLE — which is the sequence the previous revision of this paragraph demanded, and the whole lesson of the `_MSC_VER` deletion above. That revision read “ARE NOT ADDED YET” and named its blocker precisely: `shippedLibs/dirent.json` and `unistd.json` were `[elf, macho]`, so `__MINGW32__` alone would have MOVED the error from `S000D` to `F001D` rather than fixing anything. Both descriptors now serve pe — `dirent.json` through a shipped-source realization, `unistd.json` as a RE-EXPORT whose `includes` edges to `io.h`/`process.h` are GATED to pe, mirroring what mingw's own `<unistd.h>` actually is — so the claim is backed at the moment it is made. ⚠ The blocker clause is REPLACED, not left standing beside its own resolution: a comment that records a fact the code no longer has is a defect this project keeps paying for. ★ AND THE BACKING IS CHECKED, NOT ASSERTED — each of the three rows carries an `impliedSurface` block naming the headers AND THE NAMES they must make visible, evaluated against the active per-format closure at load, so removing pe from `unistd.json` fails the build AT THE CLAIM instead of at some later `#if` that silently took the wrong arm [[D-LANG-PREDEFINED-MACRO-REQUIRES-REALIZED-SURFACE]]. ⚠ `impliedSurface` is MANDATORY on EVERY row here: `null` is the DECLARED absence, and an OMITTED field is a load error — because a defaulted absence is indistinguishable from an author who never asked the question, and “no one asked” is exactly the state that shipped `_MSC_VER` for months. ★ NOTE THE SHAPE: the identity fix did not CREATE the directory-API gap, it UNMASKED one — pe64 had been borrowing sqlite's MSVC-only shim on the strength of a claim that was false, which is the same mechanism, and the same lesson, as the `hwtime.h` mis-route above.  The pair is now pinned MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE FOR EVERY TARGET by `mutuallyExclusivePredefinedMacros` below, so no future target can re-co-define them. ⚠ ★★ WHY THE KEY IS `impliedSurface` AND NOT `requires`, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS BRIEFLY THE LATTER AND THE REASONING IS THE REUSABLE PART. `requires` was ALREADY carrying two unrelated meanings in this project — the DOCUMENT-LEVEL grammar-HOLES contract (`asm.lang.json`, `{rules,tokens}`: names an importing document must supply) and the sqlite harness's confound ENVIRONMENT-PROBE list (`legs.json`) — so a third would have been the second collision, not the first. ⚠ “Different scopes, no parse ambiguity” is a true statement about the PARSER and the WRONG TEST for a config key: the parser was never the reader at risk. The two relations are not alike — holes mark known INCOMPLETENESS, this marks a hard load-time REFUSAL on the honesty of an identity claim — and a reader carrying the first meaning into the second reads the empty form as “no known holes” rather than “this macro implies no platform surface”. THAT MISREAD WOULD DEFEAT THE ONE DEVICE THIS MECHANISM HAS AGAINST RECURRENCE, because the explicit-`null` form only works if writing it forces a thought. ★ The name states WHAT THE CLAIM IMPLIES rather than what it needs, which is what reads correctly in the `null` case — and the `null` case is the one that matters.

predefinedMacros.$comment: TF-C83: WHO DSS ACTUALLY IS -- the one row here that is honest rather than a dialect claim, and the only one always true on every format. `kind: version` packs the repo-root VERSION file (0.0.2) with `componentWeights` into ONE ordering-preserving integer: 0*1000000 + 0*1000 + 2 = 2, so 0.0.2 < 0.1.0 (1000) < 1.0.0 (1000000) compares correctly in `#if`. The weights use the GCC_VERSION shape ON PURPOSE -- sqliteInt.h:112 computes __GNUC__*1000000 + __GNUC_MINOR__*1000 + __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__, and the three __GNUC_* rows below exist to make that evaluate to 4002001, so this codebase has ONE version-encoding convention rather than two that differ by 100x. The weights also DERIVE the overflow bound (component i must stay under weights[i-1]/weights[i], i.e. < 1000 here); a VERSION of 0.0.1000 would encode identically to 0.1.0 and FAILS LOUD at load instead. NO `__DSSCP_VERSION__` string ships alongside: there is no measured demand for one in the 189-TU corpus, and an unbacked macro is the same small false claim that kept __clang_major__/__VERSION__ out of this table -- the `version` kind makes adding it a one-row change the day a real consumer appears.
predefinedMacros.name: __DSSCP__

impliedSurface.note: A version stamp on this compiler itself. Consuming code that branches on it is reaching for the DSS feature set at that version, which is a real claim and is not stateable as a header+names pair. Filed here rather than given its own tag because it is the `__GNUC__` shape with a different vendor, and a category with one member is not a category.

predefinedMacros.$comment: TF-C83 dialect claim. The LEFT side of TargetConditionals.h:342's conjunction; alone it opens nothing. Value 4 is what /usr/bin/clang reports (MEASURED).
predefinedMacros.name: __GNUC__

impliedSurface.note: GNU C language extensions, not a shipped header: statement expressions, `__asm__` with operand constraints and clobbers, `__attribute__`, `__inline__`. DSS genuinely delivers these — extended inline asm shipped this arc — so the claim is BACKED; it is simply not stateable as a header+names pair. Do not read this tag as "nothing to claim".

predefinedMacros.$comment: GCC_VERSION component. sqliteInt.h:112 computes __GNUC__*1000000 + __GNUC_MINOR__*1000 + __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__; shipping __GNUC__ alone would yield 4000000 instead of the truthful 4002001.
