impliedSurface.note: A GCC_VERSION component of the `__GNUC__` claim; see that row. It has no surface of its own and is meaningless apart from the triple.

predefinedMacros.$comment: GCC_VERSION component (see __GNUC_MINOR__). 4.2.1 is what /usr/bin/clang genuinely reports (MEASURED) -- NOT tuned to hold mutex_unix.c:101's >= 4001000 gate shut; provenance is the point.
predefinedMacros.name: __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__

impliedSurface.note: A GCC_VERSION component of the `__GNUC__` claim; see that row. It has no surface of its own and is meaningless apart from the triple.

predefinedMacros.$comment: TF-C83: the OR arm of TargetConditionals.h:342 -- `defined(__GNUC__) && (defined(__APPLE_CPP__) || defined(__APPLE_CC__) || defined(__MACOS_CLASSIC__))`. Gated macho because it is an Apple-toolchain fact, and it is USELESS without __GNUC__ above. NOT __APPLE_CPP__: that is Apple's C++ macro and real clang does not define it, so claiming it would be unbackable.
predefinedMacros.name: __APPLE_CC__

predefinedMacros.$comment: TF-C83: clears NONE of the TargetConditionals ladder -- it appears nowhere in it. Its ONLY job is sys/cdefs.h arm 1: `(__STDC_VERSION__ >= 199901L && !defined(__GNUC_GNU_INLINE__) && (!defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)))`. Once __GNUC__ is set, only __clang__ satisfies it. Arm 2 needs __GNUC_STDC_INLINE__ AND the gnu_inline attribute DSS lacks; without this row we land in arm 3 -- GNU-C89 `extern __inline`, the OPPOSITE of the C99 semantics TF-C79 shipped, i.e. silently wrong linkage rather than a parse error.
predefinedMacros.name: __clang__

impliedSurface.note: The clang dialect claim, the same shape as `__GNUC__`: language-level behaviour (and the `sys/cdefs.h` `extern __inline` linkage arm it was added to close), not a header surface.

predefinedMacros.$comment: TF-C115 (D-PP-ENDIANNESS-PREDEFINES): the GNU/clang BYTE-ORDER NAMING VOCABULARY -- the three constants a program compares `__BYTE_ORDER__` against. THEY LIVE ON THE LANGUAGE, NOT THE TARGET, FOR THE SAME REASON `__LP64__` LIVES ON THE FORMAT: declare a fact on the layer where it DOES NOT VARY. MEASURED 2026-08-04 (`clang-19 -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>`, Ubuntu clang 19.1.1, plus gcc 13.3.0 native and aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc-13): all three carry the SAME values 1234/4321/3412 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc AND on the BIG-ENDIAN aarch64_be-linux-gnu -- they do not vary by CPU, by object format, by data model, or even by the machine's actual byte order, because they are NAMES, not the answer. Restating three identical rows in both *.target.json files would falsely imply a per-CPU axis that does not exist. They are a GNU-dialect vocabulary rather than ISO C, which is exactly the class this table already carries (`__GNUC__`/`__GNUC_MINOR__`/`__GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__`/`__clang__` above). The per-machine ANSWER -- `__BYTE_ORDER__`, whose value REFERENCES one of these names -- is per-CPU and is declared in `<arch>.target.json`; `__LITTLE_ENDIAN__` likewise. WHAT THE ABSENCE COST, MEASURED: with none of these defined, `#if __BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__` evaluated `0 == 0` and was silently TRUE on a little-endian target (C 6.10.1p4 makes an unknown identifier 0) -- observed directly at TF-C115 probe F. That is a SILENT WRONG-BRANCH selection, not a missing feature, and sqlite3.c:16138 + :218892 (`SQLITE_BYTEORDER`) test exactly that shape. The cross-layer coupling (a target-declared `__BYTE_ORDER__` whose body names a LANGUAGE-declared `__ORDER_*`) is the same coupling clang has, and it is pinned by examples/c/endianness_predefines -- delete these three rows and that example's `#error` legs fire.
predefinedMacros.name: __ORDER_LITTLE_ENDIAN__

predefinedMacros.$comment: ★★★ THE GNU-ON-WINDOWS IDENTITY, COMPLETED — and it lands in the SAME change that makes it backable, which is the sequence [[D-LANG-PE64-HAS-NO-POSIX-DIRECTORY-API]] spelled out and the sequence `_MSC_VER` violated for months. ✔MEASURED (`x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc -dM -E -x c` on an empty TU, gcc 13.2.0, `-dumpmachine` `x86_64-w64-mingw32`): `__MINGW32__` 1, `__MINGW64__` 1, `__MSVCRT__` 1, `_WIN32` 1, `_WIN64` 1, `__GNUC__` 13, and NO `_MSC_VER` — so a compiler claiming `__GNUC__` and `_WIN32` while withholding these three presents an identity no real toolchain has, the same BIDIRECTIONAL defect as the union it replaced. ★★ WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, ✔MEASURED against the same-platform oracle under the sqlite harness's OWN 39-flag set: `bld/shell.c:178` selects its POSIX directory API with `#if (!defined(_WIN32) && !defined(WIN32)) || defined(__MINGW32__)`, and gcc compiles that TU with **0** errors where DSS reported **24**. The nested `#if defined(__MINGW32__)` arm also supplies sqlite's own `#ifndef S_ISLNK / #define S_ISLNK(mode) (0)` — which is why `sys/stat.json` must NOT declare `S_ISLNK` on pe ([[D-CONFIG-SYS-STAT-OVER-DECLARES-S-ISLNK-ON-PE]]): the two halves fit together only if DSS leaves that name to the source that guards it. ★ THE `impliedSurface` BLOCK IS THE POINT, NOT DECORATION — AND IT NAMES SYMBOLS, NOT JUST A HEADER. Header granularity is very nearly VACUOUS once re-export exists: `<unistd.h>` resolves on pe the MOMENT the `io.h` edge fires, even if the only name that arrives is `getpid` — so a claim guarded at header granularity is one the macro satisfies trivially, and the guard asserts nothing. Naming the NAMES is what makes it an audit instead of a formality. It is CHECKED against `<unistd.h>`'s and `<dirent.h>`'s ACTIVE TRANSITIVE CLOSURE on pe — the same walker and the same per-format edge gate the compile itself uses — so if a later edit takes `unistd.json`'s pe arm away, THIS ROW FAILS THE BUILD LOUDLY instead of quietly resuming the `_MSC_VER` failure mode one layer down. That is the entire difference between an identity claim and a checked consequence [[D-LANG-PREDEFINED-MACRO-REQUIRES-REALIZED-SURFACE]].
predefinedMacros.name: __MINGW32__

predefinedMacros.$comment: The 64-bit half of the same identity: real mingw defines BOTH on an x86_64 target and neither on a 32-bit one, so shipping `__MINGW32__` alone would be a 32-bit toolchain's spelling on a target that is `_WIN64`. It carries the SAME `impliedSurface` DELIBERATELY rather than a weaker or empty one — the surface it promises IS the same POSIX-on-Windows layer, and a sibling claim that asserts less would be the softer of two spellings of one fact, which is exactly the shape this mechanism exists to refuse. ⚠ pe is x86_64-only today; the day a 32-bit pe target ships this row needs a per-target arm, not a wider one.
predefinedMacros.name: __MINGW64__

predefinedMacros.$comment: ★ `__MSVCRT__` NAMES THE MICROSOFT C RUNTIME **FAMILY**, NOT THE `msvcrt.dll` FILE — stated because DSS links UCRT ([[project_pe_ucrt_migration_arc_2026_08_03]]) and the spelling invites the opposite reading. 📄DOCUMENTED in mingw's own headers: `_mingw.h:226-228` derives `_UCRT` from `__MSVCRT_VERSION__` and treats it as an axis INDEPENDENT of `__MSVCRT__`, which gcc predefines for every mingw-w64 target (✔MEASURED here: it appears in `-dM -E` with no header included at all, so it is a COMPILER predefine, not a header one). The runtime it excludes is the ancient `__CRTDLL__`/`crtdll.dll`, which DSS is not. ★★ WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, ✔MEASURED: sqlite `src/test_fs.c:71` gates `#if !defined(_WIN32) || defined(__MSVCRT__)` → `<unistd.h>` + `<dirent.h>`, and gcc compiles that TU with **0** errors where DSS reported **38**. `impliedSurface` names the `_`-prefixed CRT spellings specifically, because those ARE the Microsoft-runtime surface — a claim naming only POSIX names would be equally true of a glibc target and would therefore check nothing about THIS one.
predefinedMacros.name: __MSVCRT__

impliedSurface.note: A TYPE spelling that expands to `long long`. It names a width, not a surface.
An inlining HINT spelling that erases to nothing; it selects no header and changes no name resolution.
A MinGW-shape attribute spelling that erases to nothing here. It selects no header and reaches no symbol; a declarator carrying it parses and is otherwise unchanged.
The underscore-single alias of `__declspec`; same erasure, same non-claim.
A calling-convention spelling that erases to nothing: pe64 has ONE convention (MS-x64), so the token is accepted and carries no ABI consequence and no header.
A calling-convention spelling that erases to nothing; see `__stdcall`.
A calling-convention spelling that erases to nothing; see `__stdcall`.

The Win32 SDK's convention macro, erased for the same reason as `__stdcall`. It appears in `<windows.h>` declarations but does not itself make any name visible, so it promises nothing the corpus could be checked against.

predefinedMacros.$comment: D-CSUBSET-COUNTER-MACRO-NOT-EXPANDED. `__COUNTER__` — a per-TRANSLATION-UNIT monotonically increasing decimal that advances ONCE PER EXPANSION, the gcc/clang facility every unique-name idiom is built on (`DSS_CAT(v_, __COUNTER__)`). ★★ IT IS A KIND AND NOT A `constant` ROW BECAUSE THE VALUE IS STATE: a constant spelling would expand to the same integer at every site, which is precisely the property the construct exists to NOT have — two uses in one TU would mint the same symbol and collide. The engine owns the count (`PredefinedMacroKind::Counter` in `materializePredefined`); this row owns the NAME and nothing else, so a language that spells it differently rebinds it here with no C++ change. ✔WHY IT IS WORTH THE ROW: MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD, a SINGLE `DSS_CAT(v_, __COUNTER__)` compiled CLEAN and minted a symbol literally named `v___COUNTER__` — the token was pasted as TEXT. That is a silent wrongness, not a refusal: it links, it runs, and only a symbol-table reader ever sees it. TWO uses collided into S0002+S0001, so the loud half was the accident of a duplicate, not a diagnostic anyone wrote. ✔THE NUMBERING AGREES WITH BOTH REFERENCES AND THE MEASUREMENT IS RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED: gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 all start at 0 and step by 1, and DSS does the same. Nothing observable SHOULD depend on the specific integer — the contract is uniqueness, not a value — but agreeing costs nothing and removes a reason for a real program's assumption to be surprised. ★ `impliedSurface` is `claims-nothing` with the `compiler-extension` reason, NOT `standard-defined`: ISO C does not mandate `__COUNTER__`, and this field is the one place where such a claim is auditable, so an approximate reason here would be a false claim in the audit itself.
predefinedMacros.name: __COUNTER__

preprocess.$fc15cComment: FC15c. `__has_include` (C23 6.10.1p4): tests header existence with the SAME resolution `#include` uses -- the angle delimiters are matched by TOKEN KIND (`hasIncludeAngleOpenToken`=LtOp / `hasIncludeAngleCloseToken`=GtOp), never the `<`/`>` bytes (agnosticism); the angle form maps `<stem>.json` on the system path (DSS ships JSON descriptors, e.g. `stdio.json`) so `__has_include(<stdio.h>)` agrees with `#include <stdio.h>`. `__has_c_attribute` (C23 6.10.1p4): reports the version int of a known standard attribute or 0; the lookup ignores leading/trailing `__` (so `__deprecated__` matches `deprecated`). The C23 standard attributes are 202311.
preprocess.$tfc82PragmaComment:
★★ TF-C82 (D-PP-PRAGMA-REGISTRY) -- `#pragma` (C 6.10.6) + `_Pragma` (C 6.10.9). WHAT THIS REPLACED: from FC15c until now a recognized `#pragma` was consumed and DROPPED in total silence, and the justification written right here was C 6.10.6p2 ('an unrecognized pragma may be ignored'). The license is real; the claim was not. MEASURED on macOS/arm64 with the harness's own recipe: of 189 sqlite corpus TUs, 15 REACH a pragma at all, and among the 112 reached lines are 40 `#pragma pack` across 5 TUs. `sys/fcntl.h`'s `#pragma pack(4)` region makes `struct log2phys` sizeof 20 / _Alignof 4; DSS computed 24 / 8 -- a wrong-ABI struct handed to a live `fcntl(F_LOG2PHYS)` syscall, arrived at through a chain every hop of which was already shipped (`__APPLE__` -> `os_unix.c` enables SQLITE_ENABLE_LOCKING_STYLE -> `<sys/file.h>` -> `<sys/fcntl.h>`). 6.10.6p2 licenses IGNORING a pragma; it does not license reporting nothing about one that silently relaid out memory.
★ THE REGISTRY IS THE POINT, NOT THE LOUDNESS. `pragmaEffects` makes an ignored pragma ignored BECAUSE A ROW SAYS SO, in config the user reads. `diagnosticsOnly` asserts a checkable thing -- 'this pragma's entire effect is to configure diagnostics of a compiler DSS is not, and DSS emits none of them' -- rather than leaving silence to be read as either 'we checked' or 'we never looked'. Anything matching NO row is LOUD (`unknownPragmaIsError`), and `unsupported` is loud too and UNSUPPRESSABLE, on the `#error` argument: a pragma with real translation semantics must not be silenceable into shipping the wrong layout.
★ THE ROW SET IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED -- BUT EVERY CENSUS IS RELATIVE TO A PROFILE, AND THIS ONE MISSED ONE. The TF-C82 REACHED census was taken with `clang -E` over all 189 TUs with the recipe's real defines/includes, ON macOS ONLY, and it reported: `clang diagnostic` 48, `pack` 40, `clang assume_nonnull` 24. It was written here as if that were universal (the words were: and NOTHING else), and THAT CLAIM WAS FALSE. `clang -E` on macOS cannot see MSVC-gated code -- it never defines `_MSC_VER` -- while DSS's **pe** profile DOES define it (`_MSC_VER=1943`). So the census covered the **macho** predefine class only; **elf** (which defines neither `_WIN32` nor `__APPLE__`) and **pe** were never instrumented. MEASURED at TF-C85 by re-running the real pe64 corpus leg through DSS itself: the pe class reaches 2135 MORE pragma lines that no row claimed -- `warning` 1685, `intrinsic` 448, `optimize` 2 -- and the pe64 build was BROKEN at 2135 error[P0020] across 113 of 189 TUs the whole time. ★ AND EVEN THAT NUMBER IS A FLOOR, NOT A TOTAL. A reached-set is a function of the manifest's defines and of how far each TU gets: `ext/rtree/rtree.c` carries two more `#pragma intrinsic` lines under the same `_MSC_VER` guard and contributes ZERO, because (MEASURED, by compiling that TU alone) its whole body sits in a not-taken `#if !defined(SQLITE_CORE) || defined(SQLITE_ENABLE_RTREE)` branch and C 6.10p1 makes an elided pragma entirely silent. A green build proves every pragma reached TODAY has a row -- never that the row set is complete. That is what the profile-census guard in the test suite exists to keep honest. `clang assume_nonnull` is in this table because it was MEASURED reached 24 times, not because it was predicted; it scopes NULLABILITY qualifiers DSS neither parses nor diagnoses, which is why `diagnosticsOnly` is a true statement about it. The `GCC system_header` / `mark` / `once` / `GCC poison` / `STDC` rows are present-in-the-SDK vocabulary that this corpus does NOT reach; they are declared anyway so the first TU that does reach one gets the row's considered answer instead of a bare unknown.
★ THE `pack` FORMS ARE MEASURED TOO. Reached spellings and counts: `pack()` 14, `pack(4)` 13, `pack(pop)` 6, `pack(push, 4)` 5, `pack(push, 1)` 1, `pack(1)` 1. So BOTH idioms are load-bearing -- the depth-less set/reset pair AND the push/pop stack -- and implementing only one is insufficient for this corpus. Bare `pack(push)` occurs 0 times in the whole SDK and the paren-less `pragma pack 8` form occurs twice (`ffi/ffi.h`, unreached); neither is built, and both fail loud rather than being guessed at.
★ AGNOSTICISM: every word here is CONFIG. The engine compares a pragma's leading tokens against these `prefix` arrays and never against a literal; deleting `pragmaDirective` restores the generic unsupported-directive fail-loud, deleting a row makes that pragma unknown, and setting `unknownPragmaIsError` false restores the pre-TF-C82 silent drop exactly. `toy.lang.json` declares none of it, so `_Pragma` is an ordinary identifier there.
preprocess.$mutuallyExclusivePredefinedMacrosCommen: ★★★ D-LANG-PE64-DEFINES-BOTH-MSC-VER-AND-GNUC — THE CO-DEFINITION PIN. Each row asserts that AT MOST ONE of `macros` may be EFFECTIVE for any one (language x target x format) triple, checked over the MERGED, already-format-filtered predefined-macro set — language + `<arch>.target.json` + `<name>.format.json` together — so a future TARGET or FORMAT that re-introduces the other name is refused exactly as a language row would be. The diagnostic NAMES THE OFFENDING OBJECT FORMAT, because the whole defect class is a pair that is individually legitimate and becomes contradictory only on the one leg where gating makes both live. ★ WHY THE RULE IS DECLARED HERE RATHER THAN BUILT INTO THE ENGINE: `_MSC_VER` and `__GNUC__` are C-DIALECT VOCABULARY, and a literal either one in shared substrate is exactly the source-language hard-coding the agnosticism bar vetoes. The engine enforces whatever groups it is handed and knows no macro name; `toy.lang.json` declares none and is unchecked. That is also this pin's RED-ON-DISABLE: delete the row below and the impossible identity is silently accepted again. ⚠ SHAPE is validated at LOAD (>=2 unique non-empty names, a non-empty `reason`), and a member is NOT required to EXIST — deliberately. A group is a PROHIBITION, and its most valuable use is naming a spelling DSS does NOT declare and must never start declaring again (which is precisely this row: `_MSC_VER` is declared by nothing now, and that is the point). Requiring every member to exist would make exactly that rule unstatable and could only be satisfied by re-adding the row the rule exists to keep out. What IS asserted, in the test suite where the whole target x format matrix is visible: at least one member of each group is real (non-vacuity), and no target x format co-defines any group. A typo in the ABSENT member cannot be caught by reading configs at all — it is caught by the red-on-disable test, which re-adds that exact spelling to the shipped text and requires this group to FIRE.

mutuallyExclusivePredefinedMacros.$comment: ✔MEASURED, Ubuntu clang 19.1.1 (`clang-19 -dM -E -x c /dev/null --target=<triple>`): `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` defines _MSC_VER/_MSC_FULL_VER/_MSC_EXTENSIONS/_WIN32/_WIN64/__clang__ and NOT __GNUC__ (clang SUPPRESSES __GNUC__ in MS-compatibility mode on purpose); `x86_64-w64-mingw32` defines __GNUC__/_WIN32/_WIN64/__clang__/__MINGW32__/__MINGW64__ and NOT _MSC_VER. DSS shipped BOTH plus _WIN32 on pe64 until this cycle, and sqlite's src/hwtime.h — whose FIRST arm is `#if defined(_MSC_VER) && defined(_WIN32)` — routed pe64 into `#include <profileapi.h>` and error[F001A] while the other four legs reached the __GNUC__ rdtsc / mrs cntvct_el0 arms. The pair is the canonical instance of the class: two identity claims that are each fine alone and cannot both be true.
mutuallyExclusivePredefinedMacros.reason: no reference compiler defines both: clang targeting x86_64-pc-windows-msvc defines _MSC_VER and deliberately suppresses __GNUC__, while clang/gcc targeting x86_64-w64-mingw32 defines __GNUC__ and not _MSC_VER (MEASURED, clang 19.1.1) — presenting the union is an identity no real toolchain can have, and every header that branches on the pair then takes an arm neither MSVC nor MinGW would take

preprocess.$tfc85OptimizeWordsComment: TF-C85: the `optimizerControl` region words. The engine owns the SEMANTIC (a lexically scoped per-function optimizer opt-out); config owns the WORDS -- a literal "off" in engine code would be an identity branch on source vocabulary, the same class of hard-coding `pragmaDirective` exists to prevent. OPTIONAL and INDEPENDENT: deleting either key makes every `#pragma optimize` form using it fail loud as unbuilt (never a silent no-op), which is this pair's red-on-disable pin.

pragmaEffects.$comment: Tunes clang/gcc WARNINGS. DSS emits none of them, so the whole effect is inert here -- a checkable claim, not an assumption. MEASURED reached 48x.
Suppresses gcc/clang warnings for the whole file. DSS has no such warning class.

Scopes NULLABILITY qualifiers (`_Nullable`/`_Nonnull`) and the -Wnullability-completeness warning. DSS neither parses nor diagnoses nullability, so nothing it does is affected. MEASURED reached 24x -- and reached via `_Pragma` inside a macro replacement list, which is why the operator spelling had to work.
An IDE navigation bookmark. No translation semantics in ANY compiler -- a stronger claim than diagnosticsOnly, hence its own verb.

MSVC warning control (`warning(disable: N)` / `push` / `pop` / `default: N` -- MEASURED, all FOUR payload shapes are reached, and ONE prefix row covers all four because the row makes NO claim about the argument list). Its entire effect is to tune warnings of a compiler DSS is not, and DSS emits none of them -- the `clang diagnostic` claim verbatim, on the other vendor's spelling. MEASURED reached 1685x on the `pe` leg (msvc.h:19-33 x 112 TUs + mutex_w32.c:40,41,64 + totype.c:439,504) and 0x on macho/elf, because the guard is `#if defined(_MSC_VER)` and only the pe profile defines it. ★ THE CONFOUND IS EARNED, not assumed: `totype.c:439` is `warning(disable: 4748)`, whose sole purpose is to silence the warning MSVC raises BECAUSE the very next line disables optimization. A warning about a warning has no translation semantics by construction.

MSVC `#pragma intrinsic(name, ...)` -- ASKS FOR A REALIZATION, NEVER FOR AN EXISTENCE. It requests that the listed names be expanded inline instead of called through the CRT; it does not declare them, does not change what calling them means, and cannot make a name available that otherwise is not. DSS chooses realization itself: a name it lowers as a builtin never becomes a CRT call, and a name it does NOT provide fails loud at the CALL SITE (S0001) whether or not this pragma was honored -- so ignoring it cannot mask a missing symbol. ★ THAT CLAIM IS ABOUT THE ENGINE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS SOUND FOR A PREFIX ROW: matching is by prefix, so this ONE row speaks for EVERY name the pragma can list, including names this implementation has never heard of. A per-name claim would be false the moment a new name appeared. MEASURED reached 448x on the `pe` leg (sqliteInt.h:312-315 x 112 TUs: `_byteswap_ushort`, `_byteswap_ulong`, `_byteswap_uint64`, `_ReadWriteBarrier`) and 0x on macho/elf. ★ DO NOT read this row as 'those four names all work' -- its truth does not depend on that, and that is exactly the point of the verb. ALL FOUR now ARE realized as always-on lowered builtins (`_ReadWriteBarrier` -> `lowering:barrier`; `_byteswap_ushort`/`_byteswap_ulong`/`_byteswap_uint64` -> `lowering:bswap`, D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP, closed 2026-07-31). ~~ A CLAIM THAT SAT HERE WAS FALSE AND IS RETRACTED: this row used to say the three `_byteswap_*` were 'unreferenced today only because SQLITE_BYTEORDER != 1234 #ifs out sqlite's fast path'. **SQLITE_BYTEORDER IS 1234 under DSS**, MEASURED end to end: x86_64.target.json:12 defines `__x86_64__` UNGATED -> sqliteInt.h:996-1002's `#elif defined(i386) || ... || defined(__x86_64__) || ...` arm fires -> `#define SQLITE_BYTEORDER 1234`. The fast path was never #if'd out. What actually selected the MSVC arm is the OTHER half of each `#elif` chain: `_MSC_VER`=1943 (line 78 above, pe-gated) clears sqlite's `MSVC_VERSION>=1300`, while GCC_VERSION = __GNUC__*1000000 + __GNUC_MINOR__*1000 + __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__ = 4002001 (lines 67-71) MISSES both `>=4003000` (util.c:1850/1863, rtree.c) and `>=4008000` (btreeInt.h:741), so every `__builtin_bswap*` arm is DEAD and the chain falls through to the `_byteswap_*` arm. That is why ONLY the pe64 leg errored -- `_MSC_VER` is the pe-gated macro, so elf/macho fall through once more to the portable byte-by-byte `#else`. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE before the fix: exactly 3 `error[S0001] got _byteswap_*` on the pe64 testfixture (btreeInt.h:743 x1, util.c:1856+1869 x2), which is why the testfixture never linked and the Windows unit corpus could not run at all. ~~ ★ STILL TRUE AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: none of the four is a LINKABLE SYMBOL. msvcrt.dll exports no `_byteswap_*` (MEASURED, objdump -p, positive control memcpy/_msize/puts) and DSS eager-imports every name a descriptor's `symbols` lists, so declaring one there breaks the pe loader with 0xC0000139. Realize them as builtins; never as symbols.
REAL. C `#pragma pack` -- a lexically scoped MAXIMUM member alignment, threaded from the preprocessor into the composite layout channel. One of the two rows with a sink.

REAL. MSVC `#pragma optimize("", off)` / `("", on)` -- a lexically scoped PER-FUNCTION optimizer opt-out, threaded from the preprocessor (per-emitted-token stamps, the `pack` mechanism) onto SymbolRecord.isNoOptimize -> HirNoOptimizeMap -> MirFunc.noOptimize, where the optimizer's shared function rebuilder swaps the pass's policy for an IDENTITY policy (it never skips the rebuild -- skipping would DELETE the function) and the inliner refuses to splice in either direction. Only the EMPTY option string is built; a selective list (`"gt"`) names MSVC optimizations DSS does not have and FAILS LOUD rather than being widened or dropped. The `on`/`off` words are config (`pragmaOptimizeOnWord`/`pragmaOptimizeOffWord`), never engine literals. MEASURED reached 2x on the `pe` leg (ext/misc/totype.c:440 off, :505 on -- bracketing `torealFunc` and `tointegerFunc`) and 0x on macho/elf. ★ STATE ITS VALUE HONESTLY: this is FAITHFULNESS to a real MSVC contract, and it is what unblocks the pe64 corpus leg. It is NOT a fix for a live floating-point miscompile. MEASURED in this tree, NO shipped release pass can perturb float arithmetic -- const_fold's fold maps are integer-only (zero FAdd/FMul/FDiv/FCmp/SIToFP arms), there is no reassociation pass, no FMA/fast-math anywhere, and `double` is SSE2 at exactly 64 bits (x87 is F80-only) -- so totype.c's actual hazard, x87 excess precision, structurally cannot occur here.

★★★ BUILT 2026-08-29 (D-PP-PRAGMA-RECOGNIZED-SEMANTICS) -- THIS VERB NOW HAS A SINK, AND THE PARAGRAPH BELOW IS KEPT ONLY AS THE AUDIT TRAIL OF WHAT IT USED TO MEAN. `#pragma once` is HONOURED: `SynthBuilder` keeps a TU-wide include-once SET keyed on `core::PathIdentity`, the REACHED pragma records this file in it, and a later `#include` naming the same file identity is SKIPPED instead of spliced. `applyPragma` is therefore SILENT on this verb -- not because the pragma is ignored, but because the include machinery already honoured it in the only phase that can (the splice happens before the macro pass runs). THE KEY IS IDENTITY, NOT CONTENT (operator ruling 2026-08-28): `./h.h`, `sub/../h.h` and a symlink all reduce to one key, while two byte-identical files at different paths stay TWO -- deliberately refusing a program WSL gcc compiles, because content-keying buys its extra acceptance by DROPPING TEXT. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-29 that a `#pragma once` inside a NOT-TAKEN `#if 0` must NOT fire (unanimous: WSL gcc 13.3.0, WSL clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0, MSVC 19.51.36252), which is why the recording arm is gated on the pre-scan's CONFIDENTLY-LIVE oracle. ⚠ ONE CELL OPEN: two HARD LINKS to one file are two `PathIdentity` keys and are NOT deduped -- three of four references dedup them (MSVC does not), and closing it needs a filesystem FILE-INDEX identity in `core/substrate`. ~~ SUPERSEDED, kept verbatim: ~~ A genuine include-model directive DSS does not implement. STILL LOUD -- `includeOnce` is a REFINEMENT of `unsupported`, not an escape from it, and applyPragma refuses it exactly as before. TF-C87 split it out for ONE other reader: the include-guard detector behind guard-aware include RE-ENTRY (D-PP-INCLUDE-REENTRY-GUARD-AWARE). Re-entry into a header already on the include stack is now PERMITTED when the header carries a macro include guard (the guard makes the second expansion empty, exactly as in cpp); refused otherwise. A `#pragma once` header carries a REAL include-once mechanism that DSS cannot honour, so it needs its OWN refusal message -- distinct both from 'no guard detected' (which would be a false accusation and would send the user hunting a detector gap) and from the depth-cap backstop. Without this verb the detector would have to recognise the WORD `once`, i.e. an identity branch in shared substrate. MEASURED: 21 headers in the macOS 26 SDK carry `#pragma once`, 18 of them (AppleArchive/*) with NO macro guard at all, so this is a real population, not a hypothetical.
Makes an identifier an ERROR if used. Real semantics; ignoring it silently accepts code the header author forbade.

★★★ D-PP-PRAGMA-RECOGNIZED-SEMANTICS, 2026-08-29 — THE NINE C23 `standard-pragma` FORMS (6.10.8), ONE ROW EACH, BECAUSE THE JUDGEMENT IS PER-FORM AND CONFIG IS WHERE A JUDGEMENT BELONGS. Longest-prefix-wins does the operand VALIDATION for free: a valid `#pragma STDC <switch> <state>` matches its own three-word row, and anything else falls through to the one-word `STDC` row below and stays LOUD. So the whole operand vocabulary is DATA -- deleting a row makes that form loud again, and the engine never compares against a literal switch or state name.
★★ TWO VERBS, NOT ONE, AND THE SPLIT IS THE POINT. A single accepting verb would be FALSE for three of the nine forms, in the direction that ships wrong numerics silently. `standardFloatState` asserts DSS's behaviour SATISFIES the requested state; `standardFloatStateDiverges` asserts it does NOT, and buys an accepted-with-notice WARNING instead of either a silent accept or a refusal. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-29, each reference invoked separately: WSL gcc 13.3.0, WSL clang 18.1.3, mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0 and MSVC 19.51.36252 ALL accept ALL NINE forms rc=0 -- so refusing any of them is below the union and a conformance defect, which is why the previous single `unsupported` row was one.
★ EVERY VERDICT BELOW IS MEASURED AGAINST C23 N3220, NOT INFERRED. 7.12.2p2: FP_CONTRACT ON `ALLOWS` contraction -- a permission, never a requirement -- so never contracting satisfies ON as well as OFF; and MEASURED, zero FMA/contraction/fast-math/reassociation sites exist anywhere in src/{opt,mir,lir,hir,asm}. 7.12.2p2 and 7.6.1p2 both make the DEFAULT state IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED for those two pragmas, so DSS defining it as never-contract / fenv-unaware conforms by construction. 7.3.4p2 says CX_LIMITED_RANGE ON informs the implementation that `the usual mathematical formulas are acceptable`, which is exactly what DSS emits.

FENV_ACCESS OFF is the PERMISSIVE state -- 7.6.1 footnote 248 lets the translator assume flags are untested and default modes hold, which is what DSS does. DEFAULT is implementation-defined (7.6.1p2) and DSS defines it as OFF.

⚠ DIVERGES. 7.6.1 footnote 248: this pragma exists to disallow `global common subexpression elimination, code motion, and constant folding` that could subvert flag tests. MEASURED, DSS's `isCseCandidateOpcode` excludes only terminators, Phi and side-effecting opcodes, so FAdd/FMul/FDiv ARE CSE candidates and an intervening call is no barrier. ⚠ NOT THE SAME CLAIM AS `unreachable`: `<fenv.h>` is not shipped (including it dies at F_ShippedHeaderNotFound) so the C-level facility is absent, but DSS has inline assembly as its own source language and a program can still change rounding modes. Not satisfied; merely hard to reach.

⚠ DIVERGES, AND `DEFAULT` DIVERGES FOR A REASON THE OTHER TWO PRAGMAS DO NOT SHARE. DSS lowers complex `*` and `/` with the usual algebraic formulas (`materializeComplexBinaryOp`; Annex-G infinity/NaN recovery is deferred at D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX-ANNEX-G), which is the ON-licensed behaviour. ★ Unlike FP_CONTRACT and FENV_ACCESS, 7.3.4p2 MANDATES the default -- `The default state for the pragma is off` -- so DEFAULT is NOT implementation-defined here and cannot be defined into conformance; it sits exactly where OFF sits. ⭐ CONSEQUENCE WORTH READING TWICE: a TU with NO pragma at all is also in the mandated `off` state, so D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX-ANNEX-G is a LIVE divergence for every program doing complex multiply or divide, independent of this row. ⓘ It is a WEAKER divergence than non-conformance: DSS defines neither `__STDC_IEC_60559_COMPLEX__` nor `__STDC_IEC_559_COMPLEX__` (MEASURED via --dump-predefined-macros), so Annex G's specific recovery algorithm is not normative for it -- 7.3.4 withholds the license without prescribing a replacement.

THE FALL-THROUGH, AND IT STAYS LOUD DELIBERATELY. Any `#pragma STDC` that is not one of the nine forms above -- an unknown switch (`NO_SUCH_THING`), a malformed state (`MAYBE`), or a LOWERCASE state -- lands here. ⚠ THE LOWERCASE CASE IS A MEASURED, DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: C23 6.10.8 spells the grammar `on-off-switch: one of ON OFF DEFAULT`, so `#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT on` is NOT a valid standard-pragma; MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 accepts it silently and clang 18.1.3 accepts it with `expected 'ON' or 'OFF' or 'DEFAULT'`. DSS REFUSES it. That is not below the union, because the union governs CORRECT constructs and this one is malformed by the grammar's own text -- 6.10.6p2 makes a non-standard STDC pragma undefined behaviour, and a malformed numerics request is precisely when guessing is worst. Deleting every row above restores the pre-2026-08-29 behaviour exactly: the whole `STDC` family loud and unbuilt.

preprocess.$fc179EmbedComment: FC17.9(h) C23 `#embed` (6.10.4) + `__has_embed` (6.10.1). `#embed "r"` resolves the QUOTED binary resource with the SAME search a quote-`#include` uses (self-dir first, then include dirs) and expands to the resource bytes as a comma-separated list of decimal `int` constants (0..255), spliced through the SAME product-token mechanism as `#`/`##` -- so the tokens are ordinary integer literals + commas the parser accepts in a brace initializer. `__has_embed` reports the C23 trichotomy NOT_FOUND(0)/FOUND(1)/EMPTY(2) (== the `__STDC_EMBED_*` macros above). CYCLE-1 SUBSET: the standard parameters (limit/prefix/suffix/if_empty + vendor) and the ANGLE form `<r>` and a macro-expanded argument are DEFERRED loud (D-PP-EMBED-{PARAMS,ANGLE,MACRO-ARG}); a resource above a ~16 MiB splice budget fails loud, never OOMs (the streaming boundary). `__has_embed` with any parameter clause answers NOT_FOUND(0) per C23 (the standard's own unsupported-signal, not an error). The angle delimiters are the SAME token KINDS as `__has_include` (hasIncludeAngleOpenToken/CloseToken), matched by KIND never the `<`/`>` bytes; the operator words are matched by TEXT, never a hard-coded spelling.
preprocess.$lineMarkerComment:
D-C-PREPROCESSED-INPUT-REFUSES-GCC-LINEMARKERS. The GNU LINEMARKER — `# 1 "file"` and its `# 1 "file" 1 3 4` flag form — is what `gcc -E` and `clang -E` WRITE where a `#line` would go. It is the SAME presumed-position facility as `#line` (the engine records both through one `recordPresumedPosition`, so `__LINE__`/`__FILE__` and every diagnostic position follow either spelling); only the surface differs, and the surface has no directive WORD, so its SHAPE is the recognizer and it needs a declaration of its own. Absent, a digit-led directive stays on the generic unsupported-directive fail-loud — the `pragmaDirective`/`embedDirective`/`lineDirective` opt-in model, unchanged for every other language.
★★ WHY IT IS WORTH THE ROW rather than the `-P` workaround: preprocessed input is how this project MEASURES its own front end against real-world headers, and `gcc -E -P` buys acceptance by DISCARDING exactly the file/line provenance a conformance census wants — every diagnostic then points into the expanded blob instead of at the header that wrote the line. It is also the shape every build system emits when it splits preprocessing from compilation (ccache, distcc, `make -E` pipelines).
★★ THE FLAGS ARE DECLARED, NOT SKIPPED, AND EVERY VALIDATION BELOW IS ONE THE REFERENCES THEMSELVES ENFORCE. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 over one `_GNU_SOURCE` TU (stdio + string + strings + a local header): gcc 13.3.0 emits 154 linemarkers, clang 18.1.3 and 19.1.1 emit 177, and between them the ONLY flag tails that occur are {}, {1}, {2}, {3}, {1,3,4}, {2,3,4}, {3,4} — no digit outside 1..4 and never both of 1 and 2. ✔BOTH references REFUSE `# 1 "f.c" 9` (an undeclared digit) and REFUSE `# 1 "f.c" 1 2`, which is why an unknown flag and an exclusive-group collision are LOUD here: that is matching them, not out-stricting them.
★ WHAT EACH FLAG MEANS TO DSS, DECIDED AND PINNED RATHER THAN DROPPED IN SILENCE. `enter-file`/`return-to-file` describe the include-STACK transition; DSS's presumed-position record is per ORIGIN BUFFER and a preprocessed TU is ONE buffer, so both mean the same thing to the record — the following lines come from the named file starting at the given number — and the pair is declared with a shared `exclusiveGroup` so that `1 2` together can be refused. ⚠ `system-header` is RECOGNISED AND CARRIES NO SUPPRESSION, and that is a UNIFORM POLICY rather than a hole in this directive: ✔MEASURED at HEAD, `src/` contains no system-header concept at ALL, so DSS already declines to suppress diagnostics inside an ordinary `#include <...>` header. A TU fed through `gcc -E` therefore reports exactly what DSS reports compiling the same headers directly — which is the property that makes a conformance census meaningful in the first place. ✔The flag DOES change reference behaviour (clang 19.1.1 warns `-Wunused-variable` in a region marked `1` and does not in one marked `1 3`), so this is a decision, not an oversight; if DSS ever gains a system-header posture, THIS row is what selects it, and the pin in tests/analysis/preprocess/test_preprocessor.cpp is what goes red when it does. `extern-c-linkage` is inert BY CONSTRUCTION, not by omission: a C front end has no second linkage to switch to.
⚠ THREE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES FROM `#line`, each measured, each stated at `handleLineMarker`: line number ZERO is legal here (gcc's own `-E` output opens `# 0 "tu.c"` and gcc recompiles it rc=0) while C23 6.10.4p2 forbids it for `#line`; the file operand is REQUIRED here (all 331 measured linemarkers carry one) while `#line`'s is optional; and the tail is a declared flag vocabulary here while `#line` rejects any tail as junk.
preprocess.$errorWarningComment: D-CPP-ERROR-WARNING. C23 `#error` (6.10.5) + `#warning` (6.10.6): the AUTHORED-DIAGNOSTIC directives. A REACHED `#error` emits P001E at Error severity (6.10.5p1 is a CONSTRAINT -- the implementation shall diagnose, and the code is in the unsuppressable closed table because an `#error` is the header author's deliberate abort); a reached `#warning` emits P001F at Warning severity and translation CONTINUES (suppressible, the ordinary advisory posture). The message carries the directive's `pp-tokens` VERBATIM: the operand is NOT macro-expanded (gcc/clang agree -- it is prose, not an invocation site) and is OPTIONAL per the grammar's `pp-tokens_opt`, so a bare `#error` with no message is well-formed and still fires. ★ REACHABILITY, not recognition: both arms sit BELOW the preprocessor's dead-branch gate (the `#pragma`/`#embed`/`#line` parity), so an `#error` in a NOT-TAKEN `#if` branch is entirely SILENT per C 6.10p1 -- load-bearing, since the Apple SDK headers guard unsupported configurations with exactly that shape. Both words are OPTIONAL and matched by TEXT: deleting a key restores the generic unsupported-directive fail-loud (P0015), and rebinding it rebinds the feature -- the engine never hard-codes `error`/`warning`.

$closingDelimiterTokenComment: D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: every `coalesce: true` body mode declares `defaultToken.closeToken` — the token KIND the tokenizer emits for the mode's CLOSING delimiter (`"` / `'` / `>`). Before this the closer was consumed with NO token at all, so the CST simply had no node for a byte that is part of the literal's source extent (a span/round-trip hole, and nothing downstream could tell a properly-closed literal from an EOF-truncated one at the tree level). The closer MUST be a DISTINCT kind from `defaultToken.kind`, never the body kind reused — the loader rejects `closeToken == kind` fail-loud. WHY that is not a style preference: `decodeAdjacentStringBodies` (core/types/string_literal_decode.hpp — THE single chokepoint every string-body consumer routes through, semantic typer AND HIR lowering alike) selects its segments by FILTERING the rule node's children on `tokenKind == bodyTokenKind`. Give the closer the body kind and it becomes just another matching child: `"abc"` decodes as the segments `abc` + `"` = `abc"`, ONE byte too long, and `"a" "b"` as `a"b"`. The corruption is SILENT and UNGUARDED — the semantic tier types the literal `Array<Char, N+1>` from that same over-long decode and the HIR tier lowers the same bytes through the same chokepoint, so both tiers AGREE on the wrong length and every cross-tier consistency guard passes. The failure would only ever surface as wrong data in a compiled binary. A distinct `StringEnd`/`CharEnd`/`HeaderEnd` kind makes the filter structurally exclude the delimiter instead of relying on a decode-time heuristic. Consequence for the GRAMMAR: every shape that spelled the opener+body pair must now also spell the closer (includeQuoteTarget / includeAngleTarget / charLiteralExpr / stringLiteralExpr — the last in BOTH its head sequence AND its adjacent-concat repeat body), and cst_to_hir's linkage-specifier scan must ignore `StringEnd` by kind (see the declarations rows' linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds). NON-coalesced body modes (line-comment / block-comment here, tsql's per-codepoint bracket-id) declare NO closeToken and are UNCHANGED — but UNCHANGED does NOT mean token-less, and it is worth being exact about why. On the per-codepoint path the closing delimiter IS consumed and emitted, like any other body codepoint and carrying the BODY kind (tokenizer.cpp, the endsAt arm: `r.advance(n); emit(Operator, bodyToken.kind, …)`). MEASURED: `/* … */` ends on a `CommentChar` token whose text is `*/` (NestedBlockCommentsDoNotNestPerCStandard, tests/tokenizer/test_tokenizer.cpp), and tsql's `[col name]` ends on a ninth `BracketIdChar` for the `]` (TsqlBracketIdScansToClosingBracket). A closer carrying the body kind is precisely the anti-pattern the coalesced path forbids — it is harmless HERE only because these bodies are off-grammar `EmptySpace` trivia that no kind-filtering decoder ever reads, NEVER because the delimiter went unemitted. The one genuinely token-less closer in this config is `line-comment`'s, and for an unrelated reason: the `//` opener declares `stringStyle.endsAtExclusive`, so the terminating newline is LEFT IN PLACE for the main scan to re-lex as its own Newline token (c22 / D-PP-LINE-COMMENT-BEFORE-DIRECTIVE). What these modes lack is a DISTINCT closer KIND, not a closer token.

directive.$comment: FC13: the line-scoped C-directive mode. `#` pushes it (popAtNewline -> auto-pops at the next newline so a malformed directive never leaks state into the following line). It is an INLINE override table that lists ONLY `include`; the tokenizer falls back to the GLOBAL table for every other lexeme, so `define`/`undef`, `"..."`, identifiers AND operators all lex normally. CRUCIALLY there is NO `<`-override here: a `<` inside a NON-include directive (e.g. `#define X 1<<2`) falls back to the global `<<`/`<` operators -- no longer catastrophically mis-lexed. The `include` override re-emits IncludeKeyword AND arms the header context (replaceMode -> header-context) so the FOLLOWING `<h>` opens a header path. Scoping the mode-switch to THIS mode (rather than to the global `include` keyword) means a bare `include` identifier at main depth never triggers a replaceMode (which would abort at main-mode depth) -- it just lexes as IncludeKeyword with no side-effect.

header-context.$comment: FC13: armed by the `include` keyword (replaceMode). An INLINE override table lists ONLY `<`; the tokenizer falls back to the GLOBAL table for every other lexeme, so `"h"` still opens the quote-string body and identifiers lex normally. The ONE override is `<` -> HeaderStart (replaceMode -> header-body, stringStyle.endsAt `>`). The override-first longest-match rule means `<` wins at length 1 and the global `<<`/`<=` are deliberately suppressed inside an include header context -- correct, since `#include <<x>>` is not valid C. popAtNewline guards a malformed `#include` with no header.

$fc2CastExprComment: FC2 Part A: C-style cast `(type)expr` (castExpr/castTypeRef/castTypeBase/castOperand shapes). castExpr shares the `( ... )` opener with compoundLiteralExpr/parenExpr inside the speculative operand alt; the probe disambiguates structurally (a brace-init follows the compound literal's `)`, an expression follows the cast's). `commitRequiresTypeName` names the type-position child rule: a structurally-successful probe COMMITS only per the parser's GENERIC type-name triage — (1) a type that is NOT a lone Identifier (keyword/struct-tag/star/const present) always commits, those forms cannot be expressions; (2) a lone Identifier the binder sketch knows as a TYPE commits; (3) one it knows as a VALUE rolls back to the value reading (shadowing-aware); (4) an UNKNOWN lone Identifier commits iff the token after the type's closer is NOT an infix/postfix/ternary operator per the operator table (the value reading could not continue), else rolls back AND records an AmbiguousTypeNameCandidate for the compilation-unit oracle's one-shot reparse (cross-file typedefs). castTypeRef duplicates typeRefAllowingStruct PLUS a bare-Identifier base (typedef names in cast position). NOTE (FC7 D-FC7-NESTED-STRUCT-FIELD): typeRefAllowingStruct ITSELF now also carries the bare-Identifier alt — but it is consumed ONLY by structField/unionField, and a struct/union body has NO expression-statement production, so the C decl-vs-expr ambiguity (`T x;` vs `a * b;`) cannot arise there (a bare name in field-type position is unambiguously a type; a non-type fails loud at semantic scope-lookup). varDecl/param do NOT use typeRefAllowingStruct — they use declHead/declHeadForParam with the binder-sketch `commitRequiresTypeName` commit — so the statement/param decl-vs-expr triage is untouched by that alt. castOperand is a second expr-entry rule re-entering the Pratt walker at PREFIX precedence (90): the cast operand binds prefix + postfix operators but NOT binary/ternary ones, giving C-correct `(int)a + b` == ((int)a)+b, `(int)x[2]` == (int)(x[2]), `-(int)x`, and `(int)(long)x` chains. Same wrapper vocabulary as `expression` (wrapper rule names are per-schema; the loader dedups).
$ff11AngleIncludeComment: FF11 angle-include lexing (FC13 mode structure). `#` pushes the line-scoped `directive` mode (popAtNewline:true -> auto-pops at the next newline, so a malformed `#include` -- or any directive -- never leaks state into the following line; C directives are line-oriented). CRUCIALLY `directive` no longer overrides `<`: the ONLY override there is `include` (-> IncludeKeyword + replaceMode to `header-context`), so a `<` in a NON-include directive (e.g. `#define X 1<<2`) falls back to the global `<<`/`<` operators -- no longer mis-lexed as a header opener (the headline FC13 lexer fix). The `<`-OPENS-a-header-path override moved DOWNSTREAM to `header-context` (armed by `include`): there `<` -> HeaderStart (replaceMode -> header-body, stringStyle.endsAt `>`), while `"h"` still opens the quote-string body. The override-first longest-match rule (language-config-spec section 9.6) makes `<` win at length 1 inside `header-context` so `<<`/`<=` are suppressed THERE only -- correct, since `#include <<x>>` is not valid C. The `header-body` mode mirrors the `string` body: a coalesced `HeaderPath` captures the raw path bytes between `<` and the closing `>` (which pops back to main); escapeKind:none. D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: that closing `>` is NO LONGER token-less — `header-body` declares `defaultToken.closeToken: HeaderEnd`, so it emits its own leaf and `includeAngleTarget` spells it (see $closingDelimiterTokenComment). It changes nothing for path RESOLUTION, which reads the raw source slice off the `<` opener's span rather than any child index. The quote form keeps the global `"`->StringStart->string body unchanged (both `#include <h>` and `#include "h"` work). The resolver reads the raw path slice (a filename, not a decoded string) for both forms, and picks the search path by which token kind it finds under the directive (imports.pathToken=StringStart -> self-dir+includeDirs; imports.systemPathToken=HeaderStart -> shippedLibDirs).

//.$endsAtExclusiveComment: c22 (D-PP-LINE-COMMENT-BEFORE-DIRECTIVE): a `//` comment ends AT the newline but EXCLUDES it — the newline must survive as its own Newline token, else a directive on the next line after `code // comment` loses its line boundary and the preprocessor fails to recognize it (firstOnLine sees the comment-consumed newline as a body char, not a boundary).

L\".$comment: C11/C23 6.4.5 wide string `L"…"`. A multi-char lexeme so the tokenizer's longestMatchInMode beats the bare `L` identifier run; pushes the SAME shared `string` mode as `"` (one coalesced StringLiteral body). Its element core (wchar_t) is FORMAT-keyed in semantic (D-FFI-STDDEF-WCHAR-PE-WIDTH), so hirLowering.stringLiteralPrefixes carries only a placeholder for it.

u\".$comment: C11/C23 6.4.5 char16_t string `u"…"` → UTF-16 code units (U16). Same shared `string` mode as `"`; longestMatchInMode makes `u"` beat the `u` id-run.

U\".$comment: C11/C23 6.4.5 char32_t string `U"…"` → UTF-32 code units (U32). Same shared `string` mode as `"`.

u8\".$comment: C11/C23 6.4.5 UTF-8 string `u8"…"` → UTF-8 bytes (char8_t=Char-width). longestMatchInMode makes `u8"` (3 bytes) beat both the `u8` id-run and the `u"` opener. Same shared `string` mode as `"`.

L'.$comment: C11/C23 6.4.4.4 wide char constant `L'x'` (wchar_t). A multi-char lexeme so the tokenizer's longestMatchInMode beats the bare `L` identifier run; pushes the SAME shared `charBody` mode as `'` (one coalesced CharLiteral body). Its element core (wchar_t) is FORMAT-keyed in semantic (D-FFI-STDDEF-WCHAR-PE-WIDTH), mirroring the wide-STRING `L"` opener.

u'.$comment: C11/C23 6.4.4.4 char16_t constant `u'x'` → one UTF-16 code unit (U16). Same shared `charBody` mode as `'`; longestMatchInMode makes `u'` beat the `u` id-run.

U'.$comment: C11/C23 6.4.4.4 char32_t constant `U'x'` → one UTF-32 code unit (U32). Same shared `charBody` mode as `'`.

u8'.$comment: C23 6.4.4.4 char8_t constant `u8'x'` → one UTF-8 code unit (U8, must be ≤ U+007F). longestMatchInMode makes `u8'` (3 bytes) beat both the `u8` id-run and the `u'` opener. Same shared `charBody` mode as `'`.

keywords.$comment: P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): the GNU `__extension__` prefix. It is RESERVED unconditionally on the same argument the dunder qualifier spellings and `asm` already ride: C 7.1.3 reserves the `__` namespace to the implementation, and DSS declares GNU mode (it defines `__GNUC__` and does NOT define `__STRICT_ANSI__` — see the `asm` row for that measurement). ⚠ It is the ONE dunder word in this table that is NOT an alias of an existing kind: `__volatile__`/`__const`/`__inline__` are SPELLINGS of a specifier, but `__extension__` occupies grammar positions no specifier occupies (a declaration PREFIX, and a unary EXPRESSION prefix) and is refused in the positions a specifier holds — `static __extension__ int g;` is rejected by gcc AND clang ✔MEASURED. Hence its own kind and its own four rules, not a row in `singleDeclSpecifier`.

P31 (2026-08-24): the three GNU COMPILE-TIME builtins, and the reason none of them is a `builtinFunctions` row is the same for all three — that table declares CALLS, whose arguments are values with types, and these have no argument list at all. `__builtin_offsetof(struct S, b)` opens with a TYPE-NAME and continues with a member DESIGNATOR that names nothing any scope an expression can see contains; `__builtin_types_compatible_p` takes two type-names; `__builtin_choose_expr` discards one operand UNEVALUATED. They are OPERATORS wearing a call's punctuation, so they are grammar rules in the `operand` alt beside `sizeof`, `_Alignof` and `_Generic` — where every other operator of that shape already lives. All three sit in C 7.1.3's implementation-reserved `__` namespace, so reserving the words cannot collide with a conforming program (the argument the dunder qualifier spellings already ride on).

[[D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-SPELLING]] closed 2026-08-17 — the BARE spelling, and it is a keyword UNCONDITIONALLY rather than behind a mode gate. ★★★ THE MEASUREMENT THAT DISSOLVED THIS ROW'S BLOCKER, AND IT IS ABOUT DSS, NOT ABOUT gcc. The row (and $gnuDunderSpellingsAreUnconditionalComment below) refused this word because `asm` is keyword-or-identifier depending on ISO-vs-GNU STANDARD MODE and DSS has no `-std=` axis to hang that on — so there was said to be nowhere to put a mode-conditional reserved word. TRUE, AND IRRELEVANT: nothing here is mode-conditional, because DSS DOES NOT HAVE TWO MODES. It has one, it is GNU, and it already SAYS SO in the machine-readable way gcc and clang themselves say it. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-17, `<cc> -dM -E -x c /dev/null`, gcc 13.3.0 / clang 18.1.3 / clang 19.1.1: `__STRICT_ANSI__` is defined by all three under `-std=c17` and by NONE of them under `-std=gnu17` or in their DEFAULT mode — it IS the ISO-mode flag. ✔MEASURED against the shipped DSS CLI with a `#error` probe carrying a POSITIVE CONTROL that fired (`P001E`): DSS defines `__GNUC__` and `__clang__` and does NOT define `__STRICT_ANSI__`. ⇒ DSS declares GNU mode, so the word is unconditionally reserved here exactly as it is unconditionally reserved in `gcc` with no flags. No standard-mode axis was introduced, and none is needed; had one been built it would have been a second, contradictable owner of a fact this config already declares.
★★ WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG BEFORE, AND IT WAS WRONG IN **BOTH** DIRECTIONS — which is the half the old note missed by only ever asking what reserving the word would COST. ✔MEASURED across gcc 13.3.0 / clang 18.1.3 / clang 19.1.1 × `c17`/`c23`/`gnu17`/`gnu23`, every arm carrying a positive control (`__asm__`, accepted everywhere) and a negative control (`__asm__zz`, rejected everywhere): in GNU mode all three ACCEPT `asm("movl $42, %0" : "=r"(x))` and all three REJECT `int asm = 7;` (`expected identifier or '('`); in ISO mode the two answers swap exactly. They are complementary, never both. DSS did the OPPOSITE of GNU mode on BOTH: it refused the asm statement (`P0002 expected 'ParenClose' — got ':'`) and it ACCEPTED `int asm = 42;` and even `static int asm(int)` at rc=0. So leaving this row out was never the neutral option the old note treated it as — it was a live divergence in the identifier direction too, and only ADDING the word fixes both halves at once [[feedback_reference_compilers_are_the_spec]].
★ WHY `contextual: true` — the shipped soft-keyword facility (`reservedWordPolicy`/`contextualKinds`, used by tsql-subset) — WAS CONSIDERED AND IS **WRONG HERE**, recorded so it is not re-proposed as the safer option. It would accept `asm(…)` AND `int asm = 7;`, i.e. a COMBINATION no reference compiler accepts in any mode, which is the bidirectional defect restated rather than avoided. It also buys a construct whose meaning depends on POSITION: with `int asm(int);` declared, the statement `asm(42);` would resolve as an asm statement while the expression `x = asm(42);` would not. A clean reservation refuses that program in one place instead of silently meaning two things.
⚠ NOT A NEW MECHANISM: this is the same many-words-one-kind facility as `inline`/`__inline`/`__inline__` above and the ten dunder qualifier aliases — every consumer keys off `AsmKeyword`, never off a spelling, so the bare word reaches `asmStmt`'s keyword role AND the after-declarator `asmLabel` rule (`int f(void) asm("_myname")`, which gcc/clang also accept bare in GNU mode) with zero grammar and zero C++.

[top level deliberately — but ⚠ THE REASON THIS BRACKET USED TO GIVE WAS OVERTAKEN, AND IS CORRECTED HERE 2026-08-12. tokenClasses.$attributeClauseNameComment:
★★ D-C-ATTRIBUTE-CLAUSE-NAME-ADMITS-ONLY-IDENTIFIER-SO-A-KEYWORD-NAMED-ATTRIBUTE-IS-REFUSED — THE SINGLE TOP PARSE BLOCKER FOR REAL GLIBC HEADERS, and it is one declaration read by TWO tiers rather than two lists that can drift.
★ WHAT IT ADMITS AND WHY THAT EXACT SET: an attribute clause NAME may be an ordinary identifier (`deprecated`, `__nothrow__`, `format`) OR any word this document's own `keywords` table claims — because glibc writes `__attribute__ ((__const__))`, whose name lexes as `ConstKeyword`, not as `Identifier`. ✔MEASURED (P31 lane G, re-measured P32 lane A): ONE `gcc -E -P` TU of `_GNU_SOURCE` stdlib/string/strings/math/byteswap/sched carries 50 occurrences of that ONE spelling, and neutralising it alone took the TU from 50 parse errors to 0.
★ `allKeywordKinds` DERIVES the keyword half from the `keywords` array above rather than listing dunder spellings, and that is the whole design: add a keyword to this language and this class grows with it, in the same edit, with no second place to remember. A hardcoded set of `__x__` spellings is exactly the drift this key exists to make impossible.
★★ THE REFERENCES DISAGREE AND THE DISJUNCTION RULE DECIDES IT. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 against BOTH, one TU per word, with a positive control: clang 19.1.7 accepts EVERY reserved word tested as an attribute name in BOTH the GNU and the `[[…]]` spelling (warning `-Wunknown-attributes`, exit 0); gcc 13.3.0 accepts them all in the `[[…]]` spelling but REFUSES a large subset in the GNU spelling — `sizeof`, `typeof`, `__typeof__`, `_Alignof`, `__alignof__`, `struct`, `union`, `enum`, `return`, `if`, `else`, `while`, `for`, `do`, `switch`, `case`, `default`, `break`, `continue`, `goto`, `_Generic`, `_Static_assert`, `true`, `false`, `nullptr`, `alignas`, `alignof`, `static_assert`, `typeof_unqual`, `__attribute__`, `__extension__`, `__asm__` — while accepting `const`/`__const__`, `volatile`, `int`, `static`, `restrict`, `inline`, every type and storage keyword, `_Bool`, `_Complex`, `_Atomic`, `_Noreturn`, `_Thread_local`, `bool`, `constexpr`, `thread_local` and `__int128`. ⚠ THE REGISTRY ROW'S FIGURE WAS NARROWER THAN THE TRUTH (it named four gcc refusals); the CONCLUSION is unchanged, because §A.3b takes the union of what any reference accepts and clang's set is the superset. Do NOT narrow this class to gcc's GNU-spelling list in the name of strictness — that would refuse code clang compiles.
★★ ONE CLASS, TWO CONSUMERS, AND THE LOADER REFUSES A HALF-MOVE. The grammar names it at the clause-name position (`attrSpec`, `attrClauseTail`, `stdAttrItem`); `semantics.attributeSemantics.clauseNameTokenClass` names it for the READER (`isAttrClauseNameToken`, which every clause-name scan in the semantic tier now routes through). Move only the grammar and `__attribute__((__const__))` parses, matches no effect row and DISAPPEARS — a silently dropped attribute, strictly worse than the parse error it replaced. Move only the reader and the extra reach is dead config. The loader's Clause-C drift guard emits C_InvalidSemantics for BOTH directions, so neither can ship.

Read $p42wSpeculativeComment for the measurement, the cost, and the disjoint-FIRST restructuring that was tried and refuted. struct/union/enum heads route to topLevelDecl (via topLevelHead's body/ref specifier forms) — the bare top-level structDecl/unionDecl/enumDecl rules were folded into topLevelDecl (optional declarator) so a `struct` lead has ONE owner here and only topLevelHead's single-level speculation runs (the two-level topLevel-speculation path was unsound — D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-BODY-VARDECL-POSITION). Those three now-unreferenced rules (+ their semantics/hirKind/scopes rows) were DELETED in the closing cycle (no dead config); the shared structField/unionField/enumerator helpers stay (the *SpecifierBody forms consume them). c81: `emptyStmt` (a lone `;`) is admitted as an external declaration — sqlite shell.c's `SQLITE_EXTENSION_INIT1;` expands EMPTY in the static-shell build, leaving a stray file-scope semicolon (x2, base64.c/base85.c sections) that gcc/clang accept (-pedantic warns; C 6.9 formally disallows it, but accepting it is the universal implementation posture). REUSES the statement-position `emptyStmt` rule exactly as c30 reuses `typedefDecl` in both positions: FIRST = {EndStatement}, disjoint from every other alt -> unique-production direct descent, and STILL no probe after P42 marked this alt speculative (the prune leaves exactly one candidate, so the speculative path takes the direct descent); its existing `hirKind: Skip` row lowers it to nothing in BOTH positions (the includeDirective->Skip top-level precedent), so no semantics/scopes row is needed.
topLevel.$p31ExtensionComment: P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): `extensionTopLevel` joins the alts — the FILE-SCOPE half of the GNU `__extension__` prefix. FIRST = {ExtensionKeyword}, DISJOINT from every other alt (a distinct exact-match keyword), so the choice stays predictively decidable at one token; P42 marked this alt `speculative: true` for an unrelated pair, and `__extension__` is unaffected -- its lone candidate still direct-descends with no probe. See `extensionTopLevel` for why `__extension__` is a DECLARATION PREFIX and not a declaration specifier.
topLevel.$p42wSpeculativeComment: P42 (D-CSUBSET-LEADING-ATTRIBUTE-BEFORE-TYPEDEF-IS-A-PARSE-ERROR): the WHY behind the `speculative: true` the paragraph above states. `typedefDecl` gained the LEADING attribute position (see `typedefDeclSpecifiers`), so FIRST(typedefDecl) now contains {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen} and OVERLAPS FIRST(topLevelDecl). ★★ THIS IS THE CONFIG SYSTEM'S OWN PRESCRIBED ANSWER, NOT AN INVENTED MECHANISM: `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` REFUSES an overlapping NON-speculative alt at load (C_AmbiguousAlternatives) and its own text names the two resolutions — restructure the grammar, or opt in to backtracking here. Restructuring was measured and REJECTED: the only shape that keeps the FIRSTs disjoint moves the leading attribute run OUT of `topLevelDecl`'s `declSpecifiers`, and that subtree is exactly what `specifierPrefixChild` hands to the linkage scan — so `__attribute__((weak)) int gv;` would parse and SILENTLY LOSE its weak binding. Trading a loud parse error for a silent linkage drop is the opposite of the fix. ⚠ THE COMMON PATH IS UNCHANGED AND THAT IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS IS AFFORDABLE: every other lead token (`typedef`, `int`, `static`, `struct`, `extern`, `__extension__`, `#`, `;`) has a UNIQUE 1-token FIRST, so the predictive prune leaves exactly ONE candidate and the parser takes the UNIQUE-PRODUCTION DIRECT DESCENT — no probe, no checkpoint, the same work as before. Only an attribute-led external declaration probes, and it probes at most twice (declared order: `typedefDecl` first, then `topLevelDecl`). ✔MEASURED: `__attribute__((weak)) typedef int T;` and `[[deprecated]] typedef int T;` were `error[P0009] expected 'Identifier', … — got 'typedef'` and now compile and run; gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=c2x`) and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c23`), probed SEPARATELY, both accept them (gcc/clang warn `attribute ignored` for `weak`, and BOTH are silent for `deprecated`).
topLevel.$p53ExternMergedComment: ★★★ P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): `externDecl` IS GONE FROM THIS ALT, and that removal is the fix — not a tidy-up. C 6.7.1 makes the declaration specifiers an UNORDERED SET, so `inline extern int p(int){…}` must parse exactly like `extern inline`; gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and MSVC 19.51.36252 accept all twelve orderings (probed SEPARATELY 2026-09-02) and `nm` shows the two orders emit the IDENTICAL `T p`, so they do not merely parse alike, they MEAN the same external definition. ★★ TWO DECLARATION BRANCHES ON ONE LEAD TOKEN CANNOT BOTH WORK AT ANY ORDER — ✔MEASURED by P53 lane `ex`, and this is what closed the design space. The obvious repair (a specifier run BEFORE `ExternKeyword` inside `externSpecifiers`) was BUILT and it REGRESSES the compiler: a leading `{repeat}` is nullable, `computePredictivePrefixes` stops without recording, and both branches survive here — so `topLevelDecl` is entered through a SPECULATIVE PROBE whose budget is `lookahead x 16` = 128 tokens while the probe must swallow the whole function BODY. Worse, the parser's ALL-FAIL REPLAY re-parses the declared-LAST structural candidate NON-speculatively with no budget, so the ORDER of these alts decides which of the two overlapping readings survives a long body and the other one DIES: with `…topLevelDecl, externDecl…` a bare `inline` definition is parse-RED at 64 statements; with the pair swapped it is exactly INVERTED. ⇒ ONE OWNER PER LEAD TOKEN, and `ExternKeyword` now leads `topLevelDecl` alone (via `singleDeclSpecifier`). With no competing branch every lead has exactly one candidate and NOTHING probes — strictly better than before, not a trade (✔MEASURED clean at 512 body statements for `inline`, `inline static`, `inline extern`, `__inline extern`, `extern`, `extern inline`, `static inline`). ⚠ THE STRUCTURAL INVARIANT IS PINNED: `tests/analysis/syntactic/test_parser_decl_specifier_lead.cpp` asserts each specifier keyword leads EXACTLY ONE branch of this alt AND of `extensionTopLevel`'s inner alt — a repair that fixes only one leaves every `__extension__`-prefixed declaration on the probe, and glibc writes that prefix. ⓘ `externDecl` still exists and is still reachable — as a BLOCK item (`statement`), where `localDeclSpecifier` does not admit `extern` so it remains the unique owner of that lead.

extensionTopLevel.$comment:
P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD, GNU C 'Alternate Keywords'): `__extension__` prefixing a FILE-SCOPE declaration — `__extension__ typedef long long T;`, `__extension__ extern int ffsll(long long);`, `__extension__ static __inline int f(void){…}`, `__extension__ unsigned long long x;`. ★★ IT IS A PREFIX ON THE WHOLE DECLARATION, **NOT** A DECLARATION SPECIFIER, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A READING OF THE MANUAL. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24, gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 19.1.7, each case its own translation unit so no failure masks the next: `__extension__ static int g;` / `__extension__ long long g;` / `__extension__ typedef …` / `__extension__ struct S {…};` / `__extension__ int f(void){…}` ALL COMPILE AND RUN; `static __extension__ int g;` and `int __extension__ g;` are REFUSED BY BOTH (`expected identifier or '('`). Adding the word to `singleDeclSpecifier`'s alt — the shape this repository reaches for first, and the one every other GNU qualifier alias took — would therefore have ACCEPTED WHAT NO REFERENCE ACCEPTS in exactly two spellings. The wrapper shape is what the reference set actually is.
★ SELF-RECURSIVE rather than a `{repeat}` of the keyword, because that is what makes `__extension__ __extension__ typedef int T;` parse (✔MEASURED accepted by both) with no second construct: the prefix of a declaration is itself a declaration.
★ `includeDirective` and `emptyStmt` are DELIBERATELY absent from the inner alt: a `#include` never survives preprocessing to reach a parser alt, and `__extension__ ;` is a null declaration no reference accepts. Listing the four real declaration productions explicitly (rather than referencing `topLevel`) is a second owner of that list ON PURPOSE — the alternative over-admits, and this rule's whole point is that its admitted set is the MEASURED one.
★ NO hirLowering ROW AND NO semantics ROW: the keyword is a TOKEN child, so the wrapper's sole MEANINGFUL child is the inner declaration and `peelToCore` (the shared sole-meaningful-child peel every unmapped wrapper already rides) hands `lowerDeclInto` the real declaration node. `__extension__` is semantically transparent — gcc's own definition of it is 'suppress the pedantic diagnostic', and DSS has no pedantic diagnostic to suppress — so a transparent parse IS the complete implementation. Zero C++.

sequence.$p42wSpeculativeComment: P42 (D-CSUBSET-LEADING-ATTRIBUTE-BEFORE-TYPEDEF-IS-A-PARSE-ERROR): speculative for the SAME reason `topLevel` is, and by the SAME mechanism — `typedefDecl` now carries the LEADING attribute position, so its FIRST overlaps `topLevelDecl`'s here too and `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` refuses the non-speculative form (✔MEASURED: it named this shape and `statement` by pointer). This is the `__extension__ __attribute__((deprecated)) typedef int T;` composition; both prefixes are declaration prefixes and they nest, so the two alts must agree.
sequence.$p53ExternMergedComment: P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): `externDecl` LEAVES this inner alt for the same reason it leaves `/shapes/topLevel` — see that alt's `$p53ExternMergedComment` for the measurement. structMemberDeclSpecifiers.$tfc94Comment:
TF-C94 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE, GNU 6.34 'Attribute Syntax' — an attribute-specifier may precede the declaration-specifiers of ANY declaration, a struct/union member declaration included): the member prefix is now a RUN OF ALTERNATIVES (`structMemberDeclSpecifier`) rather than a run of `alignasSpec`, so the LEADING GNU form parses — `struct TclStubs { __attribute__((__noreturn__)) void (*tcl_Panic)(const char *, ...) …; }` (real witness `/opt/homebrew/opt/tcl-tk@9/include/tcl-tk/tclDecls.h:1893/:2024/:2185`, the `TCL_NORETURN1` macro from `tcl.h:116`). MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD: `error[P0009] expected 'Identifier', 'BlockClose', 'VoidKeyword', … — got '__attribute__'` at the member, plus two cascading `got '('` — the diagnostic pointed at the `#define`, the gap was at the USE site.
★ THE SHAPE IS THE `declSpecifiers`/`singleDeclSpecifier` AND `localDeclSpecifiers`/`localDeclSpecifier` PAIR, VERBATIM — a plural SEQUENCE wrapping a singular ALT — and reusing that shape rather than inventing one is the whole point. The prefix node keeps its rule NAME, so `specifierPrefix` on the structField/unionField rows, the decl_prefix_strip.hpp index strip, and `specifierPrefixChild` are all UNTOUCHED; the extra `structMemberDeclSpecifier` wrapper level is transparent because every prefix consumer (`firstAlignasSpecInPrefix`, `specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn`, `scanAttributeSemantics`→`collectAttrNodes`) is a BOUNDED DESCENDANT WALK over `visibleChildren`, never a fixed-child-index read — the same property `compositeAttr` already relies on.
★★ THE POSITION IS A STRICT SUPERSET OF THE ALREADY-SHIPPED TRAILING MEMBER SLOT, WHICH IS WHY OPENING IT CANNOT INTRODUCE A NEW SILENT DROP — the check `compositeAttrList`'s $packedStaysNoneComment demands of every new attribute POSITION, discharged STRUCTURALLY rather than name-by-name. `structMemberAttrList` (TF-C73) already reaches `scanAttributeSemantics` on the SAME declaration node via `declarationAttrSlotRules`, so both slots fold into ONE `declAttrFacts` and the TF-C93 decl-kind gate judges them identically (MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD: `struct S { int x __attribute__((noinline)); };` → `warning[S005F]`, the gate is already live for members). This slot is read by everything that one is, PLUS the three specifier scans that only ever look at a `specifierPrefix`: `specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn`, `specifierPrefixHasConstexpr`, `specifierPrefixHasInline`. More consumers, never fewer ⇒ every name in the effects table behaves the same or better here than in the shipped position. One attribute does not mean two things depending on which side of the declarator it is written.
★ `noreturn` IS THE NAME THAT MADE THIS POSITION WORTH OPENING, AND IT IS HONORED, NOT PARSED-AND-DROPPED. `specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn` reads THIS node (it cannot see the trailing slot at all — MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD, `struct S { void (*p)(int) __attribute__((__noreturn__)); };` compiled clean with the attribute discarded in SILENCE), and the sink gate was widened the same cycle from `isFnSig` to `isFnSig || isFnPointerType`, so the fact lands on `SymbolRecord.isNoreturn` for a POINTER-to-function declarator — the Tcl shape — exactly as it already did for a function declarator. See semantic_analyzer.cpp's `declHasNoreturn` apply.
★ `stdAttr` IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, so FIRST(structMemberDeclSpecifier) = {AlignasKeyword, AlignasLegacyKeyword, AttributeKeyword} — no BracketOpen. Disjoint from FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct) (type keywords / Identifier / const-volatile-atomic / struct-union-enum / typeof / _BitInt / __int128 / _Complex-_Imaginary), so the enclosing `{optional}` stays predictively decidable and NOTHING becomes speculative; and disjoint from the `BlockClose` that ends structBody/unionBody, so the member `{repeat}` still exits on one token. The C23 `[[…]]` leading-member form (which clang DOES accept and honor — MEASURED, `struct S { [[deprecated]] int x; };` warns at the use site) stays a LOUD parse error, unchanged from before this cycle: it is NAMED RESIDUE, not a silent gap, and it is the `structMemberAttrList` posture applied one position to the left.
structMemberDeclSpecifiers.$p31ExtensionComment:
P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): the MEMBER half of the GNU `__extension__` prefix — `struct S { __extension__ long long b; };` and `struct S { __extension__ union { … }; };`, both of which glibc's `bits/pthreadtypes.h` and `bits/atomic_wide_counter.h` write. The run's FIRST element became an INLINE `{alt}` admitting an `extensionRun`; the SINGULAR `structMemberDeclSpecifier` is UNTOUCHED, so the keyword is admissible ONLY in the LEAD position. ★ THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT: ✔MEASURED gcc 13.3.0 + clang 19.1.7 — `__extension__ __attribute__((aligned(4))) int x;` COMPILES in both; `__attribute__((aligned(4))) __extension__ int x;` and `_Alignas(8) __extension__ int x;` are REFUSED by both. Putting the keyword in the singular alt (the one-line change) would have admitted all four.
★ AN INLINE `{alt}` AND A `specifierPrefix`-INTERNAL WRAPPER, NEVER A WRAPPER AROUND `structField`: `structBody`'s $staticAssertMemberComment states the rule for this position — a named wrapper rule pushes each field one level down, 'the class of change that parses fine and then drops members in silence'. Everything added here lives INSIDE `structMemberDeclSpecifiers`, which is the declared `specifierPrefix` and is STRIPPED by decl_prefix_strip.hpp before positional-child counting, so `structField`/`unionField`'s `head:0, declaratorList:1` are byte-identical and `fieldChildren` still finds every field as a DIRECT child of the body.
★ FIRST(structMemberDeclSpecifiers) gains {ExtensionKeyword} — disjoint from FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct) and from the BlockClose that ends the body, so the enclosing `{optional}` and the member `{repeat}` both stay predictively decidable and NOTHING becomes speculative. The rule also stays NON-nullable (the lead alt is required), which is what keeps that `{optional}` decidable at all.

extensionRun.$comment: P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): one or more `__extension__` keywords, as the LEAD of a struct/union member's specifier prefix. A named rule (not an inline `{repeat}`) only so the lead `{alt}` above has a single branch to name; it emits a wrapper node INSIDE the stripped `specifierPrefix`, where every consumer is a bounded descendant walk over `visibleChildren` and no fixed-child-index read can see it. Carries no semantics and no hirLowering row — `__extension__` is transparent.

structMemberDeclSpecifier.$comment: TF-C94 + P31: the LEAD struct/union member declaration-specifier — a `__extension__` run (P31, LEAD ONLY — see `structMemberDeclSpecifierTail`), an alignment specifier (`alignas(16)` / `_Alignas(16)`) or a GNU attribute specifier (`__attribute__((…))`). The `singleDeclSpecifier` / `localDeclSpecifier` alt, restricted to what a MEMBER declaration can carry: no storage class (C 6.7.2.1p1 admits none in a specifier-qualifier-list), no `inline`/`_Noreturn`/`constexpr` (function/object specifiers with no member surface — they stay LOUD parse errors here, matching clang), and no `stdAttr` (see the parent rule's $tfc94Comment for the FIRST-set reason and for why the `[[…]]` member form is named residue). The alt branches have disjoint FIRST sets ({AlignasKeyword, AlignasLegacyKeyword} vs {AttributeKeyword}), so the enclosing `{repeat}` is predictively pruned — non-speculative, no probe budget.

structMemberDeclSpecifierTail.$comment:
P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): every member specifier AFTER the first. Identical to `structMemberDeclSpecifier` MINUS `extensionRun`, and that single difference is the whole point: `__extension__` is admitted ONLY as the LEAD of a member's specifier run. ✔MEASURED gcc 13.3.0 + clang 19.1.7 — `__extension__ __attribute__((aligned(4))) int x;` compiles in both, while `__attribute__((aligned(4))) __extension__ int x;` and `_Alignas(8) __extension__ int x;` are REFUSED by both.
★ THE SPLIT IS A PAIR OF RULES AND NOT AN INLINE `{alt}` IN THE LEAD SLOT, AND THAT IS A SHIPPED PIN'S DOING. An inline alt emits NO wrapper node, so the FIRST specifier would have become a bare `attrSpec` child of `structMemberDeclSpecifiers` while every later one stayed wrapped — one element meaning two different shapes depending on where it is written, which is the asymmetry this file rejects everywhere else. ✔MEASURED: it also reds `ParserCSmoke.StructMemberLeadingGnuAttributeRidesTheSpecifierPrefix` and `StructMemberLeadingAlignasStillRidesTheSamePrefix`, which pin exactly that shape. Keeping `structMemberDeclSpecifier` as the LEAD name leaves both pins passing untouched.
⚠ FIRST(structMemberDeclSpecifierTail) = {AlignasKeyword, AlignasLegacyKeyword, AttributeKeyword} — unchanged from what the run admitted before, so the enclosing `{repeat}` is still predictively pruned and nothing became speculative.

structField.$comment: c23 D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-MULTI-DECLARATOR: a struct/union field is a type-specifier HEAD + an OPTIONAL `structMemberDeclaratorList` (a comma-separated list of per-slot declarators sharing the head base type, e.g. `int *a, b[4], *c;` — C 6.7.2.1) + `EndStatement`. SUPERSEDES c10's single `{optional declarator}{optional bitfieldDeclSuffix}`: each slot (`structMemberDeclarator`) now holds its OWN `declarator` AND its OWN `bitfieldDeclSuffix` so `int a:3, b:5;` resolves each width per-slot. Routing the member through the SAME `declarator` every other position uses (params/locals/globals) makes a function-pointer member (`int (*f)(int);`) parse + type-derive identically; the array suffix (`int arr[3];`) lives inside the declarator's OWN directDeclarator suffix chain. The LIST is OPTIONAL to admit the `int ;` declares-nothing form; a single-slot list with absent declarator + present suffix is the anonymous bit-field (`int : 3;` / zero-width `int : 0;`); the over-admitted nameless non-bitfield forms FAIL LOUD at semantic composition (anonymous member must be a bit-field). C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): an OPTIONAL leading `structMemberDeclSpecifiers` (`alignas(N) …`) precedes the head — declared as the `specifierPrefix` (below) so it is stripped before the head:0/declaratorList:1 count.
structField.$tfc73AttrComment: TF-C73: an OPTIONAL `structMemberAttrList` after the declarator list carries `int x __attribute__((aligned(8)));`. It is a TRAILING optional, so `head:0` / `declaratorList:1` are byte-identical whether or not a member is decorated — see that rule's comment for why it must be a DIRECT child here rather than nested in the per-slot declarator.

bitfieldDeclSuffix.$comment: FC8 D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD: the `: width` suffix; the width is a constant-expression evaluated + range-checked against the field's integer type at semantic.
