structMemberDeclarator.$comment: c23 D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-MULTI-DECLARATOR: ONE slot of a struct/union member list — an OPTIONAL `declarator` (its OWN pointer/array/fn suffixes; the `*` binds PER-SLOT so `int *a, b;` is Ptr<int> then int) + an OPTIONAL `bitfieldDeclSuffix` (now INSIDE the slot so `int a:3, b:5;` resolves widths independently). The declarator is optional to admit an anonymous bit-field (`int : 3;` — absent declarator, present suffix). The engine's `memberDeclaratorRule` role descends to the inner `declarator` for name + type derivation.

structMemberAttrList.$comment:
TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): the AFTER-DECLARATOR member attribute run — `struct S { int x __attribute__((aligned(8))); };` (the SDK audit measured MEMBERS at 17.6% of all 204 `aligned` sites). Before this the shape did not parse in EITHER direction: `structMemberDeclSpecifiers` admits `alignasSpec` only, and no member position carried a trailing run, so it died on `P0001 expected 'EndStatement' — got '__attribute__'`.
★ WHY IT SITS ON `structField`/`unionField` AND NOT INSIDE `structMemberDeclarator`, which is where GNU's per-declarator binding would put it: `declarationAttrSlotRules` matches DIRECT visible children of the DECLARATION node. Nested one level deeper inside the per-slot declarator, this run would be structurally invisible to the scan and its attributes would parse and be SILENTLY DROPPED — a member decorated `aligned(16)` would lay out at its natural alignment with no diagnostic. Direct-child placement is what makes the slot reachable, hence honored, hence loud when unrecognized.
★ NON-NULLABLE (`compositeAttr` + `{repeat}`) under an `{optional}` — the `compositeAttrList` trailing-slot pattern, NOT the always-emitted `typedefAttrRun` pattern — precisely so it emits NOTHING when absent and `head:0` / `declaratorList:1` keep the values they have today in both the decorated and undecorated cases. An always-emitted node here would land at index 1 whenever the (optional) declarator list is absent — the `int ;` declares-nothing form — and `declaratorList:1` would then address an attribute run instead of the EndStatement it addresses today.
★ GNU `attrSpec` ONLY — the C23 `stdAttr` is DELIBERATELY excluded here, and the schema validator is what proved it must be. `structMemberDeclarator` is fully nullable ({opt declarator}{opt bitfieldDeclSuffix}), so `structMemberDeclaratorList` is nullable too and its FIRST leaks into whatever follows — including `BracketOpen` from the abstract array-declarator base (`int [3];`, the over-admitted nameless form). Adding `stdAttr` (FIRST `[[` → BracketOpen) made those two adjacent optionals share a 1-token lead and the loader REFUSED the schema: `C_AmbiguousAlternatives at /shapes/structField: alt branches share FIRST token 'BracketOpen'`. That is a genuine ambiguity, not a loader over-reach — `int x[[a]]` cannot be told from an array suffix at one token, and C23 only escapes it by treating `[[` as one token, which this tokenizer does not. Restricting the slot to `attrSpec` makes FIRST = {AttributeKeyword}, disjoint from every declarator lead and from the `EndStatement` that follows, so the `{optional}` is predictively decidable and nothing becomes speculative. `[[…]]` on a MEMBER is therefore named residue — loud, never silent.
RESIDUE (loud, never silent): a MID-LIST decoration (`int a __attribute__((aligned(8))), b;`) and a decoration before a bit-field `:` (`int x __attribute__((packed)) : 3;`) still fail loud, exactly as they do today — this slot admits the after-LIST position only.

structMemberDeclaratorList.$comment: c23 D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-MULTI-DECLARATOR: `structMemberDeclarator (, structMemberDeclarator)*` — mirrors `initDeclaratorList` for struct/union members. The engine's `memberListRule` role iterates the slot children (commas skipped).

structTypeRef.$comment: c25: the REF-ONLY struct specifier, kept for the param/cast positions (declHeadForParam, castTypeBase) where a struct type is a pure tag reference. The DECLARATION-head positions no longer use this pair-with-body form — they route through the UNIFIED `structSpec` (below), which folds body-vs-ref into ONE rule so it is the SOLE candidate for `struct` at those heads → the parser's unique-production direct descent parses the member body NON-speculatively (no probe, no token budget — the c25 fix for `struct sqlite3`).

structSpec.$comment: c25 D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER: the UNIFIED struct specifier (C 6.7.2.1 struct-or-union-specifier) — `struct {opt tag} {opt body}`. ONE rule for BOTH the type-DEFINITION form (`struct P { … }` — a `structBody` child is present) and the bare tag-REFERENCE form (`struct P` — absent). Replaces the former `structSpecifierBody | structTypeRef` SPECULATIVE pair in the 4 body-bearing declaration-head alts (topLevelCompositeSpec, typeSpecifierForDecl, typedefHead, typeBaseAllowingStruct). Because it is now the SOLE candidate keyed on StructKeyword in those alts, the parser's LL(k) unique-production DIRECT DESCENT (parser.cpp ~1804-1844) dispatches it NON-speculatively — the member list parses with NO speculation budget, so an arbitrarily large body (`struct sqlite3`) never trips the 4096-token probe cliff. The body-vs-ref split becomes an INTERNAL 1-token (`BlockOpen`) decision via the `{optional structBody}`, also non-speculative. The binder is DUAL-MODE on the SAME node (semantics: `definesWhenChild: structBody`): body present ⇒ the EXACT former `structSpecifierBody` define path (mint type, bind tag, open scope, compose fields from the `structBody` subtree); body absent ⇒ the EXACT former `structTypeRef` tag-reference path (isTagReference). FOLLOW-independent (the rejected D2): no prune of the ref candidate is needed because there IS no separate ref candidate here.
structSpec.$tfc73LeadComment: TF-C73: `compositeAttrLead` (ALWAYS emitted, even empty) sits after the keyword so `struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) T { … };` parses. Visible children are the FIXED [StructKeyword(0), compositeAttrLead(1), Identifier(2), structBody(3), compositeAttrList(4)] — the row's tag index moved 1 → 2 ONCE, deterministically, and cannot shift again with or without a decoration. See `compositeAttrLead` for why an always-emitted node under a DISTINCT rule name is the only shape that keeps the tag index and the trailing `packed` scan both correct, and for why this landed a cycle AFTER the consumer that makes it safe.

structBody.$comment: c25: the brace-delimited struct member list, factored OUT of `structSpec` so its PRESENCE is the define-vs-reference discriminator (the binder's `definesWhenChild`). NOT a scope rule itself: the fields bind into the scope opened by the enclosing `structSpec` (the analyzer's Pass-1.5 field collection walks that scope, not direct children, so the extra nesting level is transparent). Member shape identical to the former `structSpecifierBody` tail.
structBody.$staticAssertMemberComment:
TF-C101 (D-CSUBSET-STATIC-ASSERT-STRUCT-MEMBER — the trigger this row waited for has FIRED: Tcl 9.0 `tclDecls.h:4046` writes one, inside a `sizeof` type-name): C11/C23 6.7.2.1p1 gives `struct-declaration` TWO productions — `specifier-qualifier-list struct-declarator-list_opt ;` AND `static_assert-declaration` — so the repeat is over that 2-way choice, not over `structField` alone. Before this, a struct-body `_Static_assert` died `P0009 … got '_Static_assert'`.
★ AN INLINE `{alt}`, NOT A NEW NAMED RULE, AND THE REASON IS THE FIELD SCAN: an inline alt compiles to an AltChoice POSITION and emits NO wrapper node, so a `structField` stays a DIRECT child of `structBody` exactly as before and `semantics.declarations.structSpec.fieldChildren` (which names the rule `structField`) keeps finding every field. A named `structDeclaration` wrapper would have pushed each field one level down — the class of change that parses fine and then drops members in silence.
★ NON-SPECULATIVE: FIRST(staticAssertDecl) = {StaticAssertKeyword, StaticAssertLegacyKeyword} is DISJOINT from FIRST(structField) (the alignas keywords ∪ FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct)), so the choice is predictively decidable at one token and the member list still parses with no probe and no budget — the c25 property this body exists to preserve.
★ THE ASSERTION IS EVALUATED HERE, NOT MERELY ADMITTED. `staticAssertDecl` needs no new semantic wiring because the FC16 check (semantic_analyzer.cpp `pass2Post`, keyed by `semantics.staticAssertRule`) is NODE-based and runs on every node it visits, at any depth — so a member-position assertion is const-evaluated by the same `constIntExpr` that folds `sizeof(T)` in an array dimension, and a FALSE one fails loud `S_StaticAssertFailed` (pinned by StaticAssertFalseInStructMemberFailsLoud). Admitting the construct without that check would have been the silent hole: this macro's assertion is load-bearing, it is what enforces `sizeof(*boolPtr) <= sizeof(int)`.
★ `hirKind: Skip` already lowers a PASSED assertion to nothing in every position, so the member list's LAYOUT is untouched — the declaration mints no field.

unionField.$comment: c23 D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-MULTI-DECLARATOR: a union field mirrors `structField` — a type-specifier HEAD + an OPTIONAL `structMemberDeclaratorList` (per-slot declarators sharing the head, e.g. `int *a, b;`) + `EndStatement`. The per-slot `structMemberDeclarator` holds its own declarator (function-pointer-member support: `int (*f)(int);`) AND its own bitfield suffix. The array suffix lives inside the declarator's directDeclarator suffix chain. C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): an OPTIONAL leading `structMemberDeclSpecifiers` (`alignas(N) …`) precedes the head — the shared member-specifier prefix (same rule + `specifierPrefix` strip as structField).
unionField.$tfc73AttrComment: TF-C73: the `structField` mirror — an OPTIONAL trailing `structMemberAttrList` (the SHARED member-attribute rule), so `union U { int x __attribute__((aligned(8))); };` parses and `head:0` / `declaratorList:1` are unmoved.

unionTypeRef.$comment: c25: the REF-ONLY union specifier, kept for the param/cast positions (declHeadForParam, castTypeBase). The declaration-head positions route through the UNIFIED `unionSpec` (below). Mirrors structTypeRef.

unionSpec.$comment: c25 D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER: the UNIFIED union specifier — `union {opt tag} {opt body}`. Mirrors `structSpec`: ONE rule for define (`union U { … }`) and reference (`union U`), the SOLE UnionKeyword candidate in the 4 body-bearing alts → non-speculative direct descent (no member-body probe budget). Dual-mode binder via `definesWhenChild: unionBody`.
unionSpec.$tfc73LeadComment: TF-C73: the `structSpec` mirror — `compositeAttrLead` (ALWAYS emitted) after the keyword, so `union __attribute__((aligned(16))) U { … };` parses and the row's tag index is the FIXED 2.

unionBody.$comment: c25: the brace-delimited union member list, factored out of `unionSpec` as the define-vs-reference discriminator. NOT a scope rule (fields bind into the enclosing unionSpec's scope). Member shape identical to the former `unionSpecifierBody` tail.
unionBody.$staticAssertMemberComment: TF-C101 (D-CSUBSET-STATIC-ASSERT-STRUCT-MEMBER): the `structBody` mirror — C11/C23 6.7.2.1p1's `struct-declaration` list is SHARED by struct and union, so a union body admits a `static_assert-declaration` on exactly the same grounds. Same inline-`{alt}` shape for the same reason (no wrapper node ⇒ `unionField` stays a direct child and `fieldChildren` still sees it), same disjoint FIRST ⇒ still non-speculative, same already-wired `pass2Post` evaluation. See `structBody` for the full rationale; the two must move together or the union half becomes the missed case.

enumTypeRef.$comment: c25: the REF-ONLY enum specifier, kept for the param/cast positions (declHeadForParam, castTypeBase). The declaration-head positions route through the UNIFIED `enumSpec` (below). Mirrors structTypeRef.

enumTypeSpecifier.$comment: C23 6.7.2.2 (D-CSUBSET-ENUM-UNDERLYING-TYPE, FC17): the OPTIONAL `: <integer-type>` clause that fixes an enum's underlying type — `enum E : unsigned char { A }`. A SEQUENCE `[Colon, castTypeBase]` (castTypeBase is the qualifier-free/pointer-free base type-name — `unsigned char`, `int`, a typedef, NOT `int *`). It carries `commitRequiresTypeName` with `requireKnownType` polarity (MIRRORS `alignasTypeName`): the enum-underlying `:` collides with the pre-existing anonymous enum-typed struct bit-field `enum Color : 4;`, so the parser SPECULATIVELY tries this clause after the `:` and the binder triage commits ONLY on a real type (keyword/tag-led base → Rule 1; a KNOWN typedef → Rule 2); a bit-field WIDTH (an int-constant `4`, or a value/unknown identifier `enum Tag : SOME_WIDTH`) ROLLS BACK, leaving the `:` for the member-level bit-field grammar. SEMANTICS live in the semantic tier (DeclarationRule.enumUnderlyingType): the resolved integer TypeKind becomes the enum's underlying scalar (scalars[0]) and each enumerator's value is range-checked against it (fail-loud S_InvalidEnumUnderlyingType on a non-integer, S_EnumeratorValueOutOfRange on overflow).
enumTypeSpecifier.$tfc101Comment: TF-C101: this clause's base is `enumUnderlyingBase`, NOT the type-name base `castTypeBase` it used to share. THE TWO POSITIONS STOPPED BEING THE SAME GRAMMAR when `castTypeBase` was widened to admit composite DEFINITIONS (see that rule) — read `enumUnderlyingBase` for why sharing became actively wrong here, and why splitting is a real distinction rather than a copy.

enumUnderlyingBase.$comment:
TF-C101: the base type-specifier of the C23 enum-underlying clause (`enum E : unsigned char { A }`). Vocabulary-IDENTICAL to what `castTypeBase` was before this cycle, and deliberately so: the ONE thing it must not do is admit a composite specifier WITH A BODY.
★ WHY IT EXISTS RATHER THAN REUSING `castTypeBase`. This slot is IMMEDIATELY followed by the enumerator-list `{`. Once `castTypeBase` routes `struct` through the unified `structSpec` — whose `{optional structBody}` is greedy — `enum E : struct Foo { A }` binds `{ A }` to the STRUCT, leaving the enum with no enumerator list. MEASURED: `clang -std=c23` binds it the same way (`redefinition of 'Foo'`, `unknown type name 'A'`), so the greedy reading is not wrong about C — C23 6.7.2.2 really does spell the clause `: specifier-qualifier-list`, and a specifier-qualifier-list really may carry a member list. But MEASURED in DSS, that reading is strictly WORSE HERE: the struct body then desyncs on `A`, the whole speculative clause rolls back, and one precise `S_InvalidEnumUnderlyingType` becomes a NINE-diagnostic parse cascade (`S_UnknownType` on the enum, `P_NoAlternativeMatched` on the `:`, six more downstream). A ref-only base keeps the `{` for the enum, so the analyzer receives an intact enum whose underlying type is a struct and rejects it by CONSTRAINT — one diagnostic, at the right tier, naming the right thing. That is better than clang here, and it is the behavior this repo already pinned.
★ THIS IS A DISTINCTION, NOT DUPLICATION — and the distinction is the reason the shared rule had to end. A type-NAME position (`sizeof`, cast, `_Generic`, compound literal) is closed by `)`, so a definition there is unambiguous and useful; this position is closed by the very `{` a definition would eat, so a definition here can only ever be a constraint violation whose diagnostic we would be degrading to buy nothing. Widening BOTH from one rule would have traded a real diagnostic for a construct no one can write correctly.
★ THE DRIFT RISK, STATED SO IT STAYS LOUD: a NEW base type form added to `castTypeBase` will not appear here automatically. That is survivable exactly because the failure mode is a parse ERROR in the enum-underlying slot, never a silent mis-read — but a form that belongs in both (a new integer specifier) must be added to both in the SAME commit.

enumSpec.$comment: c25 D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER: the UNIFIED enum specifier — `enum {opt tag} {opt underlying-type} {opt body}`. Mirrors `structSpec`: ONE rule for define (`enum E { A, B }`) and reference (`enum E`), the SOLE EnumKeyword candidate in the 4 body-bearing alts → non-speculative direct descent. Dual-mode binder via `definesWhenChild: enumBody`. The enumerator-list (with trailing comma) lives in `enumBody`. FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ENUM-UNDERLYING-TYPE / D-PARSE-SPECULATIVE-OPTIONAL): the optional C23 `: <integer-type>` clause (`enumTypeSpecifier`) sits between the tag and the body as a SPECULATIVE optional so `enum E : unsigned char { A }` fixes the underlying type while the pre-existing anonymous enum-typed bit-field `enum Color : 4;` still parses (the clause is TRIED after the `:` and ROLLS BACK to the bit-field reading when a type doesn't follow — the whole point of the speculative-optional engine capability).
enumSpec.$p34LeadComment: P34 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-TYPE-POSITION): `compositeAttrLead` — the SAME always-emitted after-keyword slot `structSpec`/`unionSpec` have carried since TF-C73 — joins `enumSpec`, closing the last composite row with no after-keyword attribute surface. `enum [[deprecated]] E { … }` is the C23 6.7.3.1 appertainment position for an enum TAG and BOTH references honor it there (gcc 13.3.0 and clang 19.1.1 each warn at every use — MEASURED 2026-08-25); before this it was error[P0009] in the C23 spelling and error[P0001] in the GNU one. INDEX: the row's tag moves 1 -> 2, deterministically and ONCE, exactly as structSpec's did — the slot is a NAMED rule over a lone `{repeat}` so its node is emitted even when the run is EMPTY, which is what keeps the index CONSTANT whether or not a decoration is written. It must NOT be an `{optional}`: the tag would then sit at 2 only when a decoration is present, and `extractNameNode` would hand `anonymousNameAllowed` a non-identifier node, binding a TAGGED enum ANONYMOUSLY with its tag discarded. FIRST(compositeAttrLead) = {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen}; what can follow it here is `Identifier` (tag), `ColonOp` (the C23 underlying-type clause) or `BlockOpen` (body) — none of which can start an attribute — so the repeat stays predictively decidable and non-speculative, and the enum's own speculative `enumTypeSpecifier` optional is untouched. The parser's incremental tag SKETCH (`recordCompositeTagIfApplicable_`) is index-based too and stays correct for the same reason structSpec's does: the slot is staged BEFORE the identifier, so at tag-consume time the staged visible children are [keyword, lead, tag].

enumBody.$comment: c25: the brace-delimited enumerator list, factored out of `enumSpec` as the define-vs-reference discriminator. NOT a scope rule (enumerators bind into the enclosing enumSpec's scope, then lift to the enclosing namespace scope per fieldChildren.liftToEnclosingScope). Enumerator-list shape (optional list, trailing comma) identical to the former `enumSpecifierBody` tail.

topLevelDecl.$comment: C declaration = decl-specifiers init-declarator-list? `;` (or a function-definition block tail). The init-declarator-list is OPTIONAL: a bare `struct P { … };` / `enum E { … };` is a type-only declaration (head introduces the tag, no object declared) — the semantic tier mints the type from the head and emits a TypeDecl; a head that introduces NO tag with no declarator (`int ;`) is a C6.7p2 'declares nothing' constraint violation (fail-loud). A trailing declarator (`struct P { … } v;`) or a block tail (`struct Tri mkTri(void){…}`) takes the normal global/function path.
topLevelDecl.$tfc77Comment: TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): `declAttrRun` — the MID-POSITION attribute slot between the type head and the declarator list (`static int SQLITE_NOINLINE f(…)`, `int __attribute__((weak)) gv;`). It is a SIBLING of `topLevelHead`, never a child (see declAttrRun's own comment for the type-hijack reasoning). Because it is a named rule over a lone `{repeat}` it is ALWAYS emitted, so the row's post-strip role children are FIXED: [topLevelHead(0), declAttrRun(1), initDeclaratorList(2), topLevelDeclTail(3)] with a declarator list, [topLevelHead(0), declAttrRun(1), topLevelDeclTail(2)] without one. The row's `declaratorList` moved 1 → 2 and `kindByChild.childPath` [2,0] → [3,0] IN THE SAME COMMIT (the `structSpec` `name: 1 → 2` precedent) — leaving either at its old value MIS-LOWERS every function definition in the TU.
topLevelDecl.$p53ExternMergedComment: ★★★ P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): this row absorbed `externDecl`'s FILE-SCOPE job. The trailing `{optional stringLiteralExpr}` is D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-LIBRARY-SYNTAX's per-declaration import-library override (`extern void* GetStdHandle(int) "kernel32.dll";` — examples/c/hello_writefile), moved here VERBATIM from `externDecl`. FIRST(stringLiteralExpr) = the string openers, DISJOINT from BlockOpen/EndStatement, so `topLevelDeclTail` still stops the list and nothing speculates. ★★ IT SITS AFTER `initDeclaratorList` AND BEFORE THE TAIL FOR THE SAME INDEX REASON `externDecl` DID, and the arithmetic is the whole risk: post-strip role children are [topLevelHead(0), declAttrRun(1), initDeclaratorList(2), topLevelDeclTail(3)] with no override and [… stringLiteralExpr(3), topLevelDeclTail(4)] with one. `declaratorList: 2` is untouched; `kindByChild.childPath [3,0]` lands on the TAIL when there is no override (block ⇒ a function DEFINITION) and on the stringLiteralExpr's own first child when there IS one — never a `block`, so the pathological `extern int f(void) "lib" {…}` stays a DECLARATION here and is caught fail-loud at HIR rather than silently dropping the body. That is `externDecl`'s exact prior behaviour, preserved by construction. ⚠ `int x = "abc";` is unaffected: the string is inside the init-declarator's initializer, which the list consumes first.

topLevelHead.$comment: Top-level head: a keyword type specifier (`typeSpecifierSeq`, e.g. `int`/`unsigned long`), a struct/union/enum composite specifier (`topLevelCompositeSpec` — the SPECULATIVE body-vs-ref alt), OR a lone Identifier (typedef name). The OUTER alt is NON-speculative: FIRST(typeSpecifierSeq)={type keywords}, FIRST(topLevelCompositeSpec)={struct,union,enum}, FIRST(Identifier)={ident} are pairwise disjoint — so a plain `int x;` routes DIRECTLY to typeSpecifierSeq (NO extra wrapper node, preserving the pre-existing tree shape) and only a struct/union/enum lead enters the single-level speculation that closes D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-BODY-VARDECL-POSITION. topLevel stays non-speculative: `struct` routes unambiguously to topLevelDecl.

topLevelCompositeSpec.$comment: c25 D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER: the struct/union/enum SPECIFIER at a top-level declaration head — now ONE unified rule per keyword (`structSpec`/`unionSpec`/`enumSpec`), each covering BOTH the body form (`struct P { … }`) AND the bare tag reference (`struct P`) via an internal `{optional body}`. The three candidates have pairwise-DISJOINT 1-token FIRSTs (StructKeyword/UnionKeyword/EnumKeyword), so the predictive prune leaves EXACTLY ONE survivor for any composite lead → the parser's unique-production DIRECT DESCENT (parser.cpp ~1804-1844) dispatches it NON-speculatively. The member body therefore parses with NO speculation budget — the c25 fix for `struct sqlite3`'s large body (the former body-vs-ref probe budget-capped at 4096 tokens). `speculative`/`lookahead` are retained but moot under the unique-survivor direct descent (kept so a future non-disjoint addition still has a probe budget). The enum body's trailing-comma enumerator-list parses cleanly (the schema compiler propagates nested-nullable FOLLOW via recomputeAltExpectedSets).

topLevelDeclTail.$comment: FIRST(block)={BlockOpen} vs {EndStatement} — disjoint. A block tail makes the FIRST init-declarator a function DEFINITION (semantic-tier checks enforce: exactly one declarator, named, fn-suffix-bearing, no initializer); an EndStatement tail makes every declarator a global variable.

singleDeclSpecifier.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): `alignasSpec` (`_Alignas`/`alignas`) joins the top-level declaration-specifier alts. Its FIRST = {AlignasKeyword, AlignasLegacyKeyword} is DISJOINT from StaticKeyword / attrSpec's AttributeKeyword / stdAttr's BracketOpen, so the repeat stays predictively pruned (non-speculative). It is stripped from the positional-child count (specifierPrefix: declSpecifiers on topLevelDecl) and IGNORED by the linkage scan (linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules). FC16 (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN): the bare `_Noreturn` keyword (NoreturnKeyword) likewise joins the alts — FIRST {NoreturnKeyword} disjoint from all the above, so no speculation impact; it is stripped from the child count and IGNORED by the linkage scan (linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds); the SEMANTIC noreturn scan reads it. The attribute forms (`[[noreturn]]`/`__attribute__((noreturn))`) ride the existing attrSpec/stdAttr alts. FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR, C23 6.7.1): the `constexpr` storage-class specifier (ConstexprKeyword) joins the alts — FIRST {ConstexprKeyword} disjoint from all the above (a distinct exact-match keyword; `const` is a headQualifier, not a specifier, so no prefix collision), stripped from the child count like the others. At FILE scope it IS a linkage specifier: C23 6.2.2p3 gives a file-scope constexpr object INTERNAL linkage, so topLevelDecl's linkageSpecifiers maps the keyword text to {binding:local} (it is deliberately NOT in that row's linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds). The SEMANTIC constexpr validation (Pass 2 validateConstexprDeclarator) reads it via semantics.constexpr.keywordToken.
singleDeclSpecifier.$threadLocalComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, C11/C23 6.7.1): the `_Thread_local`/`thread_local` twin keywords (the _Alignof/alignof spelling precedent) join the alts — FIRST {ThreadLocalKeyword, ThreadLocalC23Keyword} disjoint from every other branch (distinct exact-match keywords), stripped from the child count like the others. The repeat admits both orders with `static` (`static thread_local` / `thread_local static`). NOT a linkage-changing specifier: the topLevelDecl row maps both spellings to {threadStorage:true} — a file-scope thread_local object keeps EXTERNAL linkage (6.2.2 untouched); Pass 1's specifier scan marks the symbol isThreadLocal and Pass 2's validateThreadLocalDeclarator enforces 6.7.1.
singleDeclSpecifier.$tfc79Comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4): the `inline` FUNCTION specifier joins the alts — FIRST {InlineKeyword} disjoint from every other branch (a distinct exact-match keyword), so the repeat stays predictively pruned and every ordering (`static inline` / `inline static` / `inline __attribute__((...))`) comes free. ★ ONE TOKEN KIND FOR ALL THREE SPELLINGS: the keyword table maps `inline`, `__inline` and `__inline__` to the SINGLE kind `InlineKeyword`. MEASURED against `/usr/bin/clang -std=c99 -O0 -c` + `nm`: `inline int p(int){…}` and `__inline int p(int){…}` produce the IDENTICAL symbol state (`U _p` — no external definition), so the spellings are synonyms and giving `__inline` its own kind would invite a semantics split that does not exist. The C99-vs-GNU89 divergence rides the LANGUAGE MODE and the `gnu_inline` ATTRIBUTE, never the spelling. ★ It is NOT a linkage specifier: `inline`'s effect depends on the co-present `static`/`extern`, so a flat `linkageSpecifiers` entry (keyed by token TEXT, context-free, last-wins) would be exactly the clobber `$constexprLinkageComment` warns about — the keyword is IGNORED by kind and the EMISSION decision is made from `SymbolRecord.isInline` at CST→HIR (see `semantics.inline`).
singleDeclSpecifier.$p53ExternComment: ★★★ P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS, C 6.7.1): `ExternKeyword` joins the alts, which is what makes C's specifier SET genuinely unordered — `inline extern`, `_Noreturn extern`, `_Thread_local extern` and `_Noreturn inline extern` (TWO leading specifiers, accepted by gcc, clang AND MSVC) all parse through the ONE `topLevelDecl` rule now. FIRST {ExternKeyword} is disjoint from every other branch, so the repeat stays predictively pruned. ★★ THE PRICE, PAID EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN INHERITED: while `extern` was `externDecl`'s rule HEAD, three facts came free from the rule's IDENTITY and they now have to be STATED. (1) NON-DEFININGNESS — `topLevelDecl`'s `linkageSpecifiers` maps `extern` to `{nonDefining:true}`, the 5th axis on LinkageSpecifierEffect; without it every `extern int e;` would become a TENTATIVE DEFINITION emitting storage in every TU, at rc 0. (2) THE UNKNOWN-SPECIFIER GATE — with no entry at all the HIR linkage fold reports `warning[H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier]` and EXITS 0, silently dropping the extern-ness (✔MEASURED under the grammar-only mutant; that is precisely why the grammar half was reverted rather than shipped in P53's first pass). (3) C 6.7.1p2 — the grammar used to refuse `extern static` BY ACCIDENT; the entry's `exclusiveGroup` now says it, and `_Thread_local` deliberately does NOT carry the group, which is how the standard's own exception is expressed. ⚠ `ExternKeyword` is NOT added to `localDeclSpecifier`: at BLOCK scope `externDecl` is still the rule and still the unique owner of that lead (D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-EXTERN needs the block-scope BINDING, not a re-home).

attrSpec.$comment: GNU `__attribute__((...))`. FC4 c1 grew the parenthesized-string form `visibility("hidden")`. TF-C62 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE) generalizes the ARGUMENT to `attrArgs` (a balanced list of identifiers / numbers / strings / nested parens) so real-header forms parse — `aligned(16)` (number), `__format__(__printf__,1,2)` (multi-arg), `__nonnull__((1,3))` (nested). It also admits a COMMA-separated run of further clauses (`__nothrow__, __leaf__`) via `attrClauseTail`. THE FIRST CLAUSE'S NAME stays a DIRECT child of attrSpec (so extractOneAttrClause + linkageFrom see it); ARGS live in the `attrArgs` subtree, which `semantics.attributeSemantics.attributeArgRule` names so linkageFrom can FLAG the arg tokens out of its specifier KEY LOOKUP while leaving them visible to the composite `<ident>:<string>` pairing. The trailing clauses nest under `attrClauseTail` so they don't pollute the first-clause name scan (multi-clause HONORING is a pinned follow-up; the first clause is honored). ★ TF-C73 (D-CONFIG-ATTRIBUTE-ARG-RULE-DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNIMPLEMENTED): this paragraph previously asserted that handling as EXISTING behavior while `attributeArgRule` resolved to NOTHING in the whole tree — no loader key, no field, no consumer — which is exactly why the leading-position arg soup survived a full cycle. It is now a real, greppable, loaded key; do not restore prose that describes a mechanism you cannot grep to an implementation.

attrClauseTail.$comment:
TF-C62: a NON-FIRST clause in a comma-separated `__attribute__((a, b))` run — name + optional args, nested so it doesn't add a direct-child name token to attrSpec's first-clause name scan.
★ P32 (D-C-ATTRIBUTE-CLAUSE-NAME-ADMITS-ONLY-IDENTIFIER-SO-A-KEYWORD-NAMED-ATTRIBUTE-IS-REFUSED): the name position is the SHARED `attributeClauseName` token class, not `Identifier` — a trailing clause is a clause, and glibc writes `__attribute__ ((__nothrow__ , __leaf__))` and `__attribute__ ((__const__))` in the same headers. Widening only the FIRST clause would have made `__attribute__((a, __const__))` a parse error while `__attribute__((__const__, a))` parsed — one construct meaning two things depending on where it is written, which this file rejects everywhere else. FIRST(attrClauseTail) widens with it, and the only place that FIRST is consulted is the `{repeat}` after a `Comma`, whose alternative is the loop-exit `ParenClose` — disjoint from every name kind, so nothing became speculative.

attrArgs.$comment: TF-C62: the parenthesized ARGUMENT of one GNU attribute — a balanced `( ... )` holding a comma-separated list of arg items (an identifier, an integer/float literal, a string, or a NESTED `attrArgs` for `__nonnull__((1))`-style double parens). ★ TF-C73: this rule is DECLARED as `semantics.attributeSemantics.attributeArgRule`, and THAT declaration is what makes the special handling real. `linkageFrom` marks every token it reaches THROUGH this node (nested arg groups inherit the mark) and skips the marked ones for the linkage-specifier KEY LOOKUP — so `format(printf,1,2)`'s `printf`/`1`/`2` are never read as specifier names — while the marked tokens STAY in the flattened token list so a LONE string inside still pairs with the preceding attribute name for the composite key (`visibility("hidden")` -> `visibility:hidden`). A wholesale `linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules` skip was MEASURED and REFUTED: it deletes that string, and `visibility("hidden")` then fails H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on the bare `visibility`. NOTE: the previous version of this sentence described exactly this behavior in the PRESENT TENSE while `attributeArgRule` existed nowhere in the tree (D-CONFIG-ATTRIBUTE-ARG-RULE-DOCUMENTED-BUT-UNIMPLEMENTED).

attrArgItem.$comment: TF-C72: one attribute argument — an `attrArgAtom` plus an OPTIONAL `= atom` tail, for the clang keyword-argument form `__attribute__((__availability__(swift, unavailable, message=_msg)))` (SDK sys/cdefs.h:332, the `__swift_unavailable(_msg)` macro). The assignment is a TAIL, not a new alt, so FIRST(attrArgItem) is UNCHANGED (still the atom's FIRST set) and the comma-separated list stays predictive — no speculation. FIRST(AssignOp)={`=`} is disjoint from the two tokens that can follow an item (Comma, ParenClose), so the `{optional}` is predictively decidable. Operator-expression args (`aligned(2*x)`) remain residue — they fail loud, never silently mis-parse.

attrArgAtom.$comment: TF-C62 (renamed from `attrArgItem` by TF-C72, which lifted the `= value` tail one level up): one attribute argument ATOM. The alt FIRST sets are disjoint (Identifier / IntLiteral / FloatLiteral / string-openers / ParenOpen) so the list stays predictive. The extra wrapper node this introduces under `attrArgs` is transparent to every consumer — `scanCompositePacked`, `linkageFrom`'s specifier-token collection and `decodeAdjacentStringBodies` are all RECURSIVE subtree walks, not fixed-child-index reads (MEASURED: `__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))` still resolves the composite linkage key and `[[deprecated("old")]]` still decodes its message).

stdAttr.$comment: C23 [[...]] attribute specifier (D14: parsed, semantically IGNORED — linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules skips the whole subtree in the linkage scan). Namespaced `[[gnu::attr]]` and a parenthesized string argument are accepted; richer argument forms are residue.

stdAttrItem.$tfc73ArgComment: TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): the C23 item's ARGUMENT is now the SHARED `attrArgs` rule instead of the former inline `( {opt stringLiteralExpr} )`. Motivation: `[[gnu::aligned(8)]]` did not parse at all (`P0009 expected 'StringStart'… — got '8'`) because the inline form admitted ONLY a string. ZERO FIRST-set widening: FIRST(attrArgs) = {ParenOpen} — byte-identical to the inline form's lead — so the `{optional}` stays predictively decidable and nothing becomes speculative. Reusing `attrArgs` (rather than growing a second argument grammar) is what makes the C23 form inherit the GNU form's machinery for free: the `semantics.attributeSemantics.attributeArgRule` token flag now covers `[[…]]` arguments too, and `collectAttrClauses` already skips an `attributeArgRule` subtree, so an argument identifier (`[[gnu::format(printf,1,2)]]`) can never mint a PHANTOM clause. The `[[deprecated("m")]]` message still decodes: the string moves from a DIRECT child to `attrArgs > attrArgList > attrArgItem > attrArgAtom > stringLiteralExpr`, and `extractOneAttrClause`'s argument search is DEPTH-AGNOSTIC by construction (it stops at the `stringLiteralExpr` rule, not at a fixed depth — the exact reshape hazard that search was written for).
stdAttrItem.$p32ClauseNameComment: P32 (D-C-ATTRIBUTE-CLAUSE-NAME-ADMITS-ONLY-IDENTIFIER-SO-A-KEYWORD-NAMED-ATTRIBUTE-IS-REFUSED): BOTH name segments are the shared `attributeClauseName` token class. ✔MEASURED that the C23 spelling needs it at least as much as the GNU one: gcc 13.3.0 accepts EVERY reserved word inside `[[…]]` (it warns `-Wattributes` and continues) including the ones it REFUSES in the GNU form, and `[[gnu::const]]` compiles clean on gcc AND clang 19.1.7. The NAMESPACE segment takes the class too — `gnu` is an identifier today, but a host language whose namespace word is a keyword would otherwise hit the same wall one segment earlier, and the two segments are the same syntactic role. ⚠ ZERO FIRST-set widening reaches an alt: `stdAttr` fixes `[[` ahead of this rule, so FIRST(stdAttr) is still {BracketOpen} and every alt that offers `stdAttr` (singleDeclSpecifier, localDeclSpecifier, compositeAttr) is unchanged; inside `stdAttr` the item list is `stdAttrItem (, stdAttrItem)*` with the loop exit on `BracketClose`, disjoint from every name kind.

compositeAttr.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-PACKED): ONE composite type-attribute — a GNU `__attribute__((…))` (`attrSpec`) or a C23 `[[…]]` (`stdAttr`), REUSING the existing attribute rules. The trailing struct/union attribute list (`compositeAttrList`) is a repeat of this.

compositeAttrList.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-PACKED): the trailing composite-attribute list after a struct/union body — one or more `compositeAttr` (`struct S {…} __attribute__((packed))` / `[[gnu::packed]]`). Referenced as a TRAILING `{optional}` on structSpec/unionSpec (after `structBody`, so it never shifts the tag's positional index). The semantic tier scans this node (semantics.packed.listRule) for a `packed` spelling. TF-C73: the after-KEYWORD position is no longer a parse error — it is `compositeAttrLead` below, a SEPARATE rule for a load-bearing reason spelled out there.

compositeAttrLead.$comment:
TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE, CLOSES D-CSUBSET-PACKED-AFTER-KEYWORD-POSITION): the AFTER-KEYWORD composite-attribute slot — `struct __attribute__((aligned(16))) T { … };` (real witness `mach-o/dyld_images.h:124`; 64 of the SDK audit's 204 `aligned` sites, 31.4%). Before it, the shape did not even fail cleanly: `structSpec` swallowed the attribute with its TRAILING `{optional compositeAttrList}` (tag and body both absent at that point) and `T { int x; }` then read as a declarator plus block tail — a FUNCTION DEFINITION, reported `S0018 a function definition's declarator must be a function declarator`, naming the wrong construct entirely.
★ A NAMED RULE OVER A LONE `{repeat}`, so the node is emitted even when the run is EMPTY (the `typedefAttrRun` device). NOT an `{optional}`: `structSpec`'s declaration row addresses the tag BY INDEX, and an `{optional}` would shift it from visible-child 2 to 3 exactly when a decoration is present — SILENTLY, since `extractNameNode` would hand `anonymousNameAllowed` a non-identifier node and a TAGGED struct would bind ANONYMOUSLY with its tag discarded. An always-emitted node makes the index CONSTANT by construction.
★ A DISTINCT RULE NAME, not `compositeAttrList` reused: an always-emitted node carrying that name would be indistinguishable from the real trailing list to any consumer that selects by rule name. This slot reaches the semantic tier through the structSpec/unionSpec rows' `declarationAttrSlotRules` instead.
★ THE ORDER THIS LANDED IN IS THE POINT. This slot was designed, built and MEASURED one cycle earlier and then DELIBERATELY REVERTED, because `scanCompositePacked` then selected the FIRST `compositeAttrList` direct child and `break`ed: a lead slot under a distinct rule name was invisible to it, and `packed` — KNOWN-and-inert in the effects table — was silently DROPPED (MEASURED: `struct __attribute__((packed)) S { int a; char b; };` compiled CLEAN at `sizeof` 8 against clang's 5, where the parse error it replaced was LOUD). Shipping the grammar first would have traded a confusing diagnostic for a wrong layout. The consumer is now surface-count-agnostic — it accumulates every `compositeAttrList` child AND every `declarationAttrSlotRules` slot — so the grammar is safe, and RE-MEASURED it is: that same input now gives `sizeof` 5 / `_Alignof` 1, matching clang exactly.
FIRST = {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen} (via `compositeAttr` → attrSpec | stdAttr); the slot is NULLABLE and the tokens that can follow are `Identifier` (tag), `BlockOpen` (body) and the spec's FOLLOW — none of which can start an attribute, so the repeat is predictively decidable. Non-speculative, no probe budget.

declarator.$comment: alt of (pointer-led, direct-led): NON-nullable (at least one star or a direct), so `int = 5;` / `int;` stay parse errors; the pointer-led branch's OPTIONAL direct admits the abstract star-only form (`int *` in param position). The branch sequences are INLINE so pointerLayer/directDeclarator land as DIRECT children — the shape the engine's declarators roles describe.

directDeclarator.$comment: Base alt is INLINE + SPECULATIVE: fnSuffix vs parenDeclarator genuinely collide on `(` (C 6.7.6.3p11) — fnSuffix probes FIRST (declared order) under its requireKnownType guard; rollback yields the parenthesized-declarator reading. Identifier rides the token-leaf route (no probe); arrayStarSuffix/arrayDeclSuffix at base are the abstract `int [*]` / `int [3]` param forms. ★ D-CSUBSET-VLA-PARAM-STAR-ABSTRACT (CLOSED, P57): that sentence described a list arrayStarSuffix was NOT IN, and the absence WAS the row's whole blocker — not, as the row stated, `abstractDirectDeclarator`'s non-speculative repeat. An UNNAMED abstract parameter routes through `param` → `{optional declarator}` → THIS rule (there is no separate abstract-param rule), so a leading `[` with no name lands on THIS BASE alt, where `[*]` had no candidate and died `P_BacktrackFailed: ... got ']'` (✔MEASURED at fcb3a9d7 on `int f(int, int [*]);`, while the NAMED `int g(int n, int a[*]);` control compiled and RAN — the named form reaches the REPEAT, which already listed arrayStarSuffix). arrayStarSuffix sits BEFORE arrayDeclSuffix for the repeat's reason: the base alt is ALREADY speculative (lookahead 64), so `[N]` / `[*p]` probe the fixed 3-token `[ * ]` first, fail at the bound position and roll back CLEANLY to arrayDeclSuffix. No speculation was added and `abstractDirectDeclarator` was NOT touched, so the cast-vs-value type-name triage the row feared is untouched by construction. ✔gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both compile and RUN the abstract form (each warns — -Wvla-parameter / -Warray-parameter — and neither refuses); MSVC ABSTAINS twice over (`C2059: syntax error: ']'` on `[*]`, and `C2057` on every VLA bound). lookahead 64 = the operand-alt precedent (1024-token probe budget): a probe must swallow a whole parenthesized param list / nested declarator. VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA): the suffix repeat is SPECULATIVE and lists arrayStarSuffix (the fixed 3-token `[ * ]`) BEFORE arrayDeclSuffix so `int a[*]` (a prototype-form unspecified-size VLA parameter) probes arrayStarSuffix first and, on a real bound (`[N]`/`[*p]`), rolls back CLEANLY to arrayDeclSuffix — enabled by the schema-compiler propagating `speculative` onto an inline repeat-alt's loopEntry (grammar_schema_json.cpp repeat arm). fnSuffix still leads (declared order) since it is FIRST-disjoint (`(`).

fnSuffixTail.$comment: VLA C4c (§B 2026-07-14): the POST-BASE (suffix-position) function-suffix `( params )` — grammar-IDENTICAL to `fnSuffix` but WITHOUT the `commitRequiresTypeName` guard. Needed because the suffix repeat is now SPECULATIVE (to disambiguate arrayStarSuffix `[*]` vs arrayDeclSuffix): a guarded `fnSuffix` there would be PROBED even as a FIRST-unique sole survivor on `(` (the sole-survivor direct-descent skips guarded candidates so the binder triage runs), and its `requireKnownType` guard would spuriously ROLL BACK a valid function's `()` (empty params) / cross-file-typedef params — breaking `int f()`, casts, every function declarator. The guard is MEANINGLESS at the suffix position (there is no `parenDeclarator` competitor — that ambiguity is resolved once, at the BASE alt which KEEPS `fnSuffix`), so dropping it is C-correct. Semantically fnSuffixTail IS a function suffix: the `fnSuffixTailRule` config role makes `directDeclaredType` fold it → `FnSig` identically to `fnSuffix`, and the fn-declarator / definition-scope detection recognizes both.

abstractDirectDeclarator.$comment: c26 D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-DECLARATOR-TYPE-NAME: the abstract twin of `directDeclarator` for the CAST/sizeof/compound/va_arg type-name tail (C 6.7.7 direct-abstract-declarator). The BASE alt is deliberately ONLY `{fnSuffix, parenDeclarator}` — NOT the full `directDeclarator` base — for two reasons. (1) `Identifier` EXCLUDED: a bare-identifier base would make `(c * c)` (a pervasive multiplication) speculatively commit as a cast `(c *<abstract-decl c>)` — the type child gains >1 leaf so the commit triage's rule-1 'not a lone identifier' fires. (2) `arrayDeclSuffix` EXCLUDED at the BASE (the bare `[N]` form): `(b[0])` (an array-INDEX value expression) would likewise mis-commit as a type-name `b[0]` (base `b` + array suffix). C's direct-abstract-declarator allows a bare `[N]` base, but it collides with the index expression under speculative type-vs-value triage — so the BARE-array type-name (`(int[10])` / `sizeof(int[10])`) is the NAMED LIMITATION D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-ARRAY-TYPE-NAME (off the c26 fn-ptr frontier; the `(*)[N]` array-OF-pointer form still works — its base is `parenDeclarator`, the `[N]` rides the suffix repeat). The remaining base forms — `parenDeclarator` (`(*)`/`(*p)` — a nested NAME still parses and is rejected loud at the type-resolve), `fnSuffix` — REUSE the existing declarator sub-rules verbatim, so the SHARED semantic `directDeclaredType` folds it (`(*)(void)`→Ptr<Fn(void)->int>) identically to `directDeclarator`. The suffix repeat KEEPS `arrayDeclSuffix` so `(*)[N]` works. Speculative base (fnSuffix vs parenDeclarator collide on `(`, exactly as directDeclarator).
abstractDirectDeclarator.$p53ArrayBaseComment:
P53 (D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-ARRAY-TYPE-NAME — CLOSED here): `arrayDeclSuffix` JOINS the base alt, so the bare-array abstract type-name C 6.7.7 requires — `sizeof(char[4])`, `sizeof(int[2][3])`, `_Alignof(int[4])`, `_Alignas(long[2])`, `(char[12]){0}`, `__builtin_types_compatible_p(int[3], int[3])` — parses in EVERY type-name position, because they all route through `castTypeRef`. ✔MEASURED at P53's base, all six were parse errors; gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x`, clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` and MSVC 19.51 `/std:clatest`, probed SEPARATELY, accept and RUN every one.
★★ THE EXCLUSION'S STATED REASON WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOW STALE, WHICH IS THE ONLY REASON THIS IS A ONE-LINE CHANGE. The $comment above says the bare `[N]` base was excluded because `(b[0])` — an array-INDEX value expression — 'would likewise mis-commit as a type-name b[0] … the type child gains >1 leaf so the commit triage's rule-1 not-a-lone-identifier fires'. That premise was retired by c55 (D-CSUBSET-CALL-IN-PAREN-CAST-AMBIGUITY): `typeNameCommitApproved_`'s rule 1 now discriminates on the BASE (leftmost) LEAF, not the leaf COUNT, so an IDENTIFIER base carrying an abstract tail falls through to rules 2-4 — the binder-sketch lookup (a known VALUE `b` ROLLS BACK to the index reading) and the follower-operator test. That row's own closing work names exactly this two-part sequence ('teach the triage … THEN re-add arrayDeclSuffix'); the first part shipped with c55 for the `f(p)` sibling and this is the second.
★ A KEYWORD BASE NEVER REACHES THE AMBIGUITY AT ALL. `int[10]` / `char[4]` hit rule 1 on the leftmost leaf (`IntKeyword` / `CharKeyword` is not the identifier kind) and COMMIT immediately — no sketch lookup, no follower test — so the shape this row exists for is the shape with no competing value reading. Only an identifier-based `(b[0])` triages, and it triages the SAME way `(c*c)` and `f(p)` already do.
⚠ THE ELEMENT-COUNT IDIOM IS THE CONTROL AND IT IS PINNED, NOT ASSUMED: `sizeof(b)/sizeof(b[0])` must stay the VALUE form. `b` is a declared object, so the sketch answers Value and rule 3 rolls back — the `sizeof_value_array_dim` corpus example and the new `sizeof_abstract_array_type_name` example assert both readings in one program.

fnSuffix.$comment: The commit guard fires ONLY when fnSuffix is probed speculatively (the directDeclarator BASE position); the post-base suffix position dispatches non-speculatively on `(` and never consults it. requireKnownType = C 6.7.6.3p11: a lone unknown identifier between the parens rolls back to the parenthesized-declarator reading AND records the ambiguous-type-name candidate for the CU oracle's seeded reparse.

initDeclarator.$comment:
TF-C62 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): an OPTIONAL after-declarator `__attribute__((...))` run (`void f(void) __attribute__((noreturn));`, `Tcl_Panic(...) TCL_FORMAT_PRINTF(1,2);`) sits between the declarator and the optional initializer. FIRST(attrSpec) = {AttributeKeyword} is disjoint from AssignOp/Comma/EndStatement, so it stays predictive (no speculation). The C23 `[[...]]` stdAttr rides here too. A run (repeat) admits `f() __attribute__((a)) __attribute__((b))`.
~~ CORRECTED TWICE, BOTH TIMES BY LATER MEASUREMENT — this sentence used to end 'These attributes are IGNORED for linkage (they are after the specifier prefix linkageFrom reads); the semantic attribute scan can still reach them via the declarator subtree — noreturn-after-declarator honoring is a pinned follow-up, parse-and-ignore is the first-increment behavior.' Both halves are now FALSE. (1) TF-C73 made this run a LINKAGE scan root (`declaratorAttrRoots`), so `int f(void) __attribute__((weak));` is honored rather than silently dropped. (2) P56 [[D-CSUBSET-TRAILING-NORETURN-NOT-HONORED]] made it a NORETURN scan root too — but only the `attrSpec` half, listed in `declarators.afterDeclaratorEntityAttrRules`, because ✔MEASURED no reference honors a trailing C23 `[[noreturn]]` (C23 6.7.13.1 puts it on the TYPE). See that key's comment for the full three-reference matrix. ~~
initDeclarator.$tfc88Comment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-ASM-LABEL-SYMBOL-RENAME — GNU/Clang ASM LABEL, GCC 6.47.5 'Controlling Names Used in Assembler Code'): `asmLabel` joins the after-declarator run — `int f(void) __asm("_myname");`. The run is the CORRECT home because the label is PER-DECLARATOR in C (`int a __asm("x"), b __asm("y");` names two different symbols), exactly like the attribute it sits beside, and because the `{repeat alt}` admits EVERY interleaving (`f() __asm("x") __attribute__((weak))` and the reverse) with no ordering rule to get wrong. FIRST(asmLabel) = {AsmKeyword}, DISJOINT from attrSpec's {AttributeKeyword}, stdAttr's {BracketOpen}, the following {AssignOp}, and the enclosing list's {Comma}/{EndStatement}/{BlockOpen} — so the repeat stays predictively pruned and nothing becomes speculative. The label is HONORED, not parse-and-ignore: it replaces the symbol's on-binary name VERBATIM (see semantics.declarators.asmLabelRule).

asmLabel.$comment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-ASM-LABEL-SYMBOL-RENAME — GNU/Clang ASM LABEL, GCC 6.47.5): `__asm("<assembler-name>")` written AFTER a declarator renames the symbol. The string is the on-binary symbol name VERBATIM — the platform C mangling (`applyCMangling`) is BYPASSED, NOT applied on top. MEASURED against /usr/bin/clang on arm64-darwin: `int gv __asm("myglobal");` emits `myglobal` (no leading `_`), `extern int f(int) __asm("_myextfn");` references `_myextfn` (the `_` comes from the SOURCE STRING), while an undecorated `caller` still emits `_caller`. This is the macOS SDK's `__DARWIN_ALIAS` family (sys/cdefs.h:791-800 — `__asm("_" __STRING(sym) __DARWIN_SUF_UNIX03)`), which is why the payload is `stringLiteralExpr` and not a single StringLiteral token: the SDK spelling is an ADJACENT-CONCATENATED run of three or four pieces, and a consumer that read only the first body would silently rename to `_`. Decoding routes through the SHARED decodeAdjacentStringBodies chokepoint. Structurally the staticAssertDecl / asmStmt clone (keyword, `(`, payload, `)`) MINUS the trailing `;` — an asm label is a declarator decoration, not a statement, so the declaration's own terminator follows. NOT admitted on a typedef declarator (typedefDeclaratorList takes BARE declarators), on a struct/union member, or on a parameter — a label there declares nothing renameable and stays a LOUD parse error, matching clang.

typeSpecifierForDecl.$comment: KEYWORD/composite-led type specifiers for declaration heads — deliberately NO Identifier arm (the typedef-name head is the ambiguous form, routed through identDeclHead/declOrExprStmt or the committed post-specifier/post-qualifier heads). SPECULATIVE (mirror typedefHead, D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-BODY-VARDECL-POSITION): admits the struct/union/enum BODY forms so a body-defined LOCAL (`struct P { int a; } v;` as a statement) parses; body forms probe FIRST, a ref with no `{` rolls back to the `*TypeRef` form. Single-level. D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF: `typeofSpecifier` (keyword-led, disjoint FIRST) is admitted here so a `typeof(...)`-headed declaration parses.

declHead.$comment: The COMMITTED any-form head: reached only after a leading storage-class specifier run (`register T x;`) — the statement is already known to be a declaration, so the Identifier (typedef-name) arm is unambiguous here.

kwDeclHead.$comment: The keyword-or-qualifier-led head (the non-speculative varDecl statement branch). Qualifier-led admits the Identifier (typedef) base — `const T x;` is committed by the `const` (no expression starts with a qualifier). Keyword-led is the plain `int x;` form. FIRSTs {Const,Volatile} vs type-keywords/struct/union/enum — disjoint.

identDeclHead.$comment: The AMBIGUOUS bare-typedef-name head (`T x;` vs the expression `T(x)`/`a*b`): lone Identifier + trailing qualifiers only. Leading qualifiers/specifiers route to kwDeclHead/varDecl instead (any of them commits a declaration).

typedefDecl.$comment: TF-C72 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): a typedef may carry a GNU/C23 attribute decoration in THREE positions, each a SIBLING of the type-resolved head — NEVER a child of it. `typedefHeadFull` is what `head` points at, and `resolveTypeNodeImpl` picks the head type FIRST-CHILD-THAT-RESOLVES-WINS while its token arm resolves ANY identifier through the scope chain: an attribute identifier placed INSIDE the head is tried as a TYPE, so `typedef int aligned; typedef __attribute__((aligned(16))) long T;` would silently resolve T to **int**. That is a SILENT MISCOMPILE and the reason all three slots are siblings (MEASURED — the anti-hijack pins in test_parser_c_smoke.cpp assert T is long in all three positions, and a negative control proves the assertion is live). The three positions: (1) AFTER the keyword — `typedef __attribute__((aligned(16))) long T;` — carried by the `typedefDeclSpecifiers` prefix below; (2) between head and declarator — `typedef int64_t __attribute__((__aligned__(8))) _OSAtomic_int64_t;` (SDK libkern/OSAtomicDeprecated.h:129,796,799) — the FIRST `typedefAttrRun`; (3) after the declarator — `typedef u_int64_t au_asflgs_t __attribute__ ((aligned(8)));` (SDK bsm/audit.h:199) and the macro-expanded `typedef void print_task_printer_t(const char*, ...) __printflike(1,2);` — the SECOND `typedefAttrRun`. INDEX STABILITY: `typedefDeclSpecifiers` is MANDATORY (it owns TypedefKeyword) so it is ALWAYS the first visible child ⇒ ALWAYS stripped by decl_prefix_strip.hpp; each `typedefAttrRun` is a NAMED rule whose body is a single `{repeat}` ⇒ it emits its node even when the run is EMPTY. So the post-strip role children are ALWAYS [typedefHeadFull, typedefAttrRun, declarator, typedefAttrRun, EndStatement] — the row's `head: 0` / `declarator: 2` never shift, whether or not a decoration is present (the shift-hazard `lowerTypeDecl` documents at cst_to_hir.cpp:8248). Positions (2) and (3) are OUTSIDE `specifierPrefixChild`'s reach, so their attributes are PARSE-AND-IGNORE — the SAME established posture (and same rule set) as `initDeclarator`'s after-declarator run, whose honoring is already a pinned follow-up; position (1) rides the prefix and IS reached by the semantic attribute scan.
typedefDecl.$tfc88Comment:
TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEDEF-MULTI-DECLARATOR, C 6.7 — the row opened by TF-C64 on 2026-07-24, whose trigger 'a real header/source uses a multi-declarator typedef' FIRED on the macOS SDK): the single `declarator` became `typedefDeclaratorList` — a COMMA-SEPARATED list of declarators sharing the head base type. `typedef mach_port_t vm_map_t, vm_map_read_t, vm_map_inspect_t;` (macOS SDK mach/vm_types.h:87) was P0001 x3 before this. C 6.7 makes `typedef` a STORAGE-CLASS SPECIFIER, so a typedef declaration is an ordinary declaration and takes the ordinary init-declarator LIST; typedef was the LAST declaration form still pinned to one declarator (topLevelDecl / varDecl / externDecl already take `initDeclaratorList`, structField takes `structMemberDeclaratorList`).
★ WHY A DEDICATED BARE LIST RATHER THAN REUSING `initDeclaratorList` — this was tried on paper and REJECTED as a SILENT DROP. `initDeclarator` carries its OWN after-declarator attribute run, and that run is GREEDY and matched BEFORE the enclosing sequence continues. So `typedef u_int64_t au_asflgs_t __attribute__ ((aligned(8)));` (SDK bsm/audit.h:199) would have its attribute swallowed by the per-slot run instead of the trailing `typedefAttrRun` — and the per-slot run is invisible to BOTH honoring channels here: `declarationAttrSlotRules` matches DIRECT children of the DECLARATION node (the run is one level deeper, inside the initDeclarator), and `declaratorAttrRoots`/`linkageFrom` early-returns because `typedefDecl` declares no `linkageSpecifiers` at all. A shipped, currently-HONORED `aligned(8)` would have started compiling clean at the wrong alignment. The bare list has no per-slot run, so the trailing `typedefAttrRun` keeps EXACTLY the role it has today.
★ It also keeps `typedef int T = 5;` a LOUD parse error (no initializer slot exists), matching clang, instead of admitting it and needing a semantic reject.
★ INDEX STABILITY: `typedefDeclaratorList` is a named rule at the SAME position the single `declarator` held, so the post-strip role children stay [typedefHeadFull(0), typedefAttrRun(1), typedefDeclaratorList(2), typedefAttrRun(3), EndStatement(4)] — the row moved `declarator: 2` -> `declaratorList: 2` IN THE SAME COMMIT; `head: 0` is unmoved. FIRST(typedefDeclaratorList) = FIRST(declarator), so every FIRST-set argument `typedefAttrRun`'s comment makes is unchanged.
★ RESIDUE (loud, never silent), the `structField` posture: a MID-LIST decoration (`typedef int A __attribute__((aligned(8))), B;`) and an asm label on a typedef declarator both stay loud parse errors — a typedef names a TYPE, which has no symbol to rename.
typedefDecl.$p51NoreturnStoreComment:
P51 [[D-CSUBSET-NORETURN-KEYWORD-PARAMETER-AND-TYPEDEF-POSITIONS]] — THE ONE PIECE OF THIS ROW THAT IS **NOT** CLOSED, STATED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE REDISCOVERED. Now that `typedefDeclSpecifiers` admits the keyword, `typedef _Noreturn void tfn(void);` PARSES and its execution meaning MATCHES gcc — but DSS emits NO diagnostic where gcc emits `warning: typedef 'tfn' declared '_Noreturn'`.
★ THE GAP IS NARROW AND ITS EDGES ARE MEASURED, not guessed: a `_Noreturn` typedef head warns CORRECTLY for every alias whose declarator is not a function — ✔MEASURED, `typedef _Noreturn __attribute__((aligned(16))) long T;` and `typedef _Noreturn void (*pfn)(void);` BOTH draw S_NoreturnNonFunctionObject. It is silent for exactly one shape: a typedef whose declarator IS a FnSig (`typedef _Noreturn void tfn(void);`).
★ WHY. The P50 arm in `semantic_analyzer.cpp` splits on the DECLARED TYPE: it STORES `SymbolRecord.isNoreturn` when `isFnSig`, and WARNS (`S_NoreturnNonFunctionObject`) when `!isFnSig`. A typedef's `tfn(void)` IS a FnSig, so this declaration takes the STORE arm and the warn arm is gated off — the arm cannot tell a TYPE-ALIAS declaration from a FUNCTION declaration, and nothing in this document can tell it (this row's `kind: "type"` is not read there). Matching gcc needs a SEMANTIC change, in a file P51's lane `np` did not own.
★★ THE RESIDUE IS A MISSING WARNING, **NOT** A MISCOMPILE, AND THAT IS MEASURED BY DIFFERENTIAL RATHER THAN ARGUED: `typedef _Noreturn void tfn(void); tfn f; int probe(void){ f(); }` draws `H_VerifierFailure` (fall-through) BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the undecorated control `typedef void tfn(void); …` — so the flag stored on the alias's Type symbol is NOT propagated to `f`, and a call to `f` is NOT wrapped `Block{call, Unreachable}`. gcc behaves the SAME WAY (its `-Wreturn-type` fires on the decorated and the undecorated form alike, and does NOT fire for the all-references-accept spelling `_Noreturn tfn f;`), so DSS and the only accepting reference agree on what the program MEANS.
⚠ THE STORED-BUT-UNREAD FLAG IS THE LANDMINE, AND IT IS PINNED: if a later cycle teaches a typedef'd function type to propagate `isNoreturn` to its uses — a reasonable improvement for the ATTRIBUTE spelling — then this KEYWORD spelling would silently begin wrapping calls in `Unreachable`, an execution divergence from gcc on a gcc-clean program. `SemanticAnalyzerC.NoreturnKeywordOnTypedefHeadIsNotPropagatedToUses` asserts the non-propagation directly, so that change goes RED instead of silent.

typedefDeclaratorList.$comment: TF-C88: a comma-separated list of BARE declarators — `declarator (',' declarator)*`, with NO initializer slot and NO per-slot attribute run (see typedefDecl's $tfc88Comment for why both omissions are load-bearing). Declared as `semantics.declarators.plainListRule`, the third list SHAPE the shared declarator walk recognizes (after `listRule` = initDeclaratorList and `memberListRule` = structMemberDeclaratorList — the c23 precedent for adding an OPTIONAL second list role rather than overloading the first). `collectDeclarators` yields its `declaratorRule` children in source order, commas skipped, so Pass-1's declarator-mode minting produces ONE Type symbol per alias with its OWN pointer/array/function suffixes folded onto the shared head — `typedef int *P, A[4], F(void);` types P as int*, A as int[4], F as a function type, which a shared-head star could not do. The repeat's exit is INTRA-rule (the `Comma` lead is unambiguous against the trailing typedefAttrRun's {AttributeKeyword,BracketOpen} and the EndStatement), so nothing becomes speculative.

typedefDeclSpecifiers.$comment: TF-C72: `typedefDecl`'s declaration-specifier prefix — the `typedef` keyword plus any attribute decorations that follow it. Declared as the row's `specifierPrefix`, so decl_prefix_strip.hpp drops it before positional-child counting AND `specifierPrefixChild` hands the subtree to the semantic specifier scans (the `declSpecifiers` on topLevelDecl / `structMemberDeclSpecifiers` on structField pattern). It differs from those two in being MANDATORY rather than `{optional}`: the keyword makes it unconditionally present, which is STRICTLY better here — there is no absent case for the strip to reason about, so the role indices are stable by construction rather than by the optional-then-strip round trip. FIRST WAS {TypedefKeyword} UNTIL P42 AND IS NOW {TypedefKeyword, AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen} — the leading position is admitted, see $p42wLeadingAttrComment. The prediction this sentence used to make was exactly right and is now PAID rather than avoided: FIRST(typedefDecl) does collide with topLevelDecl's `declSpecifiers`, and `topLevel` / `statement` / `extensionTopLevel`'s inner alt are `speculative: true` as a result. Only `attrSpec`/`stdAttr` are admitted — no storage-class keyword — so `typedef thread_local int T;` still fails loud exactly as before (the 6.7.1p2 note below relies on that).
typedefDeclSpecifiers.$p42wLeadingAttrComment:
P42 (D-CSUBSET-LEADING-ATTRIBUTE-BEFORE-TYPEDEF-IS-A-PARSE-ERROR): the FOURTH position — a run BEFORE the keyword — now parses, so the paragraph above's closing clause ('deliberately NOT admitting a decoration BEFORE the keyword') is SUPERSEDED and kept only as the record of why it was deferred. Its reasoning was correct and its conclusion is now paid for rather than avoided: FIRST(typedefDecl) does gain {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen}, it does collide with `topLevelDecl`'s `declSpecifiers`, and `topLevel` / `statement` are therefore marked `speculative: true` — the resolution `detectAmbiguousAlternatives`'s own refusal text prescribes. See `topLevel`'s $p42wSpeculativeComment for why the restructuring alternative was measured and rejected (it would silently drop `__attribute__((weak)) int gv;`'s linkage) and for why the common path costs nothing.
★ THE PREFIX STAYS MANDATORY AND THE ROLE INDICES STAY FIXED. `TypedefKeyword` is still unconditionally present inside this rule, so `typedefDeclSpecifiers` is still always the first visible child and still always stripped by decl_prefix_strip.hpp — the row's `head: 0` / `declarator: 2` are untouched, which is the one property the $comment above says must not move.
★ THE LEADING RUN RIDES THE **SAME** SPECIFIER PREFIX AS THE POST-KEYWORD RUN, so the semantic attribute scan reaches it through `specifierPrefixChild` with no second owner and no new row — which is why `__attribute__((deprecated)) typedef int T;` warns S003D at the alias's USE exactly as the mid position already did (✔MEASURED, both positions, same code, same span rule). Still ONLY `attrSpec`/`stdAttr`: no storage-class keyword is admitted here either, so `thread_local typedef int T;` stays a loud refusal.
★ `stdAttr` IS ADMITTED HERE THOUGH `declAttrRun` EXCLUDES IT, AND THE TWO DECISIONS ARE CONSISTENT BECAUSE THEY REST ON DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS. `declAttrRun`'s exclusion rests on (1) the one reference that accepts `int [[deprecated]] gv;` IGNORES the attribute, and (2) FIRST(stdAttr)={BracketOpen} collides with the declarator's abstract-array lead that immediately follows it. Neither holds here: ✔MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=c2x`) and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c23`) SEPARATELY, `[[deprecated]] typedef int T;` compiles at file AND block scope on BOTH and BOTH warn `'T' is deprecated` at the USE — the attribute is HONOURED, not ignored — and this run is followed by `TypedefKeyword`, not by a declarator, so there is no bracket ambiguity to resolve. DSS now matches: warning[S003D] at the use, ✔MEASURED for `__attribute__((deprecated))` and `[[deprecated]]` alike, at file scope, at block scope, and under `__extension__`.
typedefDeclSpecifiers.$p51NoreturnComment:
P51 [[D-CSUBSET-NORETURN-KEYWORD-PARAMETER-AND-TYPEDEF-POSITIONS]]: the POST-keyword run gains a THIRD branch, `NoreturnKeyword`, so the C11 `_Noreturn` KEYWORD is admitted in a typedef head — `typedef _Noreturn void tfn(void);`. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD: `error[P0009] expected 'Identifier', 'VoidKeyword', … — got '_Noreturn'` plus two cascading P_UnexpectedToken.
★ THE BRANCH IS ADDED TO THE **INLINE** ALT RATHER THAN BY WRAPPING THE RUN IN A NAMED RULE, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT STYLE: a named wrapper would put every already-parsing attribute ONE CST LEVEL DEEPER, which `ParserCSmoke.TypedefPostKeywordAttributeRidesTheSpecifierPrefix` pins as `tok:TypedefKeyword/rule:attrSpec` — MEASURED, the wrapper version turned that pin RED. An inline branch leaves the shape of every previously-accepted input BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the only observable change is the token now admitted. (The parameter position takes the named-rule form instead precisely because ITS run was ALREADY a run of a named rule, so there the swap adds no level either.)
★★ THE REFERENCES SPLIT AND THE DISJUNCTION DECIDES ACCEPTANCE. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-01, each probed SEPARATELY at `-std=c11` AND `-std=c2x`: gcc 13.3.0 ACCEPTS (rc=0, `warning: typedef 'tfn' declared '_Noreturn'`); clang 18.1.3 REJECTS (`error: '_Noreturn' can only appear on functions`); MSVC 19.51 REJECTS (`error C3829`). ONE accepting reference makes PARSING required.
★★ AND gcc DROPS THE SPECIFIER — MEASURED BY DIFFERENTIAL, NOT ASSUMED, because this is the one place the shape could become a silent execution divergence. `typedef _Noreturn void tfn(void); tfn f; int probe(void){ f(); }` draws gcc's `-Wreturn-type` 'control reaches end of non-void function' — BYTE-IDENTICAL to the undecorated control `typedef void tfn(void);` — while the accepted-by-all-three spelling `typedef void tfn(void); _Noreturn tfn f;` draws NO such warning. So gcc honors the keyword on the DECLARATION and drops it on the TYPEDEF: a `_Noreturn` typedef head does NOT make its aliased function type noreturn, in the only reference that compiles it at all. DSS must therefore NOT store the flag from this position. See `typedefDecl`'s `$p51NoreturnStoreComment` for what DSS does today and the named residue.
★ FIRST(the post-keyword repeat) grows {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen} -> {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen, NoreturnKeyword}, still DISJOINT from FIRST(typedefHeadFull) (headQualifier keywords / type keywords / Identifier / struct-union-enum / typeof) — a distinct exact-match keyword — so the repeat still exits on one token and NOTHING became speculative.
★ THE **LEADING** RUN IS DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED, and that is NAMED LOUD RESIDUE, not an oversight: `_Noreturn typedef void tfn(void);` is ✔MEASURED accepted by gcc (same warn-and-ignore) and refused by clang/MSVC, so it IS below the union — but admitting it there would put `NoreturnKeyword` into FIRST(typedefDecl), where it collides with `topLevelDecl`'s `declSpecifiers` (which already admits the keyword) at `/shapes/topLevel`; that is the `C_AmbiguousAlternatives` wall `externSpecifiers`' $tfc77Comment records as its own anchor rather than a variation. It stays a LOUD P0009, never a silent mis-parse.

typedefAttrRun.$comment: TF-C72: a possibly-EMPTY run of attribute specifiers at a fixed position inside `typedefDecl` (used TWICE — before and after the declarator; the `emptyStmt`/`typedefDecl` reuse-one-rule-in-two-positions precedent). A NAMED rule wrapping a lone `{repeat}` rather than a bare inline `{repeat}` precisely SO the node is emitted even when the run matches nothing — that is what keeps the declaration row's `head`/`declarator` indices fixed. FIRST(attrSpec)={AttributeKeyword} is disjoint from FIRST(declarator)={Identifier, ParenOpen, StarOp, BracketOpen}, so the GNU form is predictively decidable and non-speculative. FIRST(stdAttr)={BracketOpen} DOES overlap declarator's abstract-array lead, and the 1-token prune resolves it in stdAttr's favour — harmless because `requireNamedDeclarators` makes a `[`-led declarator invalid in a typedef anyway (C 6.7.8p3: a typedef declares a NAME); MEASURED: `typedef long [3] T;` still fails loud (`expected 'BracketOpen' — got '3'`), never silently mis-parses, and `typedef long A[4];` is untouched because its bracket suffix follows the NAME.

typedefTrailingAttrRun.$comment:
P56 (D-CSUBSET-TRAILING-ATTRIBUTE-RUN-IS-READ-AT-THE-WRONG-GRANULARITY): the AFTER-DECLARATOR-LIST typedef attribute run — position (3) of the three `typedefDecl` describes — SPLIT OUT of `typedefAttrRun` into its own rule name. Byte-identical body; the only thing that changed is that it can now be spoken about separately.
★★★ WHY THE SPLIT WAS FORCED, AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC. `declarationAttrSlotRules` now declares an `appertainsTo` grain PER RULE NAME, and `typedefAttrRun` occupied BOTH the lead position (before the declarator list) and the trailing one (after it) in a single shape — two positions with two DIFFERENT grains under one name, which no per-rule key can describe. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-03, gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 agreeing: `typedef int A, B __attribute__((deprecated));` warns at a use of **B** and is CLEAN at a use of **A** (the trailing run reaches the LAST alias only), while `typedef __attribute__((deprecated)) int A, B;` warns at a use of A (the leading run reaches every alias). One rule name, one grain — the `asmLabelRule` discipline (two roles, two keys) applied to two positions of one run.
★ INDEX STABILITY IS UNTOUCHED, and that is the property this split had to preserve. Like `typedefAttrRun` this is a NAMED rule over a lone `{repeat}`, so it emits its node even when the run is EMPTY. The post-strip role children stay [typedefHeadFull(0), typedefAttrRun(1), typedefDeclaratorList(2), typedefTrailingAttrRun(3), EndStatement(4)] — `head: 0` and `declaratorList: 2` cannot shift, decorated or not.
★ FIRST(typedefTrailingAttrRun) = FIRST(typedefAttrRun) = {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen}, unchanged, and it sits where the second `typedefAttrRun` sat — so every FIRST-set and predictive-decidability argument `typedefAttrRun`’s own comment makes about that position carries over verbatim. Nothing became speculative.

declAttrRun.$comment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): a possibly-EMPTY run of GNU attribute specifiers between an object/function declaration's TYPE HEAD and its init-declarator list — `static int SQLITE_NOINLINE walIndexPage(…)` (the MODE-2 sqlite spelling: 20 of its 119 `SQLITE_NOINLINE` sites, = 16 × `static T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(` + 4 × `T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(`) and `int __attribute__((weak)) gv;`.
★ CENSUS SCOPE, STATED SO THE TWO FIGURES CANNOT BE CONFUSED AGAIN: 119 counts sqlite's `.c` files ONLY and splits 90/9/16/4 = mode 3 (`static SQLITE_NOINLINE T f(`) / leading / `static T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(` / `T SQLITE_NOINLINE f(`; including the 3 `.h` prototype sites gives 122 = 90/10/16/6, i.e. 22 in mode 2. The figure 99 that used to sit here is NOT this slot's — it is MODE 3 (90) plus the 9 leading sites, a position this rule does not cover. Used TWICE, in `topLevelDecl` and in BOTH branches of the block-scope `varDecl` (the `typedefAttrRun` reuse-one-rule-in-two-positions precedent), because ONE attribute must not mean two different things depending on scope. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD both were P0009 ('expected Identifier, ParenOpen, StarOp, EndStatement, BracketOpen or BlockOpen — got __attribute__').
★ A NAMED RULE OVER A LONE `{repeat}`, NOT a bare inline repeat, for THREE independent load-bearing reasons: (1) the node is emitted even when the run is EMPTY, so the declaration rows' positional indices are CONSTANT rather than shifting by the number of attributes present; (2) the rule NAME is how each row's `declarationAttrSlotRules` selects it, which is what routes it to the semantic attribute scan AND (via `linkagePrefixRoots`) to the HIR linkage fold; (3) the repeat's exit stays INTRA-rule, so `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` never compares the loop body against the parent's continuation.
★ IT IS A SIBLING OF THE HEAD, NEVER A CHILD OF IT. Putting this run inside `topLevelHead`/`declHead` would place the attribute inside the TYPE-RESOLVED head, and `resolveTypeNodeImpl` is first-child-that-resolves-wins with a token arm that resolves ANY identifier through the scope chain — so `typedef int weak; int __attribute__((weak)) gv = 3;` would silently resolve `gv` to the typedef. That is the SILENT MISCOMPILE `D-CSUBSET-TYPEDEF-HEAD-DECORATION-TYPE-HIJACK` exists to prevent, and the anti-hijack pin in test_parser_c_smoke.cpp asserts against it.
★★ `stdAttr` IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, AND ITS ORIGINAL JUSTIFICATION WAS RE-MEASURED IN P34 AND FOUND HALF WRONG — THE EXCLUSION STANDS, ON A DIFFERENT GROUND. It used to read: MEASURED with `/usr/bin/clang -std=c23 -fsyntax-only`, `int [[deprecated]] gv;` is an ERROR ('deprecated attribute cannot be applied to types'), so admitting it would make DSS accept C that NO TOOLCHAIN DOES. That last clause is FALSE. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-25 across the whole roster at `-std=c2x`: clang 19.1.1 and clang 18.1.3 do refuse it, but gcc 13.3.0 ACCEPTS it (`warning: 'deprecated' attribute ignored [-Wattributes]`), at file scope and at block scope alike. ONE reference accepting is enough under the bar, so this P0009 IS a (small) divergence and must not be recorded as conformance. ⚠ The lesson is the one this repository keeps paying for: a ONE-compiler probe is not a roster verdict. ★ WHAT THE EXCLUSION ACTUALLY RESTS ON. (1) VALUE — the single reference that accepts the form IGNORES the attribute, so admitting it would buy a parse plus an 'it was ignored' warning and nothing else; the DECLARATOR position `int x [[deprecated]];`, which every reference HONOURS, already carries the idiom and already works here (✔MEASURED, warning[S003D]). (2) COST — `FIRST(stdAttr)` is {BracketOpen}, which is also `FIRST(declarator)`'s abstract-array lead, and this run sits immediately before the declarator list: the same overlap `typedefAttrRun` and `paramTrailingAttrRun` each record. ⚠ `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` would NOT catch it — it compares ALT branches, and a repeat's exit against its parent's continuation is not an alt, as this rule's own third reason for being a named rule already says. With `attrSpec` alone FIRST(declAttrRun) = {AttributeKeyword}, DISJOINT from FIRST(declarator) = {Identifier, ParenOpen, StarOp, BracketOpen} and from the {BlockOpen, EndStatement} tails, so the run stays predictively decidable and non-speculative. The residue is NAMED and LOUD (a positioned P0009), never a silent drop.

typedefHead.$comment: SPECULATIVE: the struct/union/enum BODY forms collide with the ref forms on their lead keyword — body forms probe FIRST (declared order); `typedef struct P MyP;` rolls back to structTypeRef when no `{` follows. lookahead 256 (4096-token budget): a body probe must swallow the whole member list. D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF: `typeofSpecifier` (keyword-led, disjoint FIRST) admits `typedef typeof(x) T;`.

externDecl.$p53ScopeNarrowedComment: ★★★ P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS) — READ THIS BEFORE THE PARAGRAPHS BELOW: THIS RULE IS NOW BLOCK-SCOPE ONLY. It was removed from `/shapes/topLevel` and from `extensionTopLevel`'s inner alt; `topLevelDecl` owns every file-scope declaration, `extern` included, because two declaration branches on one lead token cannot both survive a long body at ANY alt order (✔MEASURED, P53 lane `ex` — see `/shapes/topLevel`'s `$p53ExternMergedComment`). The rule survives UNCHANGED for `statement`/`extensionDeclStmt` (D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-EXTERN), where it is still the unique owner of the `extern` lead because `localDeclSpecifier` does not admit the keyword, and where the block-scope BINDING (C 6.2.1 shadow correctness) is exactly what a merge into `varDecl` would destroy. ⚠ EVERY SENTENCE BELOW THAT SAYS 'FILE SCOPE' IS HISTORY, and two are now false as written: `FIRST(externDecl) stays {ExternKeyword}` is still true but no longer says anything about `/shapes/topLevel`; and 'The REVERSE order `thread_local extern` stays a loud parse error (topLevelDecl's head never matches `extern`)' is FALSE AT FILE SCOPE since P53 — every ordering parses there — while it remains true INSIDE A BLOCK, which is this rule's only remaining position. The file-scope halves of D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR / D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-LIBRARY-SYNTAX / D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-FN-DEFINITION / D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-INCOMPLETE-ARRAY are all served by `topLevelDecl` now, using the SAME semantics facets and the SAME `lowerExternDeclInto`; nothing was reimplemented.
externDecl.$comment: D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-FN-DEFINITION (§B 2026-07-21): the trailing `externDeclTail` (a `{ block | EndStatement }` alt, the twin of `topLevelDeclTail`) admits `extern` on a FUNCTION DEFINITION — `extern int f(void){…}` (valid C 6.9.1, symmetric with `static int f(){…}`; the Tcl `EXTERN int Sqlite3_Init(…){…}` shape). A `block` tail → a function definition with EXTERNAL linkage (via the row's `kindByChild`, effectiveKind Function, a DEFINING symbol); an `EndStatement` tail → the ordinary non-defining declaration below.
