See externDeclTail for the disambiguation + fail-loud notes. c23 D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR (SQLite testfixture arc, 2026-07-18): a C 6.7 extern declaration is `extern` + a decl-specifier HEAD + an init-declarator LIST + `;` — the extern-flavored twin of `topLevelDecl`. SUPERSEDES the legacy single-declarator spine (`externSpecifiers typeRef Identifier externTail`), which bound exactly ONE `name` at a fixed child index and P0009'd on `extern int a, b;` (test1.c:9341 `extern int sqlite3_sync_count, sqlite3_fullsync_count;`). The head is `typeRefAllowingStruct` — the SAME star-free base-type head struct FIELDS use (base type + cv-qualifiers, NO pointer stars): pointer stars MUST bind PER-DECLARATOR (inside each slot's `declarator` pointerLayer) so `extern int *a, b;` types a as int* and b as int (a shared-head star would mis-type b). It admits struct/union/enum aggregates (D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-AGGREGATE-TYPE preserved — typeBaseAllowingStruct carries the same specifiers the retired `typeBase` did) + typedef-names + typeof + a `volatile` head (a strict gain over the retired `typeRef`, which had const only). The `initDeclaratorList` is the PROVEN `initDeclarator (, initDeclarator)*` list every object declaration uses; each `declarator` owns its pointer/array/fn suffix, so a function prototype (`extern int f(int);` — a declarator with an fnSuffix), an incomplete-array object (`extern char v[];`), and a mixed list (`extern int a, *p, g[4], h(void);`) ALL parse through ONE list — no bespoke func-vs-object tail. Pass-1 routes through the DECLARATOR-MODE minting (head:0/declaratorList:1) which mints N `nonDefiningDeclaration` symbols; CST→HIR's `lowerExternDeclInto` emits N ExternGlobal/ExternFunction nodes (one per declarator). FIRST(externDecl) stays {ExternKeyword} (unique-production direct descent, non-speculative). TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): child 0 stays the `externSpecifiers` HEAD WRAPPER (`extern` + an optional thread-storage run) so `extern thread_local int e;` parses (C11 6.7.1p3); it is the row's `specifierPrefix` (stripped before the head:0/list:1 count, so the indices are stable whether or not a specifier is present). The REVERSE order `thread_local extern` stays a loud parse error (topLevelDecl's head never matches `extern`). D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-LIBRARY-SYNTAX: a TRAILING `{optional stringLiteralExpr}` after the list carries the DSS per-declaration import-library override (`extern void* GetStdHandle(int) "kernel32.dll";` — examples/c/hello_writefile); FIRST(stringLiteralExpr) = string-openers, DISJOINT from Comma/`=`/`;`, so the list stops before it (non-speculative) and it applies to EVERY declarator in this declaration. CST→HIR's `lowerExternDeclInto` decodes it (extractLibraryOverride) into each emitted extern's import-library map. It sits AFTER initDeclaratorList so it never shifts the head:0/list:1 indices.

externDeclTail.$comment: D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-FN-DEFINITION (SQLite testfixture MAIN harness, §B 2026-07-21): the extern-declaration TAIL — the extern twin of `topLevelDeclTail`. A `block` tail makes the declaration a FUNCTION DEFINITION with EXTERNAL linkage (`extern int f(void){…}` — the Tcl `EXTERN int Sqlite3_Init(Tcl_Interp*){…}` shape, ×14 in tclsqlite-ex.c; `EXTERN` is the tcl.json macro → `extern`); an `EndStatement` tail makes it the ordinary non-defining declaration (`extern int a, b;` / a prototype / an object ref / the `"kernel32.dll"` import-library override — BYTE-IDENTICAL to pre-cycle, only the `;` token now rides this wrapper). FIRST(block)={BlockOpen} vs FIRST(EndStatement)={Semicolon} are DISJOINT, so the alt is predictively decided — NON-speculative, exactly like `topLevelDeclTail`. The `{optional stringLiteralExpr}` library override sits BEFORE this tail (a per-DECLARATION override) so it stays a DIRECT role child (externLibraryOverride's scan is unchanged); it is decl-only, so the pathological `extern int f() "lib" {…}` — a body AND an override — is caught FAIL-LOUD at HIR (H_ExternDeclMalformed, cst_to_hir lowerExternDeclInto), never a silent body-drop. externDecl's semantics row gains `kindByChild` (childPath [2,0] = this tail's block child → whenKind function); when a body is present the SHARED declarator-mode minting upgrades effectiveKind to Function (a DEFINING symbol, isExtern suppressed) and CST→HIR lowers a real Function (body emitted) via the same path topLevelDecl's function-definition arm uses. externDecl is added to `scopes` (the empty scope is harmless for a plain declaration — the topLevelDecl precedent — and dominates the params+body for a definition, via the generic declNodeIsFunctionDefinition scope logic). A function DEFINITION in BLOCK scope (a nested function via `extern` — not valid C) fails LOUD (cst_to_hir block-scope ExternDecl guard), never a silent hoist.

externSpecifiers.$comment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): `extern` plus an optional storage-specifier run — the thread-storage twins (`extern thread_local` / `extern _Thread_local`) and, since TF-C77, a GNU attribute run. FIRST(repeat) = {ThreadLocalKeyword, ThreadLocalC23Keyword, AttributeKeyword}, DISJOINT from FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct) (type keywords / Identifier / typeof / struct/union/enum) → predictively pruned, non-speculative. As externDecl's specifierPrefix this subtree is scanned by linkageFrom: the row maps both thread-local spellings to {threadStorage:true} and ignores ExternKeyword by kind (the extern-ness is the RULE's identity — externDecl mints a non-defining declaration — not a linkage entry).
externSpecifiers.$tfc77Comment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 1): `attrSpec` joins the run so the glibc/Tcl AFTER-KEYWORD shape `extern __attribute__((__noreturn__)) void die(int);` parses. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD it was P0009 ('expected Identifier, VoidKeyword, … — got __attribute__').
★ THE ATTRIBUTE RIDES INSIDE THIS HEAD WRAPPER, NEVER BEFORE `ExternKeyword`. FIRST(externDecl) MUST stay {ExternKeyword}: putting a decoration ahead of the keyword would put AttributeKeyword in FIRST(externDecl), colliding with `topLevelDecl`'s `{optional declSpecifiers}` (whose alts include `attrSpec`) at `/shapes/topLevel`, and the loader REFUSES that — MEASURED with a throwaway patched config tree, adding `ExternKeyword` to `singleDeclSpecifier` gives `error[C_AmbiguousAlternatives] at /shapes/topLevel: alt branches share FIRST token 'ExternKeyword'` + `D_SchemaLoadFailed`, at LOAD time, exit 1. The wall is real and loud, not silent — so the leading-position order `__attribute__((...)) extern int g;` is its own anchor, not a variation of this one.
★ ZERO NEW WIRING, AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS SAFE. `externSpecifiers` IS this row's `specifierPrefix` and is MANDATORY (it owns the keyword), so it is ALWAYS `kids.front()` and ALWAYS returned by `specifierPrefixChild` — every prefix consumer already reaches it: `linkageFrom` (via `linkagePrefixRoots`, so `weak` and `visibility("hidden")` are HONORED and an unknown name is loud H000C), `scanAttributeSemantics`, and `specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn` (which is what makes the `TCL_NORETURN`-shaped spelling actually MEAN noreturn rather than merely parse).
★ `stdAttr` is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. MEASURED with `/usr/bin/clang -std=c23 -fsyntax-only`: `extern [[deprecated]] int dg;` is an ERROR ('an attribute list cannot appear here'). Admitting it would make DSS accept C that no toolchain does. The exclusion also keeps FIRST(repeat) free of BracketOpen, so nothing here can collide with an abstract array declarator.
externSpecifiers.$tfc79Comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4p7): `InlineKeyword` joins the run so `extern inline int f(int){…}` and the DECLARATION form `extern inline int f(int);` parse. FIRST(repeat) gains InlineKeyword, still disjoint from FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct), so the prune stays predictive. The keyword rides INSIDE this head wrapper for the same reason `attrSpec` does — FIRST(externDecl) must stay {ExternKeyword}. MEASURED with clang: `extern inline int p(int){…}` emits `T _p` (a real external definition), which is what this row already produces via its `block`-tail function-definition path — so no emission override is needed here, only the ignore-by-kind entry below.
externSpecifiers.$p53NoreturnComment: P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS, the half that CAN close here): `NoreturnKeyword` joins the run, so `extern _Noreturn void die(int);` parses. ✔MEASURED at P53's base it was `P_NoAlternativeMatched … got '_Noreturn'` — the keyword was simply missing from a run that already carried `inline` and both thread-local spellings — while gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x`, clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` and MSVC 19.51 `/std:clatest`, probed SEPARATELY, all accept and RUN it. FIRST(repeat) gains NoreturnKeyword, still disjoint from FIRST(typeRefAllowingStruct), so the prune stays predictive; FIRST(externDecl) is UNCHANGED at {ExternKeyword}, which is the property the note below is about. It also needs the row's `linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds` entry — see there.
externSpecifiers.$p53OrderRefutedComment:
★★★ P53 — WHY THE OTHER HALF OF D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS IS NOT DONE HERE, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. C 6.7.1 makes the declaration specifiers an unordered SET, and DSS still refuses `inline extern`, `__inline extern`, `_Thread_local extern`, `thread_local extern` and `_Noreturn extern` while accepting all five mirror images (✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI; gcc, clang and MSVC accept and RUN every one). The obvious repair — a companion run BEFORE `ExternKeyword` inside this shape — WAS IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED IN P53 AND IT REGRESSES THE COMPILER, so it was reverted.
★ WHAT BREAKS, WITH THE NUMBER. A leading `{repeat}` is NULLABLE, so `externDecl`'s entry position becomes a nullable variable-width element and `computePredictivePrefixes` STOPS WITHOUT RECORDING (that is its documented soundness guard: a nullable stop element's true admissible set is FIRST(stop) ∪ FIRST(continuation), so recording the narrower set could drop a candidate that legitimately matches). `predictivePrefixLen(externDecl)` is then < 2 and `predictivePrefixPrunes` returns false for EVERY input — the LL(k) prune can no longer separate `inline int …` from `inline extern int …`. Both branches survive at `/shapes/topLevel`, the UNIQUE-PRODUCTION DIRECT DESCENT is lost, and `topLevelDecl` is entered through a SPECULATIVE PROBE whose budget is `lookahead × 16` = 8 × 16 = 128 tokens — while the probe must swallow the whole function BODY. ✔MEASURED by bisecting body size: `inline int payload(int x){…}` compiles at 0, 1, 2 and 4 statements and FAILS from 8 statements upward, at every size tested to 256. Every non-static `inline` function definition in real C is bigger than four statements.
★★ THIS IS [[D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-BEFORE-EXTERN-KEYWORD]]'s ESCAPE (i) REFUTATION, ARRIVING FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION AND WITH A MEASUREMENT. That row rejected 'make topLevel speculative' because a top-level probe must swallow whole function definitions; P42 then made `/shapes/topLevel` speculative anyway and it was affordable for exactly ONE reason — every lead token still had a UNIQUE 1-token FIRST, so the predictive prune left one candidate and nothing probed. Widening FIRST(externDecl) is what actually spends that budget. ⇒ **FIRST(externDecl) MUST STAY {ExternKeyword}** — TF-C77's constraint is still binding, though its ORIGINAL reason (the C_AmbiguousAlternatives load refusal) is indeed stale: `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` exempts speculative alts, so the loader now accepts the overlap and the parser pays for it at runtime instead.
★★★ THE ONE DESIGN LEFT, and it is that row's escape (ii): FACTOR THE SHARED PREFIX so `extern` is an ordinary `singleDeclSpecifier` in ONE declaration rule that admits both heads and discriminates AFTER the prefix. It is strictly BETTER than today rather than a trade — with no competing branch there is exactly one candidate for every lead token, so nothing probes at all — and it is the only shape that makes the specifier set genuinely unordered. Its cost is real and is why it is not a side change: `externDecl` is `nonDefiningDeclaration` with `allowFlexibleArray`, its own `linkageSpecifiers`, its own child indices and its own asm-label slot, so the merged row needs a CONDITIONAL non-defining facet keyed on the specifier, and it moves every `extern` declaration in the corpus, the FFI import-synthesis route and the shipped header surface at once.
⚠ Enumerating `InlineKeyword ExternKeyword` / `NoreturnKeyword ExternKeyword` / … as separate two-token-lead rules WOULD restore the prune (a literal TokenLeaf lead gives prefixLen 2). It is rejected: four declaration rows duplicating one row's facets, that must never drift, supporting one leading specifier and not two — a workaround, not an implementation.

initValue.$comment: FC5: assignmentExpr (NOT expression) — the comma-gate. Covers ALL three initializer consumers (initDeclarator, structField, braceInitList initElement), so `int a = b, c;` stays 2 declarators (not `a = (b,c)`).

arrayDeclSuffix.$comment: VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA, C99 §6.7.6.2/6.7.6.3): the ONE array-declarator suffix `[ … ]`, SHARED across EVERY declarator-mode row (param, varDecl, structField, typedefDecl, forDecl, externDecl). It admits the C99 array-PARAMETER decorations — a leading `static` and/or cv-qualifier run before the length BOUND (`int a[static 3]`, `int a[const n]`, `int a[const static 10]`). These are legal ONLY inside a function-parameter declarator; a NON-param use is a constraint violation caught SEMANTICALLY (the paramDecay-gated S_ArrayParamQualifierNonParameter), mirroring the typeSpecifierSeq → S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination discipline — the parser is deliberately permissive rather than forking a param-only sub-grammar. The qualifier run is INLINE keyword tokens (they land as DIRECT children, like typeSpecifierSeq's specifier run) and is FIRST-disjoint from the bound (no expression begins with static/const/volatile/restrict), so it is NON-speculative — a plain leading run before the unchanged `{optional expression}` bound. `int a[*p]` (a deref-sized VLA, LEGAL) keeps parsing `*p` as the bound EXPRESSION (unchanged). The bound's CST position is NO LONGER a fixed index (a leading qualifier shifts it) — every bound-locating site skips the decorations via the shared arraySuffixBoundNode helper keyed on DeclaratorConfig.arraySuffixModifierTokens. LANDED (D-CSUBSET-VLA-PARAM-STAR): the bare unspecified-size `*` form `int a[*]` (a prototype VLA-parameter marker) is admitted via the DISTINCT `arrayStarSuffix` = `[BracketOpen,StarOp,BracketClose]` rule (NOT this `arrayDeclSuffix`) + the speculative-repeat-alt schema-compiler engine fix (grammar_schema_json.cpp propagates `speculative` onto an inline repeat-alt's loopEntry, so the suffix repeat probes `arrayStarSuffix` then rolls back CLEANLY to this `arrayDeclSuffix` for a real bound). `int a[*p]` (a deref-sized VLA, LEGAL) still parses `*p` as THIS rule's bound EXPRESSION — the star-modifier is its own fixed-3-token rule, so this flat bound locator is UNTOUCHED. `StarOp` also stays in arraySuffixModifierTokens (the arraySuffixBoundNode scan skips a stray `*`).

arrayStarSuffix.$comment: VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA, C99 §6.7.6.2p4): the bare unspecified-size `[ * ]` array-declarator suffix — a prototype-form VLA-parameter marker. A FIXED 3-token sequence with its OWN CST node (distinct from arrayDeclSuffix), so the flat bound-locator / lengthChild / captureVlaSize sites that read arrayDeclSuffix's children are UNTOUCHED. It sits BEFORE arrayDeclSuffix in the SPECULATIVE suffix repeat (directDeclarator/abstractDirectDeclarator): `[*]` matches here; a real bound (`[N]`, or the deref-VLA `[*p]` whose `*p` is an expression) fails at the `]` / `*` position and the speculative loopEntry rolls back CLEANLY to arrayDeclSuffix (enabled by the schema-compiler honoring `speculative` on an inline repeat-alt). Semantics: an arrayStarSuffix suffix decays to a pointer EXACTLY like an absent-length `[]` for a parameter; a NON-parameter `[*]` is a constraint violation caught by the SAME paramDecay-gated S_ArrayParamQualifierNonParameter (0xE054).

typeSpecifierSeq.$comment: FC3 c1: C 6.7.2 type-specifier run — one-or-more specifier KEYWORDS in any order (`unsigned long long int` == `long long unsigned int` == `long unsigned long`). The inner alt is INLINE (no named wrapper rule) so the matched keyword TOKENS land as typeSpecifierSeq's DIRECT children — the semantic engine's multiset arm requires all-token children. Which multisets are VALID (and what core each resolves to, per data model) is the semantics.typeSpecifiers table; invalid combos (`unsigned float`, `short long`) parse fine here and reject SEMANTICALLY by absence from the table (S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination). The seq SUBSUMES the former single-token Void/Int/Long/Char alts (a one-keyword run). Keyword-led, so castExpr's commitRequiresTypeName triage rule 1 (not-a-lone-identifier) always commits a seq-led cast type. D-CSUBSET-BITINT: the `bitIntSpecifier` rule (`_BitInt(N)`) joins the element alt so `unsigned _BitInt(40)` parses as ONE run [unsigned-token, bitIntSpecifier-node] — keyword-led + FIRST-disjoint, so it only adds `_BitInt` to the element FIRST set (no speculation). A run CONTAINING a bitIntSpecifier is NOT all-tokens → the multiset arm skips it and the semantic engine's bitInt arm (semantics.bitInt) resolves it, scanning the sibling signedness tokens. D-CSUBSET-UINT128-TYPE (TF-C94): the three 128-bit spellings join the element alt as PLAIN TOKENS (Int128Keyword `__int128`, Int128TypeKeyword `__int128_t`, UInt128TypeKeyword `__uint128_t`) — unlike bitIntSpecifier they carry no sub-node, so a run containing them stays ALL-TOKENS and resolves through the ORDINARY semantics.typeSpecifiers multiset arm (`unsigned __int128` is just the {UnsignedKeyword, Int128Keyword} multiset). ★ MEASURED: they must appear in BOTH the leading alt AND its `repeat` twin — the two arrays are independent, and adding them to only one breaks exactly the orderings that lead with the OTHER keyword (`unsigned __int128` parses but `__int128 unsigned` does not, or vice versa). Keyword-led + FIRST-disjoint like every sibling here, so no speculation is introduced.

typeBaseAllowingStruct.$comment: FC7 D-FC7-NESTED-STRUCT-FIELD: the trailing `Identifier` alt admits a typedef-name (user struct/union type) as a struct/union FIELD type. A struct/union body has no expression-statement context, so a bare Identifier in field-type position is UNAMBIGUOUSLY a type-name (no binder-sketch guard needed); a non-type name fails loud at semantic scope-lookup. Tried last, so keyword/tag/enum forms keep priority. D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-BODY-VARDECL-POSITION: also admits the struct/union/enum BODY forms (an inline nested definition `struct Inner { int x; } in;` as a field) — SPECULATIVE (mirror typedefHead), body-before-ref. This makes the body-in-head form RECURSIVE: a structSpecifierBody contains structFields, each of which may itself BE a structSpecifierBody (arbitrary nesting), the recursion falling out of the grammar — single-level speculation at each structField, never nested. c23 D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR: also the extern-declaration head type-base (via `typeRefAllowingStruct`), so an aggregate extern (`extern struct Foo g;`) resolves through the SAME arms — the retired `typeBase` sibling folded into this rule.

typeRefAllowingStruct.$comment: c23 (D-CSUBSET-STRUCT-MULTI-DECLARATOR): the struct/union member-head TYPE-SPECIFIER (base type + cv-qualifiers ONLY — NO pointer stars). The head qualifier slot is `{repeat headQualifier}` (= const|volatile) so a member head admits `volatile int isInterrupted;` (the SQLite case) and `const volatile`; mirrors the head-qualifier slots on topLevelHead/declHead/kwDeclHead. ★ The prior `{repeat StarOp}` slot was REMOVED: with the c23 member-declarator LIST, pointer stars MUST bind PER-DECLARATOR (inside each slot's `declarator` pointerLayer) — a head star applies to ALL declarators, so `int *a, b;` would wrongly type b as a pointer too (the silent layout miscompile c23 fixes). Each slot's `declarator` now owns its stars, exactly like every other declaration position (params/locals/globals). A head-position volatile FOLLOWED by a declarator `*` is a pointer-to-volatile-POINTEE — still rejected loud S_VolatilePointeeNotSupported by the per-declarator typing arm (head volatile + declarator star), so the reject stays complete. The TRAILING slot is `{repeat headQualifier}` (= const|volatile|atomic), SYMMETRIC with the leading slot AND with topLevelHead's trailing `{repeat headQualifier}` — C 6.7.1: decl-specifiers may appear in ANY order, so a base + EAST qualifier run (`int const`, `LONG volatile`, `int const volatile`, west of any declarator star) is a legal type head. It SUPERSEDES the prior `{optional ConstKeyword}` (const-only), which admitted only EAST `const` and P0009'd at a trailing `volatile`/`_Atomic` on either a typedef-name OR a builtin base — `extern LONG volatile sqlite3_os_type;` (D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR; test1.c:9346, `LONG` = windows.json) and `struct S { int volatile x; };` both failed although the leading forms (`volatile LONG` / `volatile int`) parsed. The trailing qualifier is read by the SAME whole-head-subtree const scan (declaratorObjectIsConst) + before-first-star volatile-base scan the leading slot uses (semantic_analyzer.cpp; typeRefAllowingStruct has no head star, so every qualifier child is scanned) — position-agnostic, no new semantic wiring. East const/volatile on a POINTER (`int * const`, `int * volatile`) still rides the per-declarator ptrQualifier.

varDecl.$comment: The COMMITTED local declaration statement — its FIRST set has NO Identifier (the bare-typedef-name form lives in declOrExprStmt). Branch 1: storage-class-specifier-led (`register T x;` — the specifier commits the decl, so the head admits the typedef-name arm); branch 2: qualifier-or-keyword-led (`const T x;` / `int x;`). Inline branches keep the children flat: [localDeclSpecifiers?, head, initDeclaratorList?, ;] — the row's specifierPrefix strip makes head=0/list=1 stable.
varDecl.$c28Comment: c28 D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-TYPE-DEFINITION: the `initDeclaratorList` is OPTIONAL — mirroring the top-level `topLevelDecl` (init-declarator-list?). A bare BLOCK-SCOPED struct/union/enum DEFINITION with no declarator (`struct Sublist { int nList; ht_slot *aList; };` as a STATEMENT inside a function — sqlite3.c:68508 walMergesort) routes through the kwDeclHead branch (Struct/Union/EnumKeyword-led → the unified c25 structSpec/unionSpec/enumSpec defines the type via `definesWhenChild`, minting the tag into the ENCLOSING BLOCK scope), takes NO declarator, and ends at EndStatement. A NON-defining no-declarator local (`int;`) parses + types but FAILS LOUD at HIR lowering (S_DeclarationDeclaresNothing) — the SAME tier + diagnostic as the top-level no-declarator path (CST→HIR's lowerVarLikeInto: no named declarator AND no composite specifier in the head ⇒ declares nothing). identVarDecl's list is deliberately NOT made optional (a bare typedef-name `T;` must stay an expression statement, NOT a no-declarator decl); only the keyword/specifier-led varDecl needs it (the struct/union/enum definition is keyword-led).
varDecl.$tfc77Comment: TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): `declAttrRun` — the mid-position attribute slot — joins BOTH branches, because ONE attribute must not mean two different things depending on SCOPE. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD, `int __attribute__((aligned(16))) x = 1;` inside a body was P0009 while the identical file-scope spelling was about to become legal; that asymmetry is the defect this branch-pair closes. The run sits AFTER the head in both branches, so the alt's own 1-token discrimination (FIRST(localDeclSpecifiers) vs FIRST(kwDeclHead)) is UNCHANGED and neither branch becomes speculative. Post-strip role children in BOTH branches are [head(0), declAttrRun(1), initDeclaratorList(2), EndStatement(3)] — the row's `declaratorList` moved 1 → 2 in the same commit. Branch 2 has no `specifierPrefix` to strip, and the always-emitted `declAttrRun` is what makes the two branches agree on the indices anyway.

autoInferredVarDecl.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE, C23 6.7.9): the HEAD-LESS initializer-inferred declaration statement (`auto y = 42;`). NO declHead — the pre-existing varDecl path can never parse this form (declHead's bare-Identifier alt greedily reads `y` as a TYPE name → P0009). The specifier prefix is REQUIRED (localDeclSpecifiers is non-nullable) and semantically GATED: the declaration row's `requiredSpecifierToken: AutoKeyword` makes the Pass-1.5 inference arm fail LOUD when no `auto` is present, so C89 implicit-int shapes (`static x = 5;` / `register y = 2;` / `alignas(4) z = 9;` / `[[maybe_unused]] w = 3;`) that parse into this rule STAY errors — pinned. Probed FIRST in declOrAttrStmt (see its $fc175Comment for the C2 order rationale): it fast-fails (≤3 tokens) on every real-typed declaration (`static int x` — `int` is not a declarator), so ordinary decls pay one cheap probe only when specifier-led.

autoInferredForDecl.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): the for-init mirror of autoInferredVarDecl — same shape MINUS the `;` (the for grammar owns it), exactly as forDecl mirrors varDecl. `for (auto i = 0; …)` is VALID C23 (6.8.5p3 admits auto in a for-init). Its declaration row copies forDecl's StaticKeyword gatedMarker so `for (static auto i = 0;;)` stays gated loud (6.8.5p3 violation).

identVarDecl.$comment: The bare-typedef-name declaration statement (`T x, *p;`). The PreferType commit guard (bare-string form — the FC2 triage): sketch-known Type commits, known Value rolls back (`a * b;` stays a multiplication), unknown runs the follower-operator test (`T x;` commits — `x` continues no value reading; `a * b;` rolls back — `*` does) and records the cross-file-oracle candidate on rollback.

declOrExprStmt.$comment: The C statement ambiguity site: FC5 prepends labelStmt (`Identifier Colon …` — a 2-token commit point disjoint from identVarDecl/exprStmt, neither of which has Colon in 2nd position), then identVarDecl BEFORE exprStmt (declared probe order is authoritative — the FC4 c0 fix). lookahead 256 (= 4096-token probe budget, vs the operand alt's 64): the identVarDecl probe must swallow an entire declaration INCLUDING initializer expressions and brace-init lists before its frame closes.
declOrExprStmt.$p31ExtensionComment:
P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): `extensionDeclStmt` joins the alt, DECLARED FIRST — the BLOCK-SCOPE half of the `__extension__` prefix. ★★ IT LIVES HERE, AND NOT IN `statement`'S ALT NOR IN `declOrAttrStmt`'S, BECAUSE `__extension__` IS THE ONE WORD THAT LEADS **BOTH** A DECLARATION STATEMENT AND AN EXPRESSION STATEMENT. `statement` is NON-speculative and its loader refuses branches with overlapping FIRST sets; `exprStmt` (this alt's own last branch) already carries ExtensionKeyword through `expression` → `operand` → `extensionExpr`. Putting the declaration reading anywhere ELSE in `statement` therefore puts ExtensionKeyword in TWO of `statement`'s branches at once — ✔MEASURED, the `declOrAttrStmt` draft failed the load with `C_AmbiguousAlternatives at /shapes/statement: alt branches share FIRST token 'ExtensionKeyword'`, this file's own FC17 refutation happening again one keyword later. Housing BOTH readings under THIS already-speculative branch keeps `statement` disjoint and makes the ambiguity site the one place that resolves it — which is what this rule is named for.
★ ORDER IS THE PRECEDENCE RULE, and it matches both references ✔MEASURED: `__extension__ int x = 0;` is a DECLARATION and `__extension__ x = 0;` is an EXPRESSION statement (gcc 13.3.0 and clang 19.1.7 accept both). The declaration reading is probed first; when every inner declaration production fails, the probe rolls back and `exprStmt` reads the same tokens as `(__extension__ x) = 0`.
★ No ordinary statement pays for this: a lead that is not ExtensionKeyword never reaches the new branch.

gotoStmt.$comment: D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO: `goto label;` (C 6.8.6.1) OR the GNU extension `goto *expr;` (indirect branch to a computed code address). Two alternatives, mirroring sizeofExpr's 2-alt triage. The leading `*` is consumed as GOTO-STATEMENT syntax — so `gotoIndirect`'s operand is the pointer expression `expr` itself (NOT a deref), distinct from the prec-90 prefix `*`. `gotoLabel` keeps the FC5 plain form; the label-vs-indirect choice is unambiguous on the token AFTER `goto` (Identifier+EndStatement is a label; StarOp begins an indirect target). Both lower in cst_to_hir (gotoLabel→GotoStmt, gotoIndirect→IndirectGotoStmt).

labelStmt.$c31Comment: D-CSUBSET-LABEL-BUDGET-CLIFF (p19 Cluster G c31): the shape STAYS `Identifier Colon statement` so a label stays correct in every context, incl. a braceless control-flow body (`if(x) L: s;` — `s` IS the if's body). `commitAfterPrefix` is a PEG cut: after `Identifier Colon` no other declOrExprStmt alt (identVarDecl/exprStmt — neither has Colon in 2nd position) can match, so once the rule's fixed leading token-prefix is consumed in the probe (predictivePrefixLen = 3: `Identifier`, `Colon`, plus the first `statement` token — one harmless extra token, still far under budget) the parser COMMITS and parses the (arbitrarily large) `statement` child NON-speculatively, off the lookahead*16 probe budget. Without it a labeled statement >4096 tokens (sqlite3.c:213922 `json_parse_restart:` before a ~900-case switch) exhausts the budget → rollback → exprStmt → P0001 'got :'.

attributeDeclaration.$comment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-STATEMENT, C23 6.8.1): the BARE attribute-declaration statement — `[[fallthrough]];` / `__attribute__((fallthrough));` — one-or-more attribute specifiers followed by `;`. REUSES `compositeAttrList` verbatim (audit-verified side-effect-free: `scanCompositePacked` runs ONLY from a structSpec/unionSpec node, never from a statement). SEMANTICS: the construct is a no-op at runtime — its hirLowering row maps to Skip (the emptyStmt precedent, zero C++); the semantic tier (pass2Post's bareStatementRule arm) runs the attribute scan over it for the UNKNOWN-standard-attribute warning only (facts discarded — no symbol to mark). DSS emits no fallthrough-placement warning to suppress, so `[[fallthrough]]` is semantics-neutral by construction (design note F7).

declOrAttrStmt.$comment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-STATEMENT): the varDecl-vs-attributeDeclaration ambiguity site. A statement led by `[[` (stdAttr) or `__attribute__` (attrSpec) is EITHER an attributed declaration (`[[maybe_unused]] int x = 5;` — the attribute rides varDecl's localDeclSpecifiers prefix) OR a bare attribute-declaration statement (`[[fallthrough]];`) — genuinely colliding FIRSTs, so the alt is SPECULATIVE (declared order authoritative, the declOrExprStmt precedent); the bare form rolls back on the immediate `;`. lookahead 256 (= the 4096-token probe budget declOrExprStmt uses): a decl probe must swallow an entire declaration incl. initializers. HOT PATH (design-audit confirmed): every statement lead in EXACTLY ONE branch's FIRST (`int`/`const`/typedef-name/... — varDecl the sole survivor) takes the parser's unique-production DIRECT DESCENT (no probe, no checkpoint), so the wrapper adds zero speculation to ordinary statements. The wrapper MATERIALIZES a CST node (named alt rules do — the declOrExprStmt golden precedent): the statement>declOrAttrStmt>varDecl shape is pinned + the 2 consumers are transparent BY MECHANISM (HIR's unmapped-statement soleMeaningfulChild PassThrough peels it; semantic passes are rule-KEYED full-tree walks).
declOrAttrStmt.$fc175Comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): `autoInferredVarDecl` joins the alt — ★ DECLARED FIRST (the design-audit's C2 MANDATORY order, NOT varDecl-first). Rationale: both decl rules' predictive prefix is 1 token, so a storage-class-led statement (`static …`) keeps 2 survivors and MUST probe; autoInferredVarDecl fast-fails within ~3 tokens on every real-typed declaration (after the specifier run, a type keyword is not a declarator), while a varDecl-FIRST order would probe varDecl under the 4096-token speculation budget and BUDGET-CLIFF existing valid `static const int big[] = {…>4096 tokens…}` declarations (sqlite3.c's largest block-scope static init is 3918 tokens = 96% of the budget — the sqlite gate would NOT catch the cliff). With autoInferred first, varDecl is the declared-LAST structural candidate for a specifier-led statement, so the parser's all-fail REPLAY (parser.cpp ~:1984) re-parses it NON-speculatively with NO budget — a genuine committed parse. Red-on-reorder pin: the >4096-token block-scope static-init test. The only dual-match shape `<specifiers> Ident ;` is invalid C either way — the diagnostic-shape pins (`auto T;` → initializer-required, `auto f(void);` → plain-identifier) hold the boundary. `auto int x;` (C89) still parses via varDecl on rollback — pinned.

extensionDeclStmt.$comment:
P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): `__extension__` prefixing a BLOCK-SCOPE declaration — `__extension__ int x = 0;`, `__extension__ typedef int T;`, `__extension__ extern int f(int);`. The `extensionTopLevel` mirror, and it must mirror it: one keyword must not mean two different things depending on where it is written (the scope-symmetry rule TF-C77 set and `localDeclSpecifier` restates). ✔MEASURED gcc 13.3.0 + clang 19.1.7: `__extension__ int x=0;` and `__extension__ typedef int T;` inside a body both compile and run; `__extension__ if(x){…}` and `__extension__ return x;` are REFUSED BY BOTH — so the inner alt lists DECLARATION productions ONLY, never `statement`. Self-recursive so `__extension__ __extension__ int x=0;` parses (✔MEASURED accepted by both).
★ THE INNER ALT IS SPECULATIVE, and that is the SAME collision `declOrAttrStmt` carries for the same two branches: `autoInferredVarDecl` and `varDecl` both admit a leading `[[…]]`/`__attribute__` run, so their FIRST sets share BracketOpen. ✔MEASURED — the non-speculative first draft FAILED THE LOAD with `C_AmbiguousAlternatives at /shapes/extensionDeclStmt: alt branches share FIRST token 'BracketOpen'`, which is that guard doing exactly its job. `autoInferredVarDecl` stays declared FIRST for the FC17.5 budget-cliff reason `declOrAttrStmt` documents.
★ `identVarDecl` IS IN THE LIST AND ITS ABSENCE WAS A REAL BUG, caught by the corpus example rather than by review: a block-scope declaration whose TYPE is a typedef NAME (`__extension__ local_u lu = 4;`) is `identVarDecl`, which lives under `declOrExprStmt` and NOT under `declOrAttrStmt` — so a list copied from `declOrAttrStmt` silently omits exactly the declarations glibc writes most (`__extension__ __quad_t x;`). ✔MEASURED before the fix: `error[P0001]: expected 'EndStatement' — got 'lu'`. It is declared AFTER `varDecl` for the same reason `declOrExprStmt` declares it after `labelStmt`: the keyword-led forms are unambiguous and cheaper to refute.
★ Transparent: the keyword is a token, so the wrapper's sole meaningful child is the declaration and the unmapped-statement `soleMeaningfulChild` PassThrough peels it — the identical mechanism `declOrAttrStmt` itself relies on. No hirLowering row, no semantics row, zero C++.

localDeclSpecifier.$comment: Local storage-class specifiers + attributes. `static` (D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-STATIC) confers STATIC storage duration (C 6.2.4) — the varDecl row's linkageSpecifiers maps it to {binding:local, staticStorage:true} and CST→HIR routes the declaration to a hidden module-global; register/auto parse and are semantically inert (C: hints/default storage). `static` in a for-init is a C 6.8.5p3 violation, gated loud by the forDecl row. C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): `alignasSpec` joins the local-specifier alts too (a block-scope `alignas(16) int x;` is legal C) — FIRST {AlignasKeyword, AlignasLegacyKeyword} disjoint from the others, so the repeat stays predictively pruned; stripped from the child count (specifierPrefix: localDeclSpecifiers on varDecl) and ignored by the linkage scan. FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR, C23 6.7.1): `constexpr` (ConstexprKeyword) joins the local alts too (a block-scope `constexpr int x = 5;` is legal C23, and forDecl reuses this prefix so `for (constexpr int i = 0; ...)` parses — VALID per C23 6.8.5p3, which admits auto/register/constexpr in a for-init) — FIRST {ConstexprKeyword} disjoint; a block-scope constexpr carries NO linkage (an automatic-storage constant), so the varDecl row IGNORES the keyword by kind (linkageSpecifierIgnoredKinds); the SEMANTIC constexpr validation reads it via semantics.constexpr.keywordToken.
localDeclSpecifier.$threadLocalComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, C11 6.7.1p3): the `_Thread_local`/`thread_local` twin keywords join the LOCAL alts too — a block-scope `static thread_local int x;` is legal C (thread storage + static storage). FIRST disjoint (distinct exact-match keywords). The varDecl/autoInferredVarDecl rows map both spellings to {threadStorage:true} (Pass 1 marks isThreadLocal); a block-scope thread_local WITHOUT static/extern is the 6.7.1p3 constraint violation Pass 2 rejects (S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern). forDecl/autoInferredForDecl share this prefix, so `for (thread_local int i…)` PARSES — those rows gate the tokens loud (gatedMarkers → S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern; a for-init admits neither static nor extern, so the pairing can never be satisfied there).
localDeclSpecifier.$tfc79Comment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4): `InlineKeyword` joins the LOCAL alts too, so a block-scope `static inline int f(int);` / `inline int f(int);` declaration parses. Omitting it would be the SCOPE ASYMMETRY TF-C77 explicitly rejected — one specifier must not mean two different things depending on where it is written. FIRST {InlineKeyword} is disjoint from every other branch, so the repeat stays predictively pruned. A block-scope `inline` carries no linkage of its own, so the varDecl/forDecl rows IGNORE it by kind; there is no block-scope function DEFINITION in C, so the emission decision (which only a definition can reach) never fires from here.

paramTrailingAttrRun.$comment:
P32 [[D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-PARAM-POSITION]]: the AFTER-DECLARATOR half of the parameter attribute surface -- `int f(int p __attribute__((__unused__)))`, which is the idiom C code actually uses to silence an unused parameter in a DEFINITION (the leading position is the C++-leaning spelling). MEASURED accepted by gcc 13.3.0 and clang 19.1.7 with `-Wall -Wextra`; before this it was `P0001 expected 'ParenClose' -- got '__attribute__'`. One attribute must not mean two things depending on which side of the declarator it sits, which is the rule `structMemberAttrList` and `initDeclarator`'s trailing run already follow.
! GNU `attrSpec` ONLY, and the exclusion of the C23 `[[...]]` spelling here is the SAME measured hazard `structMemberAttrList` records rather than a preference: FIRST(stdAttr) is {BracketOpen}, which is also the lead of an ARRAY declarator suffix, so `int p[[a]]` could not be told from an array suffix at one token. Restricting the slot to `attrSpec` makes FIRST = {AttributeKeyword}, disjoint from the `Comma` and `ParenClose` that can follow a parameter, so the `{optional}` is predictively decidable and nothing became speculative. `[[...]]` after a parameter declarator is therefore named residue -- loud, never silent.
* It is a TRAILING optional, so `head: 0` / `declarator: 1` are byte-identical decorated or not, and it joins the row's `declarationAttrSlotRules` beside the leading run so both positions are HONOURED by the same scan.

paramDeclSpecifiers.$comment:
P32 [[D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-PARAM-POSITION]]: the PARAMETER-position attribute run -- `void f([[maybe_unused]] int p)` and `void f(__attribute__((__unused__)) int p)`, both MEASURED clean on gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 19.1.7 with `-Wall -Wextra`. Before this the position was a PARSE ERROR: `declHeadForParam` has no attribute surface, so the shape real headers write on unused parameters died at `P0009`.
* IT REUSES `compositeAttr` RATHER THAN DECLARING A SECOND `attrSpec | stdAttr` ALT. That alt already exists and already means 'one whole-declaration attribute in either spelling'; a second copy is the drift this file rejects everywhere else -- add a spelling to the attribute surface and only one of the two copies would learn it. Only the RUN is new, and only because a run needs a NAME to be a `specifierPrefix`.
* FIRST = {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen}, DISJOINT from every lead `declHeadForParam` admits (headQualifier keywords, the type-specifier alt, `Identifier`, `typeof`) and from `ellipsisParam`'s `Ellipsis` -- so `paramOrEllipsis` stays predictively decidable and nothing in the parameter list became speculative.
! IT IS THE ROW'S `specifierPrefix`, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON THE INDICES SURVIVE: `param` is read as `head: 0, declarator: 1`, and a child in front of the head would otherwise silently BECOME the head. `decl_prefix_strip.hpp` removes this node before positional counting, exactly as `declSpecifiers` is removed for `topLevelDecl`, so both indices are byte-identical decorated or not.
* AND IT IS ALSO THE ROW'S `declarationAttrSlotRules`, which is not belt-and-braces: without that key the run would parse and then be invisible to `scanAttributeSemantics` -- parsed-and-silently-dropped, the exact failure this project refuses.
paramDeclSpecifiers.$p51NoreturnComment:
P51 [[D-CSUBSET-NORETURN-KEYWORD-PARAMETER-AND-TYPEDEF-POSITIONS]]: the run is now a run of `paramDeclSpecifier` ALTERNATIVES rather than a run of `compositeAttr`, so the C11 `_Noreturn` KEYWORD is admitted in a parameter's specifiers — `void g(_Noreturn void (*p)(void));` and `void g(_Noreturn int p);`. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD both were `error[P0009] expected 'EndStatement' or 'BlockOpen' — got '('` (the parameter list never opened).
★ THE SHAPE IS `structMemberDeclSpecifiers`/`structMemberDeclSpecifier`'s, VERBATIM — a plural SEQUENCE wrapping a singular ALT, the same widening TF-C94 applied to the member prefix — so the prefix node keeps its RULE NAME and `specifierPrefix` / `declarationAttrSlotRules` / decl_prefix_strip.hpp are UNTOUCHED. The extra wrapper level is transparent because every prefix consumer (`specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn`, `scanAttributeSemantics`→`collectAttrNodes`) is a BOUNDED DESCENDANT WALK over `visibleChildren`, never a fixed-child-index read.
★★ THE REFERENCES SPLIT AND THE DISJUNCTION DECIDES ACCEPTANCE. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-01, each reference probed SEPARATELY at BOTH `-std=c11` and `-std=c2x`: gcc 13.3.0 ACCEPTS (rc=0, `warning: parameter 'p' declared '_Noreturn'` — warn-and-IGNORE); clang 18.1.3 REJECTS (`error: '_Noreturn' can only appear on functions`); MSVC 19.51 REJECTS (`error C3829`). ONE accepting reference makes the behaviour REQUIRED, so DSS must PARSE it — and must then reproduce gcc's MEANING, which is to DROP the specifier. It does: a parameter is never a FnSig, so `specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn`'s keyword arm reaches the P50 warn-and-drop path (S_NoreturnNonFunctionObject, Warning) with NO new semantic code.
★ FIRST(paramDeclSpecifiers) grows {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen} -> {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen, NoreturnKeyword}, still DISJOINT from every lead `declHeadForParam` admits (headQualifier keywords, the type-specifier alt, `Identifier`, `typeof`) and from `ellipsisParam`'s `EllipsisOp` — a distinct exact-match keyword — so `paramOrEllipsis` stays predictively decidable and NOTHING in the parameter list became speculative.

paramDeclSpecifier.$comment:
P51: ONE parameter-position declaration specifier — the C11 6.7.4 `_Noreturn` KEYWORD, or one whole-declaration attribute in either spelling. The singular half of the plural-SEQUENCE-wrapping-a-singular-ALT pair this file uses for every specifier run (`declSpecifiers`/`singleDeclSpecifier`, `localDeclSpecifiers`/`localDeclSpecifier`, `structMemberDeclSpecifiers`/`structMemberDeclSpecifier`); it earns its own name for the same reason those three do — each admits a DIFFERENT set, so a shared rule would have to be the union and would silently widen all four.
★ `compositeAttr` IS REUSED RATHER THAN RE-SPELLED as a second `attrSpec | stdAttr` alt — the choice `paramDeclSpecifiers` already made and stated. Add a spelling to the attribute surface and this position learns it in the SAME edit.
★ IT REPLACES `compositeAttr` AT THE SAME DEPTH, so the parameter prefix's CST shape is BYTE-IDENTICAL for every already-parsing input: the run was already a run of a NAMED rule, and one named rule swapped for another emits the same one node per specifier. Nothing that reads this subtree (`specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn`, `scanAttributeSemantics`→`collectAttrNodes`) sees a new level.
★ FIRST = {NoreturnKeyword} ∪ {AttributeKeyword} ∪ {BracketOpen} — three pairwise-DISJOINT single-token leads, so `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` has nothing to report and the enclosing repeat stays predictively pruned.

param.$comment: FC4 c1: head + OPTIONAL declarator (named `int v`, pointer `const char *s`, abstract `int` / `int *` / `int (*)(int)`). The head admits a lone Identifier — C23 semantics: a lone identifier in param position is ALWAYS a type name (K&R identifier-lists were removed), so `int f(T)` is an unnamed param of type T (S_UnknownType when T isn't one).

statement.$c30Comment: c30 D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-TYPEDEF: `typedefDecl` is admitted as a block item (a BLOCK-SCOPED typedef — `typedef void(*LOGFUNC_t)(void*,int,const char*);` inside a function, sqlite3.c:187603). FIRST = TypedefKeyword, DISJOINT from every other statement alt (varDecl is qualifier/type-keyword/storage-class-led; declOrExprStmt is Identifier-led; the rest are their own keywords), so a unique-production DIRECT DESCENT and NO probe -- unchanged by P42 marking this alt `speculative: true` for the attribute-led pair, because a lone surviving candidate takes the direct descent. The whole typedef-name machinery is ALREADY scope-keyed: Pass-1 binds the alias into `current` (= the enclosing block scope) in the Ordinary namespace; the type resolver (`resolveTypeNodeImpl` SE5 arm) and the parse-time oracle (`BinderSketch`) both walk the scope chain, so a block-scoped typedef-name resolves IN the block, SHADOWS an outer same-name typedef, and does NOT leak out (red-on-disable pins enforce the non-leak). HIR→MIR's `lowerStmtNode` lowers a statement-position TypeDecl as a NO-OP (a typedef emits no code; mirrors the TOP-LEVEL TypeDecl). Mirrors c28 (block-scoped struct/union/enum definition).
statement.$blockExternComment: D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-EXTERN (TF arc C10, SQLite testfixture 2026-07-18): the FILE-scope `externDecl` rule is ALSO admitted as a block item, so a block-scope `extern` declaration parses — `extern int f(int);` (a function prototype) AND `extern T *p;` (an object reference) inside a function body (C89 6.7.1; 6/44 sqlite src/test*.c hit this FIRST, e.g. test_thread.c:116 `extern int Sqlitetest_mutex_Init(Tcl_Interp*);`, test_btree.c:32 `extern BtShared *sqlite3SharedCacheList;`). FIRST(externDecl) = {ExternKeyword}, DISJOINT from every other statement alt (nothing else leads with `extern` — before this it P0009'd 'got extern'), so a unique-production DIRECT DESCENT and NO probe -- unchanged by P42 marking this alt `speculative: true` for the attribute-led pair, because a lone surviving candidate takes the direct descent. REUSES the file-scope externDecl semantics + HIR lowering WHOLESALE: Pass-1's rule-keyed full-tree walk mints the `nonDefiningDeclaration` symbol into `current` (= the enclosing BLOCK scope, C 6.2.2p4 name scope) exactly like the c30 block-typedef / c28 block-struct; CST→HIR's lowerStmt routes the synthesized ExternFunction/ExternGlobal to the module-decls accumulator (the D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-STATIC / D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-PROTOTYPE pattern) and lowers the STATEMENT to a no-op (the Skip precedent); collectExterns registers the symbol so a block use resolves via GlobalAddr, identical to a file-scope extern. ★ DELIBERATELY does NOT re-home to file scope the way D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-PROTOTYPE does for bare prototypes: block-scope binding is REQUIRED so a block-scope extern OBJECT that shadows an outer local (C 6.2.1) reads the extern, not the local — a file-scope re-home would mis-bind the shadow (design-audit Finding 3). A same-TU DEFINITION of the extern name in ANOTHER TU resolves at the LK11 cross-CU merge (import stripped); a same-TU FILE-SCOPE definition does NOT merge with the block extern (different scope), so the extern stays a real import (the cross-CU witness shape, examples/c/block_scope_extern).
statement.$fc17Comment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-STATEMENT): `varDecl` is REPLACED by `declOrAttrStmt` (= alt{varDecl, attributeDeclaration}) — the ONLY varDecl-as-alt-branch site — so a `[[fallthrough]];` statement parses. A DIRECT statement-alt addition of attributeDeclaration was REFUTED: varDecl's FIRST already carries BracketOpen/AttributeKeyword (via localDeclSpecifiers' stdAttr/attrSpec), so the two branches collide → C_AmbiguousAlternatives at load. Every non-attribute-led statement still direct-descends (see declOrAttrStmt's hot-path note). P42 UPDATE: that collision reasoning was right and has now been PAID rather than avoided -- `typedefDecl` gained the leading attribute position too, so `declOrAttrStmt` and `typedefDecl` collide on {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen} and this alt is `speculative: true`. Only an attribute-led block item probes, and at most twice.
statement.$p42wSpeculativeComment:
P42 (D-CSUBSET-LEADING-ATTRIBUTE-BEFORE-TYPEDEF-IS-A-PARSE-ERROR): speculative, for the reason the FC17 note above ALREADY records about this very alt — `declOrAttrStmt`'s FIRST carries {AttributeKeyword, BracketOpen}, and `typedefDecl` now carries the LEADING attribute position, so the two branches collide exactly as that note predicted for a different addition (✔MEASURED: `detectAmbiguousAlternatives` named `/shapes/statement` and `AttributeKeyword` by pointer). c30 admits `typedefDecl` as a BLOCK ITEM, so `__attribute__((deprecated)) typedef int T;` inside a function body must parse for the same reason its file-scope twin must — before this it was `error[P0001] expected 'EndStatement' — got 'typedef'`, a DIFFERENT code from the file-scope P0009 because the two positions failed at different rules.
⚠ THIS IS THE HOTTEST DISPATCH IN THE GRAMMAR AND THE COST WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. Nineteen of the twenty branches keep a UNIQUE 1-token FIRST, so the predictive prune leaves exactly one candidate and the parser takes the UNIQUE-PRODUCTION DIRECT DESCENT — no probe, no checkpoint. Only an attribute-led block item probes, and at most twice.

forStmt.$comment: FC4 c1: the init clause mirrors the statement-level decl split — committed keyword/qualifier/specifier-led forDecl vs the identifier-led forInitAmbig probe. Both are semicolon-LESS (the for grammar owns the `;`).
forStmt.$fc175Comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): `autoInferredForDecl` joins the init alt — declared FIRST, the SAME C2 audit order as declOrAttrStmt (see its $fc175Comment; the >4096-token budget-cliff rationale applies identically to a for-init). The speculative/lookahead flags ride the OPTIONAL (the D-PARSE-SPECULATIVE-OPTIONAL shape — the enumTypeSpecifier precedent): the optional's own AltChoice is the DECISION POINT (its candidate enumeration flattens the inner alt's rules and EXCLUDES the skip branch), so flags on the inner alt object would never be consulted — empirically, `for (constexpr int i = 0;;)` first-match-committed the inference rule and P0001'd on `int` until the flags moved out here (the ConstexprInForInitAccepted pin caught it). No named wrapper, so the CST shape is UNCHANGED: forStmt's init child is still the forDecl/autoInferredForDecl/forInitAmbig node directly. Ordinary for-inits keep cheap decisions (`for (int i…` — `int` is in forDecl's FIRST only → its probe is the sole survivor; `for (i…` — Identifier → forInitAmbig), the multi-survivor probe fires only on a specifier-led init (`for (auto i…` / `for (static …` / `for (constexpr …`). An ABSENT init (`for (;;)`) rides the speculative optional's nullable-skip arm (parser.cpp ~:1941) exactly as before.

sehTryStmt.$comment: c115 (SEH arc 2/3): MSVC `__try compound-statement (__except '(' expr ')' compound-statement | __finally compound-statement)` — learn.microsoft.com/cpp/cpp/try-except-statement. FIRST = {TryKeyword}, disjoint from every other statement alt -> unique-production direct descent, NON-speculative; the except/finally fork is disambiguated one level down by sehHandler's own disjoint FIRSTs (ExceptKeyword vs FinallyKeyword). Both bodies REUSE the `block` rule — MSVC requires compound statements (braces), so the grammar enforces it by construction. The filter expression is an ordinary `expression`; its special context (where _exception_code()/_exception_info() are legal) is a SEMANTIC property checked at CST->HIR lowering + the HIR verifier, not a grammar one. __finally parses (so the diagnostic is a positioned lowering fail-loud citing D-CSUBSET-SEH-FINALLY, not a raw P0001 cascade) but has NO consumer (sqlite ground-truth: zero uses) — trigger-gated.

sehLeaveStmt.$comment: c115: `__leave ;` parses (FIRST = {LeaveKeyword}, disjoint) so the diagnostic is a positioned lowering fail-loud citing D-CSUBSET-SEH-LEAVE rather than a parse cascade. NO consumer (sqlite: zero uses) — trigger-gated; the lowering rejects it.

assignmentExpr.$comment: FC5: a C `assignment-expression` — every operator EXCEPT the comma (the two-level expression gate). minPrecedence 15 folds assignment (prec 15) and everything tighter but STOPS before the comma operator (prec 10, looser), so a `,` at a separator site (argList / initValue / enumerator) is left for the surrounding rule's separator, never swallowed as a comma-operator. The top-level `expression` rule (minPrec 0) keeps the comma operator for expr-statements / for-clauses / return / parens / index / conditions.

operand.$p31StmtExprComment:
P31: `stmtExpr` (GNU `({ … })`) and `extensionExpr` (GNU `__extension__ e`) join the operand alts.
★★ THE `commitAfterPrefix` CUT IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART, AND THE **ORDER** IS NOT — WHICH IS A CORRECTION THIS COMMENT EARNED THE HARD WAY. It first asserted that `stmtExpr` MUST precede `compoundLiteralExpr`/`castExpr`/`parenExpr` because all four lead with ParenOpen and the predictive prefix of the other three stops at their first sub-rule (so peek(1) = `{` prunes none of them). The FIRST half is true and the CONCLUSION is false. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 by a red-on-disable mutant that moved `stmtExpr` to the END of the alt, after `parenExpr`: the scoped gate stayed GREEN, 6/6. `operand` is SPECULATIVE, so each paren-led sibling is TRIED, fails one token in (no C expression begins with `{`, and no type-name does either), rolls back, and `stmtExpr` then commits. Position here buys latency — three failed probes avoided on the common case — never correctness. A comment that claims a property no mutant can red is a comment nothing is checking.
★ WHAT IS ACTUALLY LOAD-BEARING: `commitAfterPrefix` on `stmtExpr`. The alt's probe budget is lookahead(64) × 16 = 1024 tokens, so a body longer than that cannot parse under a probe at all; the two-token prefix `( {` — a sequence no other operand alt can begin — cuts the probe and the body then parses with NO budget. That claim IS measured, by `ParsesABodyLongerThanTheSpeculationBudget` in tests/analysis/semantic/test_gnu_extension_and_statement_expr.cpp, which builds a ~4000-token body; removing the cut reds it.
★ `extensionExpr`'s FIRST = {ExtensionKeyword} is disjoint from every sibling, so its position is genuinely free; its own `commitAfterPrefix` buys the same no-budget parse for `__extension__ ({ … })`, the spelling glibc's math.h and assert.h use.
operand.$lookaheadComment: FC2 Part A: raised 8 -> 64. The speculation budget is lookahead*16 tokens per probe (parser SpeculationProbe); a castExpr probe must consume the ENTIRE cast operand expression before its frame closes, so the old 128-token budget was a correctness cliff for casts of long expressions (and for large compound-literal brace inits). 64 -> 1024-token probe budget.

stmtExpr.$comment:
P31 (D-C-GNU-STATEMENT-EXPRESSION, GNU C 6.1 'Statements and Declarations in Expressions'): `({ stmt… expr; })` — a compound statement in expression position whose VALUE is its last statement, when that last statement is an expression statement. ★★ WHY IT IS WORTH THE ROW: ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 over `/usr/include` (C headers only, the C++ tree excluded, every pattern carrying a positive control): 59 occurrences across 15 headers, `assert.h`, `math.h`, `ctype.h`, `unistd.h`, `netinet/in.h`, `bits/stdio.h`, `bits/select2.h` and `bits/cpu-set.h` among them; 7 of those sites are written `__extension__ ({`, which is why the two constructs are ONE row's worth of work and not two.
★★ THE BODY IS INLINED (`ParenOpen BlockOpen {repeat statement} BlockClose ParenClose`) RATHER THAN REFERENCING `block`, AND THE ORIGINAL REASON WAS REFUTED, SO HERE IS THE ONE THAT SURVIVED. The inlining was introduced to give the rule a TWO-token predictive prefix `( {` for a `commitAfterPrefix` cut, because `predictivePrefix` stops at the first sub-rule and `[ParenOpen, block, ParenClose]` would have had a one-token prefix (cutting on `(` alone would steal every parenthesised expression in the language). ⚠ **THE CUT WAS THEN MEASURED TO DO NOTHING AND WAS REMOVED** — see $refusalComment. What the inlining still buys is real and is why it stays: the rule OWNS its braces, so it is the `semantics.scopes` entry (a nested `block` node would put the scope one level down and split ownership between two rules), and the CST→HIR lowering reads the statements as its own DIRECT children rather than through a `block` whose `Block` hirKind row would then have to be suppressed in expression position.
★ THE SCOPE COMES FROM `semantics.scopes` NAMING THIS RULE, exactly as it names `block`: a statement expression's declarations are block-scoped (`({ int _a = a; … })` is the whole idiom, and the temporaries must not leak or collide between two uses in one function).
★ THE VALUE LOWERS TO `HirKind::SeqExpr` — WHICH ALREADY EXISTED FOR THIS, and whose own header comment names GCC statement expressions as what it models. It was built as the substrate for value-yielding `++`, assignment-as-a-value and complex-lvalue compound-assign; MIR's SeqExpr arm already runs each statement child through `lowerStmt` (an ARBITRARY statement, not just an assignment) and yields the last child's value, and `collectLocalDecls` already walks the WHOLE body subtree, so a declaration nested inside an expression already gets its entry-block Alloca. Zero new HirKinds, zero MIR change, zero LIR change — the construct was anticipated by the substrate and only the front end was missing.
stmtExpr.$cutMeasurementComment:
P31 — WHY THERE IS NO `commitAfterPrefix` HERE, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-ADDED. This rule shipped its first draft WITH the cut, and the comment claimed it was `the only reason a statement expression longer than the 1024-token probe budget parses at all`. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24, three independent instruments, all against the shipped CLI:
  (1) BODY LENGTH — bodies of 100 / 400 / 1000 / 3000 statements (up to ~30 000 tokens), bare and behind `__extension__`, at top level: rc=0 and the SAME wall time (±0.03 s) with the cut and without it.
  (2) NESTING — the same bodies as a cast operand, a call argument, a parenthesised sub-expression, a ternary arm and an initializer: IDENTICAL verdicts with and without.
  (3) DIAGNOSTICS — four MALFORMED bodies (an assignment with no rhs, an unterminated body, a bad declaration, and the same behind `__extension__`): identical CODE, identical column, with and without.
The budget case is covered by the parser's ALL-FAIL REPLAY instead: when every speculative candidate fails, the surviving one is re-parsed non-speculatively with no budget, and `( {` can only ever be this rule. ⇒ the cut was config that asserted a soundness obligation and bought nothing measurable, so it is gone. ⚠ THE ONE PLACE A CUT WOULD HAVE HELPED IS NOT THIS RULE: a statement expression used as a CAST OPERAND cliffs on the OUTER `castExpr` probe's budget (~50 statements), and a cut inside an inner rule cannot refund an outer probe. That cliff is PRE-EXISTING and not this construct's — ✔MEASURED with a control, an ordinary `(int)(0 + 0 - 0 …)` operand cliffs the same way at ~200 terms — and it is filed as [[D-C-CAST-OPERAND-SPECULATION-BUDGET-CLIFF]]. `castExpr` cannot take a cut anyway: `commitAfterPrefix` and `commitRequiresTypeName` are documented as mutually exclusive and `castExpr` already carries the latter.
stmtExpr.$refusalComment: P31: the two refusals, both MEASURED against gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 19.1.7 as refusals THERE TOO, so neither is a DSS-only narrowing. (1) A statement expression whose last statement is NOT an expression statement has type `void` (`({ int a = 1; })`); using it as a VALUE is `error: void value not ignored as it ought to be` in gcc and `initializing 'int' with an expression of incompatible type 'void'` in clang, and is S_StatementExprHasNoValue here — DSS admits it in a DISCARD position exactly as both references do. (2) At FILE scope both references refuse it (`braced-group within expression allowed only inside a function` / `statement expression not allowed at file scope`); here the grammar admits it and the SEMANTIC tier refuses it with S_StatementExprAtFileScope, which is the fail-loud shape — a fabricated module-initializer would be the silent miscompile.

extensionExpr.$comment:
P31 (D-C-GNU-EXTENSION-KEYWORD): `__extension__ e` in EXPRESSION position — glibc's `math.h` and `assert.h` write `__extension__ ({ … })`, and `bits/byteswap.h` writes `__extension__ (…)` around a wide constant. ✔MEASURED gcc 13.3.0 + clang 19.1.7: accepted before a literal, a parenthesised expression, a statement expression, `sizeof`, a unary minus, and inside a call argument; and doubling it (`__extension__ __extension__ 0`) is accepted too — which this rule gets for free, since `assignmentExpr` reaches `operand` reaches here.
★ THE OPERAND IS `assignmentExpr`, NOT `expression`, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A REAL BUG AVOIDED: `expression` admits the COMMA operator, so `f(__extension__ a, b)` would have parsed as ONE argument `(a, b)` instead of two — silently, with no diagnostic. `assignmentExpr` is the same minPrecedence-15 entry `argList` and `initValue` already use for exactly this reason. Binding the whole assignment-expression (rather than gcc's formal `cast_expression`) is harmless BECAUSE the construct is transparent: `__extension__ a + b` and `(__extension__ a) + b` denote the same value.
★ NO `commitAfterPrefix`, AND THE REASON IS STRONGER HERE THAN ON `stmtExpr`: FIRST = {ExtensionKeyword} begins no other operand alt, so this rule is a UNIQUE-PRODUCTION DIRECT DESCENT — the parser never opens a probe for it at all, and a cut that can never fire is not an optimisation, it is an unfalsifiable claim. The first draft carried one; ✔MEASURED 2026-08-24 across body length, five nesting positions and four malformed-body diagnostics, removing it changed no verdict, no wall time and no diagnostic column. See `stmtExpr`'s $cutMeasurementComment for the full instrument.
★ Transparent by MECHANISM, not by a lowering row: the keyword is a token, so the node's sole meaningful child is the operand and `lowerExpr`'s unknown-wrapper PassThrough peels it. Zero C++.

compoundLiteralExpr.$comment: FC3.5 sweep-c3 (D-CSUBSET-COMPOUND-LITERAL-TYPEDEF): the type position is castTypeRef (typedef-admitting via its bare-Identifier base alt) with the SAME commitRequiresTypeName binder triage castExpr uses. The `{` follower makes most forms unambiguous (triage case 4: BlockOpen is not a continuable value-reading operator -> COMMIT for unknown names); a KNOWN-value identifier `(a){...}` rolls back to the value reading, whose `(a)` parenExpr then hits the orphan `{` -> LOUD parse error (C says the form is invalid anyway).

sizeofExpr.$comment: FC6: `sizeof ( type-name )` | `sizeof unary-expression` (C 6.5.3.4). The type form reuses FC2's castTypeRef + commitRequiresTypeName binder triage — `sizeof(int)` / `sizeof(struct S)` / `sizeof(char*)` commit as types; `sizeof(x)` for a value `x` rolls back to the value form (a parenExpr operand); `sizeof x` (no parens) is the value form directly. The result type is size_t (U64); the operand is UNEVALUATED — only its type reaches the SizeOf node.

alignofExpr.$comment:
[[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-VALUE-OPERAND]] (closed 2026-08-24, cycle P31): `_Alignof ( type-name )` | `_Alignof unary-expression` — the `sizeofExpr`/`sizeofType`/`sizeofValue` TRIPLE, verbatim, one operator across. ISO C makes alignof type-name-only, but EVERY reference compiler measured on this host also takes an EXPRESSION operand, and takes it for EVERY spelling: ✔MEASURED with matched positive+negative controls on gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 (`-std=gnu17` and each oracle newest `-std`), all rc=0 — `__alignof__(d)`, `__alignof(d)`, `_Alignof(d)`, `alignof(d)`, and the paren-free `_Alignof d`. Before this rule DSS accepted NONE of them (✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI at HEAD `60198126`: `error[P0009]` naming `AlignofKeyword` in the expected set, plus a P0001 cascade).
★ WHY A WRAPPER AND NOT A SECOND `operand` ALT: two `operand` branches leading with the same keyword is exactly the `C_AmbiguousAlternatives` the loader refuses, and it is right to — one token cannot tell a type-name operand from a value one, so the split has to be an INTERNAL decision, which is already how sizeof does it. The speculation-cost argument is INHERITED rather than re-derived: `operand` is ALREADY a speculative alt at lookahead 64 whose branch list ALREADY contains `sizeofExpr`, an identically shaped speculative wrapper reached by the SAME probe loop — so this adds one more branch of a shape the hot path already pays for, not a new class of work. The keyword-led FIRST set (`AlignofKeyword`/`AlignofLegacyKeyword`) is disjoint from every other branch, so the LL(k) predictive prune ([[D-PARSE-SPECULATION-OPERAND-QUADRATIC]]) discards this branch in ONE token for every operand that is not an alignof, and the type-vs-value probe runs only for operands that really are.
★ THE PAREN-FREE FORM COMES FREE, and that is a property of `castOperand` rather than a second feature: `alignofValue` ends in the same precedence-90 expression atom `sizeofValue` ends in, so `_Alignof d` lands with `_Alignof(d)` and the parens in the value form are a `parenExpr` OPERAND, not part of this rule.

alignofType.$comment:
C11/C23 6.5.3.4: `_Alignof ( type-name )` / `alignof ( type-name )`. The TYPE-NAME arm of the `alignofExpr` pair (`alignofValue` is its sibling — [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-VALUE-OPERAND]], closed 2026-08-24). Reuses FC2's shared castTypeRef + commitRequiresTypeName binder triage (so `_Alignof(int)` / `_Alignof(struct S)` commit the parens as a type; a non-type name fails loud at type-resolve, never silently treated as a value). The two-arm choice lives in the `alignofExpr` WRAPPER (speculative, lookahead 64 — `sizeofExpr` verbatim), not here. Result type is size_t (U64); folds to the type's alignment via the type_layout engine, exactly like sizeof reads size.
★ [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-GNU-SPELLING]] (closed 2026-08-11): the keyword table now also spells `__alignof__` and `__alignof` as `AlignofKeyword`, so BOTH GNU forms arrive at THIS rule. They are ALIASES, not a second operator — the inline keyword-alt at child 0 already matches a SET, so nothing here changed and no C++ changed either (the semantic tier keys off `alignofTypeRule`, never off a keyword identity). WHY THE GNU SPELLING IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: `_Alignof` is C11-and-later and `alignof` is C23-and-later, while `__alignof__` works at EVERY -std level, so that is the form a header which must still compile as C89 writes. The `inline`/`__inline`/`__inline__` rows are the N-spellings-one-kind precedent. MEASURED on this host with matched positive+negative controls (gcc 13.3.0 `-std=gnu17` and `-std=c2x`; clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 `-std=c23` and `-std=gnu17`): all three oracles accept `__alignof__(double)` and `__alignof(double)`.
★ THE RESIDUE THIS COMMENT USED TO NAME IS CLOSED (2026-08-24, cycle P31), and the fix is the one this paragraph predicted: the same three oracles ALSO accept the VALUE operand — `__alignof__(expr)`, `_Alignof(expr)`, and even the paren-free `_Alignof d` — and DSS now accepts every one of them through the `alignofValue` sibling below and the `alignofExpr` wrapper above. It was never a GNU-spelling gap: it hit the already-shipped `_Alignof` exactly as hard, which is why the fix is a FORM and not a keyword row.

alignofValue.$comment:
[[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-VALUE-OPERAND]]: the VALUE arm of `alignofExpr` — `sizeofValue` verbatim, with the alignof keyword-alt at child 0 instead of the sizeof keyword. The operand is UNEVALUATED (C 6.5.3.4p1, and GNU documents the same of `__alignof__`): only its TYPE reaches the node, derived by the SAME `subtreeType` deriver the sizeof value arm uses, so there is no second scan that could disagree with the first.
★ NAMED DIVERGENCE, MEASURED not assumed: gcc reports the DECLARED alignment of an over-aligned OBJECT here (`int x __attribute__((aligned(64))); __alignof__(x)` is 64 on gcc but 4 under the type reading), while clang reports the TYPE alignment. DSS takes the TYPE reading — the one both the C text and clang give, and the one this rule can state without inventing an object-vs-type axis the grammar does not have. It is anchored, not absorbed: [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-VALUE-OVERALIGNED-OBJECT]].

typeofSpecifier.$comment:
★ [[D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF-GNU-SPELLING]] (closed 2026-08-11): the keyword table also spells `__typeof__` and `__typeof` as `TypeofKeyword`, so both GNU forms arrive at this specifier and at BOTH its operand arms. They map to the QUALIFIER-PRESERVING kind because that is what GNU `__typeof__` means — it is `typeof`, not `typeof_unqual`. Pure ALIASES: the inline keyword-alt at `typeofType`/`typeofValue` child 0 already matches a SET, the semantic tier keys off `typeofTypeRule`/`typeofValueRule` (never a keyword identity), and `typeofStripQualifiersToken` stays `TypeofUnqualKeyword` — so a `__typeof__` operand is NEVER qual-stripped, which is the one way this alias could have been wrong. Reachable from all seven alt-lists that admit `typeofSpecifier`, for free. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ISO SPELLING: `typeof` is C23-only; `__typeof__` works at EVERY -std level, so a header that must still compile as C89 writes the GNU form. MEASURED on this host with matched positive+negative controls: gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=gnu17`, `-std=c2x`), clang 18.1.3 and clang 19.1.1 (`-std=c23`, `-std=gnu17`) all accept `__typeof__(x)` and `__typeof(x)`. ★★ `__typeof_unqual__` AND `__typeof_unqual` ARE KEYWORD ROWS ONTO `TypeofUnqualKeyword` SINCE 2026-08-24 ([[D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF-UNQUAL-GNU-SPELLING]], P33 lane B) — the already-shipped qualifier-STRIPPING arm (`typeofStripQualifiersToken`), so they are pure aliases exactly as `__typeof__`/`__typeof` are onto the preserving one, and no semantic tier changed. ⚠ THE SENTENCE THAT STOOD HERE IS RETRACTED, AND ITS MEASUREMENT WAS NOT WRONG — ITS RULE WAS SUPERSEDED. It read: 'DELIBERATELY NOT ADDED … gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 REJECT it and only clang 19.1.1 accepts, so shipping it would make DSS accept what two of three reference compilers refuse'. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-24 on this host, one TU per spelling, rc captured directly, with a matched POSITIVE control (`typeof_unqual`, the ISO spelling all three accept under `-std=c2x`) and a NEGATIVE control (`__typeof_unqual_dss_never__`, all three refuse): the roster is UNCHANGED — gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=gnu17`, `-std=c2x`) and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=gnu17`, `-std=c2x`, `-std=c23`) still refuse BOTH spellings, clang 19.1.1 accepts BOTH at every `-std` tested. Still 1 of 3. ★★ WHAT MOVED IS THE TEST, NOT THE ROSTER: the retracted sentence applied a MAJORITY rule; the operator ruling of 2026-08-19 (bar §A.3b, 'the goal is to WORK — one working reference makes the behaviour REQUIRED') makes the test a DISJUNCTION and says in terms that the converse — 'accepting what no reference accepts is also a defect' — turns on NO, not on one. ✔AND THE SPELLING GENUINELY STRIPS, which is the half a parse-only probe cannot see: under clang 19.1.1 `const int x = 1; __typeof_unqual__(x) y = 2; y = 3;` compiles clean, while the identical program spelled `__typeof__(x)` fails 'cannot assign to variable with const-qualified type' — so the alias is verified to mean typeof_unqual and not merely to lex. ⚠ DO NOT re-derive the old sentence from the roster: 1-of-3 is exactly the state it describes, and under §A.3b that state now REQUIRES the feature.
C23 6.7.2.5 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF): `typeof`/`typeof_unqual` — a TYPE-SPECIFIER whose meaning is the operand's type (typeof preserves top-level qualifiers, typeof_unqual strips them). Two operand forms, disambiguated SPECULATIVELY (parallel to sizeofExpr's type-vs-value alt): the TYPE-NAME form (`typeof(int)`/`typeof(volatile char)`/`typeof(int*)`) probes FIRST, and a VALUE operand (`typeof(x)`/`typeof(a.b)`) rolls back to the value form. FIRST-set-safe: the two brand-new disjoint keyword tokens make a `typeof` lead select this specifier unambiguously in every alt-list it is appended to — the inner alt is where the type-vs-value ambiguity lives, so the speculation budget applies only once a `typeof(` is already committed. The wrapper materializes a `typeofSpecifier` node containing the chosen `typeofType`/`typeofValue` (like sizeofExpr); the semantic tier resolves the inner form's operand and the HIR lowering recovers the stamped result via resolveStampedTypeBelow.

typeofType.$comment: C23 6.7.2.5 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF): the TYPE-NAME operand form — `typeof ( type-name )` / `typeof_unqual ( type-name )`. Reuses FC2's shared `castTypeRef` (so `typeof(int*)` / `typeof(volatile char)` / `typeof(MyTypedef)` all resolve) + the `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage. POLARITY = `requireKnownType` (NOT sizeofType's PreferType default), mirroring `alignasTypeName`: a bare identifier commits the TYPE reading ONLY when it is a KNOWN typedef-name; an ENUM CONSTANT or other non-type identifier (binder-sketch Unknown) rolls back to `typeofValue` and is typed as an expression — the C 6.7.6.3p11-style disambiguation (under PreferType a bare `typeof(ENUM_CONST)` would wrongly commit as a type → a spurious S_UnknownType). A keyword-led type (`typeof(int)`) still commits (triage rule 1). The inline 2-keyword alt at child 0 mirrors alignofType (no wrapper) — visible-child 2 is the castTypeRef (same layout as sizeofType/alignofType).

typeofValue.$comment: C23 6.7.2.5 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF): the EXPRESSION operand form — `typeof ( expression )` / `typeof_unqual ( expression )` (reached when the type-name reading rolls back). The operand is the full comma-inclusive `expression` (C23-correct — `typeof(a, b)` takes the comma expression's type). UNEVALUATED (6.7.2.5p2): only the operand's TYPE reaches the semantic tier (via subtreeType), which strips top-level volatile for typeof_unqual; a bit-field operand is a constraint violation (S_TypeofBitfieldOperand). visible-child 2 is the expression (same keyword+paren layout as typeofType).

bitIntSpecifier.$comment: C23 6.2.5/6.7.2 (D-CSUBSET-BITINT): the `_BitInt ( constant-expression )` bit-precise integer TYPE-SPECIFIER — structurally the typeofType twin (keyword + '(' + operand + ')'), a PLAIN sequence (NO speculative parsing: the distinct `_BitInt` keyword + the unambiguous `(` make it FIRST-set-disjoint from every other specifier). It is an ELEMENT of `typeSpecifierSeq` (NOT a standalone type-base alt), so `unsigned`/`signed` compose with it through the SAME C 6.7.2 specifier run, order-independently (`unsigned _BitInt(40)` == `_BitInt(40) unsigned`): the run lands the bitIntSpecifier NODE plus any signedness TOKENS as sibling children, and the semantic tier (semantics.bitInt) reads the width from `assignmentExpr` (child 2 — the comma-free const-expr rule bit-field widths / array dims / alignas / static_assert also use), scans the run for a signedness token (DEFAULT signed), const-folds + validates N (0xE04A-0xE04D + the C1 N>64 gate), and interns `bitInt(N, signed)`. A run mixing `_BitInt` with a NON-signedness specifier (`int _BitInt(4)`) rejects as S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination.

alignasSpec.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): the `_Alignas ( … )` / `alignas ( … )` alignment SPECIFIER — a DECLARATION-SPECIFIER (NOT an expression operand), so it is a SEQUENCE (its tree node is `alignasSpec`, which the specifier-prefix mechanism matches in singleDeclSpecifier/localDeclSpecifier/structMemberDeclSpecifiers). Two spellings: the reserved `_Alignas` (AlignasKeyword) and the C23 `alignas` (AlignasLegacyKeyword). The parenthesized operand is `alignasArg` — EITHER a type-name (`alignas(int)` contributes _Alignof(int)) OR a constant-expression (`alignas(16)`). SEMANTICS live in the semantic tier (semantics.alignas): the value/type is computed + validated (power-of-two, ≤256, ≥ the declared type's natural alignment) + STORED on the SymbolRecord (variables) / fed into the struct's fieldAligns (members). The specifier is STRIPPED before positional-child counting (decl_prefix_strip.hpp) so name/type indices stay stable, and IGNORED by the linkage scan (linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules) — exactly like `__attribute__`.

alignasArg.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): the operand of an `alignas` specifier — the TYPE form (`alignasTypeName`, e.g. `alignas(int)` / `alignas(struct S)`) OR the VALUE form (a constant-expression, `assignmentExpr` — the SAME comma-free const-expr rule staticAssertDecl's condition + a bit-field width + an array dimension use, so `alignas(16)` / `alignas(2*8)` / `alignas(ENUM_VAL)` all fold). SPECULATIVE, with the type branch carrying the `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage: the operand position is genuinely type-vs-value AMBIGUOUS (`alignas(int)` type vs `alignas(ENUM_VAL)` value). The guard lives on the `alignasTypeName` BRANCH (not on this alt) — the parser's triage is keyed off the PROBED branch rule, exactly like `operand`'s `castExpr` branch. The semantic tier discriminates the committed reading by the child rule (alignasTypeName ⇒ type form → _Alignof(T); else value form → const-eval).

alignasTypeName.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): the TYPE-form branch of an `alignas` operand — a lone `castTypeRef` wrapped in a SEQUENCE so it can carry `commitRequiresTypeName` (the guard must sit on the speculative BRANCH the parser probes; a bare `castTypeRef` alt-branch would be probed as `castTypeRef` and `typeNameCommitRule(castTypeRef)` is not set → the guard would never fire). POLARITY = `requireKnownType` (NOT the PreferType default): a bare identifier commits the TYPE reading ONLY when it is a KNOWN typedef-name (sketch/oracle Type); an ENUM CONSTANT or any non-type identifier (sketch Unknown) rolls back to the VALUE reading and const-folds — the C 6.7.6.3p11-style disambiguation. Under PreferType a bare enum-constant `alignas(AL)` would wrongly commit as a type (no follower operator) → a spurious S_AlignasNonConstant. A keyword-led type (`alignas(int)`) still commits (triage rule 1).

labelAddressExpr.$comment: D-CSUBSET-COMPUTED-GOTO: the GNU `&&label` label-address expression.
