A DEDICATED operand rule (parallel to sizeofExpr) — NOT the prec-90 prefix `&` doubled — because its operand is a LABEL name in the label namespace, NOT a value: routing it through the ordinary identifier-operand path would resolve `label` as an (undefined) variable and fail to parse. The `Identifier` here is a RAW token (like labelStmt's), recovered by the CST→HIR lowering which resolves it to the label's per-function ordinal and stamps the result `void*`. The leading `&&` is the single AndAndOp token (no lexer change).

vaStartExpr.$comment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): `va_start(ap, last)`. Takes the `va_list` lvalue (assignmentExpr — the comma-free, non-comma-operator form) and an OPTIONAL second `last` arg that is parsed-and-ignored (the SysV gp/fp offsets derive from the FnSig, not from `last`). A leaf form in the operand alternative list, parallel to sizeofExpr.

vaArgExpr.$comment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): `va_arg(ap, T)`. The SECOND argument is a TYPE — it reuses FC2's shared `castTypeRef` rule + `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage so `va_arg(ap, int)` / `va_arg(ap, MyTypedef)` commit the type position as a type (and `va_arg(ap, x)` for a VALUE x fails loud at the type-resolve, never silently treating a value as a type). The dedicated HIR lowering recovers T from the semantic stamp, exactly like sizeof.

vaEndExpr.$comment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): `va_end(ap)`. Takes the `va_list` lvalue; a no-op teardown in the SysV model.

genericExpr.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-GENERIC-SELECTION): C11/C23 6.5.1.1 `_Generic ( controlling-expression , generic-assoc-list )` — a PRIMARY EXPRESSION whose value+type IS the selected association's expression. A leaf in the operand alternative list (parallel to vaArgExpr). The controlling expression is `assignmentExpr` (comma-free — a `,` here separates associations, so the comma-operator form must not swallow it, exactly like vaArgExpr's ap arg). The assoc-list is a NON-EMPTY comma-separated list of `type-name : assignment-expression` (genericAssoc) or `default : assignment-expression` (genericDefaultAssoc); the list shape (first + `{repeat {, item}}`) mirrors initDeclaratorList. Each genericAssoc's type position is `castTypeRef` + the SAME `commitRequiresTypeName` binder triage va_arg/casts use, so `int:`/`MyTypedef:` commit as a TYPE and a VALUE in type position fails loud at the type-resolve (S_UnknownType). SELECTION is compile-time in the SEMANTIC tier (semantics.generic): the controlling expr's type (after lvalue conversion — top-level volatile stripped) is matched against each association's resolved type for COMPATIBILITY (interned TypeId equality); EXACTLY ONE must match, else the `default` — a no-match-no-default is S_GenericSelectionNoMatch and >1 match is S_GenericSelectionAmbiguous (both unsuppressable constraint violations). Pass 2 stamps the genericExpr node with the WINNER's result type + records the winning association's expression node; the dedicated HIR lowering (hirLowering.genericRule → lowerGeneric) lowers ONLY that sub-expression (its type + value), discarding the rest (the non-selected expressions are UNEVALUATED per 6.5.1.1p3, imposing no constraints beyond being syntactically valid).

genericAssoc.$comment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-GENERIC-SELECTION): ONE `type-name : assignment-expression` OR `default : assignment-expression` association of a `_Generic`. The `default` form is a distinct alt (genericDefaultAssoc) so the DefaultKeyword lead is unambiguous; otherwise the type position is `castTypeRef` (typedef-admitting, with the shared `commitRequiresTypeName` triage — a value in type position fails loud). The two alts share the `: assignmentExpr` tail shape; the semantic tier discriminates default-vs-typed by the DefaultKeyword child.

builtinOffsetofExpr.$comment:
[[D-FFI-OFFSETOF-MACRO]] (closed 2026-08-24, cycle P31): GNU `__builtin_offsetof ( type-name , member-designator )` — a member's byte offset within a completed struct/union, as a `size_t` CONSTANT.
★★★ THIS IS WHAT `<stddef.h>`'s `offsetof` EXPANDS TO, WHICH IS WHY IT OUTRANKED EVERY OTHER ROW IN THE DIRECTION-A CENSUS. ✔MEASURED by reading `-E` output on this host, gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 19.1.1: `offsetof(struct S, b)` expands LITERALLY to `__builtin_offsetof(struct S, b)`. The classic `((size_t)&((T*)0)->m)` text this feature was once sized around is NOT what a real SDK header hands a compiler any more ⇒ a TU that reaches ANY real header trips this token without the program ever writing it.
★★ THE OPERANDS ARE A TYPE-NAME AND A DESIGNATOR, NOT AN ARGUMENT LIST — which is the whole reason this is a grammar rule and not a builtin-function row: `struct S` is not an expression, and `b` names a MEMBER, a name that lives only in the composite's own member scope and resolves to nothing (S0001) through the ordinary identifier path. Before this rule DSS failed `error[P0002] expected 'ParenClose' — got 'struct'` (✔MEASURED through the shipped CLI at HEAD `60198126`): it was reading the whole thing as a CALL.
★ `castTypeRef` IS THE SHARED TYPE-NAME CHOKEPOINT, not a new one — the same rule `sizeofType`, `alignofType`, `typeofType`, `vaArgExpr`, `genericTypedAssoc` and `castExpr` reach their base through. So `(struct S, ...)`, `(union U, ...)` and `(MyTypedef, ...)` all work here for free, and what this rule accepts as a type can never drift from what a cast accepts.
★ NO `commitRequiresTypeName`, DELIBERATELY: that triage exists to ROLL BACK to a sibling VALUE reading, and this rule HAS no sibling. Keeping it would convert a precise `S_UnknownType` (that is not a type) into a speculation failure with nothing to say. The keyword-led FIRST set already makes the branch a unique production.

memberDesignator.$comment:
C 7.19's offsetof member-designator: a member name followed by any run of `.field` / `[index]` steps — `q`, `q.y`, `r[2]`, `q.inner[3].z`. ✔MEASURED on gcc 13.3.0 and clang 19.1.1: BOTH accept `.` and `[]` designators here, and both accept the RESULT in a static initializer AND as an array bound, so it must fold to a CONSTANT rather than merely type-check.
★★ THE STEP RULE IS THE SHIPPED `designator` — the VERY SAME one a designated initializer uses (`{ .a = 1, [2] = 3 }`), not a private copy. That is the point: `.field` and `[index]` are ONE piece of this language's vocabulary, and a second spelling of them would be two owners of one grammar, free to drift. Only the LEADING member name is spelled here, because an initializer designator leads with `.` and this form does not.

builtinTypesCompatibleExpr.$comment:
GNU `__builtin_types_compatible_p ( type-name , type-name )` — `1` when the two types are COMPATIBLE (C 6.2.7), `0` otherwise, as an `int` CONSTANT. Accepted by all four GNU-family oracles (✔MEASURED); DSS failed `error[P0002] expected 'ParenClose' — got 'int'` at HEAD `60198126`, again because it was reading a call.
★★ THE COMPATIBILITY PREDICATE IS NOT A NEW ONE. It is the SAME interned-TypeId identity `_Generic` matches an association with, after the same top-level-volatile strip — which is the identity [[D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY]] made NAME-keyed rather than representation-keyed. That is what makes this answer 0 for `(long, int)` on LLP64, where the two SHARE a representation, exactly as gcc does: the vocabulary entry is compared, not the width. A second predicate here would have been a second, contradictable owner of type identity.
★ WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITS OWN LINE: paired with `__builtin_choose_expr` below it IS GNU's pre-C11 `_Generic`, and that pair is how a portable header writes a type-dispatching macro that still compiles as C89. Neither half is much use alone, which is why they land together.

builtinChooseExpr.$comment:
GNU `__builtin_choose_expr ( const-expr , expr1 , expr2 )` — the compile-time `?:`. The controlling expression MUST be an integer constant expression; the chosen arm becomes the whole expression's value AND type, and the arm not chosen is UNEVALUATED and is not even type-checked as a value (gcc: the unused expression may be of any type). ✔MEASURED accepted by all four GNU-family oracles, INCLUDING the shape that proves the discard — `__builtin_choose_expr(1, 42, "not an int")`, which type-checks only if the string arm is genuinely dropped. DSS answered `error[S0001] __builtin_choose_expr` at HEAD `60198126`: an undeclared identifier, because it was, once more, a call.
★★ IT REUSES `_Generic`'s MACHINERY WHOLESALE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS CHEAP. `_Generic` already makes a COMPILE-TIME choice among sub-expressions, records the winner in the `nodeToSelectedExpr` side table, stamps the node with that winner's type, and lowers ONLY that sub-expression. The ONE thing this rule changes is HOW the winner is picked: an integer constant instead of a type match. Same side table, same lowering, same discard. A private selection path would have been two owners of `which sub-expression survives`.
★ THE ARMS ARE `assignmentExpr` (comma-free) for the reason `genericExpr`'s controlling expression is: a `,` here separates OPERANDS, so a comma-operator reading would swallow the next one. A comma expression is still spellable, in parens.

staticAssertDecl.$comment: C11/C23 6.7.10 `_Static_assert(constant-expression, string-literal);` and the C23 1-arg `_Static_assert(constant-expression);` — a static-assertion DECLARATION valid at BOTH file scope (topLevel alt) AND block scope (statement alt). Two spellings: the reserved `_Static_assert` and the C23 `static_assert` (both keywords). The condition is `assignmentExpr` (comma-free — a `,` here separates the optional message, so the comma-operator form must not swallow it, exactly like vaStartExpr's ap arg). The message is an OPTIONAL adjacent-string-concat literal (the vaStartExpr optional-second-arg pattern; ABSENT = the C23 1-arg form). SEMANTICS live in the semantic tier (semantics.staticAssertRule): the condition is const-evaluated by the SAME evaluator that folds `sizeof(T)`/enum/arithmetic in an array dimension — ZERO ⇒ S_StaticAssertFailed (message = the string literal), NONZERO ⇒ nothing. The `hirKind: Skip` row lowers a PASSED assertion to nothing in BOTH positions (the emptyStmt/includeDirective Skip precedent), and — because it is a MAPPED rule — makes peelToCore STOP here (never descending into the sole condition child of the 1-arg form).

castTypeBase.$comment:
C11/C23 6.7.7 type-name — the specifier-qualifier-list BASE, and the SOLE chokepoint for it: every type-name position in the language (castExpr, sizeofType, alignofType, typeofType, alignasTypeName, vaArgExpr, genericTypedAssoc, compoundLiteralExpr) reaches its base through `castTypeRef` → here, and `enumTypeSpecifier` reaches it directly. Widening this ONE alt is therefore how a base form becomes available to all nine at once.
★ TF-C101 (D-CSUBSET-TCL9-HEADER-CONSTRUCTS gap 2a): the three composite arms are the UNIFIED specifiers `structSpec`/`unionSpec`/`enumSpec`, NOT the ref-only `structTypeRef`/`unionTypeRef`/`enumTypeRef` they replaced. C 6.7.7p1's specifier-qualifier-list admits a struct-or-union-specifier WITH a member list, so `sizeof(struct { int dummy; })` is a conforming type-name operand (6.5.3.4p2 + 6.7.2.1p1) — MEASURED as what Tcl 9.0's `tclDecls.h:4046` TCLBOOLWARNING writes, and it previously died `P0001 expected 'ParenClose' — got '{'` because a ref-only arm cannot consume the body.
★ WHY THE SWAP AND NOT A SECOND ARM: two arms keyed on StructKeyword is exactly the `C_AmbiguousAlternatives` the loader refuses, and it is right to — one token cannot tell a tag reference from a definition. c25 (D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER) already solved that shape for the four DECLARATION-head alts by folding body-vs-ref into ONE rule whose `{optional structBody}` makes the split an INTERNAL 1-token (`BlockOpen`) decision; this reuses that rule rather than inventing a parallel path. The binder needs no new wiring: `structSpec` is ALREADY dual-mode registered — the DEFINITION arm in `semantics.declarations` (`definesWhenChild: structBody`) and the tag-REFERENCE arm in `semantics.references` (`isTagReference`, `nameMatch: lastIdentifier`) — and it is ALREADY in `semantics.scopes`, so a body defined here mints its type and opens its member scope wherever the node lands, expression position included. The pre-existing `sizeof(struct X)` tag-reference reading is unchanged: with no body present the reference arm resolves the tag exactly as `structTypeRef` did (pinned by SizeofNamedStructTagStillResolves).
★ RESIDUE, LOUD AND NAMED: `declHeadForParam` still carries the ref-only arms, so an inline composite DEFINITION in a PARAMETER head (`void f(struct { int x; } p)`) still fails loud at parse. That form is legal C but names a type no caller can spell, no consumer needs it, and widening a second alt has its own FIRST-set cost — it stays a parse error, never a silent mis-parse.

castTypeRef.$comment: c27 D-CSUBSET-VOLATILE-POINTEE: the two qualifier slots are `{repeat headQualifier}` (const|volatile, either order) — admitting a volatile-qualified cast type-name `(volatile u32 **)p` (sqlite 67392). The resolver wraps the base in VolatileQual when a volatile precedes the stars, so the cast builds Ptr<Ptr<VolatileQual(u32)>> and a deref of it is volatile; const stays ignored. (Was two `{optional ConstKeyword}` slots pre-c27.) c11 D-CSUBSET-EAST-CONST-CAST: a cast/sizeof type-name admits const PRE-base (`const char *` — west) AND POST-base before the stars (`char const *` — EAST, the SQLite-pervasive form). In a DECLARATION the `*` lives in the declarator so the head `char const` already parsed; a cast bundles base+stars here, so the post-base const slot is what admits east-const. The const resolver IGNORES const for type identity (a cast yields an rvalue), so all forms intern the same pointer type. The two const slots straddle the REQUIRED base token (no ambiguity); a POST-stars qualifier (`char * const` / `u32 * volatile`) RIDES INSIDE the pointer layer (c29 D-CSUBSET-POST-STAR-CAST-QUALIFIER): the leading stars are `{repeat pointerLayer}` (= `StarOp {repeat ptrQualifier}`, c ~500) NOT bare `{repeat StarOp}`, so the post-star const/volatile is present ONLY with a star — NO zero-star adjacency (the c11 ambiguity a separate post-stars optional would have caused). The resolver counts each pointerLayer child as ONE star for ptrDepth and STRIPS its ptrQualifiers: a cast yields an RVALUE with NO top-level cv (C 6.5.4) — `(int * const)p` and `(int *)p` intern the SAME `Ptr<int>`, and a post-star VOLATILE is dropped (no VolatileQual on the cast POINTER) — the c27 PRE-stars-volatile pointee path (`volatile u32 *`→`Ptr<VolatileQual(u32)>`) is SEPARATE and unbroken. c26 D-CSUBSET-ABSTRACT-DECLARATOR-TYPE-NAME: an ABSTRACT direct-declarator (`(*)(void)`/`(*)(int)`/`[N]`/`(*)[N]`) may follow the base+stars — the fn-pointer/array type-name forms (`(int(*)(void))p`, the sqlite osGeteuid cast). It reuses `abstractDirectDeclarator` (the abstract twin of `directDeclarator`, sharing parenDeclarator+fnSuffix+arrayDeclSuffix), so the semantic resolver folds the type via the SHARED `directDeclaredType` (Ptr<Fn(void)->int>) — the SAME machinery a declaration's declarator takes. It is the ABSTRACT twin (Identifier base EXCLUDED) NOT `directDeclarator` because a bare-identifier base would make `(c * c)` (a multiplication) speculatively commit as a bogus cast; and it is NOT the full `declarator` because the leading POINTER STARS are consumed by `{repeat pointerLayer}` above (a star-led declarator's FIRST `pointerLayer` would collide with the repeat — C_AmbiguousAlternatives). OPTIONAL: a star-only cast (`int*`) leaves it empty — none of {fnSuffix,parenDeclarator,arrayDeclSuffix} matches the closing `)`, so `(int*)` stays `castTypeBase`+pointerLayer(StarOp). A NAMED declarator with the name NESTED in parens (`(int (x))expr` / `(int(*p)(void))expr`) parses (via parenDeclarator) but is rejected LOUD at the type-resolve via `S_TypeNameDeclaratorNotAbstract` — never silently parsed as the bare base.

charLiteralExpr.$comment: C11/C23 6.4.4.4: a character constant is opener + coalesced body + closer. The opener is an INLINE token alt (`'`|`L'`|`u'`|`U'`|`u8'`) — token-leaf alt branches consume EXACTLY one token and push it DIRECTLY (no wrapper node; the stringLiteralExpr precedent), so the opener token stays a DIRECT child of this node and charLiteralNodeOf / the semantic char-typing override find it AND recover its SPECIFIC kind (the C23 element-type discriminator). D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: the trailing `CharEnd` is the closing `'`, now a real token (charBody's `defaultToken.closeToken` — see $closingDelimiterTokenComment); it is a DISTINCT kind from the `CharLiteral` body precisely so a kind-filtering body reader can never mistake the delimiter for a second body segment. Children go 2 → 3; every consumer locates the body by KIND (hirLowering.charLiteral.bodyToken=CharLiteral), not by index, so nothing shifts.

stringLiteralExpr.$comment: C 5.1.1.2 phase 6 (D-CSUBSET-ADJACENT-STRING-CONCAT): adjacent string literals concatenate — `"a" "b"` is `"ab"`. The first opener+StringLiteral+StringEnd TRIPLE is required; the zero-or-more repeat captures each further triple as FLAT children (sequences inline, no wrapper node), so a lone string yields exactly 3 children. ★ D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: `StringEnd` (the closing `"`, now a real token — `string` mode's `defaultToken.closeToken`, see $closingDelimiterTokenComment) MUST appear in BOTH the head sequence AND the repeat body. Omitting it from the REPEAT would not merely under-describe the tree — the repeat would fail to match at the second piece's closer and ADJACENT STRING CONCATENATION (`"a" "b"`) would stop parsing as one literal. And it must stay a kind DISTINCT from `StringLiteral` because `decodeAdjacentStringBodies` selects segments by filtering children on the body kind: give the closer the body kind and this exact rule silently decodes `"abc"` as `abc"` and `"a" "b"` as `a"b"`, with the semantic Array<Char,N+1> typer and the HIR lowering both reading the SAME over-long decode through the SAME chokepoint — agreeing on the wrong length, so no cross-tier guard fires. The opener is an INLINE token alt (C11/C23 6.4.5: `"`|`L"`|`u"`|`U"`|`u8"`) — token-leaf alt branches consume EXACTLY one token and push it DIRECTLY (no wrapper node; the typeSpecifierSeq precedent), so the opener token stays a DIRECT child of this node and stringLiteralNodeOf / decodeAdjacentStringBodies find it AND recover its SPECIFIC kind (the element-core discriminator). Concatenation is at the DECODED code-unit level (each body decoded FIRST, then joined) via the single chokepoint every body consumer routes through. Safe in every use site: primaryExpr, attr args (terminate at `)`), the externDecl library-override tail (terminates at `;`) — none has a string opener in its follow set. Prefix-mixing across adjacent pieces (`u"a" L"b"`) is a LATER cycle — the element core is taken from the FIRST opener today.

argList.$comment: FC5: assignmentExpr (NOT expression) — the comma here is an arg SEPARATOR, never a comma-operator, so `f(a, b)` is 2 args. A comma-operator arg is written parenthesized: `f((a, b))`.

semantics.$volatileMarkerComment: c21 (D-CSUBSET-VOLATILE-QUALIFIER): the language's volatile qualifier token. Read by the type-position resolver's CO-LOCATED pointer arm (castTypeRef cast/sizeof type-names) to reject a pointer-to-volatile-POINTEE (`volatile int *`) position-aware (volatile-before-star = pointee = REJECT; after-the-star = pointer-object = ACCEPT). DECLARATION forms — objects, params, AND struct/union members (c23 removed the head star from typeRefAllowingStruct, so a member's `*` now binds per-declarator like every other declaration position) — reject via the per-declaration-rule volatileMarker (head-volatile + a declarator star); the two arms together make the fail-loud complete.
semantics.$atomicMarkerComment: FC17.9(d) cycle 1b (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): the language's `_Atomic`-class qualifier token — the LIVE SemanticConfig-level driver of the type-qualifier wrap, EXACTLY parallel to `volatileMarker` above. The type-position resolver (resolveTypeNodeImpl's CO-LOCATED base arm + declaratorDeclaredType's east/pointer-layer arm) reads THIS token: an `atomicMarker` BEFORE the first `pointerToken` wraps the base pointee (`_Atomic int *` => Ptr<atomicQualified(int)>); an `atomicMarker` INSIDE a pointer layer (east) wraps that pointer object (`int * _Atomic` => atomicQualified(Ptr<int>)). It COMPOSES with `volatileMarker` in the ONE shared {volatile,atomic} bitset skin (cycle 1a `qualified` merges bits, order-independent). NOTE: unlike volatile, `_Atomic` is a NEW qualifier with NO legacy per-DeclarationRule marker — object-atomicity is derived UNIFORMLY from the resolved TYPE (isAtomicQualified) at access lowering, exactly as c27 made volatile do (the per-DeclarationRule `volatileMarker` scan was RETIRED at c27; a parallel per-declaration atomicMarker would be write-only dead config, so it is deliberately NOT added). Source-agnostic: the engine reads THIS token, never a hardcoded keyword.
semantics.$shippedLibDirsComment: FF11 (2026-06-05) + Model 3 (2026-06-09): the SYSTEM include search path (C's /usr/include analogue) for the angle form `#include <h>`. A directory under src/dss-config/; the header stem maps to a language-NEUTRAL JSON descriptor (`<stem>.json`, e.g. stdio.json) read by src/ffi/shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp — its symbols (name + hir-text signature) are injected into semantic scope before Pass 2, then flow through FF5 synthesizeFfiFromSourceDecls like a program's own extern. Model 3 made each descriptor PLATFORM-NEUTRAL: ONE descriptor per header, carrying a per-object-format `library` map ({"pe":...,"elf":...,"macho":...}); the active compilation target's format selects its runtime image at compile_pipeline resolution (keyed via objectFormatKindName), so a SINGLE neutral directory serves every target. This DISSOLVED the former per-platform-directory selection + D-FFI-SHIPPED-LIB-PLATFORM-SELECT. The full surface (stdio/stdlib/string/ctype/math) + provenance/variadic-exclusion notes live in src/dss-config/shippedLibs/README.md.
semantics.$pointerConversionsComment: D-LANG-POINTER-VOID-CONVERT (step 13.2, 2026-06-02): C-standard §6.3.2.3 — `void*` converts implicitly to/from any object-pointer type without a cast. The two directions are configured INDEPENDENTLY (matching C++'s split, where only the safe direction is implicit). c declares BOTH true (C-family semantics). A future C++ frontend would declare {implicitToVoidPtr: true, implicitFromVoidPtr: false} matching ISO C++ §7.11. Rust/Swift would declare both false. DEFAULT is false (struct-init); strict typing is the safety-respecting default, opposite of the Array→Ptr decay opt-out direction (which is pervasive C-family idiom; void-ptr conversion is a safety relaxation). Pointer arithmetic on void* and void*↔fn-pointer conversions are separate concerns anchored at D-LANG-VOIDPTR-ARITH-REJECT and D-LANG-VOIDPTR-FN-CONVERT respectively.
semantics.$pointerAliasingComment: Two orthogonal C99-derived alias-analysis opt-ins. `strictAliasingOnDistinctTypes` (C99 §6.5): accessing an object through a pointer of an incompatible type is undefined behavior — lets the MIR optimizer's CSE/LICM Load admission prove Ptr<I32> and Ptr<I64> don't alias (Rule 6 in mirMayAlias). `charTypesAliasAll` (C99 §6.5 ¶7): character-type pointers may alias an object of any type — the canonical strict-aliasing carve-out for serializers/hash-visitors/memcpy. C-family languages declare both true. A Rust frontend or strict-typed DSL would declare `charTypesAliasAll: false` (the type-checker enforces aliasing at a higher tier). See D-OPT-LOAD-ALIAS-ANALYSIS for the substrate's design.
semantics.$nonObjectTypeSizesComment: D-CSUBSET-VOID-POINTER-ARITHMETIC-REFUSED: GNU C's 'Arithmetic on void- and Function-Pointers' (gcc manual 6.24), which clang implements identically. gcc states it as ONE rule — 'the size of a void or of a function' is 1 — and everything follows: `sizeof` and `_Alignof` of `void` or of a function type yield 1, and pointer arithmetic on a `void *` / a function pointer scales by 1, i.e. it is BYTE arithmetic. ISO C forbids all of it (6.5.3.4p1 forbids sizeof of a function or an incomplete type; 6.2.5p19 makes `void` permanently incomplete; 6.5.6p2 admits `p +- n` only for a complete OBJECT type), so under `DSS = (gcc union clang union MSVC) union ISO C` the UNION decides and a unanimous ACCEPTANCE settles it. MEASURED at P42 through the shipped CLI: gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x` and clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23`, probed SEPARATELY and every binary RUN, both accept `void *p; p = p + 1` / `p += 2` / `p++` / `++p` / `--p` / `p -= 1` / `q - p` / a `const void *` / `sizeof(void)` / `sizeof(*p)` / `sizeof(f)` / `sizeof(*f)` / `_Alignof(void)` / `_Alignas(void)` / `fp + 0`; DSS refused all 19 with H0009 or S0029. ONE declaration, TWO tiers: the semantic const-fold (`_Static_assert`, an array bound) and, threaded through `MirLoweringConfig` by compile_pipeline, HIR->MIR (`sizeof`/`_Alignof` and the element stride) both read it through the single `operandLayout` query, so the tiers cannot drift. THIS IS THE OPERAND SIZE, NOT AN OBJECT LAYOUT: `computeLayout` still refuses both kinds, so `void x;`, `const void cv;`, `typedef void V; V y;`, file-scope `void g;`, `struct T { void x; };`, `union U { void x; int i; };` and `void a[3];` were all made to FAIL LOUD, and that work is DONE rather than outstanding — D-CSUBSET-VOID-OBJECT-DECLARATION-ACCEPTED is CLOSED, so this clause is a record of a decision taken, not a refusal still to be implemented. Every one is a constraint violation both references reject, and the first six were SILENTLY ACCEPTED by DSS before P42. ✔RE-MEASURED 2026-08-27 (P42 lane AI) through the shipped CLI on x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec, all seven, and SIX of the seven match the sentence exactly: `void x;`, `const void cv;`, `typedef void V; V y;` and file-scope `void g;` give S_IncompleteTypeObject, and the two composite members give S_IncompleteTypeMember. ⚠ THE SEVENTH DID NOT, AND THE SENTENCE WAS HIDING IT INSIDE A LIST — FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: `void a[3];` passed the SEMANTIC tier entirely and was refused only at the object producer, as error[K_NoMatchingObjectFormat]. It WAS refused — never a miscompile — but at the wrong tier and under a diagnostic about object formats, which tells a user nothing about C 6.7.6.2p1's *the element type shall not be an incomplete or function type*. The same declaration arm now tests the array's ELEMENT chain, so all seven shapes give a positioned semantic diagnostic and the seventh joins the other six on S_IncompleteTypeObject (✔MEASURED, all seven, after the fix). ⚠ The test is `void`, not *incomplete*, and the narrowness is deliberate: an array of an incomplete STRUCT may be a file-scope TENTATIVE definition a later definition completes, which C permits and both references accept, while `void` is the one element type C 6.2.5p19 says can never be completed. D-CSUBSET-VOID-ARRAY-REFUSED-AT-THE-OBJECT-PRODUCER-NOT-THE-SEMANTIC-TIER. An INCOMPLETE composite pointee is likewise still refused — `operandLayout` names these two kinds and nothing else, so `struct S; p + 1` keeps failing loud as gcc and clang both do. NOTE the values are SIZES, not booleans: a language wanting the strict-ISO refusal OMITS the block (every non-C schema does, and is byte-identical to the pre-P42 engine), and a 0 is refused at config load because a stride of 0 makes every element of an arithmetic sequence alias byte offset 0. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this block -> `SemanticAnalyzerC.SizeofAndAlignofOfNonObjectTypesFoldInAConstantExpression`, `.AFalseAssertionAboutVoidsSizeStillFails`, `.SizeofVoidFoldsInsideAnArrayDimension`, `MirLoweringC.VoidPointerAdditionStridesOneByteWithNoScalingMul`, `.VoidPointerDifferenceIsAByteCountWithNoDivide`, `.SizeofAndAlignofNonObjectTypesFoldToOne` and `examples/c/c_void_pointer_arithmetic` all go RED, while every refusal pin stays green (MEASURED in exactly that state, before this key was added).
semantics.$declaratorsComment: FC4 c1 stage 2a: the C 6.7.6 declarator role vocabulary. The shared declarator walk (name extraction — binder sketch + analyzer) and the Pass 1.5 inversion engine consume ONLY these resolved roles. The pointer/fn/array/group structure lives in the DECLARATOR; heads carry the base type alone.

declarators.$groupRuleComment: D-CSUBSET-PARENTHESIZED-FUNCTION-DEFINITION-DECLARATOR-REFUSED: the REDUNDANT-PARENTHESIS level of C 6.7.6p1 (`direct-declarator := '(' declarator ')'`). It is not cosmetic vocabulary and it is not only about function POINTERS. The shared upward walk (`innermostNameDerivation` in core/types/declarator_walk.hpp) STEPS OUT through this role to find the derivation that actually types the name, which is what makes `int (foo)(int x) { … }` a FUNCTION DEFINITION rather than a refusal — the standard glibc/musl idiom for defining a name that is ALSO a function-like macro, since `(name)` suppresses the macro at the definition site while leaving it live for ordinary calls. The same walk makes `int (foo)(int x);` a PROTOTYPE, makes the definition's parameters the DEFINITION's own (body-visible) instead of a function pointer's (isolated), and hands CST->HIR the suffix its parameter harvest reads. ✔MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both compile and RUN every such shape; before the walk learned this role DSS produced four different failures from the one blindness (S0018 at the definition, S0002 at the prototype/definition pair, S0001 on the definition's own parameter, H0009 on the lowered arity). ⚠ Stepping out must NOT lose what is written INSIDE the parentheses: a pointer layer there reaches the name first, so `int (*fp)(int) { … }` stays the loud refusal it must be. A language whose declarator grammar has no grouping level simply omits this role and the ascent arm never runs.
declarators.$arraySuffixModifierTokensComment: VLA C4c (D-CSUBSET-VLA, C99 §6.7.6.2/6.7.6.3): the token kinds that decorate an array-PARAMETER suffix — a `static`, the three cv-qualifiers, and the unspecified-size `*` — none of which is part of the length BOUND. The shared arraySuffixBoundNode / arraySuffixHasModifier helpers skip these (DIRECT children only) so a bound behind a decoration (`int a[static n]`) is still located, and a bare decoration (`int a[*]`, `int a[restrict]`) reads as an ABSENT bound (decays like `[]`) rather than a runtime VLA. ENGINE-AGNOSTIC: a language without array-parameter decorations simply omits this list (empty ⇒ the plain first-non-bracket-child view, unchanged).
declarators.$p56AfterDeclaratorGrainComment:
P56 (D-CSUBSET-TRAILING-ATTRIBUTE-RUN-IS-READ-AT-THE-WRONG-GRANULARITY): each after-declarator run now DECLARES what its attributes appertain to, and the two runs that share this source position do NOT agree, which is the whole reason the key had to gain a grain rather than a subset.
★★ `attrSpec` (GNU) => `declarator`: the run confers on the declared ENTITY, in EVERY declarator shape. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-03, gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3, each probed separately at -std=c11, c17 and c2x, by use-site differential against an undecorated control: `void f(void) __attribute__((deprecated));`, `int x __attribute__((deprecated));`, `int arr[3] __attribute__((deprecated));`, `void (*p)(int) __attribute__((deprecated));` and `void (*p)(int) __attribute__((__noreturn__));` all confer on the entity in both. MSVC 19.51 implements no `__attribute__` in ANY position (error C2061 at /std:c11, /std:c17 AND /std:clatest), so it ABSTAINS — an abstention is not agreement, and two working references make the GNU spelling REQUIRED.
★★★ `stdAttr` (C23) => `declaratorUnlessTypeDerived`: the grain depends on the DECLARATOR, and all THREE references agree on the split. ✔MEASURED the same day, four attributes (`deprecated`, `nodiscard`, `maybe_unused`, `noreturn`) x two declarator shapes:
  • after a bare IDENTIFIER declarator the run confers on the ENTITY — `int x [[deprecated]];` draws gcc’s and clang’s -Wdeprecated-declarations at the USE and MSVC /std:clatest’s C4996 at the USE; `int x [[maybe_unused]] = 1;` silences -Wunused-variable in gcc and clang where the control warns.
  • after an ARRAY or FUNCTION declarator it appertains to the TYPE and NOBODY confers it — `void f(void) [[deprecated]];` and `int arr[3] [[deprecated]];` each give gcc `‘deprecated’ attribute ignored` with no warning at the use, clang `error: ‘deprecated’ attribute cannot be applied to types` (rc=1), and MSVC `warning C4649: attributes are ignored in this context` with no C4996 at the use.
C23 6.7.6p1 puts the sequence after an identifier on the declared entity while 6.7.6.2p1/6.7.6.3p1 put the one after an array- or function-declarator on the array or function TYPE. THE ANSWER IS A PROPERTY OF THE SHAPE, CONSTANT ACROSS THE FOUR ATTRIBUTES — which refutes the assumption that granularity is per-attribute here.
⚠ THIS REPLACES THE SHORT-LIVED `afterDeclaratorEntityAttrRules` SUBSET KEY (P56 lane `nr`, hours earlier). Every measurement behind that key RE-DERIVED true; the SHAPE was wrong. A subset can only say entity-or-not, so `stdAttr` had to be either IN — which invents `void f(void) [[deprecated]]`, a meaning no reference confers — or OUT, which drops `int x [[deprecated]]`, a fact all three references confer. ✔MEASURED at this base through the shipped CLI: DSS did BOTH of those at once, conferring on `f` (above the union) and on `x` (correct), out of the SAME over-broad read. Only a grain that can depend on the declarator gets both right.
ⓘ The subset CROSS-CHECK is retired rather than weakened: a grain written ON an entry cannot disagree with the list it is in.
declarators.$afterDeclaratorEntityAttrRulesComment:
★★★ P56 [[D-CSUBSET-TRAILING-NORETURN-NOT-HONORED]]: the SUBSET of the run above whose attributes appertain to the declared ENTITY rather than to its TYPE — the positions from which a consumer may confer an entity-level semantic fact. This is the SEMANTIC QUESTION that row said had to be settled before the wiring, and it is settled by measurement, each reference probed SEPARATELY, by -Wreturn-type differential against an undecorated control (✔MEASURED 2026-09-03).
★★ THE GNU RUN CONFERS. `void die(int) __attribute__((__noreturn__));` — gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 are BOTH silent at a non-void caller whose last path calls `die`, where the undecorated control draws `control reaches end of non-void function` / `non-void function does not return a value in all control paths`, at `-std=c11`, `-std=c17` and `-std=c2x` alike. Same for the `extern` spelling, the `__attribute__((noreturn))` undunder spelling, two clauses in one specifier, two specifiers in one run, the DEFINITION rather than the prototype, and a later REDECLARATION carrying it alone. MSVC 19.51 does not implement `__attribute__` in any form (`error C2061: syntax error: identifier '__attribute__'` at `/std:c11`, `/std:c17` AND `/std:clatest`), so it casts NO vote on the GNU spelling — a reference that never accepts the construct is not a reference that refuses its meaning. Two references that WORK ⇒ REQUIRED.
★★ `stdAttr` IS EXCLUDED, AND NOT ONE REFERENCE DISAGREES. `void die(int) [[noreturn]];` — gcc `warning: 'noreturn' attribute ignored` and the caller STILL draws -Wreturn-type; clang `error: 'noreturn' attribute cannot be applied to types` (rc=1); MSVC `/std:clatest` `warning C4649` plus `C4715 'probe': not all control paths return a value`. C23 6.7.13.1 is the reason rather than a coincidence: an attribute-specifier-sequence written AFTER a declarator appertains to the TYPE that the declaration specifiers and that declarator determine, and `noreturn` does not apply to a type. Honoring it would be an INVENTED EXTENSION — the half of `DSS = (gcc ∪ clang ∪ MSVC) ∪ ISO C` that binds upward.
★ THE SPLIT IS GENERAL, NOT A `noreturn` QUIRK, AND THE RESIDUE IS NAMED: ✔MEASURED the same day, `void f(void) [[deprecated]];` is ignored by gcc and refused by clang while the GNU twin warns at the use site in both. The FC17 `scanAttributeSemantics` per-declarator loop still folds the WHOLE `afterDeclaratorAttrRules` list, so a trailing `[[deprecated]]`/`[[nodiscard]]` is over-applied to the entity today. Narrowing that scan also moves its unknown-name diagnostic and the TF-C93 decl-kind gate across four more verbs, so it is left to its own row rather than half-fixed under this one.
★ WHY A SECOND KEY RATHER THAN A FLAG ON THE FIRST: this is the `asmLabelRule` situation exactly — several things share one after-declarator source position and mean different things, so the shared `isDeclaratorDecorationRule` skip stays over the WHOLE position while each ROLE gets its own key. The loader REFUSES an entry that is not also in `afterDeclaratorAttrRules` (a name outside that list would be a run the init-detection scans do not skip, i.e. a node the declarator walk believes is an initializer). ABSENT or EMPTY ⇒ no trailing run confers an entity fact, which is the pre-P56 behaviour and the right answer for toy/tsql, which declare no such run at all.
RED-ON-DISABLE (REMOVE direction): delete this key and `analysis/test_semantic_analyzer_c` goes red on `SemanticAnalyzerC.NoreturnIsHonoredInEveryAttributePosition` (its trailing arms) and on `SemanticAnalyzerC.TrailingNoreturnIsPerDeclaratorAndDeclarationLevelIsNot`, while `SemanticAnalyzerC.C23TrailingStdAttrNoreturnAppertainsToTheTypeNotTheEntity` — whose leading CONTROL arm is the same scan through a different root — stays green.
declarators.$plainListRuleComment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEDEF-MULTI-DECLARATOR): the THIRD declarator-list SHAPE the shared walk recognizes — a comma-separated run of BARE `declaratorRule` nodes with no per-slot wrapper, no initializer slot and no attribute run. It is the c23 `memberListRule` precedent applied once more: an OPTIONAL extra role rather than overloading `listRule`, because the three shapes carry genuinely different per-slot grammar (an initDeclarator owns `= init` + an attribute run; a structMemberDeclarator owns a bit-field width; a plain declarator owns neither) and `collectDeclarators` must descend each correctly. A language that has no such list omits the key and the walk behaves exactly as before.
declarators.$asmLabelRuleComment: TF-C88 (D-CSUBSET-ASM-LABEL-SYMBOL-RENAME): the rule that carries an explicit assembler NAME for the declarator it follows. Declared HERE — beside `afterDeclaratorAttrRules` — because it occupies the same after-declarator position and the same PER-DECLARATOR granularity, and because every init-detection scan (`the first visible Internal child that is not the declarator IS the initializer`) must skip it or it is mis-read as the initializer. It is DELIBERATELY not a member of `afterDeclaratorAttrRules`: that list also feeds the LINKAGE fold (`declaratorAttrRoots` -> `linkageFrom`), which would walk an asm label's tokens as attribute clauses and fire a bogus H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on `__asm`. Two roles, two keys, one shared skip predicate.

semantics.$parametersComment: C 6.7.6.3p10: a parameter list of exactly `(void)` declares ZERO parameters. The engine applies this at the ONE param-harvest chokepoint when the sole param resolves to lattice Void AND is unnamed; a NAMED void param or void-mixed-with-others is S_InvalidVoidParam. Languages without the flag keep raw param lists.

declarations.$p44RestrictMarkerComment: P44 D-C23-REDECL-QUALIFIER-AXIS-HAS-THREE-UNCLAIMED-SOURCES (part b) — `restrictMarker` rides beside `constMarker` on EVERY declarator-mode row that has one, and the all-or-nothing is the design: the two markers feed ONE positional `QualifierSpine`, so a row that declared `const` and not `restrict` would emit a spine whose restrict bits are all zero — a claim of 'not restrict-qualified' rather than 'no claim', and the oracle would then refuse `int f(char *restrict *);` against a matching declaration. ✔MEASURED, gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=c2x`) and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c23`) probed SEPARATELY: `int f(char *restrict *); int f(char **);` and `char *restrict *g(void); char **g(void);` are REFUSED by both (a POINTEE qualifier, C 6.7.6.1p2), while the matching pair and the top-level `int f(char *restrict); int f(char *);` are ACCEPTED by both (6.7.6.3p15 drops a parameter's own top-level qualifier and names no particular qualifier). DSS accepted all four before this key existed — `restrict` is neither interned nor was it declarable anywhere. ★ IT IS A ROLE, NOT A `QualBit`: `restrict` is an ALIASING PROMISE that changes no layout, no calling convention and no codegen DSS performs, so interning it would perturb every type comparison in the compiler to serve one rule — the same reasoning `const` already carries. ⚠ The engine reads it from POINTER LAYERS ONLY (C 6.7.3.2p1 confines `restrict` to pointer types), so a head `restrict` is a constraint violation for the type resolver, never a qualification claim.
declarations.$tfc77AttrSlotComment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): the BLOCK-SCOPE mid-position attribute slot — `int __attribute__((aligned(16))) x = 1;` inside a body, MEASURED as P0009 before this cycle. `declaratorList` moved 1 → 2 IN THE SAME COMMIT as the grammar (the always-emitted `declAttrRun` now sits at role index 1); leaving it at 1 makes every local declaration address the attribute run as its declarator list. The slot IS honored: `aligned(N)` written here reaches `scanAttributeSemantics` through this key and applies (MEASURED — `int __attribute__((aligned(32))) x;` on an address-taken local is 32-BYTE ALIGNED AT RUN TIME, which it can only be if the value reached frame layout. ⚠ THIS USED TO READ "fails loud L_OverAlignedStackLocal" and was true until 2026-09-01, when D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS-OVERALIGNED-STACK-LOCAL closed and an over-stack-aligned local became HONORED rather than refused).
★★ `unknownStrictAttributeIsError` IS DELIBERATELY **NOT** SET HERE, AND THE REASON IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. It was tried and REVERTED in this cycle. The strict gate fires whenever a GNU clause name is absent from `semantics.attributeSemantics.effects` — but at file scope a second, DISJOINT vocabulary is also legitimate: the LINKAGE one (`linkageSpecifiers` keys + `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames`), which carries `weak` and `visibility` and which the strict gate cannot see. Turning the flag on here therefore rejected REAL C: `__attribute__((deprecated, __visibility__("hidden"))) int x = 0;` inside a body — a shipped pin (SemanticAnalyzerC.GnuSiblingClauseStringIsNotThisClausesMessage) and clang-clean code — became a loud S0031. A gate that refuses valid C is worse than the silence it replaces.
★ THE RESIDUAL GAP, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: an unrecognized GNU name at BLOCK scope is SILENT — in this new slot AND in the pre-existing LEADING slot alike (MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD: `__attribute__((frobnicate_xyz)) int x = 1;` compiled clean, exit 0, no diagnostic from any tier). This row lists `attrSpec` in `linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules` WHOLESALE, so the linkage tier is blind here by construction. That silence PREDATES this cycle and is not widened by it — the two block-scope positions behave IDENTICALLY, which is the property that actually matters (one attribute must not mean two things depending on where it is written). Closing it needs the strict gate to consult the row's LINKAGE vocabulary as well as the effects table — an engine change with its own design, not a flag flip. File scope is unaffected: `topLevelDecl` does not ignore `attrSpec`, so an unknown name there is a loud H000C in BOTH positions (MEASURED).
~~ CLOSED 2026-08-27 (P42), AND **NOT** BY THE FLAG THIS COMMENT WARNS ABOUT — `unknownStrictAttributeIsError` IS STILL DELIBERATELY UNSET HERE, AND MUST STAY UNSET. Two corrections, both measured. **(1) THE PRESCRIBED FIX WAS WRONG AS WRITTEN.** Consulting *the row's* linkage vocabulary closes nothing: `varDecl`'s `linkageSpecifiers` holds `static`/`_Thread_local`/`thread_local`, which are KEYWORDS and can never spell an attribute clause name, and the rows whose gate is strict (`typedefDecl`, the composites, the members) declare NO linkage vocabulary at all. ✔MEASURED — a per-row union leaves `typedef __attribute__((weak)) int T;` a loud `S0031`, which gcc 13.3 (`-std=c2x`) and clang 18 (`-std=c23`) each compile with a warning and exit 0. The union that closes it is LANGUAGE-WIDE (`languageModelsAttributeName` in semantic_analyzer.cpp walks every declaration row's `linkageSpecifiers` keys + `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames`), because "does this language KNOW this name" is a language-level question and "may it appertain HERE" is the decl-kind gate's separate one. **(2) THE SEVERITY WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG TOO.** ✔MEASURED, both references separately: at BLOCK scope `__attribute__((cleanup(f)))`, `__attribute__((section("s")))` and `__attribute__((used))` are accepted with NO diagnostic by gcc AND clang, and all three are accepted by DSS today — so an ERROR here would newly REJECT three real GNU attributes to catch one typo, which is the very trap the paragraph above records. The block-scope gap is closed with the SUPPRESSIBLE Warning `S_UnknownAttribute` (S003C), the same code the C23 `[[...]]` form already uses for the same fact, promoted by `--warnings-as-errors` for anyone who wants the strict posture. ✔MEASURED after the change: `__attribute__((frobnicate_xyz)) int x = 1;` and `int __attribute__((frobnicate_xyz)) x = 1;` inside a body BOTH warn S003C at rc=0 (the two positions stay IDENTICAL, which is this row's real requirement), while `__attribute__((deprecated, __visibility__("hidden"))) int x = 0;` in a body stays CLEAN. ★ AND NO NEW CONFIG KEY WAS NEEDED: which tier owns the unknown-name verdict is DERIVED from the config that already exists — a row that lists `attrSpec` in `linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules` (this one) is invisible to `linkageFrom`, so the semantic tier owns it; `topLevelDecl` does not, so the linkage tier keeps its H000C and one typo is never reported twice. ~~
declarations.$prototypeSynthesizesExternComment: c86 (D-CSUBSET-BARE-PROTO-EXTERN-SYNTHESIS): a BLOCK-scope bare prototype (`int f(int);` inside a body — re-homed onto the file scope per D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-PROTOTYPE, C 6.2.2p4) that survives with no in-TU definition synthesizes the same no-library extern as a file-scope proto (routed to the module decls, mirroring the static-local accumulator). Same three-way resolution as topLevelDecl's flag.
declarations.$staticStorageComment: D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-STATIC: a block-scope `static` confers static storage duration (C 6.2.4). CST→HIR's linkageFrom folds {binding:local, staticStorage:true} from the SAME prefix scan and routes the declaration to a hidden module-global (internal linkage). register/auto/attribute specifiers carry no linkage and are ignored (ignoredKinds/ignoredRules) so they never trip the unknown-specifier diagnostic.
declarations.$volatileComment: c27 (D-CSUBSET-VOLATILE-POINTEE): `volatile` is a TYPE qualifier (TypeKind::VolatileQual). The resolver wraps the base in VolatileQual when a volatileMarker precedes the stars (`volatile int *` => Ptr<VolatileQual(int)>) and wraps the pointer for an east ptrQualifier (`int * volatile` => VolatileQual(Ptr<int>)); object-volatility is read off the symbol's top-level VolatileQual type at access lowering, pointee-volatility rides the accessed type at the deref/index/member (MirInstFlags::Volatile). ALL pointee/member/param/typedef forms now compile — the prior S_VolatilePointeeNotSupported reject is retired. const stays ignored (no wrapper).
declarations.$threadLocalLinkageComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, C11 6.7.1p3): both thread-storage spellings map to {threadStorage:true} so the LEGAL block-scope form `static thread_local int x;` resolves cleanly (without these entries the tokens would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on legal C). threadStorage does NOT itself confer static routing — a bare block-scope `thread_local int x;` is rejected by Pass 2 (S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern) before lowering.
declarations.$noreturnIgnoreComment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN): the bare `_Noreturn` keyword carries NO linkage — ignored by kind (like RegisterKeyword/AutoKeyword). The attribute form `__attribute__((noreturn))` on a LOCAL is already covered by attrSpec ∈ linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules (wholesale). The SEMANTIC noreturn scan reads the keyword/attribute; without this ignore the `_Noreturn` token would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier.
declarations.$constexprIgnoreComment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR, C23 6.7.1): a BLOCK-scope `constexpr` carries NO linkage (it declares an automatic-storage constant object; only the FILE-scope form has C23 6.2.2p3 internal linkage — see topLevelDecl's linkageSpecifiers) — ignored by kind like RegisterKeyword/AutoKeyword. The SEMANTIC constexpr validation (semantics.constexpr.keywordToken) reads it; without this ignore the `constexpr` token would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier at block scope.
declarations.$stringEndIgnoreComment: D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: the closing `"` of an attribute's string argument is now a REAL token (`StringEnd` — see $closingDelimiterTokenComment), so it reaches cst_to_hir's flat specifier-prefix token scan. That scan already skips the string OPENER and BODY kinds structurally (cfg.stringStartToken / cfg.stringBodyToken, consumed by the `<identifier>:<decoded-body>` composite pairing), but the closer is neither — untouched it would fall through to the strict `linkageSpecifiers` lookup with the key `"` and fire H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on the perfectly legal `__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))`. Listing it here also keeps the composite probe's ignored-kind skip-ahead correct, so the closer is not mistaken for the start of a second (unsupported) adjacent-concat piece. StringEnd ONLY: `attrArgItem` admits no character constant (Identifier | IntLiteral | FloatLiteral | stringLiteralExpr | attrArgs), so `CharEnd` cannot occur in a specifier prefix — a char constant there already fails loud today, unchanged — and `HeaderEnd` exists only inside a `#include` directive line.
declarations.$inlineIgnoreComment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER, C99 6.7.4): a BLOCK-scope `inline` — legal C on a function DECLARATION (`static inline int f(int);` inside a body) — carries no linkage, so it is ignored by kind here exactly as at file scope. MEASURED: this is the ONE block-scope row the keyword actually reaches. `forDecl` and `autoInferredForDecl` declare NO `linkageSpecifiers` at all (a static/thread for-init must ERROR, not route to a hidden global), so `linkageFrom` early-returns on them and an entry there would be INERT config — a probe of `for (inline int fi = 0; …)` produced ZERO H000C before this edit, while the two block-scope varDecl forms produced two. Applying the keyword to a non-FUNCTION is a 6.7.4p1 constraint violation and is caught LOUD by the SEMANTIC gate (S_InlineNonFunction), not by this tier — the linkage scan is the wrong place to enforce a type constraint.
declarations.$alignasIgnoreComment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): an `alignasSpec` in the local specifier prefix (`alignas(16) int x;`) carries NO linkage — its subtree (`_Alignas ( … )`) is skipped WHOLESALE by the linkage scan (exactly like the C23 `stdAttr` `[[…]]`). The alignment is read by the SEMANTIC alignas scan, not here. Without this the `_Alignas` keyword token would fail loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier.

declarations.$forStaticComment: D-CSUBSET-LOCAL-STATIC (MF-2): `static` parses in the shared localDeclSpecifiers prefix, but a static (or any non-auto/register) storage class in a for-statement init-declaration is a C 6.8.5p3 constraint violation — gate it LOUD (never silently lower as an automatic loop variable). NO linkageSpecifiers here: a static for-init must error, not route to a hidden global. The StaticKeyword gatedMarker stays; only the S_VolatileNotSupported gate is removed (volatile is implemented — c21). TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): both thread-storage spellings parse in the shared prefix too — gated loud with S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern (C11 6.7.1p3: thread_local needs static/extern, and a for-init admits neither, so the requirement is unsatisfiable there; WITHOUT the gate `for (thread_local int i…)` would silently lower as a plain automatic — the row has no linkageSpecifiers, so the Pass-1 threadStorage scan finds no entry).

declarations.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE, C23 6.7.9): the HEAD-LESS initializer-inferred declaration. NO `head` — `inferTypeFromInitializer` waives the loader's declarator-mode head requirement and routes typing through the Pass-1.5 inference arm (single plain named declarator → initializer required → braced-single unwrap → infer → array/function DECAY → loud rejects for void/nullptr_t/unresolvable → stripVolatile → write). `declaratorList: 0` — post-strip children are [initDeclaratorList, EndStatement] (the specifierPrefix strip removes the REQUIRED localDeclSpecifiers prefix before positional counting; varDecl's is 1 because a declHead precedes its list). `requiredSpecifierToken: AutoKeyword` is the ★C1 presence gate — checked FIRST in the arm; without it `static x = 5;` (which PARSES into this rule) would silently become C89 implicit-int. ★M1: NO constMarker/volatileMarker — with no head, the const/volatile fallback scans span the WHOLE declaration INCLUDING THE INITIALIZER (the c58 initializer-const-leak: `auto p = (const char*)s;` would false-mark p const); C23 6.7.9 constrains auto to unqualified plain declarators anyway (`const auto x` is a loud parse error — D-CSUBSET-AUTO-QUALIFIED). NO prototypeSynthesizesExtern (a headless decl can never be a prototype; the plain-identifier gate rejects `auto f(void);` loud). linkage/ignored entries mirror varDecl so `static auto s = 1;` routes to a hidden module-global and `constexpr auto k = 5;` validates through the constexpr hook against the INFERRED type (P1 prefix scan → P1.5 infer → P2 validator ordering, audit-verified).
declarations.$threadLocalLinkageComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): mirror of varDecl's thread-storage entries — C23 6.7.1 admits `auto` beside thread_local, so `static thread_local auto s = 1;` is legal and must resolve; a bare `thread_local auto x = 5;` (no static) is Pass 2's S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern.
declarations.$stringEndIgnoreComment: D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: mirrors varDecl's `StringEnd` entry — the closing `"` of an attribute string argument is now a real token and must be ignored by kind, else `static auto s __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) = 1;` fires H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on the closer.
declarations.$inlineIgnoreComment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): mirrors varDecl's entry, and it is REACHABLE rather than defensive — MEASURED, `inline auto ai = 5;` inside a body parses into THIS row and fired one H000C before this edit. `inline` on an inferred OBJECT is a C99 6.7.4p1 constraint violation, but the LINKAGE tier is the wrong place to say so (it would report a type constraint under a linkage code and pre-empt the real diagnostic); the SEMANTIC gate S_InlineNonFunction owns it, so this row ignores the keyword exactly like varDecl. The `autoInferredForDecl` twin below needs NO entry — like `forDecl` it declares no `linkageSpecifiers`, so its scan early-returns.

declarations.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): the for-init mirror — same inference row as autoInferredVarDecl, but like forDecl it carries NO linkageSpecifiers (a static for-init must ERROR, not route to a hidden global) and COPIES forDecl's StaticKeyword gatedMarker so `for (static auto i = 0;;)` fails loud S_StaticStorageInForInit (C 6.8.5p3). TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): copies forDecl's thread-storage gatedMarkers too — `for (thread_local auto i = 0;;)` fails loud S_ThreadLocalRequiresStaticOrExtern (6.7.1p3 is unsatisfiable in a for-init).

declarations.$paramAdjustmentsComment: ★ THIS FLAG DECLARES 'this row is a C PARAMETER, apply the C 6.7.6.3 PARAMETER-TYPE ADJUSTMENTS to it' — BOTH of them. The key is a member of the CLOSED vocabulary owned by the schema loader (`kDeclarationRowKeys` in src/core/types/grammar_schema_json.cpp) and it names the whole rule, not one half of it; the engine helper it drives is named for the same thing (`adjustParamDeclaredType`). ~~ ★ IT IS ALSO THE ROW'S PARAMETER-NESS ITSELF, and the Pass-1 declarator mint reads it as such: a parameter is NEVER a function PROTOTYPE, so `isProto` (semantic_analyzer.cpp) is suppressed on this row. That is not a convenience — the INLINE p8 spelling `int f(int g(int))` writes exactly the syntax a prototype writes (a name carrying a `()` suffix), and without the suppression the parameter re-homes onto the FILE scope (two functions whose parameters merely share a name then collide, S0022 — legal C rejected, MEASURED) and CST→HIR's prototype gate emits NO VarDecl for it, so the parameter SLOT vanishes while the FnSig keeps its entry (`H_UnsupportedLoweringForKind: Function param count 1 mismatches FnSig param count 2`, MEASURED). The TYPEDEF spelling never had either defect — its declarator carries no `()` suffix at all — so only the inline form witnesses it. ~~ p7 (c82, D-CSUBSET-PARAM-ARRAY-ADJUSTMENT): a parameter declared 'array of T' — sized (`int a[64]`), unsized (`int a[]`), or multi-dim (`int a[][5]` -> ptr to int[5]) — ADJUSTS to 'pointer to T'. The flag (a) permits the absent-length `[]` on the param's OUTERMOST suffix (resolving via the incomplete-array path, like allowFlexibleArray) and (b) rewrites the resolved top-level Array to Ptr<element>. An inner-dimension `[]` (`int a[4][]`) still fails loud (S_FlexibleArrayInAggregate via the incomplete-element guard), matching C's ill-formedness. ~~ p8 (D-CSUBSET-PARAM-FN-TYPE-ADJUSTMENT): a parameter declared 'function returning T' — written inline (`void f(int g(int))`) or reached through a FUNCTION typedef (the macOS SDK's `memory_reader_t` / `vm_range_recorder_t` / `print_task_printer_t`, malloc/malloc.h:537,546,550, which are function and NOT function-pointer typedefs and are used bare as parameters) — ADJUSTS to 'pointer to function returning T'. Ptr<FnSig> is already adjusted and is left alone. ~~ BOTH adjustments run at BOTH resolution sites — the definitive Pass-1.5 visit that binds the param symbol (so sizeof(param)==8, and body uses index / CALL through the pointer) and the FnSig param harvest (so call-site checking matches the adjusted argument) — because both sites call the ONE helper. That is what makes a prototype and its definition structurally equal instead of drifting into S0022/S0003. ~~ RED-ON-DISABLE for p8: drop the FnSig arm from `adjustParamDeclaredType` and a function-typed parameter falls through to the FnSig-typed-Variable arm of the bind -> S0018 'function prototype declarations are not supported here'. Suppressing THAT diagnostic instead of adjusting the type would leave the parameter typed FnSig — a function value in a parameter slot, a silent miscompile.
declarations.$p32ParamAttrComment: P32 [[D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-PARAM-POSITION]]: the parameter-position attribute run. `specifierPrefix` keeps `head: 0` / `declarator: 1` byte-identical whether or not the parameter is decorated (decl_prefix_strip.hpp removes the node before positional counting); `declarationAttrSlotRules` is what makes the run HONOURED rather than merely parsed -- without it the attributes would reach no reader at all and be dropped in silence. * `unknownStrictAttributeIsError` is DELIBERATELY NOT set here, for the reason varDecl's $tfc77AttrSlotComment measured and this file has already been bitten by once: the strict gate fires on any GNU name absent from the effects table and cannot see the DISJOINT linkage vocabulary, so turning it on refuses real C.
declarations.$p56ParamGrainComment: P56 (D-CSUBSET-TRAILING-ATTRIBUTE-RUN-IS-READ-AT-THE-WRONG-GRANULARITY): this row is the clearest case of the conflation, because its TWO slots sit on OPPOSITE sides of the declarator. `paramDeclSpecifiers` is the leading specifier run => `declaration`; `paramTrailingAttrRun` is the after-declarator position => `declarator`. ⓘ A param declares exactly ONE declarator, so the two grains happen to select the same symbol here — the grain is stated for what it MEANS, not for what it currently selects, because a consumer reading it for the wrong reason is how this row was opened. ✔MEASURED: gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 both accept `void f(int x __attribute__((deprecated)));` clean.

declarations.$tfc77AttrSlotComment:
TF-C77 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-WITH-STORAGE-CLASS, mode 2): the FILE-SCOPE mid-position attribute slot — `static int SQLITE_NOINLINE f(…)` (a function DEFINITION; the MODE-2 sqlite spelling, 20 of sqlite's 119 `SQLITE_NOINLINE` sites, census over `.c` files ONLY — see `declAttrRun`'s own comment for the full 90/9/16/4 split and the `.h`-inclusive 122) and `int __attribute__((weak)) gv;`. Both were MEASURED as P0009 before this cycle.
★ THIS KEY AND THE ENGINE'S `linkagePrefixRoots` EXTENSION ARE ONE UNIT. `declarationAttrSlotRules` routes the slot to the SEMANTIC attribute scan (so `aligned(N)` here is applied); `linkagePrefixRoots` pushing every `declarationAttrSlotRules` child as a scan root is what routes it to the HIR LINKAGE fold (so `weak`/`visibility` here bind, and an unknown name fails loud H000C). With the grammar and this key but WITHOUT the engine change, `int __attribute__((weak)) gv;` parses clean and SILENTLY DROPS the weak binding — and swallows unknown names silently too, because this row does not set `unknownStrictAttributeIsError` and the GNU form's loudness here comes ENTIRELY from the linkage tier. That intermediate state is the silent-drop state and must never be a stopping point.
★ `unknownStrictAttributeIsError` is deliberately NOT set on THIS row (unlike `varDecl`): the linkage tier already makes an unknown GNU name a loud H000C here (MEASURED), so adding the semantic strict gate would report the same typo twice under two different codes.
★ INDEX MOVE: `declaratorList` 1 → 2 and `kindByChild.childPath` [2,0] → [3,0], both in this commit.
declarations.$prototypeSynthesizesExternComment: c86 (D-CSUBSET-BARE-PROTO-EXTERN-SYNTHESIS, C 6.2.2p5): a file-scope bare prototype with NO in-TU definition (`void sqlite3_free(void*);` — the sqlite3.h splice shape; SQLITE_API expands empty) synthesizes an ExternFunction with NO library binding. The LK11 merge resolves it against a sibling TU's definition (import stripped, calls direct); a bare re-declaration of a SHIPPED descriptor name re-binds to the descriptor's library (goal-2 suppression recorded the map); a survivor with neither fails LOUD at link (K_SymbolUndefined naming the symbol — ld's behavior). `static`/weak protos never synthesize (internal/weak linkage must not bind a sibling TU's public symbol) — they keep the loud H0009. RED-ON-DISABLE: drop this flag -> the shell.c 2-TU probe regresses to H0009 'Ref to unbound symbol' at the first sqlite3_* call.
declarations.$linkageSpecifiersComment: D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-SPECIFIERS: 'static' -> internal (Local) binding; '__attribute__((weak))' -> Weak; FC4 c1 adds the COMPOSITE key 'visibility:hidden' — linkageFrom forms '<identifier>:<decoded-string-body>' when a specifier identifier is immediately followed by a parenthesized string literal (__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))). 'linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules' skips C23 [[...]] stdAttr subtrees wholesale (D14: parsed, ignored).
declarations.$constexprLinkageComment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR): C23 6.2.2p3 (N3096) — a FILE-scope object declared `constexpr` has INTERNAL linkage (constexpr joins static in the 6.2.2p3 list). The keyword text maps to {binding:local}; it COMPOSES with an explicit co-present `static` idempotently (both map to local; last-wins is a no-op). This is NOT the noreturn {binding:global}-clobber hazard — that was a no-op default entry overwriting a co-present static's INTERNAL binding; here both entries agree. ~~ P53 CORRECTION, BY MEASUREMENT (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): this sentence used to read '`extern constexpr` is a parse error in both orders (externSpecifiers admits only the thread-storage twins after `extern`)'. That was TRUE and is now FALSE — `extern` is an ordinary `singleDeclSpecifier`, so both orders PARSE and the refusal moved from the grammar's shape to a stated constraint: the `exclusiveGroup: "storage-class"` cells make it `error[S078] S_ConflictingStorageClassSpecifiers`, still rc=1, still matching gcc + clang + MSVC (all three refuse both orders — ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02, separately). The CONCLUSION survives; only the mechanism moved, which is exactly the shelf-life class [[feedback-a-rows-premise-has-a-shelf-life]] names. RED-ON-DISABLE: drop this entry -> the mir_lowering file-scope-constexpr Local-binding pin goes red.
declarations.$threadLocalLinkageComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): both thread-storage spellings map to {threadStorage:true} — the 4th ORTHOGONAL effect axis. A file-scope `thread_local int g;` keeps EXTERNAL linkage (C11 6.2.2 is untouched by 6.7.1p3 — deliberately NO binding entry, so a co-present `static`'s {binding:local} composes without clobber in either order). Pass 1's specifier scan reads threadStorage → SymbolRecord.isThreadLocal; Pass 2 validates.
declarations.$visibilityDefaultComment: TF-C92 (D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-SPECIFIER-VOCABULARY-INCOMPLETE-VS-REAL-HEADERS): `visibility:default` is HONORED, not ignored -- the composite twin of `visibility:hidden` below, and the completion of the mechanism [[D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-VISIBILITY-SYNTAX]] shipped at FC4 c1 with only the `hidden` VALUE. It arrives from Tcl, not sqlite: tcl.h:210 `#define DLLEXPORT __attribute__((visibility("default")))` under `defined(__GNUC__) && __GNUC__ > 3`, which DSS honestly satisfies (`__GNUC__`=4 above), reaching tclsqlite-ex.c via TCL_STORAGE_CLASS/EXTERN on 13 declarations. MEASURED: 1 of the 31 arm64/macho sqlite residuals at TF-C91 HEAD 75172fe, and the SOLE error in that TU, so this row alone closes it. NO engine work was needed: `symbolVisibilityFromName` (grammar_schema_json.cpp) already accepted "default", `SymbolVisibility::Default` (symbol_attrs.hpp) already existed, and `isExternallyVisible` already threads it to all three linkers (link/format/elf.cpp, macho.cpp, pe.cpp). ** WHY THIS IS A `linkageSpecifiers` ROW AND NOT A `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` ENTRY (see [[D-TEST-IGNORE-LIST-IS-A-LICENSE-TO-DROP]]): the row THREADS THE FACT -- the decl carries SymbolVisibility::Default, the value the three linkers already consume -- where an ignored-name entry DISCARDS the token. ~~ CORRECTED 2026-07-30, SAME CYCLE, BY MEASUREMENT: an earlier draft of this comment justified the row by claiming that a `hidden` specifier followed by a `default` one must WIDEN back to Default, and called that widening this row's red-on-disable witness. **That justification was WRONG and is retracted.** MEASURED with the host /usr/bin/clang (-Wall -Wextra), BOTH orders: clang REJECTS two conflicting visibility attributes on one declaration as a HARD ERROR -- `error: visibility does not match previous declaration` -- and emits no object file. GCC is documented to warn and keep the EARLIER one. DSS's plain last-wins fold is therefore NEITHER behaviour: it is a SILENT DIVERGENCE, already tracked as [[D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-SPECIFIER-CONFLICT-SILENT-LAST-WINS]], and pinning the widening would have enshrined that divergence as this row's contract. Do NOT re-derive the widening as a witness. ~~ THIS ROW'S REAL, NON-DIVERGENT WITNESS: a legal single `default` visibility must lower with ZERO `H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier` in BOTH declaration positions and apply SymbolVisibility::Default; red-on-disable = delete the row and the diagnostic returns. On a non-conflicting decl the row is honestly VALUE-NEUTRAL, because Default is recordLinkage's unspecified state (Global+Default stores nothing) -- its job is to make legal C compile with the fact threaded, not to change bytes.
declarations.$p53ExternLinkageComment:
★★★ P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): the `extern` ENTRY, and the `exclusiveGroup` cells beside it, are what the file-scope rule merge OWES. `extern` used to be `externDecl`'s rule HEAD, so its two facts came free from the rule's identity; here it is one member of an unordered specifier set and both facts have to be STATED.
★ `{nonDefining:true}` is the 5th ORTHOGONAL axis on LinkageSpecifierEffect (beside binding / visibility / staticStorage / threadStorage) and it is NOT optional garnish: ✔MEASURED under the grammar-only mutant, WITHOUT it every `extern int e;` became a TENTATIVE DEFINITION emitting storage in every TU while `dsscp` printed `warning[H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier]: 'extern' is not a recognized linkage specifier` and EXITED 0 — a silent miscompile at rc 0, which is exactly why P53 lane `ex` built the grammar half, measured it, and REVERTED it rather than shipping it alone. Pass 1 ORs it with the row's own `nonDefiningDeclaration` (`declarationIsNonDefining`) and CST→HIR routes the declaration to `lowerExternDeclInto` on it — the import synthesis is SELECTED BY THE FOLDED SPECIFIER, never by which rule matched.
★★ `exclusiveGroup: "storage-class"` is C 6.7.1p2 AS CONFIG — 'at most one storage-class specifier may be given in the declaration specifiers in a declaration, except that _Thread_local may appear with static or extern'. The exception is stated by `_Thread_local`/`thread_local` simply NOT carrying the group, so the standard's own sentence lives in the vocabulary document rather than as an engine carve-out; the engine holds no pair list (the agnosticism rule that [[D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-SPECIFIER-CONFLICT-SILENT-LAST-WINS]] set for conflict policy). Until P53 the grammar refused `extern static` BY ACCIDENT (the keyword was a rule head); the merge deletes the accident, and without this DSS would compile `extern static int g;`, `static extern int g;`, `extern constexpr int g = 1;` and `constexpr extern int g = 1;` at rc 0 — ABOVE the reference union on four spellings. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02, three references probed SEPARATELY: gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x`, clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` and MSVC 19.51.36252 `/std:clatest` each REFUSE all four.
⚠ DISTINCT members, not repeats, and that too is MEASURED: clang ACCEPTS `static static int g;` and `extern extern int g;` where gcc and MSVC refuse, so under `DSS = (gcc ∪ clang ∪ MSVC) ∪ ISO C` a repeated specifier must keep compiling. The engine compares the two spellings and reports only a genuine pair.
★★ `compatibleWith` IS C 6.7.1's OWN 'except that …' CLAUSE, AND A FLAT GROUP CANNOT SAY IT. C23 6.7.1p3 excepts TWO pairings, not one: `thread_local` with `static`/`extern`, and `constexpr` with `auto`/`register`/`static`. So `static constexpr` is LEGAL while `extern constexpr` is a constraint violation. ✔MEASURED, and gcc 13.3.0 is the ONLY reference that can answer it — it compiles `static constexpr double PI2 = 3.5 * 2;` at rc 0 and refuses `extern constexpr int K = 4;` with "'constexpr' used with 'extern'"; clang 18.1.3 and MSVC 19.51.36252 do not implement C23 `constexpr` in C at all ("unknown type name 'constexpr'" / C2054), so they ABSTAIN on this pair rather than voting against it. ⚠ THE FIRST CUT OF THIS TABLE OMITTED THE FIELD AND REFUSED A SHIPPED EXAMPLE — `examples/c/constexpr_array_dim` writes exactly that `static constexpr` line, and it went red. A group alone is the right shape for 'at most one' and the WRONG shape for 'except with'. The list is read SYMMETRICALLY (either entry naming the other suffices); both directions are declared here because a half-declared pair reads as an accident. ⓘ The thread-local half of the exception needs no entry: those spellings carry no group at all, and their own complement (`_Thread_local register`) is already owned by `semantics.threadLocal.incompatibleSpecifierTokens`.
⚠ `weak` / `visibility:*` carry NO group: they are ATTRIBUTE names, not storage classes, and their own conflict policy is the already-closed binding/visibility guard one tier over.
declarations.$p53FlexibleArrayComment: ★★ P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): `allowFlexibleArray` is DELIBERATELY **NOT** SET ON THIS ROW, and that decision is a MEASUREMENT, not a preference. This row now owns `extern char v[];` at file scope (D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-INCOMPLETE-ARRAY, witness `examples/c/extern_incomplete_array_crosscu`), which `externDecl` used to admit via that flag — so the obvious move was to copy it here. ✔MEASURED: it reds **20 tests**. The flag is read TWICE, and its second reading is the gate on the init-inference completion (`if (!decl.allowFlexibleArray) declTy = completeIncompleteArrayFromInit(...)` in semantic_analyzer.cpp), so setting it stops every file-scope `char msg[] = "hello";` in the corpus from being sized by its initializer (S_IncompleteTypeObject) and silently turns `int v[0];` from S_ArrayLengthOutOfRange into an incomplete array. A ROW-WIDE flag cannot express `incomplete is fine on the declarations that do not define`. ⇒ the admission is a PER-DECLARATION fact instead, read from the `{nonDefining:true}` specifier (`declarationIsNonDefining` feeds the resolver's `allowIncomplete`) — the second conditional facet the merge inherits, for the same reason as the first. C 6.9.2 is the warrant: a NON-DEFINING declaration may name an incomplete array because the defining declaration elsewhere completes it. ⓘ `externDecl` KEEPS its own `allowFlexibleArray` (it is still the BLOCK-scope rule, and it takes no initializer there). ⓘ A BARE `int v[];` at file scope stays refused, unchanged from before the merge — ✔MEASURED 2026-09-02 that gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and MSVC 19.51.36252 all ACCEPT it as a C 6.9.2 tentative definition of an incomplete array, so that IS a divergence; it is PRE-EXISTING, untouched by this row, and deliberately not widened here (see the row's cross-refs).
declarations.$stringEndIgnoreComment: D-TOK-CLOSING-DELIMITER-HAS-NO-TOKEN: THE row the closer matters most for — this is where `__attribute__((visibility("hidden")))` resolves its COMPOSITE `visibility:hidden` key. cst_to_hir's scan skips the string OPENER + BODY structurally (cfg.stringStartToken / cfg.stringBodyToken) and the composite pairing consumes them, but the newly-tokenized closing `"` (`StringEnd`) is neither — untouched it falls through to the strict lookup with the key `"` and fires H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on legal C. It also has to be ignorable so the post-pair skip-ahead does not read the closer as a second adjacent-concat opener. `CharEnd`/`HeaderEnd` are deliberately absent: attrArgItem admits no character constant and HeaderEnd only exists inside a `#include` line, so neither can reach a declaration-specifier prefix.
declarations.$commaIgnoreComment: TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-ARG-SOUP): a comma SEPARATING attribute clauses (`__attribute__((__nothrow__, __leaf__))`) is a DIRECT child of `attrSpec`, so the `attributeArgRule` token flag — which only covers what is INSIDE `attrArgs` — does not reach it; untouched it falls through to the strict lookup with the key `,` and fires H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on legal C. ★ WHY THIS IS SAFE, and it is NOT the tempting 'nothing else in declSpecifiers has a comma' (that claim is FALSE — `stdAttr` at :635 is literally `stdAttrItem (Comma stdAttrItem)*`; it is saved only by being in this row's linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules, which is a DIFFERENT mechanism and could be changed independently). The REAL reason is exhaustive over `declSpecifiers`' alternatives: StaticKeyword / ConstexprKeyword / ThreadLocalKeyword / ThreadLocalC23Keyword / NoreturnKeyword are single tokens; `alignasSpec` is `[ kw, '(', alignasArg, ')' ]` with ONE comma-free argument; which leaves `attrSpec` and `stdAttr` as the ONLY comma sources. In BOTH, every comma is an attribute clause- or argument-SEPARATOR. So a comma reaching this scan can never be a linkage specifier, whatever the ignoredRules list happens to contain.
declarations.$inlineIgnoreComment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): the `inline` FUNCTION specifier confers NO binding and NO visibility, so it is ignored BY KIND — one entry covering all three spellings (`inline`/`__inline`/`__inline__` share the kind). ★ A `linkageSpecifiers` ENTRY WAS REJECTED, and not on style grounds: that map is keyed by token TEXT and is context-FREE, while `inline`'s effect depends entirely on what it is written BESIDE — `static inline` emits a Local body, `extern inline` emits a Global body, and a BARE `inline` whose every co-declaration is also inline emits NOTHING (C99 6.7.4p7). A flat `{binding: …}` entry could only pick one of those three and would last-wins-clobber a co-present `static`, which is the order-dependent silent linkage miscompile `$noreturnIgnoreNamesComment` records. The emission decision instead rides `SymbolRecord.isInline` (semantics.inline) and is made where the co-present specifiers are already folded. MEASURED: WITHOUT this entry all four baseline spellings fail loud H000C ('inline' is not a recognized linkage specifier) — the grammar can never land silently.
declarations.$alignasIgnoreComment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): an `alignasSpec` in a file-scope declaration's specifier prefix (`alignas(32) int g;`) carries NO linkage — skipped wholesale by the linkage scan (like `stdAttr`); the alignment is read by the semantic alignas scan. `attrSpec` is deliberately NOT ignored here (its `__attribute__((weak/visibility))` tokens ARE meaningful linkage). FC16 (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN): the bare `_Noreturn` keyword carries NO linkage → ignored by kind (NoreturnKeyword).
declarations.$noreturnIgnoreNamesComment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN): the GNU `__attribute__((noreturn))` form shares the `attrSpec` rule with the HONORED linkage attributes (`weak`, `visibility`), so attrSpec CANNOT be ignored wholesale here — the `noreturn` IDENTIFIER is skipped by NAME instead (dunder-normalized, so it also covers `__noreturn__`). A no-op `{binding:...}` linkageSpecifiers entry was REJECTED: it would clobber a co-present `static`/`weak` last-wins (an order-dependent silent linkage miscompile). Any OTHER unknown attribute identifier still fails loud H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier. `[[noreturn]]` rides stdAttr (already wholesale-ignored).
declarations.$attrIgnoreNamesComment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-SEMANTICS): the GNU spellings of the SEMANTIC standard attributes — `__attribute__((deprecated[("m")]))` / `((unused))` / `((warn_unused_result))` and the `[[...]]`-vocabulary names when spelled GNU — carry NO linkage; each joins the by-NAME skip (dunder-normalized; a parenthesized string argument is independently skipped by the string-token guard, so `deprecated("msg")` passes whole). WITHOUT these the file-scope GNU spellings hard-fail H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier (probe-confirmed at HEAD). The SEMANTIC meaning is read by the semantic tier's attribute scan (semantics.attributeSemantics), not here. No collision with the honored keys (static/constexpr/weak/visibility:hidden).
declarations.$hintIgnoreNamesComment:
TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-ARG-SOUP): the ABI-NEUTRAL glibc/tcl/SDK hint attributes.
