declarations.$multiDeclaratorComment: c23 D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-MULTI-DECLARATOR (2026-07-18): externDecl is now a DECLARATOR-MODE row (the extern twin of topLevelDecl) — head:0 (`typeRefAllowingStruct`, the star-free base type) + declaratorList:1 (`initDeclaratorList`), POST-STRIP indices (the `externSpecifiers` specifierPrefix at child 0 is stripped, so head/list stay 0/1 whether or not `extern thread_local` is spelled). SUPERSEDES the legacy `name:1/type:0/kindByChild[externFuncTail]` single-declarator row. Pass-1's declarator-mode minting (semantic_analyzer.cpp) mints ONE `nonDefiningDeclaration` symbol PER named declarator — `extern int a, b;` mints a AND b, each with its OWN per-declarator pointer/array/fn suffix folded onto the shared head base type (`extern int *a, b[10];` → a:int*, b:int[10]). `requireNamedDeclarators` fails loud (S_DeclarationDeclaresNothing) on an abstract declarator (`extern int *;`) — an extern must name a symbol. A FUNCTION declarator (`extern int f(int);` — its name carries an fnSuffix) is detected as a prototype (hasFnSuffixOnName → isProtoDeclaration) and lowered to ExternFunction; an OBJECT declarator to ExternGlobal — no bespoke func/object tail. Function-ness NO LONGER upgrades the kind to Function (it stays Variable+isProto, the same model topLevelDecl uses for a bare prototype `int f(int);`); the observable HIR (ExternFunction import) is unchanged. constMarker/volatileMarker mirror topLevelDecl so `extern const int x;` marks x const via the per-declarator declaratorObjectIsConst path. allowFlexibleArray preserves the extern INCOMPLETE-array object (D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-INCOMPLETE-ARRAY, `extern char v[];`) through the declarator's absent-length `[]`. TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the `externSpecifiers` specifierPrefix carries `extern thread_local` — the declarator-mode storage scan reads {threadStorage:true} and marks every declarator's symbol isThreadLocal; ExternKeyword is ignored by kind (extern-ness IS the rule's identity — nonDefiningDeclaration mints the record). RE-HOME: a block-scope extern (object OR function) binds in the CURRENT block scope, NOT re-homed to file scope — the Pass-1 isProto file-scope re-home is SUPPRESSED for a non-defining extern (D-CSUBSET-BLOCK-SCOPE-EXTERN shadow correctness; see semantic_analyzer.cpp).
declarations.$kindByChildComment: D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-FN-DEFINITION (§B 2026-07-21): the extern twin of topLevelDecl's function-definition discriminator. Post-strip role children are [typeRefAllowingStruct(0), initDeclaratorList(1), {stringLiteralExpr?}, externDeclTail]. childPath [2,0] = the externDeclTail's first child (with NO library override present — the definition case never carries one): a `block` node ⇒ a function DEFINITION (whenKind function), else the EndStatement token (a declaration; whenRule never matches a token). When a library override IS present the tail shifts to role index 3 so childPath[2] lands on the stringLiteralExpr (not a block) ⇒ stays a declaration — and the pathological override+body `extern f() "lib" {…}` is caught fail-loud at HIR, never mis-lowered. On a Function match the SHARED declarator-mode minting (semantic_analyzer.cpp) suppresses isExtern (a definition is DEFINING, not non-defining, despite nonDefiningDeclaration on this row) and binds the params/body via the externDecl scope (added to `scopes`); CST→HIR's lowerExternDeclInto delegates to the topLevelDecl function-definition lowering (a real Function with an emitted body), NOT ExternFunction. paramsPath/bodyPath ABSENT: declarator-mode params live in the declarator's fnSuffix and the matched block IS the body.
declarations.$afterDeclaratorVocabularyComment: ★★ TF-C73 REGRESSION FIX — WHY THIS ROW GREW A VOCABULARY AT ALL. TF-C73 made the AFTER-DECLARATOR attribute run (`initDeclarator`'s trailing `{repeat: attrSpec|stdAttr}`) a linkage SCAN ROOT for every declarator-mode row. `externDecl` is such a row, and it carried only `{_Thread_local, thread_local}` + an `ExternKeyword` ignore — so every raw token of a trailing run hit the strict lookup and the LITERAL glibc idiom `extern int gg(void) __attribute__((__nothrow__, __leaf__));` (which real clang accepts with 0 errors and 0 warnings under -Wall -Wextra, and which this compiler accepted before TF-C73) failed with EIGHT H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier errors — one per token, including `'('` and `','`. The keys below are what an `extern` declaration can actually SPELL, derived from the grammar reachable from this row (`externSpecifiers` = ExternKeyword + thread-local keywords; the trailing run = attrSpec | stdAttr) and clang-verified case by case — NOT copied wholesale from topLevelDecl.
declarations.$linkageSpecifiersComment: MEASURED against real clang on macOS, one shape each: `extern int ea __attribute__((weak));` and `extern int ev __attribute__((visibility("hidden")));` BOTH compile clean (0 errors, 0 warnings, -Wall -Wextra) and both name a real ABI fact, so both are HONORED here — dropping them would be a silent wrong-linkage, the exact bug class this cycle exists to close. topLevelDecl's other two bindings are deliberately ABSENT: `extern static int x;` is `error: cannot combine with previous 'extern' declaration specifier` and `extern constexpr int x;` is `error: unknown type name 'constexpr'` — neither is legal C on an extern declaration, and `externSpecifiers` cannot even parse them, so declaring them would be dead vocabulary that only weakens the strict lookup. An `__attribute__((static))` spelling is not a real attribute in any dialect, so leaving `static` out keeps it LOUD rather than silently binding it to internal linkage.
declarations.$visibilityDefaultComment: TF-C92 (D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-SPECIFIER-VOCABULARY-INCOMPLETE-VS-REAL-HEADERS): the `externDecl` twin of the `topLevelDecl` row -- and THE one sqlite/Tcl actually reaches, because tcl.h:306 spells `#define EXTERN extern TCL_STORAGE_CLASS`, putting the attribute AFTER `extern` and so into externSpecifiers' TF-C77 repeat rather than declSpecifiers. Both rows are added together on the house rule that one attribute must not mean two different things depending on where it is written. Full provenance, the measurement, and the ignored-names discriminator are on the topLevelDecl sibling; see also [[D-CSUBSET-LINKAGE-VISIBILITY-SYNTAX]] (mechanism, closed) and [[D-TEST-IGNORE-LIST-IS-A-LICENSE-TO-DROP]] (why not an ignore-list entry).
declarations.$ignoredKindsComment: The STRUCTURAL syntax of the trailing run, kind by kind, each one reachable from THIS row's grammar: `AttributeKeyword` + the two `ParenOpen`/`ParenClose` pairs are `attrSpec`'s own frame, and `Comma` separates CLAUSES (`attrSpec`'s `{repeat: Comma attrClauseTail}`) — a clause comma is a DIRECT child of attrSpec, so the engine's attribute-ARGUMENT token flag (which only marks what is inside `attrArgs`) never reaches it and it would otherwise hit the strict lookup with the key `,`. topLevelDecl's `NoreturnKeyword` and `StringEnd` are deliberately ABSENT: `_Noreturn` is a declaration-specifier and `externSpecifiers` admits only `extern` + the thread-local keywords, so no NoreturnKeyword token can appear under this row; and a string literal's CLOSING delimiter is skipped by `linkageFrom`'s own `closeTokenForCoalescedBody` arm for EVERY row, unconditionally, so listing it here would be inert config (MEASURED: `extern int ev __attribute__((visibility("hidden")));` resolves its composite `visibility:hidden` key with this list exactly as written).
declarations.$inlineIgnoreComment: TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): `externSpecifiers` now admits `InlineKeyword` (`extern inline int f(int);` / `extern inline int f(int){…}`), so the keyword reaches this row's strict scan and must be ignored by kind here too — the same no-binding argument as topLevelDecl. Unlike topLevelDecl this row needs NO emission override: an `extern`-spelled inline definition provides an external definition under C99 6.7.4p7, which is exactly what this row's `block`-tail path already emits (MEASURED with clang: `extern inline int p(int){…}` → `T _p`).
declarations.$p53NoreturnIgnoredComment: P53 (D-C-EXTERN-MUST-LEAD-THE-DECLARATION-SPECIFIERS): `NoreturnKeyword` joins the IGNORED kinds because `externSpecifiers` now admits `_Noreturn` on both sides of the keyword, and `linkageFrom` walks EVERY token of the specifier prefix — an unlisted one is a LOUD H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier, so admitting the token to the grammar without this entry would trade a parse error for a linkage error. It is exactly the topLevelDecl row's own entry, for the same reason: `_Noreturn` is a FUNCTION specifier, not a linkage one. ⚠ IGNORED BY THE LINKAGE SCAN IS NOT DROPPED — `specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn` reads this same prefix subtree (`externSpecifiers` IS the row's specifierPrefix and is always kids.front()), so `extern _Noreturn void die(int);` and `_Noreturn extern void die(int);` both MEAN noreturn rather than merely parse.
declarations.$ignoredRulesComment: `stdAttr` — the C23 `[[…]]` spelling, admitted by `initDeclarator`'s trailing run, so `extern int ec [[deprecated]];` (clang-clean) must not fail loud on `[`/`deprecated`/`]`. topLevelDecl's `alignasSpec` is deliberately ABSENT: `alignas` is a declaration-specifier and neither `externSpecifiers` nor the trailing attribute run can produce an `alignasSpec` node under this row, so it would be unreachable config.
declarations.$ignoredNamesComment: The ABI-NEUTRAL hint vocabulary — IDENTICAL to topLevelDecl's list, and that identity is the point rather than laziness: an `extern` declaration is precisely WHERE the C library puts these. `__nothrow__`/`__leaf__` are glibc's `__THROW`; `nonnull`/`malloc`/`alloc_size`/`warn_unused_result` are its `__attribute_malloc__`/`__wur` family; `availability` is the macOS SDK's `__swift_unavailable`/deprecation machinery; `format` decorates every printf-family extern. Each is ignored on the SAME ground the topLevelDecl row states — DSS models none of them, so there is no sink a value could be lost from, which makes the skip strictly conservative rather than a silent drop. `aligned` rides the same list here (its layout effect is read by the attribute-SEMANTICS scan, not by the linkage fold) and any name NOT listed still falls through to the strict lookup and fails loud.
declarations.$noinlineIgnoreNamesComment:
TF-C78 (D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE) + TF-C81 (D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE): ★ `noinline` AND `always_inline` APPEAR IN THIS LIST BUT ARE **HONORED**, NOT IGNORED — and the distinction matters, because every other name here really is inert. The list answers ONE narrow question: may the LINKAGE scan skip this identifier without failing H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier? For both names the answer is yes (neither confers binding or visibility), so they belong here; but a SECOND, disjoint consumer — the `attributeSemantics.effects` `noInline` / `alwaysInline` verbs — folds them onto SymbolRecord.isNoInline / isAlwaysInline, through HirNoInlineMap / HirAlwaysInlineMap, onto MirFunc.noInline / MirFunc.alwaysInline, where the optimizer's inlining pass REFUSES to splice the callee (noinline) or WAIVES its size threshold for it (always_inline). Membership here says 'not linkage', never 'not honored'. The loader ENFORCES exactly that reading: its attribute-vocabulary drift cross-check REQUIRES every declaration-attached effect name (any verb but `none`) to appear in this list for a row that runs the strict linkage scan, so removing any of these names from here fails the LOAD rather than silently disarming the effect — the edits are mechanically coupled and cannot drift apart.
★★ TF-C92 ADDS `no_sanitize_thread` AS THE **THIRD** HONORED-BUT-LISTED NAME, AND ITS SINK IS A DIFFERENT KIND FROM THE FIRST TWO — read this before assuming the pattern. `noinline` and `always_inline` are honored by an optimizer PASS that changes its decision. `no_sanitize_thread` is honored by being STORED: the `noSanitizeThread` verb folds it onto SymbolRecord.isNoSanitizeThread, through HirNoSanitizeThreadMap, onto MirFunc.noSanitizeThread, where `mir_text`'s `appendFuncAttrs` prints it as `nosanitizethread` and the parser reads it back. MEASURED: `grep -rni sanitiz src/` returns ZERO hits — DSS ships no sanitizer, so there is no pass for it to switch off and the serializer is its only consumer. It still belongs in the list on the list's own narrow question (it confers no binding and no visibility), and it still belongs in `effects` on the standing rule that a new attribute gets a REAL sink rather than an ignore-list entry ([[D-TEST-IGNORE-LIST-IS-A-LICENSE-TO-DROP]]) — an ignore-list-only entry would have discarded the fact three tiers before MIR, leaving a future instrumentation pass to re-derive from source what the front end had already parsed. So the count of names here that are HONORED rather than inert is now THREE, and the discriminator for the next one is unchanged: does DSS have a sink for it, wired in the same commit.
declarations.$p42oIgnoredNameDriftComment: P42 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-UNKNOWN-NAME-GATE-ASYMMETRY): the five C23 statement/label hint names join this list, and they are a DRIFT REPAIR rather than a vocabulary addition. The loader's Clause-B cross-check requires every effects row with a NON-`none` verb to appear here, and DELIBERATELY EXEMPTS the `none` row — so the `none` names were added by hand, one cycle at a time, and eight of them were never added at all. ✔MEASURED with the shipped CLI at the P42 tree, all rc=1: `__attribute__((fallthrough)) int gv = 7;` → `error[H000C] 'fallthrough' is not a recognized linkage specifier`, likewise `likely`, `unlikely`, `reproducible`, `unsequenced`, `packed`, `may_alias`, `transparent_union` — every one of them a name THIS FILE declares KNOWN in the effects table three hundred lines below. ✔MEASURED against the references, each probed separately (gcc 13.3 `-std=c2x`, clang 18 `-std=c23`, `-Wall -Wextra`): all five of the names added here compile with a warning and exit 0 on BOTH. DSS was REFUSING them. ⚠ THE THREE THAT ARE DELIBERATELY **NOT** ADDED, and the reason is the opposite of an oversight: `packed`, `may_alias` and `transparent_union` carry real LAYOUT / ALIASING / ABI weight that DSS does not implement, and the file-scope refusal is the only tier still saying so — silencing it here would trade a loud refusal for a SILENT DROP with observable consequences (a leading `__attribute__((packed)) struct S {…} s;` is not reached by the composite scan, so it would go from `error[H000C]` to a wrong `sizeof`). The five names added here have NO sink anywhere in DSS by construction (design note F7: the C23 hints are semantics-neutral), so their inertness costs nothing.
declarations.$p44DerivedIgnoredNamesComment: P44 D-CSUBSET-GNU-UNKNOWN-NAME-GATE-ASYMMETRY: the 28-name roster that stood here is DERIVED now — see the full note on the `topLevelDecl` row. This row declares `weak` and `visibility:*` as its own linkage specifiers, so the derivation excludes them and the extern binding is unaffected.

references.$c25Comment: c25 D-CSUBSET-UNIFIED-COMPOSITE-SPECIFIER: the REFERENCE arm of the unified specifiers. A body-ABSENT `structSpec`/`unionSpec`/`enumSpec` (`struct S v;` / `struct S;`) is a TAG reference — these rows resolve its tag in the Tag namespace, exactly as the former `structTypeRef`/etc. did, via the SAME isTagReference path. The DEFINITION arm (body present) is the paired declarations-row above; the engine routes per-node on the body child's presence (`definesWhenChild`), so a definition is never double-processed as a reference. `nameMatch: lastIdentifier` extracts the tag from [Kw, Identifier]. c35 (D-CSUBSET-FORWARD-STRUCT-DECLARATION): `compositeKind` drives the forward-mint of an INCOMPLETE composite on a tag MISS (an opaque `struct S *` / `typedef struct S S;` whose S is never defined — sqlite3_stmt), so the reference resolves to a sizeable Ptr<incomplete> instead of S_UnknownType; a VALUE/by-value-member/sizeof of it still fails loud (computeLayout incomplete guard). `enum` keeps the fail-loud miss (value-typed).

semantics.$scopesComment: FC4 c1: topLevelDecl replaced funcDefTail — a function's params now live INSIDE its declarator's fnSuffix, so the scope that holds them must dominate BOTH the declarator and the block; the topLevelDecl node is that dominator (harmless for variable-kind topLevelDecls — nothing binds into the scope). D-CSUBSET-EXTERN-FN-DEFINITION (§B 2026-07-21): externDecl joins the list for the SAME reason — an `extern int f(void){…}` DEFINITION's params/body need a dominating scope; the empty scope opened for a plain `extern int a,b;` / block-scope extern is harmless (same as a variable-kind topLevelDecl, and isDefinitionAtNode defaults true here so the scope opens uniformly, while a definition's params bind into it via the generic declNodeIsFunctionDefinition gate and a bare-proto's params still isolate via isPrototypeParamScopeNode). c25: the unified `structSpec`/`unionSpec`/`enumSpec` rules are the fieldChildren composites (they REPLACE the retired *SpecifierBody rules). Each opens a scope ONLY in DEFINITION mode (body present) — Pass 1 gates the pushScope on the `definesWhenChild` body-child presence, so a body-absent tag reference (`struct S v;`) opens no scope. The member-body wrapper rules (structBody/unionBody/enumBody) are deliberately NOT scope rules — their fields bind into the enclosing XxxSpec scope.
semantics.$p31StmtExprScopeComment: P31 (D-C-GNU-STATEMENT-EXPRESSION): `stmtExpr` joins the scope rules for the SAME reason `block` is here — a GNU statement expression IS a compound statement, and its declarations are block-scoped (C's block-scope rule, applied to the construct's own braces). The whole `({ __typeof__(x) __x = (x); … })` idiom depends on it: without a scope of its own, two uses of the same macro in one function would redeclare `__x`, and the temporary would leak into the enclosing block. It is listed alongside `block` rather than nested inside one because `stmtExpr` inlines its own brace body (see that rule's comment for why the `commitAfterPrefix` cut requires the inlining).
semantics.$castsComment: FC2: explicit C cast `(T)expr`. typeChild/operandChild are visible-child indices into castExpr = [ '(' , castTypeRef , ')' , castOperand ]. Pass 2 resolves+stamps the type child (typedefs incl. cross-tree-injected ones resolve through the standard type-position resolver), stamps the cast node's RESULT type, and validates the pair against the explicit-cast matrix (scalar<->scalar incl. float<->int, ptr<->ptr, ptr<->int; struct values / void / arrays -> S_InvalidCast).
semantics.$sizeofComment: FC6: sizeof typing. sizeofType = [ SizeofKeyword, '(', castTypeRef, ')' ] → typeChild 2 is the castTypeRef (resolved + stamped through the SAME type resolver casts use). sizeofValue = [ SizeofKeyword, castOperand ] (the operand is typed normally). Both forms are stamped size_t (U64).
semantics.$alignofComment:
C11/C23 6.5.3.4: alignof typing. alignofType = [ { alt: AlignofKeyword | AlignofLegacyKeyword }, '(', castTypeRef, ')' ] → typeChild 2 is the castTypeRef (the inline keyword-alt matches ONE token at visible-child 0, '(' is child 1 — SAME layout as sizeofType, so the same index 2). Pass 2 resolves + stamps the type child through the SAME type resolver sizeof/casts use, and stamps the node size_t (U64).
★ [[D-CSUBSET-ALIGNOF-VALUE-OPERAND]] (closed 2026-08-24): `valueRule` = `alignofValue`, the EXACT counterpart of the one sizeof declares on the line above. Pass 2 stamps the value arm operand with its full EXPRESSION type (`subtreeType`) and the node size_t; CST→HIR then reads that DIRECT stamp and NEVER descends past it, which INHERITS the [[D-CSUBSET-SIZEOF-DEREF-ARRAY-SILENT-FALLBACK]] discipline rather than re-deriving it — a descent would make `__alignof__(*p)` report the alignment of the POINTER, silently, exactly as it once mis-sized `sizeof(*p)`. Absent `valueRule` ⇒ the language has only the type-name form (the pre-2026-08-24 state) and the value form fails loud at parse.
semantics.$synthesizedTypesComment: D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY: the standard types the ENGINE synthesizes rather than the source spelling them. C says `sizeof`/`_Alignof` yield `size_t` and a same-pointee `p - q` yields `ptrdiff_t`, and BOTH are ALIASES of a standard NAMED type whose spelling is DATA-MODEL-dependent: `size_t` IS `unsigned long` on LP64 and `unsigned long long` on LLP64; `ptrdiff_t` IS `long` / `long long`. Minting a bare anonymous U64/I64 (what the engine did before type identity was split off representation) produces a THIRD type matching NEITHER named entry — so `_Generic(sizeof(int), unsigned long: 1, unsigned long long: 2, default: 0)` silently selects `default` instead of the arm C requires. Each role maps a data model to a `typeSpecifiers` VOCABULARY NAME; the loader resolves it once (identical machinery to `integerLiteralTyping`), so the engine carries only a resolved (core, tag) pair and never compares a spelling. The REPRESENTATION still comes from the target — `unsigned long` is U64 on LP64 and U32 on LLP64, and the per-model choice of NAME is what keeps size_t 64-bit on both. ILP32 rows are declared for completeness (a declared role must cover every data model, else it would silently fall back to an anonymous core on the uncovered one); an ILP32 format still fails loud at S_UnsupportedDataModel long before these are consulted. Omit the whole block and every consumer keeps its historic anonymous core — a language with no C `size_t` notion (toy / tsql) is unaffected.

synthesizedTypes.$offsetofComment: C 7.19: `offsetof` yields size_t — the SAME named alias `sizeof` yields, given its own role rather than sharing sizeof's slot so that reading this block answers `what type does offsetof have` without a cross-reference, and so a language could differ without editing the engine.
synthesizedTypes.$typesCompatibleComment: gcc: `__builtin_types_compatible_p` yields `int`. Declared per data model like every other role even though the answer does not vary, because a role covering only SOME models silently falls back to an ANONYMOUS core on the rest — the exact third-type bug this whole block exists to prevent.

semantics.$typeofComment: C23 6.7.2.5 (D-CSUBSET-TYPEOF): typeof typing. `typeRule` = `typeofType` = [ { alt: TypeofKeyword | TypeofUnqualKeyword }, '(', castTypeRef, ')' ] and `valueRule` = `typeofValue` = [ { alt: ... }, '(', expression, ')' ] — `operandChild` 2 is the castTypeRef / expression in BOTH (the inline keyword-alt matches ONE token at visible-child 0, same layout as alignofType/sizeofType). The semantic tier's resolveTypeNodeImpl arm resolves the operand (the type form recurses the SAME type resolver casts/sizeof use; the value form reads the operand's type via subtreeType — UNEVALUATED per 6.7.2.5p2) and, when the leading keyword is `stripQualifiersToken` (`typeof_unqual`), strips top-level qualifiers (only VolatileQual is interned, so strip == stripVolatile; const/restrict are not interned). The result is stamped on the typeof node so HIR's resolveStampedTypeBelow recovers it. CRITICALLY, the typeof operand subtree is made OPAQUE to the coarse volatile/const qualifier scans (subtreeContainsToken / declaratorObjectIsConst) so `typeof_unqual`'s stripped qualifier is never silently re-applied. A bit-field value operand → S_TypeofBitfieldOperand (6.7.2.5 constraint). `stripQualifiersToken` is OPTIONAL — absent ⇒ typeof never strips (a language with only the qualifier-preserving spelling). Absent block ⇒ the language has no typeof surface.
semantics.$bitIntComment: C23 6.2.5/6.7.2 (D-CSUBSET-BITINT): the `_BitInt(N)` bit-precise integer type-specifier. `specRule` = the `bitIntSpecifier` shape = [ BitIntKeyword, '(', assignmentExpr, ')' ] → `widthChild` 2 is the constant-expression whose value is N (const-folded via the SAME constIntExpr sizeof/alignas/static_assert/array-dims use). `unsignedToken`/`signedToken` name the C 6.7.2 signedness keywords the semantic tier scans for among the specifier run's sibling tokens (DEFAULT signed when neither is present). The resolveTypeNodeImpl bitInt arm validates N (non-constant → S_BitIntWidthNotConstant; N≤0 → S_BitIntWidthNotPositive; signed N<2 → S_BitIntSignedWidthTooSmall; N>__BITINT_MAXWIDTH__ → S_BitIntWidthExceedsMax) and interns `bitInt(N, signed)` for ANY valid width — N>64 is a runnable multi-limb type (the C1 N>64 gate S_BitIntWidthAboveC1Limit is RETIRED in C2). Absent block ⇒ the language has no _BitInt surface. Source-agnostic: nothing hardcodes `_BitInt`.
semantics.$alignasComment: C11/C23 6.7.5 (D-CSUBSET-ALIGNAS): the `_Alignas`/`alignas` alignment specifier. `specRule` = the `alignasSpec` shape = [ { alt: AlignasKeyword | AlignasLegacyKeyword }, '(', alignasArg, ')' ] → `argChild` 2 is the `alignasArg` (the inline keyword-alt matches ONE token at visible-child 0, '(' is child 1 — SAME layout as alignofType). `typeFormRule` = `alignasTypeName` (the guarded TYPE-form wrapper branch): the semantic tier reads alignasArg's committed reading and discriminates the TYPE form (the committed child's rule == alignasTypeName → alignment = _Alignof(T) via computeLayout(...)->align of the castTypeRef INSIDE the wrapper) from the VALUE form (else → const-evaluate the constant-expression via the SAME constIntExpr sizeof/static_assert/array-dims use). The computed alignment is validated (power-of-two → S_AlignasNotPowerOfTwo; ≤256 → S_AlignasExceedsMax; ≥ the declared type's natural align → S_AlignasWeakerThanNatural; non-constant value → S_AlignasNonConstant; on a typedef/function/parameter/bit-field → S_AlignasInvalidContext) and STORED (SymbolRecord.explicitAlignment for a variable; fed into the composite's fieldAligns for a member). `alignas(0)` is an explicit NO-OP (6.7.5p3) — treated as no override, no error. Absent block ⇒ the language has no alignas surface.
semantics.$packedComment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-PACKED): C/C23 `__attribute__((packed))` / `[[gnu::packed]]` on a struct/union. `listRule` = the `compositeAttrList` shape (the trailing attribute list after a struct/union body). `attributeNames` = the identifiers that mean `packed` (matched dunder-normalized via the shared stripDunder, so `__packed__` ≡ `packed`; `gnu::packed` matches by its final segment `packed`). The semantic tier scans a structSpec/unionSpec node for a `compositeAttrList` child, extracts each `attrSpec`/`stdAttr` identifier, and marks the composite `packed` (→ the interner's completeComposite → computeLayout removes all inter-field padding + sets natural alignment 1). An unrecognized `__attribute__((X))` identifier fails loud S_UnknownTypeAttribute (typo protection like H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier); an unrecognized `[[…]]` is standard-ignorable (the [[deprecated]] precedent). packed + a bit-field member is SUPPORTED (D-CSUBSET-PACKED-BITFIELD-INTERACTION): it takes the same two per-ABI bit-field packers `#pragma pack(N)` takes, with the member baseline dropped to 1 and the GNU straddle bump suppressed — MEASURED byte-identical to `#pragma pack(1)` under gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3, which is the equivalence that made this a deletion rather than a new algorithm. It used to fail loud S_PackedBitfieldUnsupported, a refusal all three references contradicted. Absent block ⇒ the language has no composite-attribute surface. Source-agnostic: nothing hardcodes the spelling `packed`.
semantics.$noreturnComment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-NORETURN): the C11/C23 `noreturn` FUNCTION attribute. `keywordToken` = the `_Noreturn` keyword (C11 6.7.4); `attributeNames` = the recognized attribute identifiers (`[[noreturn]]`/`__attribute__((noreturn))`/`[[gnu::noreturn]]`, dunder-normalized at the scan so `__noreturn__` matches). The semantic tier scans a declaration's specifier prefix (specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn) for EITHER form and marks the symbol isNoreturn; a DIRECT call to such a function is wrapped `Block{ ExprStmt(call), Unreachable }` at HIR lowering (the wrapIfProvablyInfinite precedent). Source-agnostic: nothing hardcodes the spelling. TF-C94: the apply gate is `isFnSig || isFnPointerType`, so a POINTER-to-function declarator carries the flag too — GNU binds the attribute to the pointee's function TYPE (host clang honors it there), and a struct/union MEMBER can never be a FnSig, so without the pointer arm the leading member position this cycle opened (`structMemberDeclSpecifier`) would have parsed the attribute and dropped it in silence.
semantics.$constexprComment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR): the C23 6.7.1 `constexpr` OBJECT storage-class specifier. `keywordToken` = the `constexpr` keyword. Pass 1 scans a declaration's specifier prefix (specifierPrefixHasConstexpr, the specifierPrefixNamesNoreturn mirror) and marks each declared symbol isConstexpr (implies isConst); Pass 2's validateConstexprDeclarator then enforces the 6.7.1 constraints AT THE DECLARATION: the initializer must be a compile-time constant (arithmetic scalars fold via the shared CST const-eval engine with floats admitted; a pointer initializer must be a null pointer constant), a missing initializer / a function declarator / a volatile-qualified object type fail loud, and array/struct/union constexpr is a NAMED loud deferral (D-CSUBSET-CONSTEXPR-AGGREGATE-TYPE). ZERO codegen: a validated constexpr object lowers byte-identically to a const object with a foldable initializer. Source-agnostic: WHICH token is per-language config; the engine never hardcodes the spelling.
semantics.$inlineComment:
TF-C79 (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-FUNCTION-SPECIFIER): the C99 6.7.4 `inline` FUNCTION specifier. `keywordToken` = the single kind all three spellings share (`inline`/`__inline`/`__inline__`). Pass 1.5 scans a function declaration's specifier prefix (specifierPrefixHasInline, the specifierPrefixHasConstexpr mirror) and marks the symbol isInline — FnSig-GATED, the isNoInline discipline, so `inline` on a non-function is not recorded on a symbol no emission decision will consult; it is instead a LOUD S_InlineNonFunction (C99 6.7.4p1: the specifier shall be used only in the declaration of a function).
★ WHAT isInline MEANS, PRECISELY: 'this declaration spells `inline` WITHOUT `extern`' — 6.7.4p7's exact clause, which is why `externSpecifierTokens` exists. It is then **AND**-merged across the proto/definition pair by the post-1.5 mergedFnDecls sweep, NOT OR-merged. AND is the whole point: 6.7.4p7 makes a definition an INLINE definition (providing NO external definition) only if **ALL** file-scope declarations spell inline-without-extern, so ONE plain declaration anywhere in the TU restores the external definition. An OR-merge would inspect the same two records and reach the OPPOSITE conclusion on the two commonest shapes.
★ MEASURED with `/usr/bin/clang -std=c99 -O0 -c` + `nm`, ten forms, and the AND-merge reproduces all ten: `inline int p(int){…}` alone → `U _p` (NOT emitted); `inline int p(int); inline int p(int){…}` → `U _p`; `__inline int p(int){…}` → `U _p` (spelling synonym pinned); `inline int p(int); int p(int){…}` → `T _p`; `int p(int); inline int p(int){…}` → `T _p`; `extern int p(int); inline int p(int){…}` → `T _p`; `extern inline int p(int); inline int p(int){…}` → `T _p`; `inline int p(int){…} extern int p(int);` → `T _p`; `extern inline int p(int){…}` → `T _p`; `static inline int p(int){…}` → `t _p` (Local).
★ ZERO-EMISSION IS NOT `Weak`. Encoding the no-external-definition state as a Weak binding was evaluated and DISQUALIFIED three ways: it collides with inlining.cpp's rule-2 refusal to inline Weak callees (turning a hint into a pessimization), it would EMIT `_fd_def.h`'s never-called bodies and drag undescribed `__darwin_check_fd_set_overflow` into every TU that includes it, and — since DSS has no on-demand emission — it would make LINKABILITY differ between `debug` and `release`. The suppressed definition instead lowers through the SAME ExternFunction path a bare prototype uses (prototypeSynthesizesExtern), so a sibling CU's definition resolves it and a genuinely absent one fails LOUD K_SymbolUndefined.
semantics.$threadLocalComment: TLS C1 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the C11/C23 6.7.1p2 forbidden-combination set for the thread-storage specifiers. `register` parses as an inert storage-class specifier in the c (localDeclSpecifiers), so `register thread_local int x;` must reject S_ThreadLocalInvalidCombination rather than silently drop one specifier (6.7.1p2 admits ONLY static/extern beside thread_local; C23 additionally admits auto — the c's auto is the C23 inference specifier and is deliberately NOT listed). `typedef` cannot co-occur grammatically (TF-C72 gave typedefDecl a `typedefDeclSpecifiers` prefix, but it admits ONLY the attribute forms `attrSpec`/`stdAttr` — no storage-class keyword — so `typedef thread_local int T;` is still a loud parse error, MEASURED) and `constexpr` co-presence is detected via the Pass-1 isConstexpr mark, so neither is listed here. WHICH tokens confer thread storage rides the declaration rows' linkageSpecifiers ({"threadStorage": true}) — this block only names the forbidden pairings.
semantics.$predefinedFunctionNamesComment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-FUNC-PREDEFINED-IDENTIFIER): the C99 6.4.2.2 predefined identifier `__func__` (+ the GNU `__FUNCTION__` alias). Pass 1 binds, for EACH spelling, one synthetic symbol into a function DEFINITION's own (param/body) scope BEFORE the params — kind=Variable, isConst (SE4's const check catches `__func__ = x` / `+=` -> S_ConstViolation), type = Array<narrow-string-core, len+1> (the element core is the language's declared string-literal core — the SAME config source string literals type from, never a hardcoded Char). A param named `__func__` collides at its own bind (S_RedeclaredSymbol). HIR lowering FOLDS a read to a string-literal-shaped constant (byte-identical to a real string literal, so rodata materialization / array->pointer decay / `__func__[i]` indexing / sizeof / `&__func__` all ride the existing string-literal paths); identical folded literals share ONE rodata global (the F2 byte-content memo — C99 requires `__func__ == __func__`). ++/--/compound-assign on it -> S_PredefinedIdentifierNotAddressable (no storage slot to write back). Source-agnostic: WHICH spellings are per-language config; the engine never hardcodes `__func__`.
semantics.$attributeSemanticsComment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-SEMANTICS, C23 6.7.13): the standard-attribute semantics TABLE — a closed verb set over per-name rows (all rows structurally identical; ONE unknown-name source of truth). `attrSpecRule`/`stdAttrRule` name the two attribute-specifier shapes (GNU `__attribute__((...))` / C23 `[[...]]`); `bareStatementRule` is the bare attribute-declaration statement (`[[fallthrough]];`). The semantic tier's `scanAttributeSemantics` walks a declaration's specifier prefix (or a bare statement), stops AT each attribute node, extracts each clause's name (last-::-segment, dunder-normalized) + optional string message (the shared decodeAdjacentStringBodies chokepoint), and folds the matched row's EFFECT: `suppressUnused` (the D8 unused-variable warning is suppressed — [[maybe_unused]]/GNU unused), `warnOnUse` (each use-site of the symbol warns S_DeprecatedSymbolUsed — [[deprecated]]), `warnOnDiscard` (a call whose result is discarded as a bare expression-statement warns S_NodiscardResultDiscarded — [[nodiscard]]/GNU warn_unused_result), `none` (KNOWN vocabulary consumed elsewhere or deliberately inert — fallthrough/likely/unlikely/reproducible/unsequenced per C23, noreturn [the FC16 scan owns it], packed [the trailing-composite scan owns it; the leading position fails loud at the HIR linkage tier] — listed so the unknown warning NEVER false-fires on them, design fix F4). An UNMATCHED name in the C23 `[[...]]` form warns S_UnknownAttribute (suppressible — C23 forbids fatal unknown standard attributes); the GNU form keeps its pre-existing loud gates (file-scope H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier; block-scope wholesale-ignore = D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-GNU-BLOCK-SCOPE-UNKNOWN-NAME). Absent block ⇒ the language has no standard-attribute semantics (toy/tsql — the scan never runs). Source-AGNOSTIC: every rule id + name is per-language config; the engine walks the closed effect-verb set only.

attributeSemantics.$clauseNameTokenClassComment: P32 (D-C-ATTRIBUTE-CLAUSE-NAME-ADMITS-ONLY-IDENTIFIER-SO-A-KEYWORD-NAMED-ATTRIBUTE-IS-REFUSED): the READER half of the clause-name widening, naming the SAME `tokenClasses` entry the grammar's clause-name slots compile from. Without it every clause-name scan in the semantic tier (`collectAttrClauses`'s trailing-clause detector, `extractOneAttrClause`'s name scan and its sibling-clause skip, the composite packed/aligned scan) would still look for `Identifier` alone — so `__attribute__((__const__))` would PARSE, match no effect row, and be dropped in SILENCE. The loader's Clause-C drift guard refuses a config where only one of the two sides moved, in either direction.
attributeSemantics.$attributeArgRuleComment: TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE-LEADING-ARG-SOUP): the attribute ARGUMENT-group shape. `linkageFrom` flags every token it reaches THROUGH an `attrArgs` node (nested arg groups inherit the flag) and skips the flagged tokens for the linkage-specifier KEY LOOKUP, so a LEADING `__attribute__((format(printf,1,2))) int h(...);` no longer reports `printf`/`1`/`2` as unrecognized linkage specifiers. The flagged tokens deliberately REMAIN in the flattened token list and REMAIN visible to the composite `<ident>:<string-body>` forward scan — `visibility("hidden")`'s string lives inside this subtree, so adding `attrArgs` to `linkageSpecifierIgnoredRules` instead (the obvious fix) DELETES it and breaks the composite key; MEASURED: that variant reports `'visibility' is not a recognized linkage specifier` on legal C. The flag is checked AFTER the by-name skip and is deliberately NOT part of `isIgnoredKind` nor of the forward scan — an ignored-by-NAME clause identifier is what blocks cross-clause string mispairing, so widening either surface would trade this bug for a worse one. OPTIONAL key: absent ⇒ nothing is ever flagged and the scan behaves exactly as before it existed.
attributeSemantics.$alignEffectComment: TF-C73 (D-CSUBSET-GNU-ATTRIBUTE): `aligned` gets its OWN effect verb rather than joining the inert `none` row, because it is the one attribute in this table that changes LAYOUT. Folding it to `none` would be a silent under-alignment — the exact class of bug the `none` row exists to keep OUT of the unknown-name warning, applied to an attribute that actually has a sink. The verb reuses the alignment machinery `alignasSpec` already drives (fold the operand, validate power-of-two / ≤256 / ≥ natural, then store on the symbol or the composite's fieldAligns), so GNU `__attribute__((aligned(N)))` and C11 `alignas(N)` converge on ONE validated path instead of two. The name is dunder-normalized at the scan, so `__aligned__` — the spelling the Apple SDK headers actually use — matches.
attributeSemantics.$noneRowComment:
TF-C73: the `none` row grew the ABI-NEUTRAL hint vocabulary. These names were ALREADY skipped for LINKAGE (topLevelDecl's `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames`), but that list only stops a file-scope declaration from failing H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier — it says nothing about the attribute-SEMANTICS scan. Now that `typedefDecl`, `structSpec`/`unionSpec` and `structField`/`unionField` carry `unknownStrictAttributeIsError`, a GNU name with no row is an ERROR in those slots, so every name DSS deliberately ignores must be KNOWN here or legal SDK headers start failing loud. `visibility` and `weak` are DELIBERATELY ABSENT: DSS MODELS both (topLevelDecl's `linkageSpecifiers` maps `weak` and the composite `visibility:hidden`), and a typedef or a struct member cannot carry linkage — so those spellings landing in one of these slots is a real error and must stay loud rather than be normalized into inertness.
~~ CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (P42, D-CSUBSET-STRICT-ATTRIBUTE-GATE-BLIND-TO-LINKAGE-VOCABULARY) BY MEASUREMENT: the last clause — 'a real error and must stay loud' — WAS WRONG, and it is the exact blindness that row was filed for. ✔MEASURED, each reference probed separately (gcc 13.3 `-std=c2x`, clang 18 `-std=c23`, `-Wall -Wextra`): `typedef __attribute__((weak)) int T;`, `typedef __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) int T;` and `struct __attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) S { int a; };` compile on BOTH with a warning (clang is outright silent on the struct) and exit 0, while DSS exited 1 with `error[S0031]` on all three. DSS was REFUSING legal C to keep a vocabulary boundary tidy. These names STAY ABSENT from this table — that part was right, because they are MODELLED by the linkage tier and giving them an inert `none` row would make DSS drop a real linkage fact — but the strict gate now consults the LINKAGE vocabulary as well as this table (`languageModelsAttributeName`), so 'absent from `effects`' no longer means 'unknown to the language'. ⚠ RESIDUAL, named rather than left to be found: because these two names carry no `effects` row they also carry no `appliesTo`, so DSS is now SILENT where the references WARN that the attribute cannot appertain to a typedef. Closing that needs the same loader change as this row's `none`-split residual — `appliesTo` permitted on an inert row — and is recorded on [[D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-IGNORED-FOR-DECL-KIND-SILENT]]. ~~
~~ AMENDED 2026-08-28 (P44, D-CSUBSET-GNU-UNKNOWN-NAME-GATE-ASYMMETRY): THE PRESSURE THIS TABLE WAS UNDER IS RELIEVED, and what the table is FOR has narrowed accordingly. The opening claim above — 'a GNU name with no row is an ERROR in those slots, so every name DSS deliberately ignores must be KNOWN here or legal SDK headers start failing loud' — no longer holds. The six rows that carried `unknownStrictAttributeIsError` now declare `false` (the measurement is on the typedefDecl row's $p44UnknownNameGateComment), so a name absent from this table is a suppressible WARNING at every one of those positions: an unlisted SDK attribute now costs a diagnostic, never a build. ★ WHAT A `none` ROW STILL BUYS, stated plainly so the table is not mistaken for dead weight: the KIND AXIS (`appliesTo`, which lives on an effects row and nowhere else) and the ABSENCE of a warning for a name DSS genuinely models. Both are real; neither is load-bearing for compilability any more. ~~
~~ ✅ THAT RESIDUAL IS CLOSED 2026-08-27 (P42 lane S), AND THE 'STAY ABSENT' RULING ABOVE IS **PARTLY REVERSED** — read this before restoring it. `weak` and `visibility` now DO carry an `effects` row, `{"names": ["weak", "visibility"], "appliesTo": ["variable", "function"], "effect": "none"}`. The concern that gave them a `none` row would 'make DSS drop a real linkage fact' was the right thing to worry about and is MEASURED FALSE for an INERT row: `effect: "none"` adds no effect and the HIR linkage tier keeps sole ownership of the meaning — ✔re-measured after the change, `__attribute__((weak)) int gv = 1;` and `__attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) int gv = 1;` still compile clean with their linkage facts threaded, and the weak/visibility pins stay green. What the row buys is the KIND AXIS, which lives on an `effects` row and nowhere else: `typedef __attribute__((weak)) int T;` and the trailing spelling now warn S005F at rc=0, matching clang 18.1.3 and gcc 13.3.0, where DSS was silent. ⚠ The LEADING position (`__attribute__((weak)) typedef int T;`) is still `error[P0009]` — a GRAMMAR gap in `typedefDecl`'s specifier prefix, NOT this table's, and out of that lane's file set; it is named rather than silently left. ~~
attributeSemantics.$packedStaysNoneComment: ★★ TF-C73 — `packed` STAYS HERE, and what that costs is now paid by the CONSUMER rather than by the grammar. `none` asserts 'KNOWN vocabulary, consumed elsewhere or deliberately inert'. For `packed` the 'elsewhere' is `semantics.packed.attributeNames`, read by `scanCompositePacked`. The claim used to hold only because the grammar admitted exactly ONE composite attribute position; the moment the after-keyword slot opened, `packed` reaching THAT surface was known-and-inert, i.e. silently dropped — MEASURED, `struct __attribute__((packed)) S { int a; char b; };` compiling clean at `sizeof` 8 against clang's 5. Removing the name from this row would have made it loud again, but the loader's vocabulary-drift guard refuses that (a name in `packed.attributeNames` must be declared known vocabulary here, else the `[[packed]]` spelling warns S_UnknownAttribute). The resolution was to make `scanCompositePacked` read EVERY composite surface — all `compositeAttrList` children plus the row's `declarationAttrSlotRules` — so the name is genuinely consumed everywhere it can appear. RE-MEASURED: that same input is now `sizeof` 5 / `_Alignof` 1, matching clang. THE RULE THIS ENCODES: a name belongs in `none` only while EVERY position that can reach this scan has a real consumer for it. Opening a new position without one turns the row into a silent drop — so a new attribute POSITION must be checked against this table, name by name, before it ships.
attributeSemantics.$appliesToComment:
★★ TF-C93 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-IGNORED-FOR-DECL-KIND-SILENT): `appliesTo` on each row below names the ENTITY KINDS the attribute may appertain to, drawn from the engine's OWN `DeclarationKind` vocabulary (`variable` | `function` | `table` | `type` — `table` is spellable but unwritten by C, inert config of the same shape as `symbolVisibilityFromName` accepting `protected`/`internal`). The semantic tier's ONE shared decl-kind gate walks THIS set against the effective kind of the declarator it is applying facts to and warns `S_AttributeIgnoredForDeclarationKind` when the kind is absent — so the engine names NO attribute and NO effect verb, it walks a config-declared kind set, and a future verb inherits the gate by being REQUIRED to declare its kinds.
WHAT IT CLOSED, MEASURED at HEAD 199fe7d with the shipped CLI — four axes, all silent, exit 0, attribute discarded: `__attribute__((no_sanitize_thread)) int gv = 7;`, `__attribute__((noinline)) int gv2 = 7;`, the `always_inline` twin, and `int gw1 __attribute__((warn_unused_result)) = 1;`. Host clang diagnoses every one of them.
★ THE KEY IS **REQUIRED** ON EVERY ROW WHOSE VERB IS NOT `none`, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. A permissive 'absent means every kind' default is the silent-permissive trap of [[D-TEST-IGNORE-LIST-IS-A-LICENSE-TO-DROP]] — a row that merely FORGOT the key would read as universal and go quiet on exactly the misuse the gate exists to report. The loader enforces it by extending the SAME `effect != none` predicate Clause B's drift cross-check already computes, and it also REFUSES the key on a `none` row (where it could never be read).
★★ SEVERITY IS **WARNING**, ON MEASURED GROUNDS, AND ONE DIVERGENCE IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED. Grounds: host clang treats `noinline`/`always_inline` on an object as `-Wignored-attributes` WARNINGS, so erroring would refuse C every real toolchain compiles (the TF-C77 lesson); the registry row prescribes 'ONE shared warning'; a warning adds ZERO corpus errors; and `--warnings-as-errors` already provides the strict posture. DIVERGENCE: clang HARD-ERRORS `no_sanitize_thread` on a data object (`'no_sanitize_thread' attribute only applies to functions`) while DSS WARNS. The gate is uniform across all four axes on purpose — one code, one severity, no per-attribute severity table — and an unrecorded divergence is how TF-C92's retracted justification happened.

TF-C81 (D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE): GNU `__attribute__((always_inline))` — HONORED, not ignored, by the exact chain its `noinline` sibling above uses: the verb folds onto SymbolRecord.isAlwaysInline (FnSig-gated, OR-merged across the proto/def pair), projects to HirAlwaysInlineMap, stamps MirFunc.alwaysInline, and the optimizer's inlining pass WAIVES its size threshold for such a callee in the §2.9 legality gate (inlining.cpp rule 6). Dunder-normalized, so `__always_inline__` matches too; there is no C11/C23 standard spelling, so no `[[…]]` name is listed.
★★ WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS, STATED NARROWLY SO THE CLAIM IS TRUE. It claims the attribute EXEMPTS THE CALLEE FROM THE INLINER'S SIZE-BASED COST MODEL. It does NOT claim the function is always inlined, and the difference is not pedantry — it is the whole honesty of the row. TWO limits, both deliberate and both MEASURED:
  (1) EVERY CORRECTNESS REFUSAL STILL WINS. A Weak callee, a same-SCC (recursive) call, an address-escaped callee, a callee with no returning path, an arity/type mismatch — each still refuses, and DSS says nothing when it does (GCC errors 'inlining failed in call to always_inline'; clang warns). The bypass is fused into rule 6's own condition rather than written as an early accept precisely so it cannot skip those scans; an early accept would turn a performance annotation into a licence to miscompile. The silence is a conservative divergence — the program compiles and is correct, it merely keeps a call — and making it loud needs a per-CALL-SITE reachability story, which is not this cycle.
  (2) ★ IT IS SCOPED TO THE INLINER, NOT TO THE PROGRAM, AND THEREFORE DOES NOTHING UNDER `--config=debug`. The shipped debug pipeline (dss-config/pipelines/debug.pipeline.json) is `Identity` only — there is no Inlining pass, hence no cost model to bypass, hence the attribute is VACUOUS and the call stays out-of-line. GCC and clang honour `always_inline` at -O0 because their inliner always runs; DSS's does not. THIS ASYMMETRY IS STATED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED. It is the same relationship `noinline` already has with the debug pipeline (a prohibition with no inliner to prohibit) read in the other direction — the difference being that a vacuous prohibition is harmless while a vacuous mandate is a missed optimization, so only this direction is worth writing down. A FORK WAS CONSIDERED AND NOT TAKEN SILENTLY: giving the debug pipeline a minimal always-inline pass would match clang, but it changes shipped debug codegen for every program to serve one attribute, so it is REPORTED as an option rather than chosen here.
RED-ON-DISABLE (all re-verified against the final build): delete this row and `always_inline` falls through to the unknown-name path (H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier, the pre-TF-C81 state); delete the `&& !mir.funcAlwaysInline(callee)` clause in inlining.cpp rule 6 and the release-arm pin goes red as the over-threshold callee's Call reappears. ★ BUT NOT EVERY HOP BEHAVES THAT WAY, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS MEASURED: dropping the flag at the `mir_rebuild_helper.cpp` propagation hop leaves the end-to-end release pin GREEN — only the dedicated flag-survival pins catch it. A `noinline` flag must keep REFUSING on all 4 release iterations, so clearing it re-arms the inliner; an `alwaysInline` flag only has to survive to the FIRST inlining opportunity, and Inlining runs first in iteration 1. That is the reverse of TF-C78's result for the identical hop, and it is why the propagation carries its own pin here rather than leaning on the end-to-end one. ★ `always_inline` COMBINED WITH `noinline` on one function (or split across its prototype and definition) is a LOUD S_ConflictingInlineAttributes, NOT a last-writer-wins: MEASURED, Apple clang 21.0.0 emits no diagnostic at all (even -Weverything) and silently resolves it to `noinline` in both source orders, which is exactly the invisible outcome this project refuses.

Two use sites, both `static <attr> T f(...)` and therefore both routed through `declSpecifiers` into the topLevelDecl row: wal.c:942 walIndexWriteHdr and wal.c:2590 walIndexTryHdr. They are the two wal-index header functions whose data races sqlite considers DELIBERATE and benign -- a statement about the program's concurrency contract, not a performance hint.
★★ WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS, STATED NARROWLY SO THE CLAIM IS TRUE -- AND IT IS A NARROWER CLAIM THAN EITHER SIBLING'S. It claims the exclusion is RECORDED and OBSERVABLE: it survives every tier and is queryable in the `.dssir` text. It does NOT claim any pass is suppressed, because there is none to suppress. MEASURED: `grep -rni sanitiz src/` returns ZERO hits -- DSS ships no sanitizer, no instrumentation pass and no `-fsanitize` surface of any kind. So `appendFuncAttrs` emitting the keyword IS the effect, and the row must never be rewritten to imply otherwise until an instrumentation pass exists to read the flag.

Both would throw the per-function FACT away three tiers before MIR, so the day an instrumentation pass lands it would have to re-derive from source what the front end had already parsed and discarded. Storing it makes this row true NOW ('DSS records the exclusion') rather than true by vacuity. The cheap config-only alternative was considered and REJECTED on exactly that ground.

That form's clause NAME is `no_sanitize`, and linkageFrom's composite-key pairing assembles `<ident>:<string-body>` BEFORE the semantic tier runs, so the key it looks up is `no_sanitize:thread`. MEASURED with the shipped CLI at TF-C92 HEAD: `static __attribute__((no_sanitize("thread"))) int g(int k){...}` -> `error[H000C] 'no_sanitize:thread' is not a recognized linkage specifier`. Matching it would require the effects table to key on a clause ARGUMENT VALUE, which no verb does and which is a mechanism change, not a row; sqlite writes only the bare spelling, so the loud refusal is the correct residue. Adding `no_sanitize` to `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` to quiet it would be strictly WRONG -- it would silently accept `no_sanitize("address")`/`("undefined")` too and record nothing for any of them.

That is why the honored spelling lives here as an effect rather than as a no-op `linkageSpecifiers` entry: a linkage entry would need one key per dunder variant. `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` sits on the normalized side with this table, which is what lets ONE name in each of the two lists cover both spellings.
RED-ON-DISABLE, ALL THREE MEASURED AGAINST THE FINAL BUILD -- AND THE FIRST ONE IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT OF THIS ROW. (1) Delete this row while LEAVING both `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` entries in place -- the shape a reviewer would call 'just the config-only version' -- and the compiler goes **SILENT**, not loud: MEASURED, `static __attribute__((no_sanitize_thread)) int f(int)` compiles with exit 0 and ZERO diagnostics while the attribute is thrown away, because the linkage tier now skips the name by NAME and no other tier claims it. That measured silence IS the ignore-list-only alternative, and it is exactly [[D-TEST-IGNORE-LIST-IS-A-LICENSE-TO-DROP]]. Only the MIR-text pins detect it (they drop to 0). (2) Delete this row AND the row's ignored name and it becomes LOUD again (H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier / H000C `'no_sanitize_thread' is not a recognized linkage specifier` -- the pre-TF-C92 state, MEASURED at HEAD 75172fe in BOTH the topLevelDecl and externDecl positions); delete ONLY the ignored name and the LOADER refuses the config with the attribute-vocabulary drift error naming this attribute, so the coupled halves cannot drift apart. (3) Delete the `if (ns)` arm in mir_text.cpp `appendFuncAttrs` and every MIR-text pin goes red while every bool-only pin (rebuild-helper, merge, semantic-tier) stays GREEN -- MEASURED -- because the printer IS this axis' only consumer.
