D-C-GNU-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-IS-WARNED-AND-IGNORED-NOT-RUN: GNU `__attribute__((constructor))` — the function joins the program's STATIC-INITIALIZER SCHEDULE and is run BEFORE the entry function. Its `destructor` twin is the row below.
★★ THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE THE NAME WAS ALREADY ACCEPTED AND SILENTLY USELESS. For one cycle DSS parsed the attribute, emitted `warning[H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier]` naming it, and DROPPED it: the same program exited 0 under DSS and 42 under mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0. Accepting the SYNTAX was the correct front-end verdict; `constructor` is simply vocabulary the references IMPLEMENT, so acceptance was never agreement.
★★ THE PRIORITY ARGUMENT IS PART OF THE UNION, NOT AN EXTRA — do not 'simplify' it away. MEASURED 2026-08-28 against gcc 13.3.0, clang 18.1.3 and mingw-w64 gcc 13.2.0, probed SEPARATELY, each function printing its own tag so stdout order IS run order: all three produce exactly `c101 c102 cBARE | MAIN | dBARE d102 d101`. So constructors run ASCENDING by priority with the BARE (unprioritized) form LAST, and destructors run that same sequence BACKWARD. The bare form is the common spelling and is NOT an error — unlike `aligned`, whose bare form this document fails loud on, because a bare `aligned` has a target-dependent meaning while a bare `constructor` has one meaning all three references agree on.
⚠⚠ ORDER AMONG EQUAL PRIORITIES IS NOT PORTABLE AND MUST NEVER BE PINNED BY A TEST: two bare same-priority constructors run 1,2 under Linux gcc and clang and 2,1 under mingw-w64 gcc — MEASURED. DSS may choose any order there. A corpus example must accumulate COMMUTATIVELY.
★ ONE FUNCTION MAY OCCUPY BOTH CHANNELS, each at its own priority — MEASURED, `__attribute__((constructor,destructor))` and the two-clause `((constructor(101))) ((destructor(102)))` both compile clean under -Wall -Wextra and run at both ends. That is why the schedule is two independent optionals rather than a phase plus a priority.
★★ ADDING THESE NAMES HERE IS WHAT SILENCES THE OLD WARNING, AND THAT IS THE HAZARD THIS ROW HAD TO LAND WITH ITS SINK TO AVOID. `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` is DERIVED from this table ([[D-CSUBSET-GNU-UNKNOWN-NAME-GATE-ASYMMETRY]]) and the derivation is VERB-BLIND, so the instant a name appears here the linkage tier stops reporting it. A row landed WITHOUT the downstream sink would therefore have turned an ANNOUNCED divergence into a SILENT one — strictly worse than the defect — which is why the config row, the semantic fold, the MIR/LIR/asm carriage, the emitted tables and the entry-trampoline calls are one edit and not five.
SINK, end to end and greppable at every hop: the `runBeforeEntry` verb folds onto `SymbolRecord::staticInit`, rides `LinkageAttr::staticInit` through `HirLinkageMap` onto `MirFunc::staticInit`, becomes a module-level `LirStaticInitEntry` list that `copyModuleSideStructures` carries across every LIR rebuild, reaches `AssembledModule::staticInitSchedule`, and is turned into CALLS the linker-synthesized entry trampoline makes around the user entry -- ordered once by `staticInitOrder`. Two more hops exist because the function is otherwise unreachable: the DCE liveness scan ROOTS it (a `static` constructor is called from nowhere in the program text, so at --config=release it would simply be deleted), and `mir_text` prints/reparses the schedule so a dropped hop shows up in a `.dssir` round trip rather than only in a run.
⚠ NO SECTION IS EMITTED, AND THAT IS A MEASURED DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION -- do not add `.init_array` here expecting it to be read. Those sections are how a program tells a C RUNTIME what to run before main, and DSS links no crt: it synthesizes `_start` and that entry IS the runtime. MEASURED on a DSS elf64-x86_64-linux-exec artifact -- `readelf -d` shows an eleven-entry dynamic section with NO DT_INIT_ARRAY and no DT_INIT, and ld.so walks the TAG, never the section; PE runs no `_initterm` because the UCRT startup object is never linked. Each object-format document declares WHO RUNS the schedule (`staticInitializers.runner`) instead, and a format that can neither run nor carry one declares nothing, which makes the linker REFUSE such a program by name.

D-C-GNU-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-IS-WARNED-AND-IGNORED-NOT-RUN: GNU `__attribute__((destructor))` — the AFTER-ENTRY twin of the row above, run after the entry function returns and before the process exits. Read that row for the measured ordering, the priority argument, the both-channels case and the reason these names could not be added without their sink.
★ IT IS A SEPARATE VERB RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT TO ONE VERB because an effect verb is what the row MEANS, and these two mean different things at different times; the phase is also what selects the emitted section, which stays a total function of the verb alone.

effects.$p32ConstNameComment: P32 (D-C-ATTRIBUTE-CLAUSE-NAME-ADMITS-ONLY-IDENTIFIER-SO-A-KEYWORD-NAMED-ATTRIBUTE-IS-REFUSED): `const` joins this row, and it is the name half of that row rather than an unrelated vocabulary addition. Admitting a keyword-spelled clause NAME in the grammar is only half a fix: `__attribute__ ((__const__))` would then parse, dunder-normalise to `const`, match NO row here, and — at file scope, where `topLevelDecl`/`externDecl` run the strict linkage scan — fail H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier on legal glibc. The 50 occurrences in ONE preprocessed TU would have swapped a P0009 for an H000C. It is `none` (parsed, recognised, deliberately INERT) for the same reason its sibling `pure` is: GNU `const` asserts a function reads no memory and has no side effects, which is an OPTIMISER promise, and DSS has no verb for that — declaring one it does not keep would be worse than declaring none. ★ It is ALSO added to `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` on `topLevelDecl` and `externDecl`, and that is NOT redundancy: the loader's Clause-B drift guard exempts `none` rows, so nothing would have forced it, and the two lists genuinely answer different questions (this one says what the attribute MEANS, that one says the linkage scan must not read it as a specifier). ⚠ The type QUALIFIER `const` is untouched by either: it is a `headQualifier`, so it lives in the type head and never enters the specifier-prefix roots the linkage scan walks — ✔MEASURED after the change, `const int cg = 7;` at file scope still compiles clean and still reads as a qualified type.
effects.$tfc93AppliesToComment:
★★ TF-C93 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-IGNORED-FOR-DECL-KIND-SILENT): THIS ROW CANNOT CARRY A CORRECT `appliesTo`, AND THE LOADER THEREFORE **REFUSES** THE KEY HERE — the exemption is mechanical, not a forgotten TODO. The row bundles names belonging to genuinely different entity kinds in ONE list: function-only (`format`, `nonnull`, `nothrow`, `leaf`, `malloc`, `pure`, `cold`, `hot`, `sentinel`, `alloc_size`, `access`), type-only (`may_alias`, `transparent_union`, `packed`), statement-only (`fallthrough`, `likely`, `unlikely`), and elsewhere-consumed (`noreturn` — the FC16 scan owns it; `packed` — the trailing-composite scan owns it; `availability` — an SDK deprecation annotation with no DSS model). Any single kind set would be wrong for most of them, and since the row's verb is `none` it is EXEMPT from the requirement by exactly the predicate Clause B's drift cross-check already computes.
★ WHAT CLOSING THIS HALF ACTUALLY REQUIRES, WRITTEN DOWN SO THE NEXT CYCLE DOES NOT REACH FOR ANOTHER KEY: a ROW SPLIT by applicable kind — several `none` rows, each with its own `appliesTo` — plus dropping the loader's refusal of the key on `none` rows. It is a config restructuring, NOT an additive key, which is why it is not folded into this cycle.
★ AND THE MEASURED LOSS IS BOUNDED, WHICH IS WHY DEFERRING IT IS DEFENSIBLE RATHER THAN A SHRUG: `cold`/`malloc`/`leaf` and friends on a DATA OBJECT are DSS-silent where clang warns (the residual gap) — RE-MEASURED 2026-07-30, DSS exit 0 + zero diagnostics against clang `warning: 'cold' attribute only applies to functions [-Wignored-attributes]`, likewise `malloc`, `leaf`, `hot`, and (with a wider applicability text) `nothrow` and `nonnull` — while `may_alias`/`fallthrough`/`transparent_union` in a leading declaration position are ALREADY LOUD `H000C` at the HIR linkage tier (RE-MEASURED, all three RC=1) — so the un-split row leaks a warning class, never a wrong fact or a wrong byte.
~~ CORRECTED 2026-07-30, SAME CYCLE, BY MEASUREMENT: this list named **`pure`** as its third exemplar, and `pure` is NOT one — host clang is **SILENT** on `__attribute__((pure)) int gv = 1;` (exit 0, no diagnostic, `-Wall -Wextra`), so DSS's silence there is AGREEMENT, not a gap. **That exemplar is retracted** and replaced with `leaf`, verified in both directions. `pure` remains correctly listed among this row's function-only NAMES above — the retraction is about which spellings clang actually diagnoses on an object, not about where `pure` applies. ~~
~~ CORRECTED 2026-08-27 (P42, D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-IGNORED-FOR-DECL-KIND-SILENT residual): the paragraph above is now HISTORY, not the state of the tree. The loader NO LONGER REFUSES `appliesTo` on a `none` row — it PERMITS it — and this row is SPLIT into the three below by applicable kind, exactly the restructuring that paragraph prescribed. What survives from it is the last clause and only the last clause: some of these names have NO expressible kind set, and those stay HERE, un-kinded, on purpose. ~~
effects.$p42UnkindedComment:
★★ P42 lane S: the names whose applicable position the four-kind `DeclarationKind` vocabulary genuinely CANNOT express. They are kept DELIBERATELY un-kinded rather than given a set that would be wrong somewhere — an `appliesTo` here would manufacture a diagnosis no reference gives, which is the false-positive half of the same bar that forbids a silent drop. Three groups, each MEASURED against clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` and gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x` SEPARATELY, on four shapes (data object / function / typedef / function-pointer object):
(a) STATEMENT attributes — `fallthrough`, `likely`, `unlikely`, `reproducible`, `unsequenced`. There is no `statement` declaration kind, and adding one is a NEW AXIS (the gate walks DECLARATIONS), not a value in an existing vocabulary.
(b) SILENT IN CLANG EVERYWHERE — `pure`, `const`, `may_alias`. MEASURED: clang emits nothing for `__attribute__((pure)) int gv = 1;` on any of the four shapes (gcc warns on three of them for `pure`/`const`; both are silent for `may_alias` everywhere). Under `DSS = (gcc ∪ clang ∪ MSVC) ∪ ISO C` the union's answer is SILENCE, so any kind set here would be DSS inventing a warning. ⓘ This also RETRACTS-IN-PLACE nothing: the 2026-07-30 correction above already established `pure` as agreement rather than a gap, and this re-measurement confirms it and extends it to `const` and `may_alias`.
(c) AGGREGATE-TYPE-DEFINITION attributes — `packed`, `transparent_union`. These apply to a struct/union/enum DEFINITION and to struct members. `type` in this vocabulary is what a TYPEDEF declares, which is not the same thing: `appliesTo: ["type"]` would stay silent on `typedef int T __attribute__((packed));` (where BOTH references warn) while risking a NEW false positive on the canonical `__attribute__((packed)) struct S { ... } s;`, which both references accept in silence and gcc HONORS. A wrong warning on the shape people actually write is worse than a missing one on the shape they do not.
`availability` is clang-only and gcc ERRORS on it (`-std=c2x`, MEASURED), so no kind judgement is available from the union at all.
⚠⚠ A KNOWN RESIDUAL ON `packed` / `may_alias` / `transparent_union`, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS TRIED AND **MEASURED TO BE A SILENT MISCOMPILE**. These three are absent from `topLevelDecl`/`externDecl`'s `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames`, so a LEADING `__attribute__((packed)) int gv = 1;` is `error[H000C]` where clang 18.1.3 and gcc 13.3.0 both compile at rc=0 (silently, for `may_alias`) — a real refusal of valid C. ⛔ Adding them to that list does NOT fix it: ✔MEASURED end-to-end with the shipped CLI, `__attribute__((packed)) struct S { char c; int v; } gv;` then went from a loud refusal to rc=0 with `sizeof(struct S) == 8`, byte-identical to the UNPACKED control (the TRAILING spelling still correctly yields 5). The linkage scan consults the ignored-name list BEFORE anything can honor the attribute, so the entry discards a LAYOUT FACT rather than a diagnostic — a wrong `sizeof` that still links, which this project ranks below a refusal. The distinction the fix needs is 'cannot honor it HERE' vs 'there is nothing here to honor', which lives at the HIR tier and not in a name roster. Pinned in BOTH directions today by `HirLoweringC.LeadingGnuPackedAttributeRejectedLoud` and `HirLoweringC.GnuWeightBearingHintNamesStayLoudAtFileScope`, so neither half can move in silence.
~~ ✅ THAT RESIDUAL IS CLOSED 2026-08-28 (P44, D-CSUBSET-GNU-UNKNOWN-NAME-GATE-ASYMMETRY), AND THE MEASUREMENT IT RESTED ON IS **REVERSED**. The claim was that adding these three to `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` turns `__attribute__((packed)) struct S { char c; int v; } gv;` into `rc=0 with sizeof == 8, byte-identical to the UNPACKED control` — a discarded layout fact ranked below a refusal. ✔RE-MEASURED against the REFERENCES rather than against the unpacked control: gcc 13.3.0 (`-std=c2x`) and clang 18.1.3 (`-std=c23`), probed separately, BOTH compile that exact program at rc=0 with `'packed' attribute ignored [-Wattributes]` and BOTH report `sizeof(struct S) == 8`, while the TRAILING spelling yields 5 on both. **8 is the CORRECT answer** — a leading `packed` reaches the composite in none of the three — so nothing was ever discarded, and the sentence two paragraphs up ('the canonical `__attribute__((packed)) struct S { ... } s;`, which both references accept in silence and gcc HONORS') is wrong in both halves: both WARN, and neither HONORS. ✔The mechanism claim fails on its own too: `deprecated` has been in that roster all along AND is honored, warning `S_DeprecatedSymbolUsed` at the use site, so ignoring a name in the LINKAGE scan does not blind the SEMANTIC one. ★ HOW IT CLOSED, and it is not by hand-listing the three: the loader now DERIVES the attribute half of every strict-scan row's `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` from THIS table, minus that row's own `linkageSpecifiers` base names. So all three go silent at file scope by construction — matching gcc and clang exactly for `may_alias`, and losing a warning DSS was giving under the WRONG code (`H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier`, i.e. 'not a recognized linkage specifier', about names this document models) for `packed` and `transparent_union`. A missed diagnostic is the safe direction; a false statement about the language's own vocabulary is not. ⚠ THE `appliesTo` JUDGEMENT ABOVE IS UNTOUCHED and still governs: these names stay un-kinded, for the reasons groups (a)/(b)/(c) give. What changed is only who adjudicates their NAME. Re-pinned by `HirLoweringC.GnuModelledInertNamesAreNotUnknownLinkageSpecifiers` (with `…GnuGenuinelyUnmodelledNameIsStillReportedAtFileScope` as its control), `HirLoweringC.LeadingGnuPackedAttributeIsAcceptedNotRefused` and `SemanticAnalyzerC.LeadingGnuPackedDoesNotPackTheComposite`, which asserts the `sizeof` in the source where no roster change can reach it. ~~

effects.$comment:
★★ P42 lane S (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-IGNORED-FOR-DECL-KIND-SILENT residual): the `none` verb's FUNCTION-ONLY half. This row exists because the loader now PERMITS `appliesTo` on an inert row; before that, one row held every inert name and no single kind set could be correct for it, so the silence was structural rather than chosen.
EVERY name here was MEASURED on four shapes against clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` and gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x`, probed SEPARATELY: all five are diagnosed by BOTH references on a data object, on a typedef and on a FUNCTION POINTER, and silent on a function. Sample, verbatim: clang `'cold' attribute only applies to functions [-Wignored-attributes]`; gcc `'malloc' attribute ignored; valid only for functions [-Wattributes]`.
★ DSS was SILENT on all of them at rc=0 before this cycle (MEASURED with the shipped CLI), which is precisely the warning class the registry row was filed for. The severity DSS emits is the shared suppressible `S005F` warning, matching both references' rc=0 — `--warnings-as-errors` supplies the strict posture for anyone who wants it. A refusal here would be worse than the silence it replaces.
★ WHY `alloc_size` IS HERE AND NOT IN THE FUNCTION-POINTER ROW BELOW, since the two rows are otherwise the same shape: MEASURED, gcc warns on `__attribute__((alloc_size(1))) int (*fp)(...)` while it is silent on the `format`/`nonnull`/`sentinel` equivalents. The split is the measurement, not a taxonomy.

★★ P42 lane S (same residual, and the second consumer of D-CSUBSET-APPLIESTO-CANNOT-EXPRESS-FUNCTION-POINTER-OBJECT's fifth spelling): the FUNCTION-OR-FUNCTION-POINTER half of the inert vocabulary. Split from the row above BY MEASUREMENT rather than by category — clang 18.1.3 and gcc 13.3.0 are both SILENT on `__attribute__((format(printf,1,2))) int (*fp)(const char*,...)` and on the `nonnull` / `sentinel` / `access` / `nothrow` twins, while both DIAGNOSE `cold`, `hot`, `leaf`, `malloc` and `alloc_size` in that same position. clang says so in its own message text for the data-object case: `'nothrow' attribute only applies to functions and function pointers`.
★★ THIS ROW IS THE REASON THE CHEAP FIX IS REFUTED. Mapping a `Ptr<FnSig>` variable to `function` at the gate — the shortcut the registry row's option (a) invited — would have silenced the row ABOVE, which both references diagnose on a function pointer. `functionPointer` had to be a fifth spelling in the `appliesTo` vocabulary, additive to `variable`, so the two halves can disagree. That is a fact that VARIES PER ROW, which is what makes it config rather than an engine rule.
★ `noreturn` sits here rather than in the function-only row for a reason that is DSS's own behaviour, not a reference measurement: TF-C94's `noreturnCarrier` already HONORS `noreturn` on a `Ptr<FnSig>` declarator (witnessed by Tcl 9's three `TclStubs` members), and clang honors it there too. Warning on a position where a shipped sink consumes the fact would contradict the compiler's own behaviour — the worst kind of diagnostic.
★ `access` is judged on gcc alone and that is deliberate: clang does not know the attribute at all (`unknown attribute 'access' ignored`), so its diagnosis carries no applicability signal. gcc's does: silent on a function and on a function pointer, `'access' attribute only applies to function types` on a data object and on a typedef.

★★ P42 lane S (D-CSUBSET-STRICT-ATTRIBUTE-GATE-BLIND-TO-LINKAGE-VOCABULARY residual): the LINKAGE vocabulary's KIND AXIS, and the reason an inert row is the right carrier for it.
`weak` and `visibility` are modelled by `declarations[].linkageSpecifiers`, not by an effect verb — that is where their MEANING lives and this row does not touch it. But `appliesTo` lives on an `effects` row and nowhere else, so before this row the decl-kind gate could not see these two names at all: MEASURED with the shipped CLI, `typedef __attribute__((weak)) int T;` and `typedef int T __attribute__((visibility("hidden")));` compiled at rc=0 with ZERO diagnostics, while BOTH references warn — clang `'weak' attribute only applies to variables, functions, and classes`, gcc `'weak' attribute ignored`. The sibling row that lane O corrected in this same file says the residual would need exactly this; it is now here.
★ THE ROW ADDS NO EFFECT AND MUST NOT. `effect: "none"` means the linkage tier keeps sole ownership of what these names DO; the row declares only WHERE they may appertain. ✔MEASURED after the change: `__attribute__((weak)) int gv = 1;` and `__attribute__((visibility("hidden"))) int gv = 1;` still compile clean and still thread their linkage facts (the weak-binding and visibility pins stay green).
★ `[variable, function]` IS THE MEASURED SET, not a guess: both references are silent on a data object, on a function AND on a function-pointer object (a function-pointer object is a `variable`, so `variable` covers it — the additive reading of the `functionPointer` refinement is what makes that true without a third entry), and both diagnose on a typedef. `Table` is absent because c declares none.
★ THE ROW IS SPELLED `visibility`, NOT `visibility:hidden`. A `linkageSpecifiers` key may be COMPOSITE (identifier + string body); the thing a programmer writes as a clause NAME is the identifier half, which is what the effects table matches on. The loader's drift cross-check learned the same split (`linkageSpecifierBaseName`) so it no longer demands `visibility` be added to `linkageSpecifierIgnoredNames` — which would have been ACTIVELY WRONG, because the HIR lowerer tests that list BEFORE assembling the composite key, so the entry would make `visibility("hidden")` be skipped by name and the visibility fact SILENTLY DROPPED.

semantics.$nodiscardComment: FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-SEMANTICS): the nodiscard DISCARD-CONTEXT rule ids for the warnOnDiscard effect. A call's result is 'discarded' when the call is the ENTIRE expression of an expression STATEMENT — structurally, the call node's parent is `expressionRule` AND the grandparent is `discardStatementRule` (the TWO-hop check, design-audit fix F1: the call's parent is the materialized `expression` node, so a one-hop parent==exprStmt check would NEVER fire). This shape makes the `(void)f();` discard idiom SUPPRESS by construction (the castExpr interposes → parent≠expression-under-exprStmt) and `x=f()`/`g(f())`/`return f()` correctly no-fire. Comma/paren-wrapped discards (`(f());`, `f(),g();`) are the named deferral D-CSUBSET-NODISCARD-INDIRECT-DISCARD-CONTEXT (warning-only miss). Absent block ⇒ warnOnDiscard rows never fire.
semantics.$nodiscardDiscardContextComment:
P32 [[D-CSUBSET-NODISCARD-INDIRECT-DISCARD-CONTEXT]]: the discard test was TWO-HOP-EXACT (parent==expression, grandparent==exprStmt), which is right for the dominant `f();` idiom and MISSED every discard reached through an interposed wrapper. MEASURED at the pre-change HEAD through the shipped CLI, one TU per shape: `(g());`, `g(), 1;`, `for(;;g())` and `for(g();;)` all compiled with NO warning, while gcc 13.3.0 AND clang 19.1.7 warn on all four (also measured, one TU per shape, with a bare `g();` positive control).
* `discardTransparentRules` names the wrappers the discarded value flows THROUGH. `parenExpr` is a plain rule entry. The COMMA is not: `binaryExpr` is the shared Pratt wrapper for every binary operator, so making the RULE transparent would make `x + g();` warn the way `g(), 1;` does -- a different question with a different answer -- and the entry therefore names the operator TOKEN too, matching only a wrapper built on `Comma`.
* `discardClauseHosts` covers the `for` clauses, which no transparent rule can express: init, condition and step are the SAME `expression` rule in the SAME node, init and step DISCARD and the condition does NOT, so only the clause INDEX separates them. Segments 0 (init) and 2 (step) are discard positions; segment 1 (the condition) is deliberately absent, and MEASURED: neither reference warns for `for(;g();)`.
! THE CLAUSE INDEX IS COUNTED WITH `hirLowering.forClauseSeparator`, WHICH IS WHY THAT TOKEN IS NOT RESTATED HERE. The CST->HIR `for` prologue segments the identical header with the identical key, so the two tiers cannot end up with two opinions about where clause 1 ends; the loader refuses `discardClauseHosts` in a document that declares no separator, because every child would then count as clause 0 and the CONDITION would start warning on legal C.
* `(void)g();` STAYS SILENT and that is a decision, not a gap: no cast rule is transparent, so the walk stops at the cast. The references DISAGREE (gcc warns, clang does not) and the cast is the universal idiom for 'I meant to discard this', so the silent reading is the one that does not fight the programmer -- the same disjunction rule that made the keyword-attribute class take clang's superset.
semantics.$variadicComment: FC12a-core (D-FC12A-VARIADIC-CALLEE): variadic-intrinsic typing. vaArgExpr = [ VaArgKeyword, '(', assignmentExpr(apChild 2), ',', castTypeRef(typeChild 4), ')' ] → pass 2 resolves+stamps the castTypeRef through the SAME resolver casts use (so the HIR lowering recovers the read type T) and stamps the node T; it type-checks `ap` is a va_list. vaStartExpr/vaEndExpr = [ kw, '(', assignmentExpr(apChild 2), ... ] → node stamped `void`; ap type-checked va_list; vaStart also flips the enclosing function's uses-va-start attribute so the LIR prologue spills the arg registers.
semantics.$staticAssertComment: C11/C23 6.7.10: the `_Static_assert`/`static_assert` DECLARATION rule. Pass 2 const-evaluates the condition child (visible-child 1 — the assignmentExpr after the keyword+'(') through the SAME evaluator that folds sizeof(T)/enum/arithmetic in an array dimension; ZERO ⇒ S_StaticAssertFailed (message = the OPTIONAL trailing string-literal child), NONZERO ⇒ nothing. The construct lowers to nothing (hirLowering staticAssertDecl → Skip).
semantics.$genericComment: FC16 (D-CSUBSET-GENERIC-SELECTION): C11/C23 6.5.1.1 generic selection. `rule` = the genericExpr shape; `controlChild` = the visible-child index of the controlling `assignmentExpr` (child 2 — after the GenericKeyword + '('). `assocRule`/`typedAssocRule`/`defaultAssocRule` name the association shapes so Pass 2 discriminates each `_Generic` child: a genericTypedAssoc's FIRST child is a castTypeRef (resolved+stamped through the SAME type resolver casts/sizeof/va_arg use — a VALUE in type position fails loud S_UnknownType) and its LAST is the result expression; a genericDefaultAssoc is the `default:` fallback (no type). Pass 2 lvalue-converts the controlling type (strips top-level volatile, the isAssignable precedent), matches it against each typed assoc's resolved type for COMPATIBILITY (interned TypeId equality via sameType), enforces EXACTLY ONE typed match (S_GenericSelectionAmbiguous on >1) OR the default (S_GenericSelectionNoMatch on none-and-no-default), stamps the genericExpr node with the winner's RESULT type, and records the winning association's result-expression node (nodeToSelectedExpr side-table). The dedicated HIR lowering (hirLowering.genericRule) lowers ONLY that recorded sub-expression.
semantics.$builtinOffsetofComment:
[[D-FFI-OFFSETOF-MACRO]]: `__builtin_offsetof` typing + folding. `rule` = the shape; `typeChild` 2 is the castTypeRef and `designatorChild` 4 the memberDesignator (keyword 0, `(` 1, `,` 3 — the sizeofType/alignofType child-index convention). Pass 2 resolves the container through the SAME type resolver sizeof and casts use, WALKS the designator over the SAME `computeLayout` engine codegen reads (so the answer carries the target's real layout — packing, `alignas`, everything — instead of a second derivation of it), and records the byte offset in the compile-time-answer side table; the node is stamped `synthesizedTypes.offsetof` (C 7.19's size_t). `fieldDesignatorRule` / `indexDesignatorRule` NAME the two shipped `designator` alternatives so the walk tells `.f` from `[i]` by RULE rather than by a token spelling it would then own a second copy of.
★ EVERY FAILURE IS LOUD — unknown member, incomplete container, a BIT-FIELD member (which has no byte offset at all, and whose address C forbids taking), a non-constant array index — because the only alternative to refusing is emitting a wrong address, and a wrong address is the silent class this compiler exists not to ship.
semantics.$builtinTypesCompatibleComment: `__builtin_types_compatible_p` typing + folding. `rule` = the shape; `leftTypeChild` 2 and `rightTypeChild` 4 are the two castTypeRefs. Pass 2 resolves both through the SAME resolver and compares them by INTERNED TYPE IDENTITY after stripping each side's top-level volatile — character for character the predicate `_Generic` uses to match an association, so the two can never come to disagree about what compatible MEANS. The answer (0 or 1) goes into the compile-time-answer side table and the node is stamped `synthesizedTypes.typesCompatible` (C's `int`, which is what gcc yields). An UNRESOLVABLE operand fails loud at the resolve and folds NOTHING — never a default 0, which would be a plausible wrong answer for exactly the type-dispatch this feeds.
semantics.$builtinChooseExprComment: `__builtin_choose_expr` selection. `rule` = the shape; `conditionChild` 2 is the controlling integer-constant expression, `thenChild` 4 and `elseChild` 6 the arms. Pass 2 const-evaluates the condition through the SAME `constIntExpr` engine `_Static_assert`, array dimensions and case labels use, records the WINNING arm's NodeId in the SAME `nodeToSelectedExpr` side table `_Generic` writes, and stamps the node with that arm's type — after which the CST→HIR lowering is literally `_Generic`'s, unchanged. A NON-CONSTANT condition is a constraint violation and fails LOUD; it is never quietly read as false, because a wrong arm is a wrong program that still builds. The arm not chosen is UNEVALUATED and is never lowered, exactly as a non-selected `_Generic` association is never lowered.
semantics.$compoundLiteralsComment: FC3.5 sweep-c3 (D-CSUBSET-COMPOUND-LITERAL-TYPEDEF): the compound-literal type position resolves + stamps through the SAME type-position resolver casts use (typedefs included). typeChild is the visible-child index into compoundLiteralExpr = [ '(' , castTypeRef , ')' , braceInitList ]. NO operandChild / cast-matrix validation — a compound literal is C 6.5.2.5 postfix syntax, not a conversion.
semantics.$builtinFunctionsComment: c103 (D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-UMULH): compiler intrinsics exposed as builtin functions (SE6 builtins scope, shadow-able by user decls). `__umulh` = the high 64 bits of the u64*u64 128-bit product (the MSVC/sqlite intrinsic used by sqlite3Multiply128/160 on _WIN64). `lowering:umulh` binds the call to a DEDICATED MIR op (x86 `mul r/m64` -> RDX, arm64 `umulh`) rather than an ordinary call/import -- a compiler intrinsic is not a linkable symbol. Available on every target that declares the umulh mnemonic vocabulary (x86_64 + arm64); a target lacking it fails loud at lowering.

builtinFunctions.$comment: D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-FENCE + D-CSUBSET-SYNC-BUILTIN-BARRIER: __sync_synchronize -- the GCC full CPU memory barrier (sqlite mutex_unix.c sqlite3MemoryBarrier's non-MSVC path; its sole S0001 before this row). An always-on lowered builtin like _ReadWriteBarrier above, but where `barrier` emits ZERO instructions (a compile-time-only fence), `atomic_fence` lowers to MirOpcode::AtomicFence with seq_cst (5) const-baked into the payload and emits a REAL fence instruction per target (x86_64 MFENCE 0F AE F0, arm64 DMB ISH 0xD5033BBF -- both MEASURED via clang+otool on __sync_synchronize, 2026-07-30). The builtin takes no order argument; GCC defines every __sync builtin as a FULL barrier.
builtinFunctions.name: __sync_synchronize

builtinFunctions.$comment: C99 _Complex (D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX §7.3): the always-injected complex builtins the <complex.h> macros route to. The `signature` form spells the `complex<f64>` result/param the scalar params/result axis cannot express (the _InterlockedCompareExchange ptr<> precedent; parseType decodes `complex<..>` via the M1 codec). `__builtin_complex(re, im)` constructs a complex from two reals (by-address materialized — the FIRST aggregate-returning builtin, CRITICAL-2). creal/cimag extract the real/imag F64 component; conj negates imag. Cycle-1 F64-monomorph (D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX-MONOMORPH-F64).

builtinFunctions.$comment: D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP: the three MSVC byte-reverse intrinsics, declared EXACTLY as the popcount/clz/ctz family above -- one shared `lowering` verb, the WIDTH carried by the param core, read back at mir_to_lir from `mir.instType(operand)`. ALWAYS-ON (no `availableObjectFormats` gate): the NAMES are MSVC's, but the OPERATION is a plain byte reverse with no platform content, and gating them would make a cross-compile of MSVC-flavoured source fail on the host's format rather than the target's -- the same reason `__umulh` (also an MSVC intrinsic spelling) is ungated. ** THEY ARE NOT SYMBOLS AND MUST NEVER BE DECLARED AS ONE: msvcrt.dll exports NO `_byteswap_*` (MEASURED, objdump -p, positive control memcpy/_msize/puts), DSS EAGER-IMPORTS every name a descriptor's `symbols` lists, and a prior draft that declared them crashed the pe loader with STATUS_ENTRYPOINT_NOT_FOUND (0xC0000139). A lowered builtin is the only correct realization -- see shippedLibs/intrin.json. ** WHY U16/U32/U64 ANONYMOUS CORES AND NEVER A NAMED TYPE-TEXT: MSVC spells these `unsigned short`/`unsigned long`/`unsigned __int64`, but `unsigned long` is 32-bit ONLY under LLP64 -- naming it here would be WRONG on every LP64 target and would collide with the per-dataModel type-identity rule (a shared typedef must resolve byte-identically per target). The core IS the contract; the spelling is not. ** MEASURED REACH: sqlite's pe64 leg emitted exactly 3 `error[S0001] got _byteswap_*` before these rows (util.c:1856 + util.c:1869 `_byteswap_ulong`, btreeInt.h:743 `_byteswap_ushort` via get2byteAligned) -- see the c `#pragma intrinsic` row above for the full macro chain that reaches them.
builtinFunctions.name: _byteswap_ushort

builtinFunctions.$comment: D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-BSWAP: the GCC/clang spellings of the three rows ABOVE -- the SAME operation, the SAME `lowering` verb, so this is three JSON rows and ZERO additional engine code (the `__builtin_popcount` / `__umulh` pattern: one lowering, many vendor spellings). Reserved `__builtin_` namespace, always-injected, shadow-able. ** THEY FLIP NOTHING TODAY, AND THEY ARE NOT SPECULATIVE -- THEY REMOVE A COUPLING. MEASURED: DSS ships __GNUC__=4 / __GNUC_MINOR__=2 / __GNUC_PATCHLEVEL__=1, so sqlite computes GCC_VERSION=4002001, which MISSES its `>=4003000` (util.c:1850/1863, rtree.c) and `>=4008000` (btreeInt.h:741) gates; sqlite therefore still takes the MSVC `_byteswap_*` arm on pe and the portable byte-by-byte `#else` on elf/macho, unchanged by these rows. The REASON to land them now is that WITHOUT them, `__GNUC__` cannot be made more truthful: a real GCC/clang is 4.3+ (and 4.8+ for bswap16), so the moment anyone corrects that version -- which is a live pressure, since 4.2.1 is what /usr/bin/clang reports and every OTHER gate keyed on it is already a judgement call -- sqlite would INSTANTLY route onto `__builtin_bswap32`/`__builtin_bswap16`, which would be UNDECLARED and produce fresh S0001 errors in exactly the file this cycle just made green. Landing the aliases alongside the lowering they already map to makes that future truthfulness fix a PURE CONFIG CHANGE. Do not delete them as dead rows: their value is that they are NOT reached yet.
builtinFunctions.name: __builtin_bswap16

semantics.$builtinStdbitComment: FC17.9(b) C23 <stdbit.h> (D-FULLC-STDBIT): the 56 `__builtin_stdc_<op>_<T>` builtins = the 14 N3096 §7.18 bit operations × 4 concrete widths {uc→U8, us→U16, ui→U32, ull→U64}. Each op's 4 width rows SHARE one `lowering` tag (stdc_leading_zeros … stdc_bit_ceil) → 14 BuiltinLowering enumerators → 14 hir_to_mir arms that COMPOSE the 3 hardware primitives (Popcount/Clz/Ctz) + universal ALU verbs (ZExt/Sub/Add/And/Or/Not/Shl/ICmp/Mul) into the exact width-correct, single-eval, branchless formula (NO new MIR op — pure composition over the proven bit-count substrate). The arm reads the operand's EXACT width W∈{8,16,32,64} from its param core (guaranteed by the pre-BuiltinCall arg coercion) → zero-extends to the promotion width P∈{32,64}. RESULT cores per C23: U32 for the 11 count/index/width ops; Bool for has_single_bit; the OPERAND core (U8/U16/U32/U64) for bit_floor/bit_ceil (they return the argument's type). These are the include-gated substrate for shippedLibs/stdbit.json's `stdc_*` macros (56 concrete + 14 per-format `ul` + 14 4-way `_Generic`); always-injected like `__umulh` (reserved `__builtin_` namespace, shadow-able). ★ MANDATORY shift-UB guard (bit_floor/bit_ceil): every `Shl(1, amt)` has amt∈[0,W-1] on EVERY branchless branch (bit_floor amt=bitWidth−(x≠0); bit_ceil amt=bitWidth(x−1)&(W−1) + the ==W overflow→0 select) — never an unguarded shift.
semantics.$builtinBitCountComment: FC17.9(b) (D-CSUBSET-BITCOUNT-INTRINSICS): the 3 hardware bit-count primitives as 6 GCC-compatible builtins (the walking skeleton for C23 <stdbit.h>; the 14 stdc_* ops layer on top). Each returns `int` (I32, the GCC signature) and takes an unsigned 32-bit (`__builtin_popcount`/`_clz`/`_ctz`) or 64-bit (`…ll`) value. `lowering` binds each call to a dedicated pure-unary MIR op (Popcount/Clz/Ctz) — like `__umulh`, a compiler intrinsic, not a linkable symbol; lowered to a native instruction (x86 POPCNT/LZCNT/TZCNT, arm64 CLZ + RBIT-then-CLZ for ctz) where the target declares the mnemonic, else a branchless SWAR bit-trick sequence (arm64 has no scalar GPR popcount). ★ DSS DEFINES clz/ctz at 0 = the width (LZCNT/CLZ/TZCNT hardware semantics — count = 32 or 64 for a zero input), NOT GCC's UB-at-0: a SAFE SUPERSET (every input GCC defines returns the same value; the 0 input GCC leaves UB is given the natural hardware answer).
semantics.$builtinAtomicCasComment: c104 (D-CSUBSET-INTRINSIC-ATOMIC-CAS): `_InterlockedCompareExchange(LONG volatile* dest, LONG exch, LONG comp) -> LONG` -- the MSVC atomic compare-and-swap intrinsic (returns the ORIGINAL *dest; stores exch iff original==comp). Win32 LONG = i32 (LLP64) -> the 32-bit CAS. The UNDERSCORE name is the real intrinsic exactly as the Windows SDK spells it; windows.json's `InterlockedCompareExchange` macro expands to it (the winnt.h convention), so sqlite's `#if defined(InterlockedCompareExchange)` takes the direct-intrinsic path and its calls land here. `signature` (full type-text, c104) instead of scalar params: the dest param is a POINTER. Lowers to x86 `lock cmpxchg` (implicit-RAX comparand/old) / an arm64 LDAXR-STLXR acquire-release loop. ★★ P54 ADDED THE 64-BIT SIBLING `_InterlockedCompareExchange64(LONGLONG volatile*, LONGLONG, LONGLONG) -> LONGLONG`, and it MINTED NO ENCODING: `x86_64.target.json`'s `lock_cmpxchg` already declared the width-64 REX.W variant, whose own $comment said it existed so that 'a future i64 CAS selects it by width instead of silently mis-encoding' — this is that consumer, so the row stopped being dead config. It is a real MSVC intrinsic spelled exactly as the Windows SDK spells it, and the param is `ptr<i64 "long long">` on EVERY data model because `long long` is 64-bit everywhere (contrast the 32-bit sibling, which needs the LLP64 override because Win32 LONG is 32-bit while POSIX `long` is not). ★ ITS FIRST CONSUMER IS DSS'S OWN ATOMICS RUNTIME (D-C-ATOMICS-RUNTIME-IS-OURS-ON-PE64, `runtime/platform/src/atomic.c`): an under-aligned 8-BYTE `_Atomic` load always straddles its natural block, so no aligned wider read can serve it and a width-native locked RMW is the only lock-free route — which needs exactly this width.
semantics.$builtinAtomicExplicitComment: FC17.9(d) atomic cycle-1 (D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC): `atomic_load_explicit(volatile A* obj, memory_order) -> C` and `atomic_store_explicit(volatile A* obj, C desired, memory_order) -> void` — the C11/C23 <stdatomic.h> §7.17.4/§7.17.7 explicit-order scalar accessors. Like `_InterlockedCompareExchange` these are always-injected compiler intrinsics (a non-linkable op, SE6-shadow-able) rather than shipped symbols; they route to the SAME MIR AtomicLoad/AtomicStore ops a bare `_Atomic` access uses, so the Phase C per-order LIR fence matrix realizes them. Monomorphized to `int` (i32) this cycle (defer atomic_long/llong/ptr → D-CSUBSET-ATOMIC-MONOMORPH-I32). The trailing `memory_order` arg (load arg[1] / store arg[2]) is CONST-FOLDED at hir_to_mir into the AtomicLoad/AtomicStore `payload` (0..5) and DROPPED from the operand list (AtomicLoad=[ptr], AtomicStore=[value,ptr]); a NON-constant order falls back to seq_cst (5) — over-fencing is C11-legal. The user-facing surface (atomic_int, memory_order_*) is include-gated in shippedLibs/stdatomic.json.
semantics.$builtinTypesComment: FC3 c1: the TEXT-keyed type-name table (typedef-style positions + the load-time fallback for single-word ladder/promotion names). The KEYWORD grammar path resolves through semantics.typeSpecifiers below (the C 6.7.2 multiset table) — both tables declare the SAME widths, and `long` carries the LLP64 override on BOTH so the two paths can never disagree (D-LANG-PLATFORM-DEPENDENT-PRIMITIVE-WIDTH).
semantics.$typeSpecifiersComment: FC3 c1: every VALID C type-specifier multiset (C 6.7.2 6) over the shipped keyword surface; combinations are ORDER-FREE (the engine canonicalizes by sorting token kinds; `long long` = LongKeyword twice). Invalid combos (`unsigned float`, `short long`) reject by ABSENCE -> S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination. `long`-bearing rows carry the LLP64 (Windows) 32-bit override; `long long` stays 64-bit everywhere. FC17.9(e) (D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE): the `long double` row carries the per-format coreByLongDoubleFormat axis — base F64 for f64-axis formats (pe64, macho-arm64: long double has double's REPRESENTATION), F80 (x87 80-bit) for x87-80 (elf/macho x86_64), F128 (binary128) for ieee128 (elf-arm64); an axis-less format (wasm/spirv) leaves the row UNREALIZED -> S_LongDoubleFormatUndeclared. D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY: this table is the LANGUAGE (vocabulary) axis; `core`/`coreByDataModel`/`coreByLongDoubleFormat` are the TARGET (representation) axis, and the two are INDEPENDENT — `name` is what identity interns on, so `long` stays distinct from `int` under LLP64 and `long double` distinct from `double` on the f64 axis (both previously COLLAPSED, making `_Generic` ambiguous and `int* p; long* q = p;` silently legal). `rank` is the C 6.3.1.1 conversion rank of the NAME (long long 4 > long 3 > int; long double 3 > double > float), used ONLY to break a usual-arithmetic-conversions tie between two operands of the SAME core. Named ONLY where a collision is possible: int/short/unsigned int/unsigned short/float/double/bool/void/plain char stay UNNAMED so they remain the ANONYMOUS representative of their core (integer promotion and enum-underlying synthesis re-mint anonymous primitives of those kinds; naming `int` would make a promoted `char+char` stop matching a declared `int`). Every row sharing a name must declare the SAME representation on every axis (loader-enforced, C_InvalidSemantics).

typeSpecifiers.$comment: D-CSUBSET-UINT128-TYPE (TF-C94): the GNU/clang 128-bit extended integer types — the last vocabulary gap between DSS and sqlite's `sqlite3_uint64` multiply path (sqlite/src/util.c:482,516-517 use `(__uint128_t)a * b` and `r += ((__uint128_t)aLo * b) >> 32`). FIVE rows, not three: the multiset key is canonicalized by SORTING the resolved token kinds (grammar_schema_json.cpp ~7374), so `unsigned __int128` and `__int128 unsigned` are the SAME multiset and come free from ONE row — what the five cover is the five DISTINCT spellings {__uint128_t} / {unsigned,__int128} / {__int128} / {signed,__int128} / {__int128_t}. Placement is DELIBERATE, at the END of the integer ladder after `unsigned long long`, NOT after the `unsigned long` row: splitting `unsigned long` from `unsigned long long` would interleave the ladder and put the 128-bit rows ahead of the 64-bit ones for a reader. ★★ THE `rank` FIELD IS NOT THE UAC WIDTH RANK. `rank` here is the interner's `vocabularyRank` (type_lattice.cpp:1010) and it is consulted at EXACTLY ONE place — type_rules.hpp:841-843, as a TIE-BREAK between two operands that already share the SAME representation (the `long` vs `long long` LP64 collision, `long double` vs `double` on the f64 axis). What actually drives the usual arithmetic conversions for these types is `signedIntRank(I128)==5` / `unsignedIntRank(U128)==5`, hardcoded in type_rules.hpp:33 — a C++ enum switch this JSON cannot reach. `"rank": 5` below is therefore CORRECT-AND-INERT: it is the honest C 6.3.1.1 rank of the name and it keeps the loader's cross-row consistency check (grammar_schema_json.cpp ~7569, which compares core+rank across every row sharing a `name`) meaningful, but no ordering decision reads it, because `__int128` is the sole I128-named type and `unsigned __int128` the sole U128-named one, so the tie-break can never fire. A future reader chasing a UAC bug must edit type_rules.hpp:33, NOT this number. The rows ARE `name`d (unlike int/short/float, which stay anonymous) because a named type is the whole point here: D-LANG-TYPE-IDENTITY-VOCABULARY, and shippedLibs/setjmp.json's pe `jmp_buf` element is tagged `u128 "unsigned __int128"` to intern the SAME TypeId (an untagged `u128` is a DIFFERENT TypeId — type_lattice.cpp:151-163 short-circuits the empty name — which is the `ssize_t` PHANTOM defect recorded in shippedLibs/sys/types.json).
typeSpecifiers.name: unsigned __int128

typeSpecifiers.$comment: C99 _Complex (D-CSUBSET-COMPLEX §6.2.5): the `complex` row flag wraps the resolved ELEMENT float core in interner.complex() at the specifier-resolve site (semantic_analyzer.cpp), so `double _Complex`→complex(F64), `float _Complex`→complex(F32). `_Complex int`/`_Imaginary` (no row) reject via the absent-multiset discipline (S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination), the `unsigned float` precedent. `long double _Complex` reuses the LD axis: its element is F80/F128 on x87-80/ieee128 (arith walls loud there), F64 on the f64-axis formats (decl/layout/sizeof/ABI-reject work).

P42 (D-CSUBSET-BARE-COMPLEX-SPECIFIER-REFUSED): `_Complex` ALONE, with no float specifier — `_Complex x;` / `__complex__ z;`. ISO C 6.7.2 does not list this multiset, and DSS therefore rejected it via the absent-multiset discipline (`error[S_InvalidTypeSpecifierCombination]`), which was the RIGHT machinery reaching the WRONG answer: ✔MEASURED 2026-08-27 through the shipped CLI (x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows-exec) against gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x` and clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23`, probed SEPARATELY and each binary RUN, BOTH compile it and BOTH give it `double _Complex` (`_Complex x = __builtin_complex(3.0,4.0);` then reading the imaginary part exits 4 on both). The bar is the DISJUNCTION `(gcc ∪ clang ∪ MSVC) ∪ ISO C`, so two accepting references make it REQUIRED — and because both accept it, admitting it is not DSS inventing an extension in the other direction. ⚠ THIS IS A ROW, NOT A DEFAULT: the element core is written here as data, so `_Complex int` (tokens {ComplexKeyword, IntKeyword}) and `_Imaginary` still have NO row and still reject exactly as before — the absent-multiset discipline is untouched and only ONE more multiset is now present.

semantics.$literalTypesComment: FC3 c1: IntLiteral's I32 is the BASE core; the integerLiteralTyping ladder below refines the width by magnitude/suffix/radix per C 6.4.4.1. FloatLiteral's F64 is the BASE core; the floatLiteralTyping suffix map below refines it per C 6.4.4.2 (FC3.5 sweep-c2 / D-CSUBSET-F32-CODEGEN closure: `1.5f` now types F32 — the F32 arithmetic surface shipped, so the typing flip pairs with real codegen). true/false are C23 keyword literals: type Bool with config-declared FIXED values (1/0) — the engine never decodes their text as a number.
semantics.$charStringLiteralComment: C 6.4.4.4: a character constant has type `int` (so sizeof('c')==4, NOT 1) — CharLiteral→I32. C 6.4.5: a string literal has type char[N+1] — StringLiteral declares stringArray:true with element core Char, so the engine builds Array<Char, decodedLen+1> per occurrence (the HIR value path independently lowers the same Array<Char,N+1> via the shared char_decode). charConvertsToArith (below) admits the C char<->int implicit conversion in BOTH directions: int->char (`char x='c';`) and char->int widening (`int y=c;`; codegen materializes the Char->int SExt). Pinned by CharParamReturnedAsIntIsClean + the char_value corpus.
semantics.$scalarConvertsToBoolComment: C 6.3.1.2 (D-CSUBSET-NULLPTR-BOOL-CONVERSION): admit the scalar->_Bool implicit assignment conversion (`_Bool b=5;`, `_Bool b=ptr;`, `_Bool b=nullptr;`, `_Bool b=(a<b);`) — the result is 0 if the value compares equal to 0 else 1. isAssignable's scalar->Bool arm admits an arithmetic (int rank/float/Char/Enum) OR pointer OR nullptr rhs into a Bool lhs; coerce() realizes it as the `!= 0` truthiness test (the SAME condition-materialization `if(x)` uses — NOT a low-bit-truncating Cast, so `_Bool b=2` is true). The MIRROR of boolWidensToArith (Bool rhs->arith lhs). Needed once a comparison result types `int` (D-CSUBSET-SIZEOF-COMPARISON-INT-TYPE): `_Bool b=(a<b)` then flows int->Bool. Flip to false -> scalar->bool errors S0003 (the scalar_to_bool_convert corpus is RED-ON-DISABLE).
semantics.$intCrossSignednessComment: C 6.3.1.3/6.5.16.1 (D-CSUBSET-INT-CROSS-SIGNEDNESS-CONVERT): admit the signed<->unsigned implicit assignment conversion (`int x=u;`, `u=i;`, `return i;`/`f(u)` across the signedness boundary) — value-preserving in range, modular out of range; needed for full-C + SQLite's int/unsigned/size_t mixing. coerce()'s arithmetic-core arm materializes the width-exact Cast. SAME-signedness narrowing (`int x=aLong`) is the SIBLING gate intSameSignednessNarrows below.
semantics.$intSameSignNarrowComment: C 6.3.1.3/6.5.16.1 (D-CSUBSET-INT-SAME-SIGN-NARROW): admit the same-signedness integer NARROWING implicit conversion (`short s=anInt;`, `signed char c=anInt;`, `int i=aLong;` across init/assign/call-arg/return) — value-preserving in range, truncating (modular) out of range; needed for SQLite, which narrows everywhere. The isAssignable rank arms admit rank(rhs)>rank(lhs) only when true; WIDENING stays unconditional. coerce()'s arithmetic-core arm materializes the width-exact Cast (MIR Trunc) — the SAME path cross-signedness narrowing already uses, so NO codegen change. Together with intCrossSignednessConverts this completes the C integer-conversion matrix.
semantics.$intFloatConvertComment: C 6.3.1.4/6.3.1.5/6.5.16.1 (D-CSUBSET-INT-FLOAT-CONVERSION): admit the int<->float implicit assignment conversion in BOTH directions, gated independently. intConvertsToFloat -> an integer flows into a float lhs (`double d=5;`, `f(anInt)` to a `double` param; the sqlite kahanBabuskaNeumaierStep(pSum,iBig) shape feeds an i64 to a `volatile double`). floatConvertsToInt -> a float flows into an integer lhs (`int n=aDouble;`, truncating toward zero). coerce()'s arithmetic-core arm materializes the MIR SIToFP/UIToFP (int->float) / FPToSI/FPToUI (float->int). Flipping either to false -> that direction errors S0003 S_TypeMismatch (the int_float_convert corpus is RED-ON-DISABLE). Completes the C arithmetic-conversion matrix alongside intCrossSignednessConverts + intSameSignednessNarrows.
semantics.$floatNarrowComment: C 6.3.1.4/6.5.16.1 (D-CSUBSET-FLOAT-FROM-DOUBLE-NARROWING): admit the implicit float->float NARROWING assignment conversion -- a WIDER floating rhs into a NARROWER floating lhs (`float f=aDouble;` F64->F32; F80/F128->F64/F32), precision-lossy (gcc's off-by-default -Wconversion), value the nearest representable. Needed for full-C + SQLite's GEOPOLY `typedef float GeoCoord` assigned from `double` RHS (geopolyParseNumber/geopolyRegularFunc). WIDENING (F32->F64) stays UNCONDITIONAL; only narrowing is gated. isAssignable's float rank arm admits rank(rhs)>rank(lhs) only when true; coerce()'s arithmetic-core arm materializes the width-exact Cast (MIR FPTrunc -- the SAME makeCast path F32->F64 widening already uses, NO codegen change). The float-ladder mirror of intSameSignednessNarrows; float->int stays the separate floatConvertsToInt gate. Flip to false -> `float f=aDouble` errors S0003 (the float_narrowing corpus is RED-ON-DISABLE).
semantics.$floatLiteralTypingComment: FC3.5 sweep-c2: C 6.4.4.2 — a floating constant's type is keyed by its SUFFIX alone (unsuffixed -> double, f/F -> float, l/L -> long double). Type names resolve through typeSpecifiers/builtinTypes at LOAD time like the integer ladder's candidates (the `long double` row copies the coreByLongDoubleFormat axis map, so `20.0L` types per-format: F64/F80/F128). The loader cross-checks every numberStyle.floatSuffixes spelling is covered exactly once + an unsuffixed rule exists. FC17.9(e): l/L are in BOTH suffix sets — the tokenizer's per-shape suffix rule keeps integer `20L` an IntLiteral (integer suffixes first on an integer-shaped token) while `20.0L`/`2e1L` take the float suffix.
semantics.$integerLiteralTypingComment: FC3 c1: C 6.4.4.1 EXACTLY — the FIRST candidate (per suffix-group x radix-class) whose range holds the decoded magnitude is the literal's type. `decimal` = no declared numberStyle prefix matched; `nondecimal` (hex/octal/binary) adds the unsigned candidates per the C table. Type names resolve through typeSpecifiers/builtinTypes at LOAD time, so LLP64's 32-bit `long` falls out of the data-model select (2147483648 is `long` on LP64 but `long long` on LLP64). Suffix GROUPS list the exact numberStyle.integerSuffixes spellings they cover; the loader cross-checks every declared suffix is covered exactly once. A magnitude beyond the last candidate -> S_IntegerLiteralTooLarge.
semantics.$arithmeticConversionsComment: FC3 c1: C 6.3.1.8 usual arithmetic conversions, declared (the engine algorithm in analysis/semantic/type_rules.hpp is closed-verb config-driven; languages WITHOUT this block keep the legacy commonType path). integerPromotion: operands below `int`'s rank promote to int; `alsoPromote` pulls char/bool (outside the width-rank lattice) into promotion WITHOUT the engine hardcoding C's view of char. mixedSignedness `rank-prefer-unsigned`: unsigned rank >= signed rank -> the unsigned type, else the (strictly wider) signed type. promoteComparisons: comparisons convert operands to the common type (so -1 > 0ul compares as U64 -> true); the SSA carrier stays i1/Bool while the SEMANTIC result type is C's `int` (D-CSUBSET-SIZEOF-COMPARISON-INT-TYPE / D-CSUBSET-COMPARISON-SEMANTIC-INT-HIR-I1-DIVERGENCE — a deliberate tier split, like char->i32). shiftResult `promotedLeft` (C 6.5.7): a shift's type is its PROMOTED LEFT operand (the right operand never contributes, so `i32 << i64` is I32) -- the engine reads this verb instead of hardcoding C's special shift rule; the alternative `commonType` types `<<`/`>>` like an ordinary binary op (common type of both).

ruleMappings.$comment: FC17.5 (D-CSUBSET-AUTO-TYPE-INFERENCE): ZERO HIR changes — lowerVarLikeInto reads the declared type off the SYMBOL (rec->type, which Pass 1.5's inference arm wrote), never re-derives it from a head, so the headless rule lowers through the same VarDecl row as varDecl.

FC17 (D-CSUBSET-ATTRIBUTE-STATEMENT): a bare attribute-declaration statement (`[[fallthrough]];`) lowers to NOTHING — the emptyStmt Skip precedent, zero C++. The enclosing `declOrAttrStmt` wrapper is deliberately UNMAPPED: the unmapped-statement soleMeaningfulChild PassThrough peels it (for BOTH branches — a varDecl statement reaches its VarDecl row through the same peel).

hirLowering.$foldedConstantRulesComment: P31: the rules whose ENTIRE meaning is a number the SEMANTIC tier already computed. CST→HIR emits the recorded value as a Literal and NEVER lowers the subtree — there is no subtree to lower, because the operands are type-names and member designators rather than expressions. A LIST and not one field per construct, because `read the folded constant` is ONE lowering verb and a second construct must not need a second dispatch arm. A rule named here whose node carries NO recorded constant is a hard REFUSAL, never a zero.
hirLowering.$chooseExprRuleComment: P31: `__builtin_choose_expr` — routed to the SAME `lowerRecordedSelection` body `genericRule` uses, because the two constructs differ ONLY in how the semantic tier picked the winner and never in what the lowering then does with it.
hirLowering.$stmtExprRuleComment: P31 (D-C-GNU-STATEMENT-EXPRESSION): the GNU `({ … })` operand rule. It routes to `lowerStatementExpr`, which builds the ALREADY-EXISTING `HirKind::SeqExpr` ([stmts…, result]) — the node whose own header comment names GCC statement expressions as what it models, and which MIR already lowers by running each statement child through `lowerStmt` and yielding the last child's value. hirLowering.$stringLiteralPrefixesComment: C11/C23 6.4.5 string-literal openers → element core. The narrow StringStart row is auto-seeded by the loader (elementCore=Char) but listed here for clarity. WideStringStart (wchar_t) declares its FORMAT-keyed width AS CONFIG DATA via elementCoreByFormat (elf/macho→I32 the POSIX width, pe→U16 the Windows UTF-16 code unit — D-FFI-STDDEF-WCHAR-PE-WIDTH, the SAME per-format axis stddef.json's wchar_t typedef declares via when.format); elementCore=I32 is the default/fallback for a format-agnostic caller. No engine tier branches on format — the semantic tier resolves the row via a pure config-map lookup (LiteralPrefixEntry::resolveElementCore, mirroring builtinTypes' coreByDataModel) and the HIR tier reads the resolved element core back off the stamped node type. All five openers share the coalesced StringLiteral body token.
hirLowering.$charLiteralPrefixesComment: C11/C23 6.4.4.4 character-constant openers → SCALAR element core (the C23 per-prefix TYPE rule — a char constant's type depends on its prefix). The narrow CharStart row is auto-seeded by the loader (elementCore=I32, the C `int`) but listed here for clarity; the semantic tier keeps it in the flat literalTypeIds int path (other integer-literal consumers depend on it) and OVERRIDES only the wide rows. WideCharStart (wchar_t) declares its FORMAT-keyed width AS CONFIG DATA via the SAME elementCoreByFormat axis the wide-string L" row uses (elf/macho→I32 the POSIX width, pe→U16 the Windows UTF-16 unit — D-FFI-STDDEF-WCHAR-PE-WIDTH); elementCore=I32 is the format-agnostic default. No engine tier branches on format — the semantic tier resolves via a pure resolveElementCore lookup and the HIR tier reads the resolved core back off the stamped body token. All five openers share the coalesced CharLiteral body token. Unlike a string (an Array), a char constant is a SCALAR value (one code unit) typed by this core.
